articles.title: 'How do you know what's real?': US utilities are making AI data centers prove they exist before handing over power connections — as 50% of planned buildouts are currently being delayed, stalled, or canceled
articles.text:
'How do you know what's real?': US utilities are making AI data centers prove they exist before handing over power connections — as 50% of planned buildouts are currently being delayed, stalled, or canceled
The AI boom should have been a golden age for America's electric utilities
- US data center developers have requested 1,066GW of grid connections, but Wood Mackenzie expects utilities to commit to only about 28%
- Utilities are demanding collateral, longer contracts, and study fees; Exelon's high-probability load fell from a whopping 18GW to 11GW once it insisted on the former
- Because grid costs are shared, phantom demand risks landing on household bills, and nobody knows how much of it is real yet
US utilities and grid operators are now demanding higher rates, longer contracts, collateral, and steep engineering study fees from data center developers, in an attempt to weed out what the industry calls "phantom" data centers.
Reporting from The Wall Street Journal claims the reasoning is straightforward: Grid costs are shared, so if a utility builds substations and transmission lines for a project that never shows up, everyone else on the network ends up helping to pay for them.
The numbers back up the nerves in play: developers have requested 1,066GW of grid connections for US data centers, according to a Wood Mackenzie analysis first reported by Bloomberg in August 2026, a figure equal to roughly 83% of the country's entire utility-scale generating capacity at the end of 2025.
A queue full of ghosts as collateral becomes the norm?
Wood Mackenzie expects utilities to commit to serving only about 28% of it: roughly 12% that already has firm service commitments, plus a further 17% that looks likely. The WSJ also cites a separate Wood Mackenzie measure that puts just 23% of disclosed requests in its high-confidence category.
Much of the gap is due to duplication; developers who don't yet know which utility can deliver power fastest file the same project with several of them and keep every option open until one pans out.
Others are simply speculators: commentary in POWER Magazine argued that private equity funds, land brokers and shell companies are claiming queue positions without site control or a signed customer, betting that land with a grid connection attached will find a buyer.
The phenomenon isn't new. Utility Dive was writing about phantom data centers in 2025, and TR reported in July that 67% of electricity executives surveyed by Capgemini were seeing speculative applications for capacity. The change is that utilities are now pricing the problem, and it is causing many adverse effects.

Exelon's attempts to lock down potential consumers
Exelon, which runs utilities across the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, offers the clearest look at what happens when developers are asked to put money down.
After it began requiring transmission security agreements (TSAs), contracts that bind customers to credit obligations, committed revenue contributions, and shortfall payments, its high-probability data center load fell nearly 40%, from 18GW at the end of 2025 to about 11GW in the second quarter. Its wider pipeline of projects under study dropped from about 43GW to 25GW.
Jeanne Jones, Exelon's CFO, told the WSJ that typical requests used to be around 50MW and now often run to 1,000MW or more. The question she kept fielding, internally and externally, was "How do you know what's real?"
Exelon, however, also told analysts its $41 billion capital plan through 2029 is unchanged, so a 40% cut in expected data center load has not, so far, shrunk the spending plan.
None of this would matter much if grid capacity were cheap, but it simply isn't. PJM, the largest US grid operator, saw its capacity auction clear at the price cap for the third time in a row this summer while missing its reliability target by 6.8GW.
In September, its independent market monitor told federal regulators that 4,017MW of forecast data center load, 42% of the growth PJM had assumed, had already been canceled or delayed.
Households are feeling the cost increase; reports in July indicated that Henrico County, Virginia, asked staff and schools to cut electricity use after a 24.9% rate increase. Virginia has also moved to stop utilities passing data center costs onto everyday users, and Texas bills are rising faster than inflation. Lindsey Short of the Ohio Manufacturers' Association warned against building the grid around "the most optimistic number on somebody's spreadsheet."
Underbuilding carries its own risks, though, especially when transformers can take years to arrive, as a recent deep dive on grid bottlenecks laid out. That is why utilities are locking in the customers they do accept. Average minimum contract lengths for large customers have risen to about 10.8 years from 4.6 before 2024, according to filings aggregated by Halcyon and cited by the Journal, and a separate research brief built on Halcyon's tracker found a similar jump.
What nobody can yet say is how much of the AI power rush is real, and that poses problems for planners, stakeholders, and households alike. Until it does, utilities are doing what any lender would: asking to see the money first; households just happen to be roadkill if things don't pan out.

articles.title: La dernière grille de Free TV ne passe pas, des chaînes thématiques déplorent une plongée des audiences
articles.text:
L'ACCES, qui représente les chaînes du câble et du satellite, a saisi l'ARCOM au sujet de la nouvelle numérotation des chaînes de Free. Elle reproche à l'opérateur d’avoir mis en avant les chaînes FAST, au détriment de leur audience.
La nouvelle numérotation des chaînes de Free TV, en place depuis le 25 août, ne passe toujours pas auprès de certains éditeurs. L'ACCES qui fédère les chaînes du câble et du satellite, vient de saisir le régulateur de l'audiovisuel et du numérique, l'ARCOM, en brandissant des chiffres de Médiamétrie. L'association des chaînes conventionnées éditrices de services explique que les canaux qui ont reculé dans la grille auraient perdu en moyenne plus d'un cinquième de leur couverture auprès des abonnés Free. Moins visibles, elles disposeraient aussi de moins de moyens pour financer leurs programmes, prévient-elle, comme l'a rapporté le média spécialisé Écran total mardi 20 octobre.
Free TV a rangé ses chaînes… mais dérangé leurs éditeurs, qui demandent des comptes
Le 25 août, près de 700 chaînes ont changé de numéro sur les Freebox et dans l’application Free TV. Free les range désormais par thème, et chaque thème démarre à une centaine ronde, facile à retenir. Il y a le cinéma et les séries au canal 100, le sport au 200, la jeunesse au 300, l’info au 600, les chaînes locales et régionales au 900, et les chaînes étrangères au-delà du 1000. Les chaînes gratuites de la TNT, elles, gardent leurs numéros habituels, TF1 en tête sur le 1. Certaines chaînes payantes, dites premium, apparaissent même deux fois, à leur nouvelle place thématique et dans un raccourci en début de liste, entre les canaux 32 et 56. beIN SPORTS 1 est par exemple accessible à la fois sur le 36 et sur le 245. Des bandeaux affichés à l’écran annonçaient le changement depuis le 11 août.
On comprend l'idée. Chaque famille de chaînes a son quartier, avec une chaîne mosaïque pour en faire le tour d'un coup d'œil, et aucune chaîne n'a disparu. Mais l'ACCES retient autre chose. Free a placé en tête plusieurs univers de chaînes FAST (pour Free Ad-supported Streaming Television), qui sont des chaînes gratuites diffusées en streaming et financées par la publicité, ainsi que d'autres chaînes 100 % numériques. Pour l'association, cette organisation modifie très concrètement les conditions d'accès du public aux chaînes conventionnées.
Pour mesurer ce que ce grand déménagement coûte vraiment à ses chaînes, l’ACCES s’est tournée vers Médiamétrie, l’institut de référence de la mesure d’audience en France. Selon les premiers retours, les chaînes dont le numéro a reculé ont perdu en moyenne 22 % de couverture mensuelle chez les abonnés Free de 4 ans et plus, par rapport à septembre 2025. Ce chiffre est à manier avec prudence, car avancé par une partie prenante, et la comparaison remonte à plus d'un an, période pendant laquelle d'autres facteurs ont pu peser.
L’ACCES demande à l’ARCOM de passer la grille de Free au crible
Pour défendre ses membres, l’ACCES affirme que ses chaînes ne jouent pas avec les mêmes règles que les chaînes FAST. Car les chaînes conventionnées, liées à l'ARCOM par une convention, doivent respecter des règles éditoriales et de protection des publics. Selon leur régime, elles sont aussi tenues de diffuser des œuvres françaises et européennes et de participer au financement de la création. Les FAST, souligne l'association, n'ont pas ces contraintes. Cette dernière réclame donc que la mise en avant dans la grille tienne compte des obligations effectives de chaque service et de sa contribution réelle à la création.
L'association déplore aussi le timing. Les chaînes thématiques subissent déjà l'éclatement des usages et la pression sur leurs revenus. Moins exposées, elles risquent de s'affaiblir davantage et de réduire les moyens qu'elles consacrent aux programmes. L'ACCES rappelle enfin que, depuis quarante ans, les chaînes payantes ont rendu attractives les offres du câble, du satellite puis des fournisseurs d'accès à Internet, en aidant à recruter et fidéliser les abonnés. Les opérateurs qui ont grandi avec ces « partenaires historiques » doivent, selon elle, préserver leur visibilité.
L'ACCES demande désormais à l'ARCOM d'examiner rapidement le plan de services de Free. Elle appelle aussi l'opérateur à ouvrir le dialogue avec les éditeurs, pour corriger les positions qu'elle estime insuffisamment justifiées et rendre aux chaînes de découverte et de documentaire une place facilement identifiable. On attend de voir quelle suite le régulateur et l'opérateur, qui misait sur un zapping simplifié, donneront à cette demande.

articles.title: Databuddy Analytics raises $500,000 from Y Combinator
articles.text: US-based AI-powered analytics startup Databuddy Analytics has raised more than $560,000 in total funding, including $500,000 in Seed funding from Y Combinator, alongside investments from Maza Ventures and through the a16z Scout programme. Founded in 2026 by Palestinian entrepreneur Issa Nassar, Databuddy Analytics develops an AI-powered product analytics platform that helps businesses identify conversion drops, customer friction and product issues through automated investigations and actionable insights. The funding will support the development of more advanced AI investigation capabilities, additional integrations, targeted hiring and improved customer onboarding, as the company seeks to expand its user base. Press release: Databuddy Analytics, the AI-driven analytics platform, has raised $500,000 in Seed funding from Y Combinator as it launches its AI intelligence platform. With investment from Maza Ventures and through the a16z Scout programme, Databuddy has raised more than $560,000 to date. The company's new AI analytics platform investigates conversion drops, customer friction and product issues on a team's behalf and brings the findings to them. Unlike the traditional web analytics approach, the platform proactively shows what changed and why, without the need to dig through reports and filters. Databuddy has grown to serve more than 3,000 businesses in the first few months since launch. "Teams don't want more charts; they want to know what's broken and what to do about it," says Issa Nassar, Founder of Databuddy. "We built Databuddy so that the answer is one question away. Y Combinator's backing lets us move faster on that and put it in front of far more teams." Issa Nassar grew up in Palestine, started coding at age 11 and dropped out of university. He was accepted into Y Combinator at 20, becoming the youngest founder in the Middle East to be accepted into Silicon Valley’s iconic accelerator. Tambi Jalouqa, Managing Partner at Maza Ventures, shared, "Most founders start by explaining the market. Issa started by showing us what he had built. Databuddy is one of those products that looks deceptively simple, which is usually a sign that someone has spent a lot of time thinking about the problem. Issa has the combination we look for at Maza: he's deeply technical, moves unusually fast, and seems more interested in making something people want than in looking like a startup founder. Those are often the founders worth betting on early." The funding will support deeper AI investigation capabilities, additional integrations and targeted hiring. Databuddy will also invest in onboarding and migration support, helping more teams connect their existing data and put the platform to work.

articles.title: Trump officials asked CISA to secretly hack a voting machine — and not disclose any vulnerabilities they found
articles.text:
Trump officials asked CISA to secretly hack a voting machine — and not disclose any vulnerabilities they found
CISA usually helps protect elections, but this time they were asked to help hack them
- Trump administration officials asked CISA to hack a voting machine just months into his second term
- CISA was told not to disclose any vulnerabilities to the voting machine manufacturer
- CISA has been gutted by job cuts and a lack of funding, with many state officials hesitant to trust the agency with securing the midterm elections
Towards the start of President Trump’s second term, allies in the Department of Homeland Security tasked the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) with secretly acquiring a voting machine with instructions to hack it and not tell anyone except the White House about the vulnerabilities they found.
ProPublica, who spoke to two former administration officials with knowledge of the request, noted that the standard practices of CISA require the agency to let manufacturers know of vulnerabilities in their technology, but the political appointees explicitly asked CISA not to.
“My thought was they could keep it in their back pocket to invalidate any [election] results they don’t like,” one of the former officials told ProPublica. “This goes against everything CISA represents.”
CISA asked to hack voting machine
CISA has been a relentless target of the Trump Administration, with the agency’s jobs being cut by one third and the majority of its senior leadership resigning or being fired.
In total, CISA has cut 1,000 jobs since the start of Trump’s second term - largely down to Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency - with additional cuts to funding in 2027 likely to result in a further 900 jobs being lost.
As a result of these job cuts, remaining CISA employees told the political appointees that the request to hack a voting machine couldn’t be fulfilled.
Since 2018, CISA has been responsible for helping to protect election infrastructure from cyber attacks and interference, but has had to cut back on much of its work in these areas due to a lack of funding and staff. Many state officials have been unable to seek election support ahead of the November midterm elections.

As a result of Trump’s cuts to CISA’s jobs and funding, many state officials fear the agency has become a shell occupied by Trump loyalists. “They’ve violated the entire premise of that information-sharing relationship,” a former high-ranking federal cybersecurity official told ProPublica. “There’s no fucking way they’re ever going to give any information to CISA. And it’s unclear if they ever will in the future.”
In response to the claims, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said, “President Trump has done more than any other President to ensure we have free and fair elections.”
“I don’t pay attention to what the president says. I pay attention to what his administration does,” said Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes. “And what they’ve done is basically cut us off and left us on our own.”
Voting difficulties start early
Early voting for the midterms has already started in some states, but early polling sites at North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University, the University of North Carolina Greensboro, and Western Carolina University have been shut down, with Guilford County board members saying the resources could be better allocated elsewhere.
Shutting the polling sites makes it significantly harder for the collective 40,000 students to vote, with university policy preventing some students from owning a car during their first year of study.
Shia Rozier, a senior at North Carolina A&T and cofounder of student organization Protect Ours NC told NPR, “In order to get to the polls, they now have to get a Lyft or get a Uber or get somebody to take them at a time where gas prices are extremely high, creating an additional barrier to the poll.”
In response, students organized a march to the nearest polling site over 45 minutes away.

articles.title: CapQuest closes $1 million pre-Seed funding to expand globally
articles.text: UAE-based fintech startup CapQuest has raised $1 million in a pre-Seed funding round, led by Oraseya Capital and AMKM Family Office, to accelerate product development and international expansion. Founded in 2023 by Antoine Bruna, Marco Banfi and Anvita Varshney, CapQuest operates an equity management platform that enables startups and established businesses to manage ownership structures, capitalisation tables, employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs), vesting schedules, fundraising transactions and shareholder communications. The funding will support product development, increased automation, enhanced equity management tools and commercial expansion, as the company seeks to grow its international customer base. Press release: CapQuest, a Dubai-based equity management platform, has announced the successful closing of its $1 million Pre-Seed funding round, led by Oraseya Capital and AMKM Family Office. Founded by Antoine Bruna, Marco Banfi, and Anvita Varshney, CapQuest is transforming how companies manage equity, ownership, and investor relations. The platform enables startups, scaleups, and established businesses to manage their cap tables, employee equity plans (ESOPs), vesting schedules, fundraising transactions, and shareholder communications through a single, centralised solution. Designed to replace fragmented spreadsheets and manual processes, CapQuest helps companies simplify complex equity operations, improve transparency, and maintain accurate ownership records throughout their growth. Growing International Traction Since its launch, CapQuest has established a growing international presence, serving companies across 11 countries, with a strong focus on the Middle East, Europe and emerging markets. Its client portfolio includes notable companies such as Holo, Erad, Avenia, and Teylor, reflecting increasing demand for modern equity management infrastructure among high-growth businesses. CapQuest's continued expansion highlights the growing importance of effective equity governance as companies navigate fundraising, employee ownership, and increasingly complex shareholder structures. Accelerating Growth and Product Innovation The funding will accelerate product development, expand CapQuest's commercial presence, and enhance its equity management capabilities through greater automation and more advanced tools. “This funding represents an important milestone for CapQuest and a strong validation of our vision,” said Antoine Bruna, CEO & Co-Founder of CapQuest. “Equity management remains unnecessarily complex for many companies, particularly as they scale and expand internationally. We’re building the infrastructure to make equity management more accessible, transparent, and efficient. With a growing international customer base and an expanding suite of products, CapQuest aims to become a leading platform for equity and investment management, connecting companies, shareholders, and investors within a unified ecosystem.

articles.title: Amazon hikes Prime membership by up to 30% in Australia ahead of Black Friday and holiday sales
articles.text:
Amazon hikes Prime membership by up to 30% in Australia ahead of Black Friday and holiday sales
Effective immediately for new members, while the price hike comes into effect from November 25 for existing subscribers
- Amazon Prime subscriptions will increase to AU$12.99 per month or AU$99 per year, up from AU$9.99 and AU$79, respectively
- These prices are effective immediately for new subscribers, while existing members will be charged starting from November 25
- Inclusions and perks like Prime Video, Music Prime and sale events remain unchanged
Amazon Australia has revealed its monthly Prime membership fee has increased from AU$9.99 to AU$12.99, effective immediately for new subscribers — a significant 30% hike from the previous cost. The annual membership price also increases from AU$79 to AU$99, a 25% rise.
In emails sent to Prime members, Amazon said the new pricing reflects the growing range of products and benefits available through the service, although the inclusions remain the same, including free and expedited delivery, Prime Video, Prime Music, Prime Reading, video games with Amazon Luna, and member-only events such as Prime Day and Prime Big Deal Days.
Existing customers will continue to pay the usual AU$9.99 per month and the price increase will apply from their first membership renewal date on or after November 25, 2026.
In a statement, an Amazon spokesperson told TechRadar that this price change is specific to Australia and attributes it largely to the expanded delivery footprint, new Prime Video content and access to Alexa+.
"We are committed to growing the value of Prime for members, and in just the last six months we have brought Prime Free overnight delivery before 8am on hundreds of thousands of products to four cities, expanded Prime Free Same-Day Delivery available now in nine regions across Australia, added new TV series and movies to Prime Video plus live sport, given free access to Alexa+, provided exclusive deals through events like Prime Day, and more," the spokesperson said.
"With the continued expansion of Prime member benefits, and so we can continue growing the offering, we will change the price of Prime to $12.99 per month or $99 per year. Prime has never offered as much value for members as it does today."
This price hike comes just in time before Amazon’s own Black Friday sale in Australia, which we expect to start a few days before the actual Black Friday date of November 27, and will run until Cyber Monday on November 30.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While the US has seen multiple price increases recently, this is Amazon’s second round of hikes in Australia since launching in 2018. Initially just AU$6.99 per month or AU$59 per year at launch, Amazon later bumped that up to AU$9.99 per month (43%) or AU$79 per year (34%) in May 2023 as more inclusions were added. As mentioned, the price doesn’t reflect better inclusions, which is surely going to factor into household costs for many regular Amazon shoppers.
Earlier this month, Amazon opened its third Sydney fulfilment centre located in western suburb of Horsley Park which is “a 12-hour drive of 80% of Australia”, meaning even more shoppers will benefit from same-day delivery. Perhaps this goes some way in justifying a price increase, along with the fact that Amazon typically offers the best prices on thousands of items even outside of major sales. However, with an additional AU$2 monthly payment to get rid of ads on Prime Video, this news is sure to sting some customers.
While the Amazon Black Friday sale in Australia isn’t a Prime-exclusive event, the best prices will be for subscribers, so it does still pay to have a subscription. Thankfully, Amazon also makes it easy to cancel your subscription any time, although you won’t be eligible for the usual 30-day free trial if you’re a returning customer.

articles.title: Ni el calendario está a salvo: así son las falsas invitaciones y reuniones para robar datos y dinero
articles.text:
Los ataques de phishing a través de invitaciones de calendario se multiplicaron por más de diez entre julio y agosto de 2026, según datos de la firma de seguridad Sublime citados por Business Insider. Una modalidad sencilla en la que un evento aparece sin aviso en la agenda, con apariencia de reunión legítima, y basta un clic para comprometer contraseñas, datos de pago o la computadora entera.
La razón del crecimiento es, sobre todo, psicológica. Muchos usuarios ya desconfían de un correo con enlaces sospechosos, pero pocos sospechan de una cita que aparece directamente en su calendario de trabajo.
Cómo funciona el engaño en el calendario digital
El mecanismo es simple. El atacante envía una invitación a una reunión falsa o incluye mensajes sobre llamadas perdidas, facturas impagas o suscripciones por renovar. El evento trae enlaces maliciosos incrustados, listos para activarse con un clic.
Según el reporte de Microsoft, las invitaciones de calendario se procesan de forma distinta a los adjuntos de correo tradicionales: un enlace dañino puede llegar directamente a la agenda del usuario sin que este tenga que abrir ningún archivo adjunto.
Ron Kerbs, director ejecutivo de Kidas, empresa que desarrolla herramientas para detectar estafas y deepfakes en llamadas de voz, explicó que las invitaciones fraudulentas suelen adoptar dos formas. En la primera, el evento contiene un enlace de reunión comprometido o un formulario diseñado para robar credenciales o instalar malware.
En la segunda, la víctima ingresa a una videollamada que parece legítima y se encuentra con un impostor que se hace pasar por alguien de confianza, muchas veces con el nombre real de un empleado pero una dirección de correo falsa.
Es importante entender por qué este tipo de ataque resulta tan eficaz: la invitación llega directamente al calendario sin pasar por el filtro mental de “correo sospechoso” y algunas aplicaciones la muestran de forma automática aunque el usuario nunca la haya aceptado, lo que le da una apariencia de autenticidad inmediata.
Kerbs agregó que los estafadores recurren a tecnología de inteligencia artificial generativa para sumar realismo al engaño. “Están usando tecnología deepfake para parecerse al mismo tipo de soporte técnico”, señaló, en referencia al uso de audio o video generado por IA que imita a un empleado real de una compañía.
Casos que muestran el alcance del engaño
Aman Gairola, cofundador de la agencia de diseño india Say Design, creyó haber conseguido un cliente en junio cuando alguien reservó una reunión a través del sitio web de su empresa. La invitación incluía un enlace a lo que parecía una carpeta de Google Drive con un resumen de proyecto.
Gairola hizo clic y llegó a una página que imitaba a Google Drive, pero algo no cuadraba. Revisó la dirección del sitio, confirmó que era falsa y evitó abrir cualquier archivo. “Si tengo que calificar qué tan convincente es, le pondría un 9,5 sobre 10”, dijo, y agregó que su empresa evalúa eliminar la opción de agendar llamadas directamente desde su web y reemplazarla por un formulario.
Otro riesgo surge incluso cuando el remitente es una persona real y conocida. La montañista y oradora Jenn Drummond sufrió el robo de su cuenta de correo mientras abordaba un vuelo, y desde esa cuenta se envió a decenas de sus contactos una invitación de calendario que advertía sobre una supuesta citación judicial, con un enlace a un aviso legal falso que solicitaba datos financieros.
“¿Qué van a pensar? Que no soy confiable, y tu marca se construye sobre la confianza”, relató Drummond.
Cómo protegerse del fraude
Los especialistas recomiendan aplicar a los eventos inesperados el mismo nivel de desconfianza que a un correo sospechoso. En la práctica, eso implica no abrir enlaces ni llamar a teléfonos incluidos en invitaciones de remitentes desconocidos, y revisar la configuración del calendario para desactivar que las invitaciones entrantes se agreguen de forma automática.
Mathew Woodyard, director de inteligencia de amenazas en la firma de gestión de identidad Okta, sostuvo que la responsabilidad principal recae en las empresas que operan los servicios, más que en la capacidad del usuario para detectar una invitación falsa.
También señaló que las passkeys pueden resolver buena parte del problema, porque se crean para una página específica y solo funcionan en el sitio web auténtico, nunca en una copia falsa.
Eso elimina la necesidad de que la persona tenga que juzgar por su cuenta si un enlace es confiable. “Hasta que los factores resistentes al phishing como las passkeys se conviertan en el estándar por defecto, los ataques de phishing van a seguir funcionando”, concluyó.

articles.title: TikTok accusé de mettre des enfants en danger et de faciliter le blanchiment d’argent
articles.text:
« Je me bats depuis des mois pour régler ça avec des gens qui ne trouvent pas les dégâts assez graves », écrivait une responsable de la sécurité de TikTok à un collègue. Avec d’autres salariés, elle a raconté sous serment comment la direction de l’application a laissé traîner leurs alertes sur l’exploitation sexuelle d’adolescents.
La radio publique américaine NPR a pu consulter ces témoignages, versés en mars 2026 au dossier d’une procédure fédérale où sont regroupées, depuis 2022, des centaines de plaintes contre TikTok, Meta, Google et Snap. Les plaignants accusent ces entreprises d’avoir conçu des plateformes nocives pour les mineurs et caché les risques qu’elles connaissaient. Aucun jury n’a encore examiné ces dépositions, et TikTok a évité plusieurs procès en signant des accords amiables, dont l’un avec l’Alabama, en septembre, contre 100 millions de dollars. Dans une déclaration envoyée après la publication de l’enquête, Nathaniel Brown, porte-parole de TikTok, a dénoncé des citations « triées sur le volet à la demande des avocats des plaignants ». Les salariés entendus ont surtout parlé de l’argent que TikTok tirait de lives où apparaissaient des mineurs, et de protections que les adolescents contournaient à l’insu de leurs parents.
Des cadeaux virtuels dont TikTok gardait une part
Les spectateurs de TikTok Live achètent des cadeaux virtuels qu’ils offrent aux personnes qui filment en direct. Ces dernières les échangent ensuite contre de l’argent, et TikTok garde une commission au passage. Reagen Maher, qui a occupé entre 2021 et 2024 des postes de responsable dans les équipes de sécurité et d’enquêtes de TikTok, a mené pendant des mois une « croisade » afin de faire remonter ses constats jusqu’à V Pappas, qui dirigeait alors les opérations. D’après elle, l’entreprise savait que des mineurs se déshabillaient sur Live avant qu’une enquête de presse ne le révèle en 2022. TikTok limitait depuis 2021 la diffusion en direct des 13-17 ans, mais ses enquêteurs internes ont trouvé, rien qu’en janvier 2022, des adolescents de 13 à 15 ans dans 112 000 vidéos en direct. Dans leur rapport, ils ont relevé des risques de pédopiégeage et des « revenus importants » tirés de cadeaux envoyés à des lives contraires au règlement.
Silvija Krupena dirige la cellule de renseignement financier du cabinet britannique RedCompass Labs. Pour elle, l’argent issu de l’exploitation d’enfants peut constituer le produit d’un crime, et les entreprises qui le traitent sciemment risquent des poursuites pour blanchiment. « Un adulte a payé. Un enfant a été exploité. La plateforme a pris sa part », résume-t-elle. Elle ajoute que les alertes adressées aux dirigeants pèsent lourd, car la responsabilité pénale dépend de ce que l’entreprise savait. TikTok assure appliquer un programme anti-blanchiment conforme aux standards internationaux. La loi américaine oblige les plateformes à déclarer les contenus pédocriminels au Centre national pour les enfants disparus et exploités (NCMEC). Interrogé par NPR, TikTok n’a pas dit s’il avait signalé ces lives, ni ce qu’il avait fait de l’argent encaissé.
Des parents tenus à l’écart, selon d’anciens salariés
TikTok a lancé en 2020 la Connexion famille, avec laquelle les parents peuvent limiter le temps d’écran de leur adolescent et filtrer certains contenus. L’année suivante, des salariés ont repéré un lien caché dans les comptes d’adolescents. Il suffisait de l’utiliser pour sortir du contrôle parental. « Ça rend la fonction un peu inutile », a écrit Jordon Furlong, alors chef de produit chargé du bien-être numérique, dans une discussion interne. Si vous avez activé la Connexion famille, TikTok assure aujourd’hui prévenir votre compte quand votre enfant la quitte.
Reagen Maher a signalé une autre faille dans sa déposition. En s’inscrivant avec un compte Google, Facebook ou Instagram, un enfant pouvait accéder à la version de TikTok réservée aux plus de 18 ans, et la direction le savait, assure-t-elle. Les dirigeants ont même évité de connaître l’âge de leurs utilisateurs. Après le rachat de Musical.ly en 2018, Adam Wang, qui dirigeait TikTok Live, et Alex Zhu, président de TikTok, ont préparé un sondage auprès des utilisateurs américains. Ils ont écarté toute question sur le niveau scolaire, de peur de révéler des enfants de moins de 13 ans, dont la loi COPPA protège les données. « Si la FTC apprend l’existence de ce sondage, elle pourrait nous en demander les résultats », notait Adam Wang sur la messagerie interne, à propos de l’autorité américaine de protection des consommateurs. Eric Han, responsable de la sécurité de TikTok entre 2019 et 2023, a signalé en interne, dès 2020, un « effet de contagion » des contenus liés au suicide. Il a indiqué dans sa déposition que TikTok n’avait pas averti les parents des dangers de l’application.
La Commission européenne a accusé TikTok en juillet de mal protéger les comptes des mineurs, après avoir estimé en février que ses contrôles parentaux demandaient trop de temps et de connaissances techniques à la plupart des parents. Ses conclusions sont préliminaires, mais si Bruxelles les confirme, TikTok risque une amende jusqu’à 6 % de son chiffre d’affaires mondial.

articles.title: Cómo saber qué dice un audio de WhatsApp sin tener que reproducirlo
articles.text:
Los mensajes de voz no siempre llegan en un momento adecuado para escucharlos. WhatsApp ofrece una herramienta integrada para convertirlos en texto y consultar lo que dicen directamente debajo del audio. No hace falta instalar otra aplicación ni reproducir el mensaje: basta con activar las transcripciones y seleccionar el idioma que se utiliza con mayor frecuencia.
La función también puede facilitar el acceso a las conversaciones a las personas sordas o con dificultades auditivas. Las transcripciones están desactivadas de forma predeterminada, así que es necesario habilitarlas desde los ajustes del teléfono antes de usarlas. WhatsApp explica que el texto se genera en el dispositivo y que los mensajes personales siguen protegidos con cifrado de extremo a extremo.
Cómo activar las transcripciones
El primer paso es abrir WhatsApp y entrar en Ajustes o Configuración. En Android, se accede desde el menú de tres puntos de la parte superior; en iPhone, desde la pestaña de ajustes o tocando la foto de perfil, según la versión de la aplicación.
Después, sigue esta ruta:
- Entra en Chats.
- Pulsa Transcripciones de mensajes de voz.
- Activa la opción.
- Toca Seleccionar idioma y elige el que hablas habitualmente en los audios recibidos.
- Si la aplicación lo solicita, descarga el paquete de idioma para completar la configuración.
La descarga prepara el reconocimiento en el dispositivo. WhatsApp indica que, por el momento, admite transcripciones en inglés, portugués, español y ruso; la disponibilidad puede depender del sistema operativo y la versión de la aplicación. En iPhone, la herramienta requiere iOS 16 o posterior y Siri activado.
Cómo leer un audio sin reproducirlo
Una vez activada la herramienta, abre el chat donde está el mensaje de voz y mantén pulsado el audio. En iPhone, selecciona Transcribir en el menú que aparece. En Android, mantén pulsado el mensaje, toca el menú de tres puntos y elige la misma opción.
WhatsApp procesará la nota y mostrará el texto en el propio chat, debajo del mensaje de voz. La transcripción puede tardar unos segundos en aparecer. Si el texto queda parcialmente visible, se puede tocar el mensaje para expandirlo y leerlo completo.
No es necesario que el remitente active nada: la transcripción se crea en el teléfono de quien recibió el audio. Tampoco se envía una notificación al remitente indicando que el mensaje fue transcrito. Según WhatsApp, el proceso se realiza localmente y la compañía no puede escuchar el audio ni leer el texto generado.
Qué hacer si la transcripción no aparece
Si no ves la opción Transcribir, comprueba que la función esté activada y que el idioma elegido coincida con el del audio. También puedes actualizar WhatsApp, verificar que el paquete de idioma se haya descargado o revisar los requisitos de iOS si utilizas un iPhone.
La herramienta no siempre reconoce todo con exactitud. El ruido de fondo, una grabación poco clara, los cambios de idioma, los nombres propios y las expresiones locales pueden afectar el resultado. Por eso, una transcripción sirve para entender el tema general de un audio, pero puede contener errores en palabras o frases concretas.
La función es distinta de la traducción: convierte la voz en texto en el idioma seleccionado, pero no necesariamente traduce lo que se dijo. Si el mensaje está en un idioma no compatible o la voz se entiende con dificultad, WhatsApp puede no generar una transcripción correcta. En esos casos, se puede cambiar el idioma desde Ajustes > Chats > Transcripciones de mensajes de voz o pedir al remitente que envíe el contenido por escrito.
Con la opción activada, basta con mantener pulsado el mensaje y elegir Transcribir para consultar su contenido sin reproducirlo. No elimina el audio ni lo convierte automáticamente al llegar: cada usuario decide cuándo solicitar el texto y qué idioma utilizar.

articles.title: Egyptian proptech Aqar Exit attracts investment at $2 million valuation
articles.text: Egypt-based proptech startup Aqar Exit has secured a $200,000 (EGP 10 million) investment from businessman Ayman Mamdouh Abbas, executive chairman of Intro Holding Group, in exchange for a 10% stake, valuing the company at approximately $2 million (EGP 100 million). Founded in July 2026 by Mahmoud Ammar, Aqar Exit operates a real estate platform that enables property buyers struggling with instalment payments to transfer their purchase contracts to new buyers, allowing sellers to recover payments and buyers to access units at their original contract prices. Since its launch, the company has reported EGP 9 billion in closed listings across 638 transactions, including 404 in its most recent reported month. However, its definition of closed transactions includes listings removed from the platform, rather than necessarily completed sales. The investment will support the launch of new products and expansion into international markets, particularly the Gulf region. Aqar Exit is targeting a $5 million funding round in 2027, with plans to attract local and international investors to support its regional growth. Press release: Egyptian proptech startup Aqar Exit has secured an investment of EGP 10 million (approximately $200,000) from businessman Ayman Mamdouh Abbas, executive chairman of Intro Holding Group, in exchange for a 10% stake in the company. The transaction values Aqar Exit at EGP 100 million (approximately $2 million) on a post-money basis, according to founder and chairman Mahmoud Ammar, who disclosed the investment in an interview with Al Arabiya Business. Founded in July 2026, Aqar Exit operates a platform for transferring property purchase contracts, targeting buyers who are struggling to meet instalment obligations on their real estate units. The platform connects these sellers with prospective buyers seeking properties at their original contract prices, without paying additional premiums, commonly known in Egypt's property market as overprice. Under the company's model, sellers can seek to recover the amounts they have already paid towards their properties without incurring contract assignment fees. The investment follows Aqar Exit's participation in the fifth season of Shark Tank Egypt, where it presented its business model to investors. According to Ammar, the company will use the new capital to develop additional products and support its expansion into international markets, with a particular focus on the Gulf. Aqar Exit has reported EGP 9 billion in closed listings since launching, covering 638 transactions, including 404 in its most recent reported month, compared with 233 in the preceding month. However, the company's definition of a closed transaction includes any listing removed from the platform, meaning the figures do not necessarily represent completed property sales or revenue generated by Aqar Exit. The platform has also registered 14,845 property assignment files submitted by 11,833 sellers, alongside 67,013 purchase requests from 32,870 prospective buyers. Average daily purchase requests increased by 58% to 1,060, from 671 in the preceding period, according to company figures. Looking ahead, Aqar Exit plans to pursue a funding round of approximately $5 million in 2027, targeting participation from Egyptian and international investors, businesspeople and investment funds. The planned financing would support the company's product development and regional expansion as it seeks to establish a broader market for transferring property purchase contracts.

articles.title: Are the Kindle Scribe e-readers as good as they sound? Here's what you need to know before you buy one
articles.text:
Should I buy a Kindle Scribe or a Kindle Scribe Colorsoft? Here's what you need to know
These e-readers also let you scribble down notes — but are they worth the extra spend?
Kindles aren't just for reading — Amazon also makes a couple of Kindles that you can scribble notes on. The Kindle Scribe and Kindle Scribe Colorsoft both have a generous, glare-free e-ink screen you can use for reading or writing; they're billed as streamlined, minimalist productivity tools that help you stay focused.
We've been impressed with both e-readers — the Kindle Scribe holds a coveted spot in our best e-readers ranking. However, there are some compromises involved in choosing one of these models rather than a reading-only option. If you're not sure which one to buy, or whether a different Kindle altogether might fit your needs more closely, you're in the right place.
In this guide, I'll provide a handy overview of the Kindle Scribe and Scribe Colorsoft, including how the specs match up and any major downsides for each model, as well as how they compare to the wider Kindle lineup. I'll also round up the different iterations so you can see your options and what they cost. Let's get started...
Kindle Scribe — Overview
The Kindle Scribe is Amazon's black-and-white e-reader with writing support included. We're on our third generation, released in the US in late 2025 and in other territories in early 2026. We awarded it an impressive 4.5 stars in our Kindle Scribe (2025) review.
Probably because it had already had a relatively recent update, the Kindle Scribe wasn't included in the big refresh the rest of the range enjoyed in October 2026 (we now have a classic Kindle 2026, a Kindle Paperwhite 2026 and a Kindle Colorsoft 2026).
The Scribe is basically a Kindle, except that if you want to take notes, you can grab the stylus and scribble down your thoughts. That's probably simplifying it a bit too much — there are a number of writing features to explore, including an adjustable-size Quick Notes pad, various workspace templates, AI-powered handwriting conversion and summary creation tools, and the ability to add notes onto a book (with text wrapping around it) or in a margin column. The newest version also includes Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive connectivity.

The Kindle Scribe is not just a Kindle Paperwhite with writing functionality, though — it diverges in both design and specs from the reading-only models. For a start, it's much bigger. The screen is 11 inches diagonally, while reading Kindles have a 6-inch or 7-inch screen. It's also heavier, clocking in at around double the weight of the Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (with 7-inch screens). Like the cheapest base model, it isn't waterproof, so it's not good for reading or note-taking in the bath.

In reading mode, the battery life is among the longest on any Kindle, but switch to note-taking, and it drops considerably. Amazon estimates around 3 weeks of writing before you'll need to recharge — still a lot longer than your average tablet, mind you. You can choose from different storage capacities, but keep in mind that all the writing features eat up quite a bit of space.
In some territories, you can choose between a model with a frontlight and one without. If you want to read or write in any lighting conditions, you'll need to stump up for the frontlight version. Assuming you have, you'll be able to choose from a range of color temperatures (from blue-toned to yellow-toned) and there's a sensor that'll adjust brightness automatically depending on your surroundings.
Kindle Scribe Colorsoft — Overview
The Kindle Scribe Colorsoft is essentially a Kindle Scribe, but with color display support. Most of what I've described in the previous section is also relevant here: there's an 11-inch screen (although the overall proportions are slightly different), no waterproofing, a range of storage capacities, and warm or cool backlighting options (you can't opt out of a backlight here).
Due to the color screen, the battery life has taken a further hit: you can expect around eight weeks of reading or two weeks of writing per charge.
View Original

View Original
View Original
This is the first-generation model, and it launched at the end of 2025. We awarded it four stars in our Kindle Scribe Colorsoft review, but there are some caveats to be aware of if you're thinking of buying one.
First, you can't use the writing and color capabilities in tandem — so you couldn't take notes on a graphic novel, for instance. Our resident e-reader expert believes that color e-ink just isn't quite there yet, which could be a deal-breaker if you're buying it specifically to enjoy graphic novels.
At this price (high), an iPad or Android tablet is a viable alternative and could deliver better value for money if you're seeking an all-round productivity tool with a colorful screen.

articles.title: Comment transférer ses playlists de Spotify à Deezer gratuitement avec Tune My Music ?
articles.text:
Non, changer de plateforme de streaming ne signifie pas forcément « repartir de zéro ». Avec Tune My Music, Deezer permet de transférer gratuitement ses playlists, ses titres, ses albums et ses artistes favoris depuis Spotify et plus de 50 autres services.
Passer de Spotify à Deezer peut sembler fastidieux lorsqu’on imagine devoir recréer manuellement plusieurs années de playlists. Pourtant, il suffit de quelques étapes à peine pour retrouver intacte sa bibliothèque musicale sur la plateforme française. Deezer intègre en effet directement Tune My Music, un service spécialisé dans le transfert de bibliothèques musicales.
L’opération peut être réalisée depuis l’application Deezer sur smartphone ou ordinateur. Et surtout, le transfert effectué depuis l’application Deezer est gratuit et sans limite de titres, sous réserve des éventuelles limites de contenu prises en charge par Deezer.
Pourquoi transférer Spotify vers Deezer plutôt que recréer ses playlists ?
Le principal intérêt du transfert est de conserver ses habitudes musicales sans devoir rechercher manuellement chaque morceau. Playlists, titres, albums et artistes favoris peuvent être importés automatiquement depuis Spotify (entre autres) vers Deezer.
Le principe est particulièrement intéressant pour tous ceux qui envisagent de changer de plateforme de streaming, mais qui hésitent à cause de leur bibliothèque existante. Il faut dire qu’une playlist soigneusement construite au fil des années peut rapidement contenir plusieurs centaines de titres, et la perspective de devoir la recréer morceau par morceau n’a donc rien de très réjouissant.
Outre Spotify, Deezer permet également d’importer une bibliothèque depuis Apple Music, YouTube Music, Tidal, Amazon Music, Qobuz et de nombreux autres services. La plateforme annonce plus de 50 services compatibles avec Tune My Music.
Comment transférer une playlist Spotify vers Deezer gratuitement ?
Depuis l’application Deezer, le transfert s’effectue en quelques étapes. Il suffit pour cela d’ouvrir les paramètres, d’accéder à l’importation de musique, de sélectionner Spotify puis de suivre les instructions de Tune My Music. Voici la procédure complète.
Comment lancer le transfert depuis l’application Deezer ?
Sur smartphone, la méthode est particulièrement simple :
- Ouvrez Deezer et rendez-vous sur votre profil
- Ouvrez les Paramètres
- Dans les préférences, sélectionnez Musique, puis Importer ma musique
- Deezer vous redirige automatiquement vers Tune My Music
- Sélectionnez Spotify comme plateforme source
- Suivez les instructions affichées à l’écran et choisissez les éléments à transférer
- Une fois l’opération terminée, sélectionnez Revenir sur Deezer
Peut-on transférer sa bibliothèque vers Deezer depuis un ordinateur ?
Oui, le transfert de bibliothèque est également accessible depuis la version ordinateur de Deezer. Dans ce cas, rendez-vous sur votre profil, ouvrez les paramètres du compte puis sélectionnez Transférer votre bibliothèque.
Il suffit ensuite de choisir le service source, de suivre les différentes étapes proposées par Tune My Music, de sélectionner la musique à importer puis de lancer le transfert vers Deezer.
Que peut-on transférer de Spotify vers Deezer ?
Tune My Music ne se limite pas aux playlists, puisque le transfert peut également concerner les titres, albums et artistes favoris. L’objectif est donc bien de récupérer une bibliothèque musicale aussi complète que possible sur Deezer.
Il faut toutefois garder à l’esprit que le catalogue n’est pas nécessairement identique entre deux plateformes. Un morceau présent sur Spotify peut ainsi ne pas être disponible dans le catalogue Deezer, ou être associé à une autre version.
Le transfert ne « copie » donc pas les fichiers audio, mais il vient retrouver les contenus correspondants dans le catalogue de la nouvelle plateforme, tant que cela est possible.
À noter que les podcasts ne sont, eux, pas concernés par cette fonctionnalité, et Tune My Music importe uniquement le contenu musical.
Pourquoi transférer sa bibliothèque musicale améliore-t-il l’expérience Deezer ?
Une bibliothèque complète permet à Deezer de mieux comprendre les goûts musicaux de l’utilisateur et d’affiner ses recommandations, notamment avec Flow. C’est un point important lorsqu’on change de plateforme, retrouver ses playlists est une chose, conserver une expérience personnalisée en est une autre.
En important ses artistes, albums et titres favoris, l’utilisateur fournit donc à Deezer davantage d’éléments pour construire ses recommandations. Flow peut ainsi s’appuyer sur une bibliothèque plus représentative des habitudes d’écoute, pour un rendu personnalisé.
Ce fonctionnement participe aussi à rendre le changement de plateforme moins contraignant. Plutôt que de considérer son historique musical comme un obstacle, l’utilisateur peut emporter une grande partie de ses habitudes avec lui.
Spotify ou Deezer : faut-il vraiment choisir entre les deux ?
On l’a vu, changer de plateforme de streaming est aujourd’hui beaucoup moins contraignant qu’il n’y paraît. La possibilité de transférer gratuitement une bibliothèque musicale permet surtout de tester une alternative sans abandonner pour autant ses playlists et ses favoris.
Deezer met par ailleurs en avant une approche plus transparente autour de certaines évolutions du streaming, notamment avec l’étiquetage des musiques entièrement générées par IA. Le transfert de bibliothèque s’inscrit dans cette volonté de rendre le changement de service plus simple, tout en permettant à l’utilisateur de conserver ses habitudes musicales.
Pour celles et ceux qui hésitent encore entre Spotify ou Deezer, le transfert constitue donc surtout un moyen de réduire considérablement le coût pratique du changement, puisque quelques étapes suffisent pour retrouver l’essentiel de sa bibliothèque, plutôt que de recommencer manuellement.
FAQ : transférer une playlist Spotify vers Deezer
Peut-on transférer gratuitement une playlist Spotify vers Deezer ?
Oui. En passant par Tune My Music depuis l’application Deezer, le transfert est gratuit et sans limite de titres.
Quelle application utiliser pour transférer Spotify vers Deezer ?
Deezer propose un accès intégré à Tune My Music, son partenaire spécialisé dans le transfert de bibliothèques musicales.
Peut-on transférer toute sa bibliothèque Spotify vers Deezer ?
Oui. Le service permet de transférer playlists, titres, albums et artistes favoris. En revanche, les podcasts ne sont pas pris en charge.
Combien de plateformes sont compatibles avec Tune My Music sur Deezer ?
Deezer indique que Tune My Music permet d’importer une bibliothèque depuis Spotify et plus de 50 autres services de streaming, parmi lesquels Apple Music, YouTube Music, Tidal, Amazon Music et Qobuz.
Peut-on transférer sa musique Spotify vers Deezer depuis un smartphone ?
Oui. Le lien vers Tune My Music est directement accessible depuis l’application Deezer. Le transfert peut également être effectué depuis un ordinateur.

articles.title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection ya se puede jugar en PC a 120 FPS
articles.text:
Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection ya puede ejecutarse de forma nativa en Windows gracias a un trabajo de ingeniería inversa asistido por inteligencia artificial. Los tres títulos que componen la recopilación (Uncharted: El tesoro de Drake, Uncharted 2: El reino de los ladrones y Uncharted 3: La traición de Drake) dejan así de estar limitados a las plataformas de Sony y llegan a ordenador con un rendimiento que alcanza los 120 FPS.
El responsable del proyecto es el desarrollador conocido como SuperMedo, la misma persona detrás de un port similar para Bloodborne. El avance resulta posible porque el hardware de las consolas no deja de ser, en esencia, hardware de PC encerrado en un ecosistema cerrado, una barrera que la inteligencia artificial ha ayudado a simplificar a la hora de portar títulos exclusivos de PlayStation.
Cómo funciona el port de Uncharted a PC
El sistema parte del código x86-64 original de los juegos de PS4, que se ejecuta de manera directa sobre la CPU del ordenador. Sobre esa base se añade una capa de compatibilidad que sustituye las funciones propias de la consola, de modo que el sistema operativo de Windows pueda interpretar correctamente las llamadas que originalmente estaban pensadas para PlayStation 4.
La parte gráfica se resuelve mediante un renderer basado en el emulador shadPS4, que traduce ese apartado visual a la API Vulkan. Este esquema es el mismo que ya se había utilizado en el port de Bloodborne, lo que confirma que la metodología empleada por SuperMedo puede extenderse a otros exclusivos de la plataforma.
No se trata de una emulación tradicional, sino de una ejecución prácticamente nativa del código original, con una capa intermedia que resuelve las diferencias de arquitectura entre consola y ordenador. Es ese punto el que explica por qué los resultados de rendimiento son tan superiores a los de un emulador convencional.
Rendimiento a 120 FPS y compatibilidad con DLSS y FSR
El launcher reúne los tres juegos de la colección y permite configurarlos para funcionar a 60 o 120 FPS, con la posibilidad de superar ese límite de forma experimental, aunque esta última opción puede generar problemas en el funcionamiento interno de los títulos.
El port incorpora, además, un conjunto de opciones gráficas propias de una edición pensada específicamente para PC. Entre ellas figura el soporte para NVIDIA DLSS y DLAA, AMD FSR 3.1 y FSR 4, así como generación de fotogramas mediante AMD FSR 3 Frame Generation y NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. Los usuarios de tarjetas GeForce RTX 50 pueden recurrir también a Multi Frame Generation.
A nivel de controles, la recopilación admite teclado y ratón, compatibilidad con mandos y la posibilidad de reasignar por completo los controles, lo que incluye el manejo de la cámara mediante ratón en Uncharted 3.
Las primeras pruebas de rendimiento respaldan estas cifras. Una configuración con un procesador AMD Ryzen 5 7500F y una tarjeta NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER logró mover los juegos a aproximadamente 120 FPS en resolución 1440p nativa.
Otros usuarios reportaron haber completado Uncharted: Drake’s Fortune con una GeForce RTX 4060, con cifras de entre 100 y 120 FPS en 1080p con DLAA activado, aunque en las secuencias más exigentes el rendimiento podía descender hasta los 80 FPS.
Errores y problemas en esta fase temprana de desarrollo
El proyecto sigue en fase de desarrollo y presenta fallos propios de una versión sin pulir. Se han reportado cierres inesperados durante las partidas, y en un caso concreto un jugador informó de una partida guardada corrupta durante el capítulo 11 del primer Uncharted.
Uncharted 3, por su parte, puede mostrar de forma ocasional artefactos gráficos en determinados personajes. Son incidencias que, de todos modos, resultan menores si se considera que el port todavía no ha recibido ningún parche oficial que corrija estos comportamientos.
El ritmo de actualizaciones, sin embargo, es constante. La versión 0.3.6 ya solucionó varios errores gráficos y un bloqueo asociado a la secuencia del accidente de tren en Uncharted 2. Actualizaciones previas habían corregido, a su vez, problemas de texturas, fallos de renderizado y distintos cierres de los juegos.
Un segundo proyecto alternativo y cómo conseguir los juegos
Paralelamente al trabajo de SuperMedo existe otro port desarrollado por BilalReloaded, que ofrece resoluciones superiores, soporte para formato ultrapanorámico y otras funciones adicionales pensadas para PC. Este segundo proyecto también se encuentra en fase beta.
Como ocurre con el resto de ports de este tipo, ninguno de los dos incluye archivos del juego. Esto implica que cada usuario deberá volcar su propia copia legítima de Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection de PlayStation 4 para poder utilizarla en PC a través de estos sistemas.

articles.title: PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert
articles.text:
PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described.
Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far.
The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'".
watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now.
PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild."
The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale.
The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described.
PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's.
Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, and records each branch's changes in its changelog. Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support.
Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch.
| PHP branches that can receive today's fix |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Branch | Current release (September 24) | PHP support status | 
|---|---|---|
| 8.5 | 8.5.11 | Active support until December 31, 2027 | 
| 8.4 | 8.4.26 | Active support until December 31, 2026 | 
| 8.3 | 8.3.35 | Security fixes only until December 31, 2027 | 
| 8.2 | 8.2.34 | Security fixes only until December 31, 2026 | 
Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version.
PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress, with CERT-EU's isolation advice added.
- Inventory every PHP install, including PHP bundled in vendor appliances, Windows software, and control panels such as cPanel and Plesk.
- Be ready to upgrade at 14:00 UTC. Patch internet-facing systems first, and check your Linux distribution and hosting provider for backported packages.
- On an end-of-life branch, upgrade, take the system off the internet, or put it behind a VPN or a web application firewall until you can.
- Where patching cannot be done at once, CERT-EU advises that you "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available."
- Watch what PHP starts. Alert on php-fpm, php-cgi, httpd, or apache2 launching shells, interpreters, or download tools. On Linux servers without endpoint detection, Florian Roth's process-watcher logs every program a PHP process starts, with its command line. It sees a program only after it has started and, in Roth's words, "prevents nothing."
- If you find something, isolate the server, preserve the web server and PHP logs, and look for web shells, new files in the web root, new cron jobs, scheduled tasks, and accounts.
Huntress said it had not seen exploitation of the flaws in its partner environments as of October 20, had not built or reproduced a proof of concept, and was not aware of public exploit code. watchTowr's FAQ lists exploitation as none reported as of October 21 and the flaws as not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
For comparison, when CVE-2024-4577, a PHP flaw in CGI mode on Windows, became public in June 2024, Akamai saw exploit attempts against its honeypot servers within 24 hours.
The release should clarify what the notice withheld: which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, whether an attack requires a particular way of running PHP, a configuration, or a login, and how PHP itself describes the flaws. At the time of writing, PHP had not released the fixes.

articles.title: Mobile developers use hidden 'dark patterns' to manipulate gamers
articles.text:
The dark side of 'free' mobile games — how developers reverse-engineer your patience to milk ad revenue
How free are free mobile games?
- Block Blast allegedly adjusts difficulty to encourage players to watch advertisements
- The free puzzle game reportedly generated $127 million from advertising in five months
- Hidden gameplay mechanisms may turn player frustration into advertising revenue
A developer known as Ayoships has reverse-engineered the code of Block Blast, a puzzle app by Hungry Games, revealing deliberate tricks that push players toward ads.
The app costs nothing to download, yet it earned close to $127 million from ads in five months from January through May 2026.
According to the developer, the app allegedly adjusts its difficulty based on what each player is worth to the developers rather than the skill of that player
How free games allegedly manipulate your patience
The game's code reportedly contains mechanisms that assess players using data such as smartphone models, geographical locations, and previous ad interactions.
These indicators can help estimate users’ purchasing power and ad value, potentially influencing how the application manages their playing experience.
Owners of expensive smartphones may be considered more commercially valuable than users with older, cheaper devices.
Similarly, geographical information can provide clues about average consumer income, helping ad systems estimate which audiences might generate greater returns.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The reported techniques extend beyond identifying potentially valuable advertising audiences.
One mechanism used by the game is “Boost then kill,” which reportedly makes a round easier before introducing greater difficulty.
This sequence can encourage players to believe they are performing exceptionally well, motivating them to continue playing rather than abandon the game.
According to the investigation, gameplay can suddenly become exceptionally difficult, encouraging players to watch a video ad in exchange for another attempt.
This approach connects frustration directly to ad revenue by making continued progress appear dependent on accepting an ad offer.
The game reportedly includes additional mechanisms that secretly increase scores, making ad-related rewards appear more valuable than they otherwise might.
References in the code include “reward,” “bait,” and “moreCleanSuccessRound,” the latter reportedly describing an easier round designed to build confidence.
If these mechanisms operate as described, players may struggle to distinguish genuine achievements from software adjustments intended to influence their decisions.
Advertising revenue drives concerns about deceptive game mechanics
Block Blast illustrates the concerns surrounding ad-supported games when commercial incentives potentially influence difficulty, rewards, and progression.
Free access does not necessarily mean users pay nothing, since their attention and viewing time can become valuable sources of income.
Optional advertisements offering extra lives or additional attempts are common in mobile gaming.
However, deliberately increasing frustration to encourage ad consumption raises different ethical questions.
Ayoships develops AI-powered mobile applications himself; therefore, independent verification is important when assessing his interpretation of Block Blast’s code.
The available findings do not establish how frequently the alleged difficulty adjustments occur or whether every player experiences the same treatment.
They also leave open whether the mechanisms respond automatically to advertising opportunities or follow other conditions built into the software.
These distinctions matter when determining whether the observed behaviour constitutes deliberate manipulation rather than ordinary gameplay balancing.
