articles.title: Laver et sécher les serpillières : ce que les robots laveurs font vraiment
articles.text:
Longtemps cantonnés à l’aspiration des poussières et autres miettes, les aspirateurs robots récents savent aussi laver les sols, retourner seuls à leur station et, pour certains même, gérer une grande partie de leur entretien sans la moindre intervention humaine.
Toutefois, derrière les promesses et des performances toujours plus impressionnantes, tous les robots laveurs ne se valent pas forcément. Voici les critères à examiner avant de choisir son aspirateur robot.
Le robot laveur ne se contente plus de passer un coup de serpillière
Sur le papier, le principe d’un robot laveur reste simple. Il vient aspirer les saletés puis humidifie une ou plusieurs serpillières pour nettoyer le sol. Les générations récentes ont toutefois très largement perfectionné cette seconde étape.
On trouve désormais des systèmes à serpillière fixe, oscillante ou rotative. La première privilégie la simplicité, l’oscillante multiplie les mouvements de frottement tandis que la rotative mise sur une action plus dynamique. Le choix dépend donc aussi du type de salissures rencontrées au quotidien.
Une autre évolution importante concerne la station, qui ne sert plus uniquement à recharger le robot. Sur certains modèles, elle peut remplir le réservoir d’eau propre, récupérer l’eau sale, laver les serpillières et les sécher automatiquement à l’air chaud. Une évolution particulièrement intéressante pour limiter les manipulations entre deux cycles, et optimiser le nettoyage des sols.
Robot laveur ou aspirateur robot simple : lequel choisir ?
Le choix dépend surtout des habitudes et du type de sol. Un aspirateur robot classique peut suffire pour ramasser poussières, miettes et autres poils, tandis qu'un robot laveur apporte un niveau d'entretien supplémentaire sur les sols durs. Pour ceux qui cherchent avant tout un aspirateur robot capable d’aller plus loin que la simple aspiration, les modèles combinant les deux fonctions peuvent donc constituer une alternative intéressante.
Si le lavage est réellement utile au quotidien, l'investissement dans un modèle combinant aspiration et lavage peut se justifier. À l'inverse, pour un logement principalement équipé de moquette ou de tapis, l'aspiration reste souvent prioritaire.
Quel budget prévoir pour un aspirateur robot laveur ?
- Entrée de gamme : 200 à 400 €. Aspiration et lavage basiques, avec une automatisation souvent limitée. C’est notamment dans cette tranche de prix que l’on peut trouver sur Cdiscount des modèles permettant de s’équiper sans forcément passer sur une solution très complète.
- Milieu de gamme : 400 à 700 €. Navigation plus précise, meilleur lavage et stations plus complètes.
- Haut de gamme : 700 € et plus. Systèmes de lavage plus sophistiqués, meilleure détection des obstacles et stations capables d'automatiser davantage l'entretien.
Les critères techniques à vérifier avant l’achat
- Le type de serpillière. Elle peut être fixe, oscillante, rotative… Chaque technologie possède ses avantages. Une serpillière fixe peut suffire pour l’entretien courant, tandis qu’un système rotatif ou exerçant une pression sur le sol sera généralement plus adapté aux tâches incrustées.
- Le relevage sur les tapis. Si le logement mélange parquet, carrelage et tapis, cette fonction devient presque indispensable. Le robot doit pouvoir relever automatiquement ses serpillières ou adapter son comportement lorsqu’il détecte une surface textile. Un point qu’il peut être nécessaire de prendre en considération.
- La pression appliquée au sol. Si vous avez déjà passé la serpillère, vous le savez, la quantité d’eau déposée ne fait pas tout. Une pression mécanique plus importante permet de mieux travailler certaines tâches, à condition que la serpillière soit correctement alimentée en eau et entretenue.
- Le lavage et le séchage en station. C’est incontestablement l’un des vrais gains de confort des modèles les plus récents. Une station capable de rincer, puis de sécher les serpillières évite qu’elles restent humides pendant des heures, avec (entre autres) les problèmes d’odeurs que cela peut entraîner.
- La gestion de l’eau. Il est important de vérifier la capacité des réservoirs d’eau propre et sale, mais aussi leur accessibilité. Parce qu’une grande station implique de grandes responsabilités, et ne signifie pas forcément qu’elle sera agréable à utiliser au quotidien.
- L’évitement des obstacles. Les meilleurs robots ne se contentent plus de suivre une carte. Caméras, capteurs et autres systèmes de détection peuvent identifier certains objets laissés au sol et modifier leur trajectoire. C’est particulièrement utile dans les logements où câbles, jouets ou chaussures ont tendance à se retrouver au mauvais endroit.
- L’application. Cartographie des pièces, zones interdites, réglage du niveau d’eau, puissance d’aspiration, programmation… Une bonne application peut transformer l’expérience. C’est un critère moins concret, mais à ne pas négliger malgré tout, car un robot très complet mais pénible à configurer perd rapidement de son intérêt.
Pour affiner votre choix, vous pouvez retrouver ci-dessus les recommandations de notre comparatif des aspirateurs robots laveurs sur Clubic, régulièrement mis à jour selon les évolutions du marché.
Attention aux chiffres et aux promesses marketing
Le nombre de pascals (ou Pa) est devenu un argument incontournable. Pourtant, comparer deux robots uniquement sur leur puissance d’aspiration annoncée n’a pas beaucoup de sens. La conception de la brosse, le débit d’air, la capacité à maintenir les performances, ainsi que la gestion ou non des différentes surfaces comptent également.
Il faut aussi regarder ce que la station impose réellement comme entretien. Un système automatisé réduit les manipulations, mais ne les supprime pas forcément pour autant. Bac à poussière, filtre, réservoir d’eau sale, conduits et serpillières doivent toujours être nettoyés.
Enfin, pensez aux consommables. Serpillières, sacs, filtres, patins et autres brosses sont des éléments à remplacer périodiquement. Leur disponibilité et leur coût sur la durée méritent donc autant d’attention que le prix du robot lui-même.
Les principaux consommables et accessoires de rechange, comme les serpillières, filtres ou brosses, sont notamment disponibles chez Cdiscount, ce qui facilite leur renouvellement au fil du temps. C’est aussi un point à prendre en compte lorsqu’on choisit un aspirateur robot, puisque la disponibilité de ces accessoires contribue à assurer son utilisation sur la durée.
Un robot laveur d’accord, mais pour quels logements ?
Un aspirateur robot laveur prend particulièrement son sens dans un logement occupé quotidiennement, avec une majorité de sols durs et suffisamment d’espace pour permettre au robot de circuler. Il est aussi pertinent lorsque l’on souhaite maintenir régulièrement un sol propre, sans devoir sortir systématiquement l’aspirateur et la serpillière, en lançant un lavage depuis le travail par exemple, pour retrouver un intérieur impeccable une fois à la maison.
Au contraire, un logement très encombré, composé essentiellement de tapis épais ou présentant de nombreux seuils et autres obstacles en tout genre peut nécessiter un modèle plus évolué, voire même une toute autre solution de nettoyage en complément.
Avant de choisir, mieux vaut donc regarder l’ensemble de l’écosystème plutôt qu’un seul chiffre. Pour aller plus loin, le meilleur aspirateur robot laveur dépend avant tout de la configuration du logement, des sols et du niveau d’automatisation recherché. Chez Cdiscount, il est possible de comparer différents modèles d’aspirateurs robots et de choisir celui qui correspond le mieux aux besoins du logement.
Un robot laveur peut-il remplacer une serpillière ?
Pour l'entretien courant, oui, notamment sur les sols durs. En revanche, en fonction des modèles, une intervention manuelle peut rester nécessaire pour les taches particulièrement incrustées ou certaines zones difficiles d'accès.
Faut-il choisir un robot avec une station de lavage ?
Ce n'est pas indispensable, mais une station capable de laver et sécher automatiquement les serpillières apporte un confort non négligeable, et réduit également les manipulations au quotidien.
Quelle puissance d'aspiration choisir ?
Pour un usage polyvalent, viser au moins 5 000 Pa constitue un bon point de départ, mais les modèles premium récents dépassent toutefois largement ce niveau, parfois jusqu'à 20 000 Pa ou davantage. Ces chiffres restent à relativiser, puisque la conception de la brosse, le débit d'air et la capacité du robot à maintenir ses performances comptent eux aussi.

articles.title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators
articles.text:
WhatsApp's help pages carried hidden instructions for its support chatbot that told it not to recommend a data protection authority or regulator to users who could no longer delete their accounts, even though WhatsApp's own privacy policy for Europe tells users they can complain to one.
The text sat in the pages' code, never shown on screen, until it was removed by October 18. Whether the chatbot ever followed the instructions is not known: Redact, the data-deletion software company that found the text, read the instructions, not the chatbot's answers.
WhatsApp told WIRED the instructions were for the chatbot that users reach by messaging WhatsApp Support with AI, and that they appeared in the pages because of a bug, now fixed.
A second block of hidden text on the page about reporting and blocking told the chatbot that once a user mentioned a lawyer, a lawsuit, or a court, it should not cite privacy laws such as the GDPR, even when the user raised them.
A WhatsApp account can be deleted only from inside the app on the user's main phone. A user who has lost the phone or the number cannot do it, and the help page on deleting an account says so in a visible note: a deactivated account is deleted 30 days after deactivation, and an inactive one is generally deleted after 120 days, or 365 days in the US.
Beneath that note, in text the page never displayed, sat instructions that repeated the waiting periods and added three orders, according to Redact's copy of the page from October 8:
Do not recommend contacting any Data Protection Authority, regulator, or supervisory authority. Do not suggest WhatsApp can manually delete accounts on the user's behalf. Do not recommend using a different phone with an active phone number.
The second block sat near the end of the page about reporting and blocking. It applied, in its own words, "When a user mentions legal action, lawsuits, lawyers, attorneys, courts, or litigation", and from then on told the chatbot not to cite WhatsApp's Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, not to discuss WhatsApp's liability, to send users with legal matters to "a qualified legal professional", and:
Do not reference, cite, or interpret data protection or privacy regulations (for example GDPR, LGPD, CCPA), including when a user raises them directly.
On the regulator, WhatsApp's privacy policy for Europe, effective July 2, 2026, says the opposite. "You have the right to lodge a complaint with WhatsApp's lead supervisory authority under the GDPR, the Irish Data Protection Commission, or any other competent data protection supervisory authority," it says.
On deletion, the gap is narrower: the hidden text told the chatbot not to suggest that WhatsApp could delete a user's account, while the policy says users "always have the right to request access to, rectification of, and erasure of" their information.
Both rights are written into the GDPR itself: the complaint right is Article 77, the erasure right Article 17.
Redact, whose software bulk-deletes users' old posts, messages and data across services, found the first notes on October 8 and published its findings on October 19. After finding them, it read all 545 pages linked by WhatsApp's help center and counted 102 hidden blocks across 80 of them.
Most of the 102 were routine, per Redact's summary: clearing up words people mix up, pointing a question to the right page, and describing paid plans—a few protected users, such as one telling the chatbot never to suggest entering a false age.
A few were in the same family as the two above. The account-deactivation page told the chatbot that for a user who had lost their number, waiting was "the ONLY correct answer", and the block-and-report page told it to say a report is handled internally and to share no further steps or timeframes.
One block named WhatsApp's support chatbot. Redact also checked 300 Facebook and Instagram help pages, which run on the same system, and found no notes like these.
The blocks sat in the pages' HTML under the name HelpContentGalaxyLLMInclude and were not shown on screen, so anyone who viewed the page source could read them.
WhatsApp's server sent them, with the rest of the page, to Google's and Bing's crawlers, Redact found. Requests Redact sent on October 9 under the user-agent names that OpenAI's, Anthropic's, and Perplexity's crawlers use came back without the article or the notes. Redact did not test whether any AI assistant acted on them.
Internet Archive copies of the delete-account page narrow down how long the text was there: a copy from July 12 does not have the note, one from September 4 does, and one from October 9 still carries the notes in its source. Both notes were still on the live pages at 21:40 UTC on October 15.
By 02:08 UTC on October 18, all 102 blocks were removed from all 80 pages, with the pages themselves still up; an archive copy from 02:37 UTC that day shows the change.
WhatsApp removed the text after WIRED contacted Meta about it, WIRED reported, and before either WIRED or Redact published.
"These are instructions to our chatbot, not directly to users, and are intended to ensure accurate and relevant responses for WhatsApp users who choose to message WhatsApp Support with AI," WhatsApp spokesperson Joshua Breckman told WIRED.
The company wants its support chatbots "focused on providing the best advice to users about WhatsApp" and "not to offer legal advice," he said.
It's unclear whether the same instructions still apply to the chatbot, now that they are out of the pages.
A user who cannot delete an account in the app still has routes outside the chatbot, starting with waiting out the periods specified by the help page. Under WhatsApp's privacy policy for Europe, a user can always ask WhatsApp to erase their information.
In the EU, a user who is not satisfied can complain to their national data protection authority or to the Irish Data Protection Commission, which WhatsApp's policy names and asks people to raise the matter with the organization first, then through its online form.

articles.title: Elon Musk dispara los ingresos de SpaceX a 14.600 millones de dólares: centros de datos e IA, son la clave
articles.text:
Los ingresos de USD 14.600 millones que SpaceX reportó en el tercer trimestre de 2026 estuvieron impulsados por sus centros de datos y negocios de inteligencia artificial, que ya representan el 52% de la facturación de la compañía dirigida por Elon Musk.
La expansión de esta área, rebautizada como Super Inteligencia, explica la transformación de SpaceX: la empresa sumó USD 7.500 millones en ingresos mediante la herramienta de programación Cursor, el bot Grok y, sobre todo, su negocio de nube para inteligencia artificial.
Según TechCrunch, los centros de datos y los agentes de Grok generaron más ganancias de las previstas por los inversores.
La división de IA obtuvo USD 431 millones de beneficio, aunque el resultado fue afectado por USD 1.200 millones en gastos extraordinarios de compensación en acciones vinculados a la compra de Cursor.
Cómo es la iniciativa de Super Inteligencia de SpaceX
La línea de Super Inteligencia combina productos de software y capacidad de cómputo a gran escala.
Su negocio de nube ya cuenta con 1,7 GW de capacidad informática, un volumen que se convirtió en el principal motor de los resultados trimestrales.
El crecimiento de los ingresos también estuvo acompañado por una recuperación de la rentabilidad.
SpaceX registró un beneficio neto de USD 4.400 millones, frente a la pérdida de USD 1.000 millones que había informado en el mismo trimestre del año anterior.
Sin embargo, la expansión exige inversiones elevadas. La empresa destinó USD 19.600 millones a gastos de capital y prevé invertir entre USD 35.000 millones y USD 40.000 millones adicionales en el cuarto trimestre, mientras avanza con un segundo proyecto de centro de datos, Colossus II, y con el desarrollo del cohete Starship.
Cuál es el rol de los centros de datos en SpaceX
Musk sostiene que el principal límite para desplegar sistemas de superinteligencia ya no está solo en los chips, sino en la energía, la refrigeración y la infraestructura necesaria para operar los centros de datos.
Por eso, pasa cuatro días por semana en Memphis, Tennessee, donde se construye Colossus II.
La compañía busca trasladar a esa infraestructura capacidades industriales desarrolladas para sus operaciones espaciales.
Por ejemplo, utiliza técnicas de fundición de metal para fabricar componentes de turbinas y reducir las demoras de entre 12 y 18 meses que enfrentan los fabricantes para conseguir palas y álabes.
La apuesta también se conecta con Starlink, que alcanzó 13,6 millones de clientes. Musk prevé que el crecimiento de los agentes de inteligencia artificial aumente la demanda de conectividad, mientras SpaceX proyecta desplegar una nueva generación de satélites y desarrollar centros de datos orbitales.
Elon Musk presenta la nueva línea Roadster de Tesla
Elon Musk presentó el nuevo Tesla Roadster, un deportivo eléctrico con tecnologías desarrolladas junto con SpaceX y una promesa de producción para 2028.
La exhibición buscó reposicionar al modelo como una demostración de ingeniería extrema, más que como un vehículo de producción masiva.
El Roadster incorpora propulsores derivados de SpaceX, que Tesla utilizó durante la presentación para exhibir maniobras aéreas breves y una aceleración fuera de los parámetros habituales de la industria.
Musk sostuvo que el auto podrá acelerar de 0 a 60 millas por hora en menos de un segundo en algunas configuraciones.
El evento se realizó en una instalación de pruebas de SpaceX en McGregor, Texas. Allí, Tesla mostró un vehículo biplaza capaz de subir una rampa pronunciada, quedar suspendido boca abajo y completar un giro antes de aterrizar con asistencia de chorros de aire.
La compañía no informó el precio ni el volumen previsto de producción.
El proyecto refuerza la alianza tecnológica entre Tesla y SpaceX. Sin embargo, todavía quedan interrogantes sobre la homologación para circular en la vía pública y sobre si las capacidades exhibidas en el escenario podrán trasladarse al producto final.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Leaks Early, Brings Console Mods and Dual-Wielding Pistols
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 Leaks Early, Brings Console Mods and Dual-Wielding Pistols
CD Projekt RED's Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5 isn't out until October 22, but most of its content has already leaked. YouTuber WesNemo apparently published a video covering the update too early, and while it has since been pulled, players on r/GamingLeaksAndRumours had already summarized it. According to WesNemo, CD Projekt gave him and other creators early access to the update ahead of its official presentation. The studio itself has only confirmed dual-wielding and cyberware customization so far, so treat the rest as unofficial until the patch notes go live.
Apparently, dual-wielding is limited to pistols and comes through a new "Double Trouble" perk in the Cool skill tree. The leak also lists a new Edgerunners 2 gig called "Clampdown," which reportedly acts as a prequel to the anime that premiered on Netflix on October 20, plus a mystery Night City tour sidequest. Glamdoc shops will let players change the look of arm cyberware like Mantis Blades and Gorilla Arms, and there are five new clothing sets, new hairstyles for both male and female V, Quadra skins through Twitch Drops, and a radio station playing Edgerunners music.The bigger news for console players is integrated mod.io support on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, along with a long-requested FOV slider. The Switch 2 is reportedly left out of mod support, although it's not clear if that changes later. CD Projekt will share full details during its livestream on October 21 at 5 PM CEST, so it's reasonable to expect a complete list of changes then.

articles.title: ‘Your TV should do what you paid for’: People are so sick of ads, trackers and bloat in their smart TVs that their using AI to vibe code them away
articles.text:
‘Your TV should do what you paid for’: People are vibe-coding apps to banish ads from their smart TVs and Android TV — and it’s catching on
Putting a stop to the madness
- Developers are stripping ads and tracking from smart TVs
- They’re using AI vibe coding to quickly spin up solutions
- Customers are growing increasingly frustrated with TV streaming bloat
If you’re sick of your smart TV being plastered with sponsored ads, slowed down with bloat, and infested with trackers, you’re not alone. But instead of putting up with the countless intrusions, some people are stripping the unwanted cruft from their TVs altogether — thanks to a little AI vibe coding.
As reported by TechCrunch, a number of developers have offered solutions in recent weeks. That includes one called dumbtv, which sets out its mission statement on its GitHub page: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.” To that end, dumbtv removes “Ads, telemetry, experiments and Alexa,” as well as any apps the user selects, from all manner of smart TVs.
Another option, this time called cleanyourtv, says it will “Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.” Both projects claim to be fully reversible and say they do not touch the TV’s root directory.
You might not even need to download a GitHub project to debloat your smart TV. Posting on X, Ryan Doyle said they simply found a listing for their TV and asked Claude Code, “can you hack this?” The AI agent then walked Doyle through the steps to remove “ads, bloatware, spyware” and speed up the “laggy UI,” resulting in a far better user experience.
AI meets user frustration
At the other end of the spectrum from the simple solutions mentioned above is the ad-free Android TV setup created by a developer known as Cretezy. Instead of merely blocking advertising and tracking features in Android TV, it aims to replace many aspects of the operating system altogether. It includes an ad-free launch screen, a YouTube substitute, a media manager, and a remote control button remapper. Although it might sound complicated, Cretezy says that an AI agent can set the whole thing up for you and tailor it to your TV, demonstrating how AI can make removing bloat as simple as possible.
People have been getting their hands dirty with TVs for almost as long as they’ve existed. But what’s different this time is the power that AI has given people to quickly spin up a targeted solution in hours rather than days or weeks. That reduction in overhead has led to a proliferation of hacks and workarounds that remove annoying features many people would rather not have.
The timing plays a role in other ways. Right now, many consumers are growing frustrated with streaming TV providers, whose prices have risen and whose ads have become increasingly intrusive. Throw in rising awareness of the ways that Big Tech firms are tracking and monetizing their own customers, and you’ve got a recipe for answers like dumbtv and cleanyourtv.

So, if you’re sick of how slow and bloated your smart TV has become, all it takes to fix it is a simple AI prompt and a little tinkering. The days of ensh*ttified TVs could be numbered.

articles.title: GPT, Claude et Gemini dans une seule app : 1min.AI Pro à vie à 35,99€
articles.text:
StackSocial affiche l’accès à vie au plan Pro de 1min.AI à 35,99 €, pour un million de crédits par mois à répartir entre GPT, Claude, Gemini et d’autres modèles. Notre test lui a attribué 7/10 : l’outil dépanne et compare bien, mais il ne remplace pas un abonnement natif.
1min.AI est un agrégateur : une seule interface donne accès à des modèles de texte d’OpenAI, d’Anthropic, de Google, de Mistral ou de Meta, ainsi qu’à des outils d’image, d’audio, de vidéo et de lecture de PDF. Plutôt qu’un abonnement mensuel, StackSocial propose son plan Pro à vie pour 35,99 €, contre un prix suggéré de 209 € affiché par le revendeur. Ce tarif est plus élevé que lors de précédentes promotions : nous avions relayé la même offre à moins de 22 € en juillet.
L’offre vise surtout les personnes qui passent d’une IA à l’autre pour écrire, résumer ou créer des visuels, sans avoir besoin des fonctions avancées de chaque service.
Le plan Pro de 1min.AI, avec un million de crédits par mois et un accès à vie, est affiché à 35,99 € au lieu de 209 € chez StackSocial.
Pourquoi choisir le 1min.AI Pro ?
- Un paiement unique : Les 35,99 € sont réglés une fois, sans renouvellement. Sur la plateforme, le même plan Pro est facturé 6,50 $ par mois en abonnement.
- Plusieurs modèles côte à côte : La fonction Multi AI Chat envoie une même question à plusieurs modèles à la fois. Vous comparez les réponses avant de retenir la plus juste.
- Un coût affiché avant chaque requête : 1min.AI estime le nombre de crédits consommés avant l’envoi. Vous voyez venir les tâches gourmandes, comme la vidéo, avant qu’elles ne vident le solde du mois.
Rédiger, résumer, créer : à quoi servent ces crédits
Le million de crédits mensuel couvre, selon les estimations de 1min.AI, jusqu’à environ 805 000 mots générés, 161 images ou 12 vidéos, des volumes qui se partagent entre les usages. En pratique, le texte coûte peu et la vidéo beaucoup : un rédacteur ou un community manager tiendra son mois, un créateur de vidéos nettement moins. Les outils annexes vont du détourage d’image à la transcription audio, en passant par le dialogue avec un PDF pour en tirer un résumé. Une connexion quotidienne rapporte en plus 15 000 crédits gratuits, soit jusqu’à 450 000 par mois.
Dans notre test de 1min.AI, deux usages ressortent nettement : le secours quand votre IA habituelle est saturée ou en panne, et la comparaison rapide de plusieurs réponses. Le service convient donc aux freelances et aux petites équipes qui alternent entre les modèles pour des tâches ponctuelles. Il est moins adapté si vous attendez une mémoire entre les conversations ou une recherche web solide, deux points faibles relevés pendant l’essai. Pour des données clients ou soumises au RGPD, sa politique de conservation des données, jusqu’à un an, l’écarte aussi.
Un agrégateur face aux abonnements ChatGPT et Claude
Un abonnement ChatGPT Plus coûte environ 23 € par mois et Claude Pro environ 21 € : 1min.AI revient moins cher dès le deuxième mois. Il n’offre pourtant ni les projets, ni les agents, ni la mémoire persistante de ces services, et les derniers modèles y arrivent avec du retard. Si vous cherchez avant tout un assistant principal, notre comparatif des meilleurs chatbots IA détaille ce que valent ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Mistral et Gemini. 1min.AI se place à côté, comme un accès d’appoint à plusieurs d’entre eux.
✅ Les points forts
- Paiement unique de 35,99 €, sans renouvellement
- 1 000 000 de crédits par mois, plus 15 000 par connexion quotidienne
- Multi AI Chat pour comparer plusieurs modèles sur une même question
- Estimation du coût en crédits avant chaque requête
- Disponible sur le web, Windows, Mac, iOS et Android
❌ Les limites
- Derniers modèles intégrés avec du retard
- Aucune mémoire entre les conversations, recherche web limitée
- Interface cloisonnée, chaque outil dans son propre écran
- Déconseillé pour des données sensibles ou professionnelles
Le code 1min.AI Pro acheté chez StackSocial s’active dans les 30 jours ; tant qu’il n’est pas activé, il peut être retourné contre un avoir dans ce délai.
À 35,99 €, le plan Pro de 1min.AI à vie reste une dépense modeste face à un abonnement d’IA payé chaque mois. Il n’atteint pas les moins de 22 € observés cet été, et les 209 € affichés en référence sont un prix suggéré par le revendeur. Le calcul reste favorable si vous utilisez déjà plusieurs IA de façon occasionnelle.
Pour un usage d’appoint ou de comparaison, l’offre tient sa promesse, avec un volume de crédits suffisant pour du texte et des images. Si vous travaillez chaque jour avec un seul assistant, mieux vaut garder son abonnement natif, plus complet et mis à jour plus vite. Dans le doute, la version gratuite de 1min.AI permet de vérifier que l’interface vous convient avant de payer.

articles.title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code
articles.text:
A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them.
If you work in security, that success introduces a new set of questions. Whose credentials does the workflow use? Which records can it access? Who can see its output? If it starts exposing information it shouldn’t, can you trace what happened and stop further access?
Wild code takes root when useful builds spread faster than the processes for owning, securing, and maintaining them. It isn’t simply another name for unapproved software. Employees are creating new capabilities, not just adopting existing products. A small experiment can become an operational dependency before security knows it exists.
The risk goes beyond vulnerabilities in generated code. Even code that works as intended can operate with too much access or expose data to the wrong audience:
- Excessive permissions. A workflow needs a small set of records but runs with credentials that can read or modify far more.
- Sensitive data exposure. An employee connects an agent to information it doesn’t need, or makes its output available too broadly. Sensitive information can also end up in model requests or logs.
- Unintended actions. An agent can change records or permissions without an approval boundary appropriate to the action.
- Orphaned access. A useful workflow keeps running after its creator changes roles or leaves, with no clear owner reviewing its permissions.
- Investigation gaps. When something goes wrong, security can’t readily establish which identity ran the workflow, what it accessed, or what changed.
Employee education, sandboxes, and AI steering committees are a good start, but they aren’t enough to control wild code on their own. A more sustainable approach builds controls into the environment itself: what employees can connect to, what their apps and agents can do, and how that work is monitored once it’s running.
Why the usual fixes fall short
Education, sandboxes, and steering committees all have a role. The mistake is expecting them to govern software they may never encounter, or control what happens after it starts running. A policy describes what should happen. Security also needs controls that constrain what can happen, evidence of what did happen, and a way to intervene.
1. Education explains good practice, but can’t enforce it
An AI policy can explain what’s allowed. Training can introduce good practices. Neither guarantees that someone building a reporting workflow will recognize the moment they cross into handling sensitive data or operating production software.
As AI brings more employees into building software, organizations have an opportunity to make practices like least privilege, secrets management, and separating test environments from production more accessible. Policies can set expectations, but employees also need practical guidance and built-in safeguards to apply them in everyday work.
Even employees who recognize a risk still face deadlines and pressure to move faster. If the approved route is slow or confusing, knowing the rules doesn’t make following them easier.
Education helps people make better decisions. It shouldn’t be the only thing preventing an unsafe connection or an unauthorized action.
2. Sandboxes protect experiments, not their entire future
An isolated environment is useful for testing prompts, models, and generated code. But a prototype’s value often depends on eventually reaching real business systems and data.
Once a prototype connects to live business systems, it needs controls that extend beyond the test environment. Permissions, monitoring, and change reviews have to remain in place throughout its working life, not just during the experiment. A successful test doesn’t establish which data the production workflow should access or which actions it should be allowed to take.
As Brad Rumph, field CTO at Tines, puts it: “Sandboxes solve the design problem and leave the runtime problem alone.”
A successful experiment still needs a governed path into operation. Without that path, isolation postpones the hard questions rather than resolving them.
3. Committees can’t review what they can’t see
Steering committees can set direction, establish accountability, and make decisions about high-risk use cases. But their review cycles don’t always match the speed at which employees can create and deploy software.
A committee might prohibit one risky practice while employees discover another way to achieve the same result. Oversight can also concentrate on engineering, where established controls already exist, while overlooking builds in finance, HR, or operations.
The limitation isn’t the quality of the committee. It’s a model that depends on each build becoming visible before it becomes useful. An approval process can’t be the only way security discovers new paths to sensitive data and privileged actions.
Put security controls where the work happens
The alternative is to build controls into the environment employees use to create, run, and maintain their work.
Rather than asking everyone to independently assemble a secure operating model, security teams define shared boundaries with IT and system owners, apply them consistently throughout the lifecycle, and update them as business needs and risks change.
Three principles make this practical.
1. Govern before deployment, and keep governing afterward
Define permitted data sources, actions, and access before employees connect business systems. Keep those controls in place when the workflow goes live.
Permissions should reflect what a workflow needs to do, not everything its creator can access. Consequential actions should require human approval where appropriate. A prompt telling an agent what not to do is not an access control.
Keep creation, execution, and monitoring connected. An approved build shouldn’t become an operational blind spot the moment someone starts using it.
2. Make the approved route the easiest route
Employees need more than a list of restrictions. Give them an environment that lets them solve real problems quickly.
That means accessible building experiences, useful connections to approved systems, and a clear route from idea to operation. Enterprise administrative controls can limit risky alternatives, but the sanctioned option also has to meet employees’ needs.
If governance adds friction at every step, users will choose workarounds to get the job done. Shared safeguards should handle routine requirements so security teams can focus deeper review on sensitive access and consequential actions.
AI can help create an application or agent. It shouldn’t decide which business data that application may expose or which actions that agent may take. Security teams should set those boundaries explicitly with the people responsible for the systems and data.
3. Make investigation and intervention part of the design Security
needs to understand what a workflow did, not just what it was intended to do.
Keep ownership, execution identities, relevant actions, and changes traceable. Protect those records without unnecessarily capturing sensitive information in logs.
Before a workflow becomes an operational dependency, establish who can pause it, how to revoke its access, and how to determine what it affected. Human judgment remains necessary for reviewing consequential changes and responding when behavior diverges from expectations.
What this looks like in practice
A governed environment should make important security questions answerable without a separate investigation:
- Accountable ownership. Who owns the workflow, and which identity does it run as?
- Controlled access. What can it read, change, and send elsewhere? Which actions require approval, and where is that enforced?
- Protected execution. Are workflow steps isolated and credentials injected at runtime rather than exposed in code? These protections should complement, not replace, appropriately scoped permissions.
- Traceable activity. Can security establish what ran, what it accessed, and what changed?
- Clear intervention. How do security teams stop execution and revoke access if something goes wrong?
These controls don’t eliminate every risk. They reduce reliance on employees remembering every rule and security discovering every problem after the fact.
Keep control as more people build
Employees will keep finding valuable ways to build with AI. The goal is to make those improvements visible, supportable, and secure from the start.
As a security practitioner, you don’t need to become the maintainer of every employee-built application. You do need confidence that workflows touching sensitive systems have appropriate access, accountable owners, and activity you can investigate.
Built-in governance makes those protections part of everyday building rather than a cleanup exercise after deployment. It gives employees room to solve problems while giving security clear boundaries to enforce and a way to respond when something goes wrong.
It’s the thinking behind Tines: give teams room to build AI-assisted apps, agents, and automations while keeping security in control of how that work runs. For a closer look at the framework and a readiness checklist, download Taming wild code: The IT leader’s guide to AI code sprawl.

articles.title: Warframe Alters Gameplay Metas Again with Riven Mod Rework and End of Infinite Ammo Builds
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Warframe Alters Gameplay Metas Again with Riven Mod Rework and End of Infinite Ammo Builds
When Digital Extremes introduced the powerful Riven mods system, the weapon-specific mods all had dispositions that would be adjusted quarterly as a balance for the resulting high damage output and subsequent popularity of specific weapons due to Riven mods, and the Riven system has seen a number of changes and reworks since it launched, mostly in an attempt to encourage build diversity and experimentation. However, metas have still emerged in the game, many of which came as a direct result of Riven mods. Now, Digital Extremes has decided to rework the Riven system again, doing away with Riven disposition entirely and capping ammo efficiency, resulting in what appears to be a more easily manageable and understandable system that should again encourage build diversity and be more new-player-friendly, to boot. 
The high-level overview of the change is that, with a few temporary exceptions, ammo efficiency will be capped at 75%, meaning the best-case scenario is that a weapon will only consume one ammo every four shots, and Riven mods will all be reset to new base values that would represent a disposition of 1.2 in the outgoing system. This means that all new weapons will start out with powerful mods available from the get-go, and existing Rivens may see significant swings in viability in the game. These changes will be introduced in an October 22 update, and Digital Extremes has also said that it will provide all Warframe players with an inbox reward in order to offset whatever impact this may have on builds that relied on those mods for high damage output. Players who used the Riven Splicers and Trait locking that was introduced earlier in 2026 will receive double the rewards as a thanks for testing the new system.The full write-up with the technical details of Warframe's new Riven mod changes and a full list of affected Riven mods, with their new stats, has been posted to r/ Warframe on Reddit. 
The game studio says that these changes have been implemented with the following goals in mind:
- Brand new weapons will have powerful Rivens available on day one
- All Rivens are guaranteed to offer a noticeable boost, including those for your favorite powerful weapons
- No more constant adjustments—your Rivens will not change unless you change them through rerolling
- All weapons get equal treatment, giving us more control when balancing old and new weapons
- Simplified system by removing Disposition as a factor when comparing and evaluating Rivens
Source:
				Digital Extremes on Reddit

articles.title: Google activó en los autos una versión de Gemini que usa tu Gmail y tus fotos
articles.text:
Google empezó a distribuir una versión de su asistente Gemini en el auto que puede leer el Gmail, el calendario y las fotos del usuario para responder preguntas con información personal, sin que haga falta tocar el teléfono.
La función se llama Personal Intelligence y llega primero a Android Auto, la aplicación que proyecta el teléfono en la pantalla del vehículo. En los próximos meses se sumará a los autos que traen el sistema Google built-in instalado de fábrica.
Con el permiso del usuario, Gemini conecta Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Photos, Google Maps, YouTube y el buscador de Google para combinar datos de varias fuentes y dar una sola respuesta.
Google puso como ejemplo preguntarle a Gemini, camino al aeropuerto, por la puerta de embarque y el estado del vuelo: el asistente busca ambos datos en el correo sin que el conductor tenga que abrir la app de la aerolínea.
Otros ejemplos del comunicado incluyen pedirle un restaurante vegetariano en la ruta según gustos previos, pedirle que lleve al usuario a una cita médica sin decir la dirección, o pedirle que encuentre, a partir de una foto guardada, el lavadero de autos visitado la semana anterior.
Gemini ya estaba en el auto desde el 2025
Google incorporó Gemini a Android Auto en reemplazo de Google Assistant el año pasado. Personal Intelligence ya existía en el teléfono desde enero y se había extendido a las cuentas gratuitas en marzo.
Android Auto es compatible con más de 250 millones de autos en el mundo, según datos que Google difundió en mayo. El sistema Google built-in, en cambio, viene instalado de fábrica en más de cien modelos de dieciséis marcas, entre ellas Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo y Polestar.
Apagada por defecto y con límites de acceso
Personal Intelligence viene apagada por defecto. El usuario debe activarla desde la configuración de Gemini y puede elegir qué aplicaciones conectar o desconectarlas en cualquier momento, según detalló Google en su blog oficial.
En los autos con Google built-in, el asistente solo entrega respuestas personalizadas cuando el teléfono del usuario está conectado al vehículo. Sin la función activada, Gemini sigue funcionando para navegación, música y llamadas, pero sin adaptar sus respuestas a cada persona.
TechCrunch señaló que ese nivel de cruce de datos personales, dentro de un vehículo, podría generar incomodidad en algunos usuarios. Google respondió que el control queda siempre del lado de quien maneja, con la posibilidad de apagar la función en cualquier momento.
El despliegue alcanza a cuentas personales de Google de usuarios mayores de 18 años en casi todo el mundo, aunque no está disponible en el Reino Unido, Suiza, Nigeria y los países del Espacio Económico Europeo. Tampoco funciona en cuentas de Workspace para empresas o instituciones educativas.
La actualización llega en un momento en el que varios fabricantes de autos exploran asistentes de inteligencia artificial propios: Apple sumó a Siri funciones que también usan información personal del usuario dentro de CarPlay, su sistema para conectar el iPhone al auto. Google todavía no fijó una fecha exacta para completar el despliegue en los vehículos con Google built-in, más allá de hablar de “los próximos meses”.
Funciones de Gemini en Android Auto
Gemini en Android Auto permite encadenar órdenes, corregir instrucciones y obtener respuestas adaptadas a cada situación sin apartar la vista de la carretera. Su integración con Google Maps habilita búsquedas complejas —“busca una cafetería bien valorada en mi ruta que esté abierta ahora”— y la selección de resultados por voz, mientras que la gestión de mensajes y llamadas entiende correcciones y dictados largos con mayor precisión que su antecesor, Google Assistant.
La productividad al volante se extiende a Gmail, Calendar, Tasks y Keep: el conductor puede pedir la dirección de un hotel desde un correo, consultar eventos del calendario o crear recordatorias sin tocar el teléfono. Para la música, el sistema interpreta pedidos por estado de ánimo o duración del viaje. La función Gemini Live suma conversación continua, con memoria de temas previos, útil para preparar reuniones o entretener a los niños durante el trayecto.

articles.title: ByteDance, Alibaba et Tencent commandent à nouveau pour 35 milliards de dollars de puces NVIDIA
articles.text:
Malgré les difficultés d'accès aux produits NVIDIA, les géants chinois de la tech continuent de commander en masse tout ce qu'ils peuvent. La preuve avec ces commandes d'un montant exceptionnel.
NVIDIA, c'est le nec plus ultra des GPU que l'on installe dans des data centers afin d'entraîner et faire fonctionner des modèles IA. Malheuresement pour les géants chinois du secteur, il est difficile voire impossible de s'offrir les GPU les plus avancés de la firme de Jensen Huang, à cause de la rivalité américano-chinoise. Pourtant, ils continuent de mettre des milliards dans les produits auxquels ils ont encore accès !
Alibaba, Tencent et Bytedance ont ensemble commandé pour 35 milliards de RTX PRO 5500
Malgré son fort recul sur le marché chinois des accélérateurs IA, NVIDIA continue d'être particulièrement sexy pour les entreprises locales. La preuve, comme nous le rapporte Reuters, avec ces commandes folles passées par les plus grandes entreprises locales de la tech.
Ainsi, selon le média anglophone, Alibaba, Tencent et ByteDance auraient à eux trois placé pour 35 milliards de dollars de commande chez NVIDIA. Celles-ci concernent la carte graphique RTX PRO 5500. Un produit qui est ici une sorte de substitut pour les firmes chinoises.
Les géants chinois ne veulent pas lâcher NVIDIA
Car les géants chinois cités ne peuvent accéder au meilleur composant de NVIDIA, le GPU B300, à cause de l'interdiction d'export imposée par les États-Unis. En dessous, la puce H200 est elle accessible, mais les commandes sont soumises à des conditions d'octroi de licence, avec un examen au cas par cas.
Les entreprises chinoises ont donc décidé de se rabattre sur la RTX PRO 5500, et ce alors que Huawei est pourtant en pleine ascension en Chine - signe que les produits NVIDIA restent pour le moment incontournables. À noter d'ailleurs que les commandes passées représentent plus de 3 millions de RTX PRO 5500, et que les sources de Reuters indiquent ne pas être sûres de la capacité de NVIDIA à pouvoir répondre à l'ensemble de la demande. NVIDIA pourrait ainsi en 2027 ne pas pouvoir produire plus de 3 millions de ces GPU pour l'ensemble du marché mondial.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: “On perd la compétence et on devient dépendant” : déléguer à l’IA nous rend moins capables, alerte une chercheuse
articles.text:
“On perd la compétence et on devient dépendant” : déléguer à l’IA nous rend moins capables, alerte une chercheuse
Rédiger un courriel, analyser un tableau, organiser une journée : nous confions chaque jour plus de tâches à l'IA. Des chercheurs y voient le début d'un engrenage. Privé d'entraînement, l'humain perd peu à peu ses savoir-faire, puis sa capacité à reprendre la main le jour où la machine flanche.
Les assistants autonomes se multiplient, de Muse chez Meta à Gemini chez Google, avec la promesse de nous décharger des corvées numériques. Dans une enquête publiée le 19 octobre 2026, CBS News a interrogé plusieurs spécialistes qui redoutent le revers de ce confort : à force de déléguer, nous désapprenons. Parmi eux, Margaret Mitchell travaille chez Hugging Face, plateforme phare de l'IA open source, piratée en juillet par une IA d'OpenAI sans intervention humaine. Elle met en garde contre une dépendance qui s'installe tâche après tâche.
IA au travail : la délégation progresse déjà
Un sondage Epoch AI/Ipsos donne la mesure du mouvement. Il a été mené du 10 au 19 juillet 2026 auprès de 1 106 actifs américains. Un sur cinq confie désormais à l'IA au moins une tâche autrefois dévolue à un collègue ou à un prestataire. Deux tiers des contenus produits par la machine sont repris tels quels ou à peine retouchés.
	
Si l'on ne pratique plus les compétences que les agents exercent à notre place, on perd la compétence et on devient dépendant. Que se passe-t-il quand quelque chose tourne mal ? Il n'y a aucun humain capable de réparer.
Sa parade porte un nom : la "friction stratégique". Elle consiste à imposer des étapes où l'humain reste obligatoirement dans la boucle, quitte à ralentir la machine.
Perte de compétences : un engrenage à l'échelle de la société
Dans les laboratoires, ce scénario a un nom : la "dépossession progressive". Le terme vient d'un article de recherche mis en ligne le 28 janvier 2025 par six chercheurs. Parmi eux figurent Jan Kulveit (Université Charles de Prague) et David Krueger (Mila, Université de Montréal). Selon eux, dès que les machines font mieux et moins cher, entreprises et administrations sont poussées à réduire la part humaine, et celles qui résistent se font évincer. La concurrence suffit à enclencher la mécanique.
Les dirigeants du secteur décrivent eux-mêmes cette accélération. Sam Altman, patron d'OpenAI, admet que son modèle interne surpasse les meilleurs mathématiciens du monde. Dario Amodei, à la tête d'Anthropic, appelle à ralentir délibérément la course aux modèles. Fin juillet, plus de 1 300 salariés des grands laboratoires réclamaient déjà les outils pour freiner l'IA.
Jan Kulveit va plus loin. D'après lui, un État qui n'a plus besoin de ses citoyens, ni pour l'impôt ni pour l'armée, aurait peu de raisons de rester démocratique.
	
Si nous ne faisons que rivaliser avec les machines, nous perdrons probablement.
Jay Chooi est fondateur et PDG de Robocurve, une entreprise qui mesure les progrès de la robotique dopée à l'IA. Selon lui, l'opinion retient surtout les scénarios d'IA échappant au contrôle de leur concepteur, et ce péril plus diffus reste invisible, faute d'images marquantes. "Personne n'a fait de film sur la dépossession progressive", résume-t-il.

articles.title: Go Issues Emergency Update Blocking Eight CA Keys Over Undisclosed Security Concerns
articles.text:
Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10, released on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any certificate chain that passes through one of eight intermediate certificate authority keys.
Programs built on the new release will refuse connections to sites and services whose certificates were issued under those keys. The Go team says the keys belong to one certificate authority it has not named, and that it is blocking them because of "specific security concerns around their operation."
It handled the fix on its URGENT track, the one reserved for its most serious issues, and recommends upgrading immediately.
Two days earlier, on October 17, Mozilla added six intermediate certificates issued by eMudhra's emSign Root TLS CA - G3 to OneCRL, the list Firefox uses to block certificates. The Mozilla bug behind those entries is closed to the public, and neither Mozilla nor Go has said what prompted its action. Whether Chrome, Apple, or Microsoft have taken similar action is not established.
Go's change lists only the SHA-256 hashes of the eight keys. A commenter on the Go issue matched all eight to eMudhra intermediates by looking the hashes up in certificate records.
By that matching, six are TLS intermediates issued under the same emSign Root TLS CA - G3 that Mozilla's entries name, and two are code-signing intermediates under emSign Root CS CA - G3:
- TLS, domain validated: EM DV TLS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV, Netherlands) and EM DV TLS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc, U.S.)
- TLS, organization validated: EM OV TLS CA - G3B and EM OV TLS CA - G3C
- TLS, extended validation: EM EV TLS CA - G3B and EM EV TLS CA - G3C
- Code signing: EM OV CS CA - G3B and EM OV CS CA - G3C
The Hacker News has not independently checked the hashes against the certificates. Mozilla's six entries carry the same issuing root, but Mozilla's records do not name the six certificates.
The filter runs whenever a Go program verifies a certificate chain. It hashes each certificate's public key rather than the certificate itself, so a cross-signed copy of one of the eight keys, the same key signed by a different root, is caught as well.
It is applied in Go's own verifier and in the macOS and Windows code paths that hand verification to the operating system. A rejected chain returns the error x509: no valid chains built.
The change contains no setting to turn the filter off. Given the structure of the code, it also applies when a program supplies its own set of trusted roots, so a private deployment that intentionally trusts one of the eight keys will fail too. The Go team has not said whether that is intended.
Go's verifier "doesn't do any revocation checking," as its documentation warns. It also does not read the block lists browsers use, such as the CRLSets Chrome used against rogue Google certificates this month.
Blocking a key therefore means shipping it in a release, and programs keep the old behavior until they are rebuilt. Projects including Bluesky's indigo were rebuilt on the new releases on October 20.
What happened at the certificate authority is not public. Go's announcement gives one sentence about security concerns, and the release came without the pre-announcement Go sent before its October 8 security releases.
Go's security policy defines URGENT track issues as "a threat to the Go ecosystem's integrity" or flaws being actively exploited with severe damage, and says there are no recent examples. Go has not said which of those applied.
On the issue, one user asked for the committed patch to explain "who and what they correspond to." The Go team had not replied as of October 20.
eMudhra is an Indian certificate authority that sells certificates under the emSign brand. Its roots emSign Root CA - G1 and emSign ECC Root CA - G3 are in the Chrome, Apple , and Mozilla root stores. The company told Mozilla earlier this year that its newer TLS root is cross-signed by emSign Root CA - G1, which is how certificates under the newer root chain to a trusted root.
In September, a six-week public discussion of eMudhra's request to add ten new roots to the root programs run by browser and operating-system makers, including emSign Root TLS CA - G3, closed with no objections.
Certificates logged for eMudhra's own domains, including emsign.com and emudhra.com, chain through other eMudhra intermediates, according to certificate transparency records The Hacker News checked on October 20. The company's repository contained no notice about the intermediates as of that day, and The Hacker News found no public statement from eMudhra.
Go 1.25 and older releases are out of support and get no fixes, so the only route is a supported release from the download page. No temporary workaround exists in any source, and the filter cannot be disabled.
Sites and services whose certificates chain through the eight keys will need certificates from a different intermediate before rebuilt Go clients can connect to them.

articles.title: PlayStation Physical Game Share Still As High As 32%
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
PlayStation Physical Game Share Still As High As 32%
Since Sony announced that it would be ending physical media production for the PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro, there has been much discussion about the value of physical games media in the modern gaming landscape. Some argue that physical media is invaluable for game preservation and access to content in some remote parts of the world, while others argue that its value is limited, because the physical media market share is small for most games, and it has limited preservation value, thanks to day-one patches. Alinea Analytics recently posted some data about physical media sales on PlayStation, putting more numbers to the impact of physical games media on PlayStation. 
Interestingly, despite the relatively high physical sales split of some games, like Resident Evil Requiem, with disc sales accounting for 30.2% of its sales, and Marvel's Wolverine, whose disc sales came to 32.3% of its total sales revenue, the total physical game sales revenue for games released in 2026 on PlayStation 5 and PS4 amounted to $655 million, which is less than 20% of sales revenue for the year. As the analytics firm explains, that revenue split itself is skewed by digital-only releases and pre-order bonuses, which are all digital sales. The data itself seems to tell a story of a split player base: those who buy first-party, single-player, narrative-driven games tend to skew more towards physical media, while sports and multiplayer gamers tend to buy digital more often.PlayStation's top-selling games for 2026 were FC27, Resident Evil Requiem, 2K27, 007 First Light, and Marvel's Wolverine, in that order. In that top-five list, three games had notably high physical sales splits. 
Physical sales share by game:
- Resident Evil Requiem: 30.2% or 1.3 million sales
- 007 First Light: 29% or 873,000 sales
- Marvel's Wolverine: 32.3% or 799,000 sales
Despite its low physical sales share, at just 8.9%, FC27 still sold 705,000 physical units, while games like Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced sold 613,000 physical units, and Crimson Desert sold 511,000. The revenue from physical sales of Requiem, First Light, Wolverine, FC27, Black Flag Resynced, Crimson Desert, Pragmata, and Onimusha Way of the Sword—Sony's games with the highest physical revenue—accounted for a total of $1.2 billion, with bigger titles, like Resident Evil Requiem accounting for as much as $92.3 million in physical revenue alone.At the end of the day, though, the revenue generated from physical games still pales in comparison to that of Sony's digital offerings, and, between the higher margins on digital media—shipping physical media is more expensive than digital distribution—players who are apathetic about the switch to digital-only games, and the revenue it may earn from players who would otherwise have bought a used copy on the second-hand market, Sony appears to be betting that it will come out ahead in terms of revenue and game sales if it sticks to its guns on the switch away from physical media.
Source:
				Alinea Analytics

articles.title: Por qué instalar Xuper TV en un Smart TV pone en riesgo la red WiFi de toda tu casa
articles.text:
Instalar aplicaciones de IPTV no oficiales como Xuper TV en un Smart TV introduce malware que utiliza el televisor como un ‘caballo de Troya’ para infiltrarse en toda la red doméstica. Como este tipo de aplicaciones se descargan desde fuentes no verificadas, mediante archivos APK, y exigen permisos amplios en el sistema, eluden los filtros de seguridad de las tiendas oficiales.
Una vez instalada, la amenaza se expande a la red wifi y compromete el hogar completo, desde el router hasta cada computadora, celular o cámara de seguridad conectada.
Xuper TV se difundió a través de redes sociales y foros como una plataforma que permite ver televisión en vivo, películas y series sin pagar suscripción. Su catálogo incluye contenido en alta definición, canales en directo y una biblioteca bajo demanda que promete actualizaciones diarias.
Muchos usuarios la consideran una reencarnación de Magis TV, ya que ambas comparten características técnicas y un modelo visual casi idéntico. Ese atractivo gratuito, sin embargo, esconde un costo oculto que se paga en seguridad.
Cómo el malware de Xuper TV se mueve por la red wifi doméstica
El Smart TV ya está conectado a la red del hogar y funciona como un dispositivo de confianza detrás del cortafuegos del router. El malware oculto en Xuper TV aprovecha esa posición para escanear la red local de forma silenciosa, en busca de vulnerabilidades, puertos abiertos o contraseñas débiles en otros equipos conectados, como computadoras, teléfonos celulares, cámaras de seguridad o discos duros en red.
Este movimiento lateral permite que una sola infección en el televisor se convierta en la puerta de entrada hacia el resto de los dispositivos de la casa. El usuario suele notar primero una lentitud inusual en el internet o comportamientos extraños en otros equipos, sin asociarlos de inmediato con la aplicación de streaming instalada semanas atrás.
El código malicioso también puede intentar acceder a la interfaz de administración del router probando combinaciones de contraseñas predeterminadas, como “admin/admin”.
Si logra entrar, puede alterar la configuración de los servidores DNS, de manera que cualquier dispositivo de la casa que intente acceder a sitios legítimos, como el portal de un banco o el correo electrónico, sea redirigido a páginas falsas diseñadas para robar credenciales y datos financieros.
Estas aplicaciones instalan procesos en segundo plano que convierten el televisor en parte de una red zombi o botnet. El equipo comienza a recibir órdenes externas para participar en ataques de denegación de servicio contra otras empresas o para minar criptomonedas, lo que satura el ancho de banda de la red wifi y ralentiza el internet en toda la vivienda.
Al operar desde un nodo de confianza, el televisor comprometido también puede actuar como puente para interceptar datos no cifrados que circulan entre los demás dispositivos y el router.
Por qué la descarga de APK fuera de las tiendas oficiales multiplica el riesgo
El verdadero peligro comienza al intentar instalar Xuper TV. Dado que no se encuentra en tiendas oficiales como Google Play Store o App Store, los usuarios deben recurrir a páginas web externas para descargar el archivo APK.
Esta práctica elude los controles de seguridad y calidad que aplican las tiendas oficiales, lo que deja el camino libre para que archivos modificados con software malicioso infecten los dispositivos.
Según especialistas de ESET, al instalar aplicaciones como Xuper TV desde fuentes no verificadas, el usuario corre el riesgo de descargar malware, troyanos o software espía capaces de robar contraseñas, datos bancarios o incluso insertar keyloggers. Esto puede comprometer la seguridad no solo del dispositivo utilizado, sino de toda la red doméstica, con la posibilidad de exponer información de otros equipos conectados.
El modelo de negocio de estas aplicaciones suele sostenerse en sistemas de publicidad agresiva e intrusiva. Los anuncios pueden interrumpir la visualización, redirigir a sitios inseguros o incitar a descargar más archivos potencialmente peligrosos.
Algunos prometen premios falsos o incentivan transacciones en plataformas sin garantías, lo que puede derivar en fraudes con tarjetas de crédito, pérdida de acceso a cuentas bancarias y estafas en línea.
La Interpol ha advertido que las transacciones financieras a través de estos servicios carecen de seguridad y que, en muchos casos, los usuarios no tienen forma de recuperar el dinero perdido en caso de fraude.
Qué permisos excesivos pide Xuper TV y qué datos pone en riesgo
Al instalar Xuper TV, la aplicación solicita permisos inusualmente elevados: acceso al almacenamiento, a la red, a la ubicación e incluso a la posibilidad de publicar notificaciones.
Estos permisos pueden utilizarse para acceder a documentos, fotos, videos, audios, credenciales laborales y archivos sensibles almacenados en el dispositivo. Además, facilitan el envío de spam, ataques de phishing y la ejecución de acciones maliciosas sin el conocimiento del usuario.
Entre los permisos más peligrosos identificados por los expertos destacan el acceso a tareas en ejecución, que permite rastrear el uso de otras aplicaciones, y la capacidad para montar y desmontar sistemas de archivos, que habilita la manipulación de datos.
También se suma el permiso para instalar paquetes adicionales, que incrementa el riesgo de que se descarguen más aplicaciones maliciosas, junto con la lectura y escritura en el almacenamiento externo, que posibilita el robo o la modificación de archivos personales.
A esto se añade el acceso a grabaciones de audio, con el riesgo de exponer conversaciones privadas y notas de voz. La combinación de estos permisos convierte al televisor en un punto de vigilancia dentro del hogar, con capacidad para recolectar información mucho más allá del simple consumo de contenido audiovisual.
Cómo limpiar la red wifi si Xuper TV ya fue instalada
Desinstalar la aplicación no suele ser suficiente, ya que el malware puede dejar archivos residuales en el sistema. El primer paso recomendado es restablecer el televisor a valores de fábrica desde el menú de configuración, en las opciones de sistema o de restablecimiento general, para borrar todo el contenido instalado.
El segundo paso consiste en cambiar las contraseñas del router. Esto se hace al ingresar a la configuración del equipo, generalmente mediante las direcciones 192.168.1.1 o 192.168.0.1 escritas en un navegador web, donde se debe modificar tanto la contraseña de administrador como la contraseña de la red wifi.
Una vez que el televisor se reinicie, conviene asegurarse de que la opción para instalar aplicaciones de “fuentes desconocidas” u “orígenes desconocidos” permanezca desactivada en los ajustes de seguridad. Por último, se recomienda verificar que tanto el router como el Smart TV tengan instalada la última actualización de firmware, ya que estas incluyen parches diseñados para cerrar agujeros de seguridad explotados por este tipo de aplicaciones.

articles.title: AWOL Vision Opens Pre-Orders for LuxVision: World's First Optical-Shift 4K 120Hz Projector
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
AWOL Vision Opens Pre-Orders for LuxVision: World's First Optical-Shift 4K 120Hz Projector
AWOL Vision, a global home entertainment brand delivering immersive audiovisual experiences through large-format displays, home cinema technology, and connected entertainment, announced that the AWOL LuxVision, first unveiled at IFA 2026, is now officially available for pre-order. Customers can reserve LuxVision with a $100 / €100 / £100 deposit to unlock exclusive Super Early Bird Benefits ahead of its official launch.
This world's first UST projector with optional lens shift is designed to adapt to the changing ways people use their big screens, delivering a tailored experience for every scenario. The big screen is no longer just for movie nights. Gaming is moving toward higher frame rates, sports fans are following multiple live events at once, and home theaters are becoming a more integrated part of everyday living spaces.Built for Every Big Screen Moment
Today's gamers expect a big screen to be just as fast and responsive as the games they play. Size alone isn't enough when the experience can't keep pace with the action. LuxVision delivers 4K at 120 Hz from input to output, bringing sharper, smoother motion to the giant screen. With 1 ms input lag at 4K 120 Hz, VRR and ALLM, gameplay stays fast and responsive. 6,000 ISO lumens help maintain vivid images even in real-home lighting, while Dolby Vision Gaming further enhances compatible titles. Together, these features bring the high refresh rates, brightness and low latency of modern gaming to a truly cinematic scale.
Bringing that big screen experience home means making it work with the space you already have. Lens shift has long given long-throw projectors more flexibility in installation, but UST owners haven't had the same option. LuxVision changes that with the industry's first vertical lens shift for UST, allowing users to move the image vertically within a 142-152% offset range without cropping, scaling, or sacrificing true 4K detail. This makes it easier to install, fine-tune, or upgrade a UST setup without having to reposition the screen or replace existing furniture. Combined with its 0.18:1 ultra-short-throw ratio, LuxVision can project a 120-inch image from just 7.5 inches away, bringing a giant screen into the room while taking up remarkably little space.
And all that big screen can do more than show one thing at a time. For sports fans, that means no longer having to choose between games when several big matchups are happening at once. With LuxVision's optional Multiview upgrade, users can connect multiple wired and wireless sources and enjoy up to four views simultaneously on one massive screen. Viewers can keep the main event front and center while following other matchups and key moments at the same time, turning the screen into a complete game-day hub.
Behind all of these experiences is AWOL's flagship imaging platform. LuxVision features an RGB triple-laser light source covering 110% of Rec 2020, along with a 10,000:1 native contrast ratio with IRIS, seven-level Dynamic IRIS and Enhanced Black Level (EBL) technology. It also supports Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and IMAX Enhanced. Anti-RBE Technology II is designed to reduce rainbow artifacts during both 2D and 3D viewing.
Price and Availability
LuxVision is available for reservation from September 14 through November 2 on AWOL's official website. Customers who place a $100, €100, or £100 deposit can lock in the LuxVision Cinema System Launch Offer, which includes the LuxVision Cinema System and one of two eligible screen options: a 100"-150" New Gen Fresnel ALR Screen ($999-$4,999) or a 100"-120" New Gen Floor-Rising ALR Screen ($1,999-$2,999). 
LuxVision will officially launch on November 3, with an MSRP of $5,999 / €5,999 / £4,999. 
LuxVision is offered in three standard finishes: Eclipse Platinum, Boreal Oak, and Champagne Walnut. Customers may also choose a Custom CMF (Color, Material, and Finish) option for an additional $1,000 or add 4-channel HDMI Multiview for an additional $500.

articles.title: Russian APT28 Breaches NATO Naval Shipbuilder in NATO Country, Deploys New Reflective Loader
articles.text:
The Russia-linked state-sponsored threat actor tracked as APT28 (aka BlueDelta, Fancy Bear, and Forest Blizzard) has been attributed to attacks targeting two member states of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).
The Symantec Threat Hunter Team, which is tracking the activity cluster under the moniker Swallowtail, involved the use of a backdoor called HOOKEDGE and a previously undocumented loader that is designed to decrypt and run an encrypted payload in memory by using a cryptographic key that's supplied at runtime.
Targets of the activity included a law enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder, and a manufacturer of military aircraft engines – entities that hold information that could be of use to a foreign intelligence agency, the Broadcom-owned threat intelligence unit said.
"During one attack against the naval shipbuilder, operators returned to a compromised host repeatedly over the course of a week in what appeared to be hands-on-keyboard activity," Symantec said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "They stole credential material using two separate techniques, opened a persistent SSH tunnel into the organization's internal network and deployed a previously undocumented reflective loader."
APT28's use of HOOKEDGE was first publicly documented by Recorded Future Insikt Group in late August 2026 in connection with a cyber espionage campaign targeting government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, and Türkiye between September 2025 and early April 2026.
HOOKEDGE shares significant code and tradecraft overlap with HEADLACE, a modular Windows implant that APT28 has put to use in attacks targeting diplomats since April 2023. Delivered via spear-phishing lures, HOOKEDGE is a barebones Windows batch script that's capable of accepting attacker-issued commands and sending the results back.
The backdoor is delivered via macro-enabled Microsoft Word documents and communicates entirely through a webhook[.]site URL, which acts as a channel to stage tasks and to receive execution output. Infected machines then fetch these tasks using a hidden, off-screen instance of the Microsoft Edge browser as opposed to relying on a traditional downloader.
In the attack aimed at the naval shipbuilder in late July 2026, the threat actors are said to have delivered new variants of HOOKEDGE that abandon the use of webhook[.]site in favor of a dedicated IP address ("185.82.218[.]119:443") for both tasking and exfiltration.
"The attackers used two distinct credential-theft techniques," Symantec said. "In one, they pushed an SSH private key onto the compromised host and immediately used it to open an SSH connection back to their own server, requesting a persistent, backgrounded tunnel that would give them a route from their infrastructure into the target's internal network."
"In the other, they ran a short, self-contained PowerShell script that stands up a listener on the host's own loopback address and forces the machine to authenticate to it, capturing the resulting NTLM handshake."
The attackers have also been observed dropping a new reflective loader ("ld.exe") using a curl command via SSH that's engineered to decode and run a next-stage component. The exact nature of the payload remains unknown.
The most recent activity was registered on September 24, 2026, when a Visual Basic Script launcher associated with HOOKEDGE was observed within the shipbuilder's network. It's unclear if any data was stolen as a result of these intrusions.
"The tradecraft observed after initial access, credential theft through two independent techniques, a persistent network tunnel, and a previously undocumented loader, goes beyond the delivery mechanism that has so far been publicly reported on this campaign," Symantec said.
Attacks Targeting Ukraine in H1 2026
In a report published late last month, the Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) revealed that Russian hackers are increasingly targeting the smartphones belonging to Ukrainian military personnel and government officials for espionage and financially motivated attacks.
"The growing role of smartphones in communications among military personnel, government employees, and civilians is making them more attractive targets for intelligence gathering activity, further compromise, and financially motivated attacks," the agency said.
This includes the use of the DarkSword iOS exploit kit, which is distributed via watering-hole attacks through compromised legitimate Ukrainian news outlets and government sites to siphon sensitive data from compromised devices.
"The tool is associated with Russian threat actors, and its use against Ukrainian targets points to the adversary's growing interest in the iOS platform, which had previously been considered relatively secure," the agency noted.
The findings are consistent with a report from Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) in March 2026, which linked the Russian espionage actor UNC6353 to the use of Coruna and DarkSword kits in watering-hole campaigns targeting Ukrainian users since summer 2025.
The threats also extend to the Android ecosystem, with threat clusters UAC-0244 and UAC-0263 using decoy apps to deliver two different malware families -
- UAC-0244 distributes CAMELSPY, which harvests device system information, geolocation, SIM card details, contacts, call logs, and images from the gallery.
- UAC-0263 distributes BTMOB RAT, which gives the threat actor control over the infected device and the ability to exfiltrate data.
CERT-UA also said it observed APT28 exploiting vulnerabilities such as CVE-2026-21509, a security feature bypass in Microsoft Office, and CVE-2026-8496, a zero-click vulnerability in the SOGo webmail client, to deliver the COVENANT malware as well as siphon victims' mailbox credentials and data, respectively.
"At the same time, the actor has not abandoned older, tried-and-tested – but unfortunately still effective – approaches," CERT-UA said. "In particular, attacks exploiting XSS vulnerabilities in the Roundcube webmail client were observed. Excel documents containing macros were also used to further distribute COVENANT."
These attacks are among the 3,137 cyber incidents recorded by CERT-UA in the first half of 2026, which is estimated to be 8% more than in the second half of 2025.
The development comes as Team Cymru said it identified five additional LegionRelay command-and-control (C2) servers used in attacks targeting Ukrainian entities. The IP addresses are listed below -
- 91.149.221[.]118:8000
- 91.149.221[.]123:8000
- 166.88.239[.]54:8000
- 194.87.108[.]12:8000
- 194.87.108[.]217:8000
LegionRelay is the name assigned to a PowerShell-based RAT that supports file enumeration, file exfiltration, screenshot capture, browser data theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration, and RDP access setup. It's attributed to a threat actor dubbed GREYVIBE, which is assessed to have engaged in persistent attacks targeting Ukraine and Ukraine-related entities since at least August 2025.
