articles.title: Teamgroup chose the worst time in history to launch a 128GB consumer-grade RAM
articles.text:
Teamgroup unveils 128GB CQDIMM DDR5 memory stick for anyone ready to second-mortgage their house for RAM
Teamgroup's 128GB DDR5 stick targets AI creators — will they pay the price?
- Teamgroup introduces a 128GB DDR5 module aimed at demanding AI workloads
- The CQDIMM reaches 8,000 MT/s at 1.1V without overclocking
- Two compatible modules provide 256GB of memory for local AI systems
Teamgroup has unveiled a 128GB DDR5 memory module for AI creators, arriving as expensive components make high-capacity upgrades increasingly difficult to justify.
The T CREATE EXPERT Ai CQDIMM has received Japan’s GOOD DESIGN AWARD 2026, recognising its design alongside its technical specifications.
Each module supports 8,000 MT/s at 1.1V without requiring overclocking, although Teamgroup has not announced pricing or retail availability.
128GB on one stick
Teamgroup combines an independent clock driver with its patented integrated circuit grading verification technology to support the module’s advertised operating speed.
Two compatible modules can provide 256GB, giving users additional capacity for running AI models locally and handling demanding creative applications.
Teamgroup describes the product as the first DDR5 CQDIMM desktop module to reach 128GB capacity, distinguishing it from conventional consumer memory.
However, buyers should check compatibility carefully because the module is designed around Intel Z890 platforms using a two-slot, single-processor channel configuration.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The specification makes this an unusual product for desktop users, particularly those who need substantial memory for local language models rather than conventional gaming.
Its intended workloads also include 4K and 8K video production, alongside complex 3D rendering tasks that can consume considerable system memory.
The module uses an aluminum-alloy heat spreader with a perforated structure designed to improve heat dissipation during demanding operations.
Its slim profile is intended to suit AI PCs, while the cooling design helps manage rising temperatures during extended workloads.
The price question matters more than another design award
The central question for potential buyers is how much Teamgroup will charge for 128GB in a single module, especially during today’s expensive memory market.
The company has not disclosed pricing, but its existing T-CREATE EXPERT 128GB DDR5-6400 kit provides a useful comparison.
B&H Photo Video currently lists the two-module kit at $2,339.99, while Tom’s Hardware recently reported comparable 128GB DDR5 pricing at $3,399.
Because the new CQDIMM packs the same capacity into one module and uses a different memory design, its eventual price remains difficult to predict.
However, a provisional estimate of $3,000 to $4,000 for one module is plausible, but remains speculation rather than confirmed pricing.
Such spending is difficult to justify for routine desktop upgrades, although AI developers and professional workstation users needing substantial memory capacity may consider it.
Teamgroup’s intended users include AI developers, 3D animators, and content creators working with computationally demanding applications.
The company has not published benchmark results establishing how much faster those applications would run.
Capacity can help when workloads exceed available memory, although it does not automatically improve performance when other hardware becomes the limiting factor.

articles.title: Comment équiper le parc informatique d'une PME ?
articles.text:
Ordinateurs, écrans, périphériques, solutions d’impression… Équiper une entreprise demande aujourd’hui de penser au-delà du simple choix des PC. Les usages, le renouvellement du matériel, le budget et l’accompagnement doivent être pris en compte pour construire un parc cohérent et durable.
La première étape consiste à partir des usages plutôt que des seules caractéristiques techniques. Un ordinateur destiné à un commercial régulièrement en déplacement n'aura pas les mêmes contraintes qu'un poste utilisé quotidiennement au bureau. De la même manière, un développeur, un graphiste ou un collaborateur principalement tourné vers la bureautique n'auront pas nécessairement besoin du même niveau de performances.
Comment choisir les équipements adaptés à une entreprise ?
L’objectif n’est pas de choisir systématiquement la configuration la plus puissante, mais bien celle qui répond aux besoins sans générer de dépenses inutiles. Processeur, mémoire vive, stockage, autonomie, qualité de l’écran et autres connectiques sont donc les éléments capitaux à considérer en fonction des métiers.
C'est dans cette logique que BELTA accompagne les entreprises, avec une offre qui ne se limite pas aux ordinateurs portables ou fixes. Son catalogue couvre également les stations de travail, écrans, stations d'accueil, claviers, souris et autres périphériques nécessaires à la constitution d'un environnement de travail complet.
L'entreprise propose également des solutions d'impression, avec une approche qui permet de regrouper plusieurs besoins auprès d'un même interlocuteur.
Pourquoi anticiper le renouvellement du parc informatique ?
Attendre la panne d'un équipement pour le remplacer peut rapidement devenir problématique. Un renouvellement planifié permet de mieux maîtriser les dépenses, de limiter les interruptions de travail et de conserver un parc homogène.
Cette anticipation passe également par une réflexion sur les configurations. Une entreprise peut, par exemple, standardiser certains modèles tout en prévoyant des configurations plus spécifiques pour les métiers qui nécessitent davantage de puissance. C'est aussi sur ce terrain que l'accompagnement d'un revendeur B2B expert prend tout son sens.
BELTA propose notamment des configurations sur mesure, ainsi que des cotations dédiées négociées en partenariat avec les constructeurs. L'entreprise peut également assurer le stockage du matériel pour ses clients, afin de faciliter le déploiement progressif des équipements lorsque plusieurs collaborateurs doivent être renouvelés ou équipés.
Enfin, chaque entreprise peut bénéficier d'un commercial dédié, avec un interlocuteur qui connaît ses besoins, qui peut le conseiller grâce à son expertise dans la durée.
Revendeur B2B ou grande distribution : quelle différence ?
Pour un achat standard, la grande distribution peut satisfaire la demande. La problématique est différente lorsqu'une entreprise a besoin de conseil pour équiper plusieurs collaborateurs, renouveler régulièrement son parc ou déployer des configurations particulières.
Un revendeur informatique B2B spécialisé peut alors apporter un accompagnement plus large : identification des besoins, configuration des machines, négociation des tarifs, stockage, livraison, suivi commercial dédié… L'intérêt est également de pouvoir centraliser plusieurs familles d'équipements et de services auprès d'un même partenaire.
BELTA s'inscrit dans cette approche depuis plus de 40 ans. 'entreprise compte aujourd'hui 120 collaborateurs et 30 000 clients, avec une activité qui couvre à la fois l'informatique professionnelle, les périphériques, le matériel et consommables d’impression. Elle met également en avant des offres et des services pensés pour simplifier la gestion des équipements, notamment avec son offre forfait, qui permet aux entreprises de disposer d'une solution simple mais personnalisable sur-mesure en fonction de chaque besoin spécifique d'impression.
L’entreprise accompagne des organisations issues de secteurs d’activité très variés, notamment l’industrie, la santé, la finance, le commerce, les collectivités ou encore l’administration. Une diversité qui lui permet de répondre à des besoins informatiques multiples, en tenant compte des spécificités et des contraintes propres à chaque structure.
« Notre offre propose l’ensemble des équipements nécessaires à un environnement de travail professionnel : ordinateurs portables et fixes, stations de travail, écrans, accessoires, périphériques informatiques associés et solutions d’impression. Elle permet ainsi aux entreprises de constituer un parc informatique cohérent, adapté à leurs usages. » explique Antoine Chevalier, responsable de l’offre de la société BELTA.
Pour une entreprise, un bon parc informatique repose avant tout sur des équipements réellement adaptés aux besoins des collaborateurs, mais aussi suffisamment évolutifs pour accompagner son développement.
Bien identifier les usages, anticiper le renouvellement, harmoniser les configurations lorsque cela se justifie et s’appuyer sur un interlocuteur spécialisé sont autant de leviers pour construire un parc informatique aussi fiable que maîtrisé. Pour aller plus loin et bénéficier d’un accompagnement adapté à votre parc informatique, découvrez les solutions proposées sur Belta.fr.

articles.title: ConnectWise Resets Credentials as Cloud Backup Remains Offline After Security Incident
articles.text:
ConnectWise on Monday said it has taken remediation measures, including strengthening administrative-access protections and resetting accounts and replacing application credentials, as it continues to respond to a security incident that led to unauthorized access to application identities associated with Cloud Backup.
The company said it has completed the following actions since it began rolling out mitigations on October 17 at 5:00 a.m. UTC, three days after the incident was first identified -
- Disabling affected application connections and suspending Cloud Backup.
- Suspending SaaS Security and Cloud Management as a precaution because they are integrated with Cloud Backup.
- Enlisting the help of independent third-party specialists for incident response and remediation.
- Enhancing administrative-access protections.
- Publishing technical guidance to help partners investigate and remediate potential unauthorized activity in their own and managed customer environments.
ConnectWise said it's validating the effectiveness of its containment measures and emphasized that it has not seen any successful threat activity in the environments it monitors. There is no evidence that any ConnectWise products and services, other than Cloud Backup and the precautionary suspensions of SaaS Security and Cloud Management, are impacted.
"This observation does not establish whether individual partner or customer Microsoft 365 tenants have been affected," it said. "Reviewing each potentially affected tenant remains essential."
"Before making changes, preserve relevant evidence, validate findings, and assess potential operational impacts. Completing these steps does not guarantee that a tenant is unaffected or that all unauthorized access has been eliminated. Do not reconnect affected applications until ConnectWise provides formal restoration instructions."
Huntress has shared the following IP addresses observed in connection with the activity, adding that the password spray and failed login attempts linked to some of them are unlikely to be related to the application sign-in activity -
- 144.172.64[.]128 - Application sign-ins with a vendor credential (primary vector)
- 144.172.64[.]99 - Failed user password spray, concentrated (October 10 to 14, 2026)
- 144.172.64[.]60 - A few failed user logins (October 18, 2026)
- 144.172.94[.]243 - Broad failed login spray, ongoing against many organizations
"In a review of application sign-ins across more than 10,000 tenants with ConnectWise applications (where we can see those logs), 144.172.64[.]128 and Microsoft-internal ranges are the only addresses that produced application sign-in activity," Huntress researchers said in an update.
"We did not see application sign-in activity from any of the other addresses listed below, all of which are in the same provider range as 144.172.64[.]128 (AS14956, RouterHosting). We did see password spray and failed login attempts from some of them."
The cybersecurity company said it also observed post-compromise actions on a second tenant, following the same modus operandi as before, in which the application granted itself Global Administrator and then added a new secret on a small number of other applications in the tenant for persistence.
While the access may have been used for Microsoft Graph directory reads, there are no signs the attackers weaponized it for mailbox or file manipulation, or to make user or policy changes.
"The choice of which applications to backdoor appeared to be random in the two tenants we reviewed," Huntress added. "Across the two compromised tenants, the identical grant flow selected two completely different sets of applications. The only consistent criteria we can point to is structural: credentials were planted in applications that are registered inside the affected tenant, without regard to what those applications can actually do."

articles.title: NVIDIA Has January Discontinuation Dates Set for RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 16 GB, Claims Leaker
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
NVIDIA Has January Discontinuation Dates Set for RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 16 GB, Claims Leaker
Earlier this month, leakers claimed NVIDIA had stopped allocating GB202 silicon to the GeForce RTX 5090, effectively discontinuing the Blackwell flagship. NVIDIA denied it a few days later, with SVP Jeff Fisher saying the RTX 5090 hasn't been discontinued and will keep shipping. Now, Moore's Law Is Dead (MLID) says the plans are still in place, and the RTX 5080 is part of them too. In the latest Broken Silicon episode, MLID read out a message from what he calls one of his oldest sources, apparently a major retailer, saying NVIDIA has set discontinuation dates for both cards in the first half of January 2027. 
According to that source, the last RTX 5090 shipments arrived in September, while the final RTX 5080 batch should land by the end of October and sell through Thanksgiving. We recently reported that Micro Center has already marked its RTX 5090 listings as "Not Carried," which could be further evidence of the RTX 5090 leaving shelves. The retailer from MLID's video also says its system already has a placeholder SKU for an RTX 5080 24 GB, which aligns with BenchLife's earlier report of a Q1 2027 launch.Of course, this should be taken with a healthy dose of salt. MLID has a mixed reputation, and his leaks tend to be hit-or-miss. Just last month, he claimed NVIDIA was targeting the first half of 2027 for its Rubin-based RTX 60-series GPUs. Leakers like MEGAsizeGPU and Kepler_L2 disputed that almost right away, and multiple leakers now point to a 2028 window instead. NVIDIA also hasn't said a word about a 24 GB RTX 5080, but there have now been multiple reports of that card's existence from different leakers. If the timeline holds, it's reasonable to expect RTX 5080 16 GB stock to thin out after the holidays, with the 24 GB model likely costing more than the current card's $999 MSRP.
Source:
				Moore's Law Is Dead

Well now. To wait or not to wait on another purchase. The current average price for the 5080 [with 16GB] is around $1200. Forget the MSRP. A SKU with the Manufacturer Suggested Ripoff Price is no where to be found [no surprise there] and the 12GB SKU is unable to cut it for most serious and eye candy'ish gamers running at higher resolution.
The 24GB SKU is worth waiting for in my opinion. The 5090 was in part inadequately equipped to effectively manage the vast amount of current that's required to use it at maximum output. The wiring and connections for power should have been split up to distribute the current more efficiently. if anyone knows of someone stateside here that is unloading a 5070Ti 16GB for under $1K, let me know as I would like a 2nd one to occupy one of my Linux boxes.

articles.title: Sam Altman creador de ChatGPT ahora lanza herramientas para distinguir humanos de deepfakes en bancos y videollamadas
articles.text:
World presentó un conjunto de herramientas de verificación de identidad pensado para bancos e instituciones financieras, con el objetivo de distinguir a personas reales de sistemas automatizados y deepfakes. El anuncio lo hizo Alex Blania, cofundador del proyecto impulsado por Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, durante la conferencia Money20/20.
Se trata del primer producto que World diseña de forma específica para un sector industrial, y llega en un momento en el que la inteligencia artificial multiplica los riesgos de fraude y suplantación.
El paquete, bautizado World ID, combina tres soluciones distintas: una aplicación de identidad digital, una extensión para verificar participantes en videollamadas de Zoom y un sistema para que agentes de IA puedan actuar en nombre de los usuarios. Cada componente apunta a un escenario distinto donde la confianza entre humanos y máquinas se ha vuelto un problema para las empresas.
Cómo funciona World ID para verificar identidad bancaria
La aplicación World ID funciona como un repositorio de credenciales digitales que certifican la identidad de cada usuario. Estas credenciales permiten demostrar que determinada acción fue ejecutada por una persona real y no por un programa automatizado, un aspecto cada vez más relevante para las instituciones financieras.
Sandro Herbig, presidente de Tools for Humanity, explicó que el avance de la inteligencia artificial está elevando la necesidad de las empresas de contar con mecanismos de verificación confiables. Según indicó, World ID busca aportar una capa adicional de confianza tanto en los sistemas internos como en los externos de los bancos.
Por ahora, World no identificó ninguna entidad bancaria que haya adoptado formalmente la herramienta, ni dio a conocer su costo. Sí mencionó como socios de diseño a OpenExchange, Bain Capital, VanEck Funds y Outtake, compañías que participaron en el desarrollo del producto sin que se haya confirmado su implementación comercial.
La urgencia detrás de este lanzamiento tiene respaldo en cifras concretas. World citó una proyección de Deloitte según la cual las pérdidas por fraude facilitado con IA en Estados Unidos podrían escalar de 12.300 millones de dólares en 2023 a 40.000 millones de dólares en 2027, un salto que explica el interés del sector financiero en herramientas de este tipo.
World ID para Zoom combate deepfakes en videollamadas
Uno de los componentes del paquete apunta directamente a un problema que ha crecido con la sofisticación de la inteligencia artificial generativa: la suplantación de identidad en videoconferencias. World ID para Zoom verifica a los participantes de las llamadas y detecta posibles deepfakes durante la interacción.
Esta función no es completamente nueva. Había comenzado una fase de pruebas limitada en abril, y tras ese período acotado, la herramienta ya quedó disponible para todos los usuarios. El objetivo es que las empresas puedan confirmar, en tiempo real, que la persona que participa de una reunión virtual es quien dice ser.
AgentKit habilita pagos y acciones de agentes de inteligencia artificial
La tercera pieza del anuncio, conocida como World ID for Agents o AgentKit, resuelve un problema distinto: permite que los usuarios autoricen a agentes de IA a presentar credenciales en su nombre. La herramienta busca simplificar las interacciones entre sistemas automatizados y plataformas externas sin perder el rastro de quién autorizó cada acción.
Este desarrollo no surge de manera aislada. En marzo, World ya había presentado una versión de prueba de AgentKit compatible con el protocolo de pago x402, de Coinbase, que permite a los agentes de inteligencia artificial realizar pequeños pagos con criptomonedas estables por servicios digitales.
La actividad en torno a ese protocolo ya muestra volumen: se han procesado más de 138 millones de transacciones a través de x402, entre ellas micropagos por datos, recursos informáticos y acceso a modelos de IA. No obstante, todavía no es posible determinar qué proporción de esas operaciones responde a una demanda comercial sostenida en el tiempo.
World sostiene que más de 18 millones de personas ya verificaron su identidad como seres humanos únicos dentro de la red. Esa base de usuarios es la que el proyecto busca capitalizar con una expansión hacia servicios financieros que combinen identidad digital y pagos.
En esa línea se inscribe World Money, una aplicación para pagos con criptomonedas estables que la compañía lanzó en septiembre. El producto se suma a un conjunto de herramientas que World desarrolla en paralelo junto con actores del sector de servicios financieros.

Le kit Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC associe un module de conversion à une batterie AB3000X de 2,88 kWh pour stocker l’électricité et la restituer selon les besoins.
Amazon propose le kit Zendure SolarFlow 2400 AC avec une batterie AB3000X à 959 €, contre un prix conseillé de 1 199 €. L’économie atteint 240 €, soit environ 20 %. articles.title: Hackers Hijack Five OVHcloud CLI Releases to Distribute Secret-Stealing Malware
articles.text:
An attacker used a contributor's GitHub account to replace the download archives on five existing releases of OVHcloud's command-line tool on Monday, October 19. The account had been hijacked, and the new files were a build designed to steal secrets stored on the disk of any machine that runs it, the cloud provider says.
They were live on GitHub for up to 94 minutes, from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC, and reached only people who installed or updated the OVHcloud CLI during that window, via a path that checks for no hash, on macOS, Linux x86_64 or arm64, or Windows x86_64.
OVHcloud deleted the swapped archives and published a clean v0.16.0 that evening as an immutable release, whose files GitHub will not let anyone change. The source code, the release tag, and the company's build pipeline were not touched: the bad build was a plain go build of a later commit, uploaded straight onto releases published between April and September.
Who Was Exposed
On v0.15.0, the attacker replaced six files: the macOS x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Linux x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Windows x86_64 archive, and the checksums.txt file, so the published hashes matched the new binaries. The same six files are now gone from v0.11.0 to v0.14.0 as well. The Linux i386, Windows i386, Windows arm64, and WebAssembly builds were left alone on every release.
OVHcloud lists v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 as compromised and v0.10.0 as clean. Those five releases were published between April 14 and September 16, so a copy installed before 12:47 UTC on Monday and not updated since is the original.
You got a swapped file if, in that window and on one of those platforms, you:
- Ran the official install script (curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ovh/ovhcloud-cli/main/install.sh | sh). It downloads the latest release archive and installs it, and has never checked a hash.
- Downloaded an archive from the GitHub release page of any of the five releases.
- Ran a CI job or build step that fetches the archive from the release download URL without a pinned hash.
- Ran the CLI's own upgrade command from a v0.12.0, v0.13.0, or v0.14.0 install on a macOS or Linux machine where the tool was installed by the script or by hand. The command downloads the archive and replaces the binary with no hash check. On a Homebrew or go install setup it only prints the command to run instead.
You did not get it if you:
- Installed with Homebrew, whose cask in force during the window pinned the original SHA-256 of each archive. Homebrew refuses a download whose hash does not match, so brew install or brew upgrade would have failed rather than installed the swapped file. Some early write-ups listed Homebrew among the exposed paths, but The Hacker News checked the tap's commit history: nothing changed between the v0.15.0 cask on September 16 and the v0.16.0 cask on Monday evening.
- Used go install or built from source. The v0.15.0 tag still points at its September commit, 760fd72.
- Pulled the Docker image. Its latest tag was last pushed on September 21, four weeks before the swap, and had not been rebuilt as of Tuesday.
- Installed before 12:47 UTC on Monday and did not update during the window.
How to Tell
The customer who caught the swap pulled the build information out of the new v0.15.0 Linux arm64 binary with go version -m, which reads the file without running it, and posted it in a GitHub issue. Three things mark the bad build:
- The module line reads v0.15.1-0.20261013083505-5ead8ef9b43d+dirty, a pseudo-version, the stand-in string Go generates for a build from an untagged commit, here one from October 13. A genuine release carries its tag number: OVHcloud's clean v0.16.0 build reads v0.16.0+dirty.
- The recorded commit is 5ead8ef, not 760fd72, the commit the v0.15.0 tag points to.
- A -ldflags="-s -w" line is present. OVHcloud's release pipeline builds with a version flag that Go leaves out of the recorded flags, so a genuine release shows no -ldflags line at all.
Advice circulating that any build marked +dirty, or carrying vcs lines, is the malicious one would flag OVHcloud's own release. The Hacker News ran the same command on the clean v0.16.0 Linux x86_64 binary: it reports v0.16.0+dirty, vcs.modified=true and the commit it was built from.
The only published hash of a swapped file is the v0.15.0 Linux arm64 archive:
- SHA-256 (swapped archive): 3833daffcaaaab27e4e0e0833240ffcb1df8df648f4ec0bc4a75c176e28933cb
- SHA-256 (original archive): 5c2beb56e6d83a4b426565a1557791ef759316abcc4effb38dd627c90aeb80e0
A build without the version flag would report its version as undefined, but running a suspect binary to find out is not advisable.
What to Do
OVHcloud founder Octave Klaba wrote on X on Monday evening that anyone affected should change every secret stored on the disk. =
The CLI keeps OVHcloud API credentials in ~/.ovh.conf and reads them from environment variables, according to its documentation, and the advice covers everything else on the disk, not only those files.
- If you ran a swapped build, or cannot tell, treat every secret readable from that machine as exposed and rotate it. OpenSourceMalware, which investigated the incident, adds: do it from a different machine.
- Remove the binary and install v0.16.0. The release is immutable and carries a release attestation, a signed record of its files. Updating replaces the program but does not revoke a key that was already copied, which is why the rotation comes first.
- Check a downloaded archive against the release with gh release verify-asset v0.16.0 FILE, as GitHub documents.
OVHcloud has not said which files the binary reads, where it sends them, or how many copies were downloaded, and no copy of a swapped archive has been analyzed in public. The company has promised a detailed postmortem in the coming days.
How It Happened
Anyone with write access to a GitHub repository can delete the files attached to a release and upload new ones with the same names, and the download URL does not change unless release immutability is enabled.
The setting, generally available since October 2025, locks a release's files and tag but protects only releases created after it is enabled.
OVHcloud had not enabled it. In a second post on Monday night, quoted by Next, Klaba wrote that the problem stemmed from the immutability option not being activated, so a user with the right permissions could modify existing releases directly on GitHub without any checks by the company's CI/CD pipeline. The option has now been enabled, and the pipelines themselves were not affected.
The five old releases now offer only the four archives the attacker did not touch.
The uploads came through the account of a contributor whose merged work is in OVHcloud's documentation repository and who is not a public member of the organization, according to OpenSourceMalware, which built a timeline from GitHub's server-side records.
The release workflow never ran: the run list shows no workflow between October 16 and the v0.16.0 tag push at 16:00 UTC on Monday. First checks found no other repository affected, Klaba wrote in his first post, and OVHcloud has not said how the account's credentials were taken.
A customer's CI job caught the swap because it pins the SHA-256 of the Linux arm64 archive and began failing. With no private reporting channel on the repository, the customer filed a public issue, at 13:50 UTC by OpenSourceMalware's timeline, and OVHcloud deleted the swapped files about half an hour later, at 14:21 UTC (16:21 in Paris). v0.16.0 followed at 17:16 UTC, published under the company's ovh-cds account with a signed tag.
The GlassWorm Question
OpenSourceMalware ties the account to GlassWorm, the malware campaign that hides code in invisible Unicode characters and fetches its next stage from the memo field of a Solana wallet's transactions. Four of the account's personal repositories were force-pushed on March 5 and 6 with an amended commit that added a loader of that kind, the researchers found.
The wallet that loader reads is the one named in GlassWorm's ForceMemo campaign, which force-pushed malware into hundreds of Python repositories in March with stolen GitHub tokens. The Hacker News confirmed that the loader file is still in one of those repositories, with the hash the researchers published.
Whether the same actor did both is "our inference," the researchers wrote. The shared account is the link, and nothing from the October binary has been tied to GlassWorm, because no copy of it was preserved.

articles.title: Minisforum’s Thunderbolt 5 dock lets mini PCs run a full desktop GPU
articles.text:
This Minisforum Thunderbolt 5 dock lets a mini PC run a full desktop graphics card for video editing, and it’s down to $219
Run a full-size desktop graphics card over Thunderbolt 5 or OCuLink
If you edit video on a mini PC and are tired of slow exports and choppy timelines, Minisforum has a solution that lets you plug in a full-size desktop GPU without sacrificing your compact setup.
We've had excellent experiences with Minisforum's own mini PC range, and right now, its DEG2 external GPU docking station is down to $219 (was $399) at Newegg when you use code SPCN6.
• Best for: video editors working on a mini PC or laptop with a Thunderbolt 5, USB4, or OCuLink port who want desktop-class GPU acceleration.
• Why we like it: The device features a full-length PCIe x16 slot for a desktop graphics card, both Thunderbolt 5 and OCuLink connections with a physical switch between them, and a spare M.2 slot for extra project storage.
• What you need to know: You'll need a mini PC with an OCuLink or USB4 port for hooking up the eGPU to your device. You'll also need a spare GPU and power supply.
An external GPU dock with a PCIe x16 slot for a full-size graphics card, two Thunderbolt 5 (80Gbps) ports, one of which supplies 140W to the host, an OCuLink (64Gbps) port, an M.2 2280 SSD slot, 2.5G Ethernet, and USB 3.2 ports. It takes a standard ATX or SFX power supply. For the full discount use code SPCN6.
Price Context & Historical Value
At $219, this is lower than any other price we’ve seen quoted. For comparison, it's currently priced at $247 over at Amazon. So, now is a good time to buy if you already own a spare GPU and power supply.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Minisforum DEG2 if... you edit video on a mini PC or laptop with Thunderbolt 5, USB4, or OCuLink, you already have a desktop graphics card and power supply to put in it, or you want one box that adds GPU power and extra SSD storage.
❌ Skip the Minisforum DEG2 if... your mini PC lacks a Thunderbolt 5, USB4, or OCuLink port, you’d have to buy a GPU and power supply from scratch, which adds a lot to the total cost, or you want a single-cable dock with plenty of USB and display ports.
Also consider
If you just want an OCuLink docking station, the DEG1 eGPU Dock turns compatible mini PCs into powerful system. Its open design supports ATX/SFX power supplies, offering a flexible, affordable external graphics upgrade.

articles.title: Une photo du visage suffit à cette IA pour repérer les patients atteints de cancer les plus à risque
articles.text:
Une simple photo du visage pourrait-elle aider les médecins à mieux évaluer l'état de santé d'un patient atteint de cancer ? Une étude montre qu'une intelligence artificielle peut identifier dans les traits du visage des signes associés au risque de mortalité, parfois difficiles à apprécier à l'œil nu.
Un visage fatigué, des traits creusés, une apparence plus âgée que l'âge réel… Les médecins savent depuis longtemps que l'apparence physique peut donner des indications sur l'état général d'un patient. Mais une IA pourrait aller plus loin, en quantifiant des signes dont l'importance est difficile à apprécier pour un observateur humain.
C'est ce qu'explorent des chercheurs américains du Mass General Brigham, qui ont développé un système capable d'analyser une photographie du visage pour évaluer le risque de mortalité chez des personnes atteintes de cancer. Leurs résultats ont été publiés le 19 octobre dans The Lancet Digital Health.
Plus de 40 millions de visages pour apprendre à repérer les signes
Baptisée FAHR-Face, cette IA a été entraînée sur plus de 40 millions de photographies issues d'un jeu de données constitué à partir d'images collectées sur Internet. Sa particularité ? Elle a d'abord appris à reconnaître les caractéristiques des visages sans disposer de diagnostics médicaux associés aux photographies. Les chercheurs l'ont ensuite adaptée à deux tâches : estimer "l'âge facial" d'une personne et évaluer le pronostic de patients atteints de cancer.
Pour cette seconde application, l'IA a été entraînée sur 34 389 photographies de patients. Le quart des patients présentant les scores de risque les plus élevés affichait un risque instantané de décès plus de trois fois supérieur à celui du quart le moins à risque, après ajustement statistique tenant compte d'autres facteurs cliniques connus.
Ce résultat ne signifie pas que l'IA peut prédire combien de temps il reste à vivre à quelqu'un. Elle établit des associations statistiques entre certaines caractéristiques du visage et la mortalité observée chez les patients étudiés.
Les chercheurs ont également constaté que leur outil d'estimation de l'âge résistait plutôt bien aux changements d'éclairage, de pose ou de maquillage. Même certaines interventions de chirurgie esthétique modifiaient peu ses résultats.
Un simple selfie pour aider les médecins ? Pas si vite
L'objectif est d'apporter aux oncologues un indicateur supplémentaire pour évaluer la fragilité d'un patient avant de lui proposer une opération ou un traitement particulièrement éprouvant.
Mais cette IA ne permet pas de diagnostiquer un cancer à partir d'un selfie. Les patients évalués dans les études cliniques étaient déjà atteints de la maladie. L'outil cherche à estimer leur pronostic, pas à détecter une tumeur.
Les chercheurs ont obtenu des résultats encourageants sur des cohortes indépendantes, avec des performances étudiées selon l'âge, le sexe, l'origine ethnique et différents types de cancers. Il reste toutefois à démontrer que cette technologie améliore réellement les décisions médicales, au-delà des méthodes d'évaluation existantes.
L'utilisation de millions de visages collectés sur Internet soulève également des questions sur l'origine et la réutilisation des données personnelles.
Déjà présentés sous forme de prépublication en 2025, ces travaux franchissent une nouvelle étape avec leur publication dans une revue scientifique. Ils suggèrent qu'une photographie ordinaire pourrait, un jour, apporter aux médecins des informations supplémentaires sur l'état de santé de leurs patients.

articles.title: Un solo hacker usó agentes de IA para infiltrarse en más de 100 sitios web de empresas
articles.text:
Un ciberdelincuente logró vulnerar más de 100 sitios web corporativos en menos de un mes, sin ejecutar prácticamente ninguna tarea técnica por sí mismo. En su lugar, delegó todo el trabajo a agentes de inteligencia artificial, a los que pagó cerca de 5.000 dólares en tókenes para completar la operación.
La campaña fue detectada por el investigador de ciberseguridad Snorre Fagerland, de la firma NorForge, mientras rastreaba instalaciones expuestas de Cairn, un motor de inteligencia artificial de código abierto diseñado para resolver problemas complejos de forma autónoma. Fagerland halló alrededor de dos docenas de estas instalaciones utilizadas con fines maliciosos, lo que le permitió observar en tiempo real una operación cibercriminal activa.
Qué es Cairn y por qué resulta atractivo para atacantes
Cairn no fue concebido como una herramienta ofensiva. Se trata de un marco de trabajo de propósito general que define objetivos, explora distintos enfoques y ejecuta acciones hasta alcanzar una solución. Según diversos medios especializados citados en la investigación, la plataforma ganó popularidad dentro de la comunidad cibercriminal pese a no haber sido diseñada con fines delictivos.
En este caso, el problema que el atacante planteó a la herramienta fue cómo ejecutar código en un sitio web sin necesidad de iniciar sesión. Los agentes de IA probaron distintas técnicas: inyección SQL, carga de archivos maliciosos y explotación de un manejo inseguro de objetos almacenados. El objetivo final, de acuerdo con el investigador, era establecer un acceso persistente a sistemas de pago y comercio electrónico que luego pudieran usarse para sustraer dinero.
Instrucciones breves, resultados masivos
Fagerland sostuvo que el atacante combinó distintos modelos de inteligencia artificial, probablemente Claude Code junto con un modelo de DeepSeek, aunque reconoció que resulta difícil determinarlo con precisión. Las instrucciones que recibían los agentes eran mínimas: generalmente menos de 100 caracteres en chino. Con esas órdenes escuetas, los sistemas automatizados intentaron penetrar más de 1.200 sitios web en menos de un mes.
En promedio, los agentes dedicaban 23 horas a explorar las vulnerabilidades de cada sitio antes de lograr el acceso o abandonar el intento. De los casos exitosos, que rondaron el centenar, el investigador calculó que el atacante gastó un promedio de 50 dólares en tókenes por cada brecha, aunque aclaró que se trata de una estimación y no de una cifra de facturación confirmada.
Las víctimas identificadas
El informe de Cybersecurity News señaló que las víctimas eran principalmente tiendas en línea de Estados Unidos, Canadá, Australia y Japón. La agencia Reuters logró confirmar algunos de los objetivos mediante la revisión independiente de la actividad del hacker en Cairn: entre ellos figuran Deere, fabricante de maquinaria agrícola; SharkNinja, empresa de electrodomésticos, y Cummins, fabricante de motores.
Dos empresas de menor tamaño también reconocieron haber sido comprometidas, aunque no respondieron a las consultas de la agencia.
Deere informó a Reuters que tomó las medidas de remediación necesarias y aseguró que no había indicios de que se hubiera accedido a información sensible. SharkNinja precisó que la vulneración afectó a un sitio independiente que solo contenía información de soporte de productos, y que la amenaza ya fue resuelta. Cummins se limitó a señalar que estaba revisando los reportes.
Una técnica que sorprendió al investigador
Hasta el momento no se sabe con certeza si el atacante logró robar información sensible de sus víctimas, ni en qué magnitud. Fagerland afirmó haber encontrado cientos de credenciales expuestas en paneles abiertos y dijo estar trabajando junto con Reuters para notificar a las empresas afectadas.
El investigador destacó la sofisticación de algunas de las técnicas empleadas por los agentes de inteligencia artificial. En un caso, tras llegar a un punto muerto contra uno de los objetivos, los sistemas automatizados rastrearon registros digitales en busca de infraestructura asociada a la empresa.
Así localizaron un panel de control de acceso público en el que detectaron una debilidad sutil en el procesamiento de datos. Les tomó horas de prueba y error, pero finalmente consiguieron ejecutar un comando malicioso en el servidor del sitio.
“No es sencillo llegar a soluciones como esa”, dijo Fagerland. “No es cosa de script kiddies.”
Ante este tipo de operaciones, los especialistas recomiendan a las empresas aplicar parches de seguridad en sus aplicaciones de cara al público, restringir el acceso a los paneles de administración y vigilar la aparición de archivos inesperados en los directorios de sus sitios web.

articles.title: Keychron Launches J3 SE QMK Wireless Mechanical Keyboard With Soft Pastel Color Palette
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Keychron Launches J3 SE QMK Wireless Mechanical Keyboard With Soft Pastel Color Palette
Deviating from its usual line-up of understated, almost professional keyboard designs that mostly feature matte black and white designs with small splashes of color, Keychron has just released the J3 SE wireless mechanical keyboard in more playful "Pink" and "Pink Blue" colorways. The J3 SE features an easy-to-use 96% layout that makes few compromises to cut down on desk space—even including a full-size zero key in the num pad. Keychron sells the J3 SE on its site for $129.99. 
The Keychron J3 SE has an ABS case, in either pastel pink or blue, while the Blue Pink colorway has a mix of white, pink, and blue keycaps, and the Pink colorway features keycaps in white, light pink, and a deeper salmon pink color. Both the Pink and Blue Pink variants of the J3 SE have double-shot PBT keycaps in the MDA profile, and there is a sizeable knob in the top right corner of the keyboard, above the num pad. Another notable feature is the inclusion of north-facing RGB backlighting, which should make it significantly easier to find shine-through keycaps that work properly with the keyboard.Keychron has equipped the J3 SE with Keychron Sakura Milk switches, which are pre-lubricated linear switches with 35 gf actuation force, 3.6 mm of total travel, and a 2 mm actuation distance. The switches have POM stems and top housings, which should result in long-term smoothness, but may have a slightly more scratchy feel initially.The Keychron J3 SE has both 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth 5.2 wireless connectivity, with a USB Type-C wired connection as a third option, and it has a 4,000 mAh battery that Keychron says should deliver up to 2,000 hours of battery life—106 hours with RGB enabled and set to the lowest brightness. The 2.4 GHz connection peaks at 1 kHz polling rate, but that should be plenty, unless you're a hardcore esports gamer. 
One of the benefits of an ABS case is that Keychron was able to include two-stage flip out feet, giving the J3 SE optional typing angles of 4.5°, 6.4°, or 8.7°. The J3 SE also uses QMK firmware, which means that it is fully customizable in Keychron's Launcher browser-based software, including key remapping, macros, sleep time adjustment, and backlighting customization.
Source:

Mais tout cela n'est que chipotage, puisqu'à notre sens, c'est l'efficacité qui prime.

articles.title: ClickFix Attackers Exploit Siemens Software Center Flaw to Deploy Remote Access Trojan
articles.text:
Siemens has addressed a DLL sideloading vulnerability impacting Siemens Software Center that it said has been exploited in ClickFix attacks.
The high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v4 score: 8.4), could allow an attacker to place a specially-crafted DLL in a directory the application searches, resulting in execution of malicious code with the same privileges as the affected service.
"The affected application loads dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from an uncontrolled search path," Siemens said in an advisory. "This could allow an authenticated local attacker to place a specially crafted DLL in a directory that the application searches, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the affected application."
The issue has been patched in version 4.0.9.8. Huntress Labs researcher Jose Oregon has been credited with discovering and reporting the shortcoming.
In a separate alert, Siemens said attackers have abused a genuine copy of Siemens Software Center with a valid signature and placed their own crafted DLL ("archive.dll") next to it to trigger the execution of malicious code.
"They chose this program as a carrier because it is signed and trusted, and because version 3.5.8.7, the latest version at the time, loaded helper files from its own folder without checking them," Siemens added.
Specifically, threat actors have been found leveraging "msiexec.exe" to launch "AllMyBasic.msi," which then executes "SiemensSoftwareCenter.exe." The activity has been attributed to a ClickFix delivery platform called Romulus, which was detailed by Forescout last week as being used to deliver Legion Loader and other malware using DLL sideloading.
According to Huntress, some of these campaigns have leveraged malicious ChatGPT Custom GPTs to direct victims to a fake URL responsible for serving a ClickFix lure, which when copied and executed by the victim, runs PowerShell code to drop an MSI installer that abuses DLL sideloading to ultimately deploy a remote access trojan.
Siemens has shared the following indicators of compromise -
- 96.62.218[.]59 (Payloading hosting and command-and-control)
- wizardexpensive[.]com (Payloading hosting and command-and-control)
- 2.27.248[.]127 (Distribution channel of AllMyBasic.msi)
Besides updating Siemens Software Center to version 4.0.9.8 or later and starting the application to apply the update, organizations are advised to block the IP addresses and domains associated with the malicious activity and look for "SiemensSoftwareCenter.exe" running from "AppData\Local\Programs" and started by "msiexec.exe."

articles.title: Thousands of Danfoss supermarket refrigeration systems exposed online
articles.text:
A nightmare scenario for supermarkets: Hidden daily passwords and command injection flaws leave thousands of Danfoss supermarket systems open to remote takeover
Critical refrigeration flaws expose supermarket infrastructural weakness
- Thousands of Danfoss refrigeration controllers were discoverable through public internet scanning
- A hidden daily code could bypass normal administrator password verification
- An email configuration flaw could enable operating system command execution
Thousands of Danfoss refrigeration management systems may face remote attacks after researchers uncovered authentication weaknesses and dangerous software flaws.
Security researchers at Claroty’s Team82 used Censys, a cybersecurity platform, to identify 2,765 publicly accessible systems.
Their investigation identified three vulnerabilities affecting the AK-SM 800A controller, which manages refrigeration equipment in supermarkets, warehouses and cold storage facilities.
Hidden passwords expose refrigeration management systems
The AK-SM 800A provides centralized monitoring and configuration of refrigeration equipment, including temperature settings, operating schedules, alarms, and notification services.
Its browser accessible management interface allows technicians to maintain installations remotely, but internet exposure can also give attackers direct access to vulnerable systems.
Team82 discovered an undocumented authentication mechanism that could allow attackers to circumvent the administrator password through a daily generated access code.
Designated CVE-2025-41450, the flaw involves an alternative verification process that checks a specially constructed credential against a value generated using the device’s current date.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Researchers reconstructed the algorithm responsible for generating this code by examining the controller’s firmware and authentication routines.
Anyone able to reproduce the algorithm could potentially obtain administrative access without knowing the legitimate password configured on the affected device.
That access could expose configuration settings and management functions normally reserved for authorized personnel.
The consequences extend beyond unauthorized account access because refrigeration controllers help operators maintain conditions required for preserving perishable products.
A second vulnerability, CVE-2025-41451, allows command injection through the controller’s email configuration functionality.
Researchers found that an email authentication password entered through the management interface could be incorporated into an operating system command without adequate sanitization.
Malicious input could therefore introduce additional shell commands, potentially enabling remote code execution after authentication.
Combined with the hidden daily password mechanism, this weakness could provide an attacker with a route from unauthorized login to execution of commands on the controller.
Configuration flaws threaten system availability
The investigation also identified CVE-2025-41452, which affects the controller’s externally accessible Nginx web server configuration.
Researchers discovered that an authenticated function could replace the headers.conf file and reload the server configuration without restarting the device.
An attacker with the necessary access could insert unauthorized routing directives, changing how the web server processes requests.
Team82 also found that requests reaching a maliciously configured route could trigger an unhandled exception in the sm_app process, disrupting the management interface.
Repeatedly triggering this failure could cause a denial of service, preventing legitimate operators from accessing the controller’s web management functions.
Such disruption could complicate monitoring and maintenance, although the researchers did not establish that every attack would cause refrigeration equipment to stop operating.
Claroty’s Team82 reported the vulnerabilities privately to Danfoss through coordinated disclosure, and the manufacturer released firmware version R4.3.1 to address the identified weaknesses.
Operators using affected AK-SM 800A controllers should upgrade to version R4.3.1 or later and restrict administrative interfaces to trusted management networks or protected VPN connections.

articles.title: PSG – Barça ce soir : comment suivre le choc du Parc des Princes en direct
articles.text:
Un an après leur duel à dans la citadelle Montjuïc, le PSG et le FC Barcelone se retrouvent ce mardi 20 octobre au Parc des Princes pour la 3e journée de la phase de ligue. Diffuseur officiel de la rencontre, CANAL+ propose son offre CANAL+ Sport à 29,99 €/mois pendant 12 mois, avec beIN SPORTS, Eurosport et Apple TV inclus.
Le coup d’envoi de ce PSG - FC Barcelone sera donné à 21 h, heure de Paris, dans le cadre de la troisième journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des Champions. Les Parisiens, qui ont remporté la compétition deux saisons de suite, abordent cette édition dans la peau d’un des grands favoris et retrouvent pour l’occasion l’adversaire qu’ils avaient déjà croisé la saison passée, à domicile cette fois.
En France, c’est le groupe CANAL+ qui détient les droits de la rencontre. Pour celles et ceux qui ne sont pas encore abonnés, l’offre CANAL+ Sport reste le moyen le plus direct et le plus légal de suivre le match en direct, que ce soit devant la télé ou en streaming sur mobile.
Profiter de CANAL+ Sport à 29,99 €/mois au lieu de 39,99 € sur CANAL+
Pourquoi choisir CANAL+ Sport ?
- C’est le diffuseur officiel de PSG - Barcelone et de 100% de la Ligue des Champions en France
- BeIN SPORTS et Eurosport sont inclus dans le même abonnement, sans avoir à cumuler les services
- Le catalogue ne s’arrête pas au sport, avec du cinéma récent, des séries et Apple TV
- Une seule facture pour couvrir football, rugby, F1, MotoGP et bien d’autres compétitions
Paris - Barça, le genre de soirée européenne qu’on ne regarde pas en différé
Il y a des affiches qui se suffisent à elles-mêmes, et ce PSG - Barcelone en fait clairement partie. Les deux clubs se connaissent par cœur, entre les remontadas, les quarts de finale à rebondissements et le duel de la saison dernière en Catalogne, que Paris avait remporté. Ce mardi, le décor change puisque la rencontre se joue au Parc des Princes, devant un public qui a pris l’habitude des grandes nuits européennes depuis le doublé parisien.
Avec le format de la phase de ligue, chaque point compte pour accrocher le top 8 et éviter les barrages, ce qui donne à ce choc d’octobre un enjeu bien réel au-delà du prestige. Pour le suivre, il faudra en revanche passer par le groupe CANAL+, qui n’est pas une chaîne en clair : sans abonnement, il n’existe pas de solution légale pour voir le match en direct en France. Le coup d’envoi étant fixé à 21 h, mieux vaut régler la question de l’accès avant le début de l’avant-match, plutôt qu’à la dernière minute.

articles.title: Gemini se vuelve un asistente al volante: resuelve dudas de vuelos y rutas sin ver el celular
articles.text:
Gemini quiere convertirse en un copiloto de voz: ya está disponible en autos de todo el mundo y promete responder consultas personalizadas sin que el conductor tenga que mirar el celular.
La novedad lleva al volante la inteligencia personal, una función que adapta las respuestas del asistente a cada usuario.
La herramienta apunta a resolver dudas durante el viaje (desde información sobre vuelos hasta rutas y planes) mediante comandos de voz. La idea es simple: que el conductor pueda pedir ayuda sin apartar la vista del camino.
La inteligencia personal permite que Gemini no responda de forma genérica, sino a partir de la información y las necesidades de cada persona. Ahora, esa capacidad llega al auto con una experiencia pensada para acompañar los trayectos sin sumar distracciones.
Qué puede hacer ahora Gemini en un auto
Con Gemini en el auto, los usuarios podrán hacer preguntas y recibir respuestas personalizadas mientras conducen. El asistente funciona con manos libres, por lo que evita la necesidad de desbloquear el teléfono o buscar información en una pantalla.
La función puede servir para despejar dudas vinculadas con un viaje. Por ejemplo, permite consultar datos sobre vuelos, pedir orientación sobre una ruta o resolver preguntas que surjan antes de llegar a destino.
El foco está puesto en la interacción por voz. En lugar de interrumpir el recorrido para revisar el celular, el conductor puede formular una consulta y escuchar la respuesta de Gemini sin dejar de prestar atención al tránsito.
La propuesta también busca que el asistente entienda mejor el contexto personal de cada usuario. La inteligencia personal de Geminies la base de esa experiencia: respuestas diseñadas para ser útiles en el momento, incluso cuando la persona está al volante.
Google cambia algunas funciones de Gemini
Google reorganiza varias funciones de Gemini y cambia la forma en que los usuarios crean instrucciones personalizadas, programan tareas o utilizan agentes de inteligencia artificial.
La modificación alcanza a Gems, Spark y Acciones programadas, con un despliegue que comenzó en octubre de 2026 y continuará hasta 2027 para cuentas empresariales y educativas.
El cambio principal es el reemplazo de los Gems por las Skills. Hasta ahora, los Gems funcionaban como asistentes personalizados independientes: se elegían desde una barra lateral y abrían una conversación separada.
Con el nuevo sistema, las instrucciones se integran directamente en el chat principal de Gemini.
Para activar una Skill, el usuario debe escribir una barra diagonal en el cuadro de consulta y elegir la función que necesita.
Gemini puede aplicarla automáticamente si detecta que coincide con el pedido. Además, permite combinar varias Skills en una misma conversación, por ejemplo, una para definir la identidad de marca y otra para establecer el tono de escritura.
Las Skills de Gemini utilizan el formato abierto SKILL.md, basado en Markdown, para crear y transferir instrucciones entre distintas herramientas.
Están disponibles tanto en la aplicación de Gemini como en Google Workspace, una integración que los Gems no ofrecían.
Sin embargo, algunas funciones todavía no pueden utilizarse dentro de una Skill. Entre ellas están Canvas, Investigación profunda, Aprendizaje guiado y la generación de video y música.
Tampoco se pueden compartir Skills ni adjuntar archivos de Google Drive, aunque Google prevé sumar esas opciones más adelante.
Spark, el agente capaz de seguir trabajando cuando el usuario cierra la computadora o bloquea el teléfono, pasa a presentarse como Tarea.
La función opera en máquinas virtuales de Google Cloud y puede realizar procesos de varios pasos, como investigar competidores o monitorear precios de vuelos.
Antes de enviar mensajes, modificar datos, hacer compras o completar formularios, solicita aprobación del usuario.
Las Acciones programadas mantienen su nombre. Permiten definir una instrucción, establecer cuándo debe ejecutarse y elegir su frecuencia, con un límite de 10 acciones activas al mismo tiempo.
El 17 de noviembre de 2026, Google comenzará a convertir automáticamente los Gems de cuentas personales en Skills. Para empresas, los Gems dejarán de estar disponibles el 1 de marzo de 2027; en educación, el cambio se completará el 1 de junio de 2027.

articles.title: Ex-OpenAI Engineer Detained in Spy Device Case as Saudi Royal Contacts Emerge
articles.text:
A U.S. court on Monday granted the U.S. government's request to detain a former OpenAI engineer accused of planting a recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco office to allegedly steal sensitive secrets.
In a new court filing Sunday, prosecutors revealed that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, was "in frequent communications via WhatsApp with a member of the Saudi Royal Family" throughout 2025 and 2026. Alfozan is said to have communicated with the Saudi royal as recently as October 5, 2026, four days before he was arrested.
"Among other things, the individual told the defendant that an artificial intelligence initiative was being launched in Saudi Arabia and wanted the defendant to join it," the filing reads. "In May 2026, the individual told the defendant, 'Saudi needs you more then [sic] the US!' to which the defendant responded '100,' indicating he agreed."
The Saudi Royal Family member is said to have repeatedly attempted to recruit Alfozan and even asked when he planned to leave OpenAI, to which the defendant said he wouldn't do so until his stock vested.
Alfozan joined OpenAI as an engineer around July 2025 with an annual base salary of $385,000. Last week, the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) revealed that he had been arrested for allegedly inserting a stealthy audio recording device into a USB port on the back of a television in the executive conference room to capture sensitive conversations.
The defendant is also said to have modified the device to prevent data transfer between it and the television and encrypted the content stored on the device's microSD card. In addition, he used his wife's personal ChatGPT account to research how to "build a continuous audio recorder" to "captur[e] microphone audio and save compressed WAV recordings to an SD card."
"In the days and weeks before placing the device, the defendant (i) used an OpenAI productivity agent to ascertain which 'meeting rooms' OpenAI 'leadership and exec[utives]' used, and where they met with 'external partners'; and (ii) spent considerable time near the conference room where he later installed the device," the filing said.
Alfozan has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. If convicted, he faces a maximum possible sentence of five years in prison.
Prosecutors also argued that Alfozan is a flight risk, stating he has "ample resources... and what appears to be considerable support from a foreign government that has (i) no extradition treaty with the United States; (ii) limitless resources; and (iii) the ability to provide extraordinary travel assistance," according to the filing.
Shortly after details of his arrest became public knowledge, it emerged that the defendant had planned to depart to Riyadh with his wife and son on a one-way ticket on October 12, 2026. Although he was arrested three days prior, his wife and son are said to have already left the U.S. without him.
The day before her departure, Alfozan's wife allegedly told the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agents that her U.S. visa was expiring and that she, along with her son, were permanently shifting back to Saudi Arabia.
"The defendant went to significant lengths to create customized, encrypted recording devices to secretly record highly sensitive meetings involving senior OpenAI personnel and executives, high-level business counterparts, and government officials, all while communicating with individuals of significance in Saudi Arabia and pursuing opportunities in – and making plans to travel to – Saudi Arabia," the filing said.
Stating the U.S. government's investigation is ongoing, prosecutors said a search of the defendant's residence and a "preliminary review" of his electronic devices, including his cellphone, uncovered several pieces of evidence -
- Several electronic components similar to those in the customized devices the defendant installed in the OpenAI conference room and had in his missing bag were identified in his residence.
- Photographs from his iPhone dated between September 22 and 28, 2026, that depict one additional concealed recording device, as well as what appear to be the input/output panels on TVs and other electronic devices in various locations in OpenAI buildings, including a second conference room where sensitive meetings took place.
- A deleted note on his cellphone from September 2026 included links to various recording devices, including those made by Seeed Studio, the same manufacturer whose devices were found in OpenAI's offices and his residence.
- Browsing history showed that the defendant accessed a folder called "Saudi Gov Docs" on October 4, 2026, and he used an OpenAI productivity agent to inquire about various Saudi-related business and government-related engagements from the Saudi Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (MCIT) between July 6, 2026, and September 21, 2026.
"The defendant leveraged his skills as a highly-educated engineer to create sophisticated recording devices that – the evidence strongly suggests – he intended to bring with him to Saudi Arabia," the filing said.
"Whether the defendant wanted to record OpenAI meetings to enrich himself by enhancing his own business prospects, or to provide aid a foreign government, or both, his conduct is criminal and it presents a danger to innovation in the Silicon Valley and a concern for the national security of the United States."

articles.title: Une panne handicape les abonnés Free, surtout dans le Sud de la France
articles.text:
Les signalements de panne Free sont assez nombreux ce mardi après-midi. Le réseau de l’opérateur tient à l’échelle nationale, mais c'est surtout dans le Sud de la France que l'internet fixe fait des siennes.
On imagine volontiers que Free s'en passerait bien, toujours est-il que l'opérateur est frappé par de petits incidents multiples dans plusieurs endroits de France. Ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, les signalements se multiplient et font état d'une coupure bien réelle, qui prive d'internet depuis ce matin des abonnés de Free, notamment dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, un département assez sévèrement frappé par les intempéries depuis cette nuit, avec d'ailleurs un décès à déplorer.
Votre Freebox ne marche plus ? La panne est bien réelle, mais surtout en Provence
Alors que se passe-t-il chez Free, en panne ce mardi comme le nos collègues de Frandroid le rapportent ? Sur Downdetector, deux signalements sur trois concernent la connexion Internet fixe, loin devant le Wi-Fi (17 %) et le réseau mobile (11 %). Pour savoir si les box sont réellement en cause, Clubic a essayé de se faire une idée de l'état du réseau Free. La plateforme Free-reseau.fr, qui justement interroge les équipements de l'opérateur toutes les quinze minutes, livrent des chiffres intéressants.
À 16h38 par exemple, seuls 27 équipements sur près de 23 700 ne répondaient plus, soit à peine 0,1 % du réseau. Le compteur affiche bien 202 incidents depuis minuit, mais la plupart sont survenus en pleine nuit, entre 0h30 et 4 heures, et ont été rapidement résolus. Vers 14 heures, rien de très important ne s'est produit.
Comment expliquer alors cette avalanche de signalements ? Free-reseau ne voit que les équipements de Free, pas un éventuel blocage plus loin sur la route des données. Pour faire le tri chez soi, le plus simple est d'ouvrir les mêmes sites en 4G. Si seule la connexion de la maison coince, le service technique répond au 3244, un numéro non surtaxé depuis une ligne Free. L'opérateur n'a, pour l'heure, fait aucun commentaire.
Dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, la fibre Free a par endroits décroché
Chez Free ce mardi après-midi, le problème se situe surtout en Provence. Le département des Bouches-du-Rhône concentre à lui seul 19 des 27 équipements hors service, et Salon-de-Provence figure d'ailleurs parmi les villes les plus citées sur Downdetector. Salon-de-Provence a été touchée dès le matin, puis la panne s'est étendue en fin de matinée à Miramas, Istres, Grans, Lançon-Provence, La Fare-les-Oliviers et Eyguières. Entre 14h30 et 15h10, elle a gagné Fos-sur-Mer et Port-Saint-Louis-du-Rhône. À 16h38, aucun de ces équipements n'était revenu. Ailleurs, quelques coupures isolées persistent, comme à Paris (rue Saint-Luc), Villeneuve-Saint-Georges, Villeneuve-sur-Lot, Colombey-les-Belles, et Marsillargues, dans l'Hérault, où un équipement ADSL ne répond plus depuis 2h45 environ.
La journée avait déjà mal commencé pour les clients Revolut, avec des cartes refusées, des virements bloqués et une application inaccessible dès le début de matinée. La néobanque britannique, qui assure que l'argent et les données de ses clients sont en sécurité, est hébergée chez Google Cloud, qui de son côté est touchée par un incident. D'autres banques européennes, britanniques surtout, ont également été touchées. D'après un site spécialisé, la région londonienne du géant américain aurait subi un incident électrique. Rien ne relie officiellement cet épisode aux soucis de Free, bien entendu. Mais pour ceux qui seraient clients Revolut et Free en même temps, et on imagine qu'ils sont des milliers, ce mardi est un vrai mardi noir.

articles.title: Hackers Use New ROMULUS ClickFix Platform to Deliver LegionLoader and Other Malware
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a ClickFix delivery platform called ROMULUS that's being used to distribute malware such as Legion Loader.
According to Forescout Research - Vedere Labs, ROMULUS is akin to a malware delivery service that employs ClickFix-style lures on bogus landing pages to trick unsuspecting users into running malicious commands and infecting their own machines.
"ROMULUS may be a privately operated panel, a commercial cybercriminal delivery service, an affiliate framework, or software that has been copied between operators," security researcher Sai Molige said in an analysis.
The cybersecurity company said it identified six IP addresses running ROMULUS -
- 96.62.224[.]81
- 86.109.75[.]7
- 151.240.151[.]223
- 23.94.145[.]224
- 93.152.224[.]118
- 2.27.248[.]127
Notably, the IP address "96.62.224[.]81" was identified as hosting a ClickFix script and an MSI installer file in connection with another campaign that has been found to leverage malicious ChatGPT Custom GPTs to direct victims to a fake URL responsible for serving the ClickFix lure.
Forescout's own analysis has since uncovered the same malware being delivered via another server, 86.109.75[.]7, that also hosted a panel codenamed ROMULUS. In addition, a separate chain triggered via ClickFix has been used to run a PowerShell script, which then delivers Legion Loader, a malware loader also called Satacom downloader, CurlyGate, and RobotDropper.
As of writing, it's not known who is behind the ROMULUS platform. However, it shares no overlaps with RomulusLoader, a malware family associated with Silver Fox (aka TA4922), a China-aligned threat actor known for repeatedly using tax-related pretexts to distribute remote access trojans like ValleyRAT (aka Winos 4.0), DcRAT, and potentially Venom RAT via DLL sideloading techniques.
The ROMULUS platform exposes two endpoints that are designed to download a PowerShell staging script, which decides the payload to be fetched next: a trojanized MSI installer carrying a malware loader or an encrypted archive containing Legion Loader that's inflated to nearly 1 GB with repetitive padding to bypass upload limits, sandbox budgets, or static-analysis thresholds. The loader, for its part, communicates with a remote server to fetch and run additional payloads.
The findings indicate how ClickFix is evolving beyond a social engineering technique into a highly effective entry point for malware. To mitigate the threat, it's essential to hunt for suspicious PowerShell commands and DLL sideloading events.

articles.title: Get Microsoft Office Professional for $27.97 with No Subscription
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Get Microsoft Office Professional for $27.97 with No Subscription
Microsoft 365 Personal now costs $99.99 per year after Microsoft bundled its Copilot AI into the plan. For a one-time payment of less than a third of an annual subscription, a Microsoft Office Professional 2021 for Windows lifetime license is on sale for $27.97 (reg. $219.99).
This is the Professional edition, so it includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and Access, plus Publisher and the free version of Teams. Access is the database app that Office Home editions leave out. Microsoft ends support for Publisher in October 2026. Your license installs on one PC running Windows 10 or 11 and ties to that device instead of a Microsoft account. Because this is Office 2021 and not Microsoft 365, there are no monthly or annual fees. A Microsoft-verified partner sells the license.You have seven days after purchase to redeem the code. This version doesn't run in Parallels or other virtual machines, so install it directly on a Windows PC.
Pay once for Office instead of every year.
Through Nov. 1 at 11:59 p.m. PT, get Microsoft Office Professional 2021 for Windows on sale for $27.97 (reg. $219.99).

articles.title: La solución de Twitch para ponerse al día con streams extensos: resúmenes de los mejores momentos
articles.text:
Twitch estrenó los resúmenes de transmisiones, una función pensada para que los espectadores puedan ponerse al día con streams extensos sin tener que reproducirlos completos. La herramienta reúne clips de una emisión en vivo y los presenta como una selección de los momentos más relevantes.
La novedad busca resolver un problema habitual en la plataforma: incluso los seguidores más fieles no siempre pueden conectarse desde el inicio o permanecer hasta el final de una transmisión. Con los resúmenes, podrán revisar en pocos minutos las jugadas, reacciones y escenas que marcaron una emisión.
Los creadores conservan el control sobre el contenido que se muestra. Twitch incluirá de forma predeterminada los clips creados por el streamer y sus editores, pero permitirá quitar fragmentos, sumar otros o modificarlos antes de compartir el resultado con la comunidad.
Cómo acceder a los resúmenes de Twitch
Los seguidores encontrarán los resúmenes en la parte superior de su feed dentro de la aplicación móvil. Así, cuando abran Twitch desde el teléfono, podrán ver una recopilación de clips de los canales que siguen y recuperar lo ocurrido durante una transmisión que no pudieron ver en directo.
Los usuarios podrán abrirlo desde el botón “+” de la aplicación móvil. Desde allí, tendrán la posibilidad de revisar los clips disponibles y decidir cuáles formarán parte de la recopilación que verá su audiencia.
De igual forma, la función estará disponible en la página de cada canal. De este modo, una persona que llegue al perfil de un creador podrá consultar sus emisiones recientes a través de una selección de momentos destacados, sin depender de haber recibido el contenido en el feed.
Para los streamers, el acceso al editor de resúmenes aparecerá después de cada transmisión.
Además de servir como una alternativa para quienes se perdieron un directo, estos resúmenes permitirán a las comunidades volver sobre los fragmentos que generaron más comentarios, reacciones o participación durante la emisión.
Cómo se generan los resúmenes de Twitch
El resumen se construye a partir de clips del canal. En el editor, Twitch mostrará una secuencia visual con los fragmentos disponibles: los que ya fueron incorporados aparecerán al comienzo con una marca de verificación, mientras que el resto podrá añadirse o descartarse con unos toques.
Los creadores podrán generar clips mientras están en vivo. Al decir “Twitch Clip That”, la plataforma creará un fragmento que se sumará automáticamente al resumen de esa transmisión.
Una vez finalizado el stream, será posible recortarlo, cambiar los subtítulos o ajustar su diseño.
La interacción con esos clips puede ayudar a los streamers a detectar qué momentos tuvieron mayor impacto.
Twitch señaló que esa actividad podría contribuir a recomendar contenido a nuevos usuarios en espacios como Clips y Live, con el objetivo de ampliar el alcance de los canales.
Twitch crea un entrenador para stream
Twitch comenzó a probar Stream Coach, una herramienta de inteligencia artificial que ofrece comentarios a los creadores después de cada transmisión en vivo.
La función está disponible para un grupo reducido de streamers y propone sugerencias opcionales sobre los elementos que funcionaron durante el directo y posibles alternativas para futuras emisiones.
La plataforma no precisó si esos consejos incluirán recomendaciones concretas sobre crecimiento de audiencia, comunidad o monetización.
Los usuarios elegibles pueden consultar la herramienta desde una pestaña específica dentro de su panel de control y desactivarla si no desean recibir sus sugerencias.
La compañía también incorporó una opción para impedir que el contenido de los canales sea utilizado en el entrenamiento de modelos de inteligencia artificial generativa de Amazon.
Para hacerlo, los creadores deben ingresar a Ajustes, abrir “Seguridad y privacidad”, buscar la sección “Entrenamiento para IA generativa” y desactivar la función.
La medida generó cuestionamientos porque todos los canales aparecen habilitados de forma predeterminada.
Si el creador no cambia esa configuración, sus transmisiones, clips, videos bajo demanda, momentos destacados, chats, textos e imágenes podrían emplearse para desarrollar futuros modelos de Amazon.

articles.title: The Acer Googlebook 14 is an excellent first attempt at a new type of laptop – but Google's software needs work
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Acer Googlebook 14 is a very good first attempt at a new breed of device: the Googlebook. Thanks to the lower starting price, 2-in-1 form factor and stylish design, it’s got a good chance of being the breakout Googlebook star. The powerful components allow Googlebook OS to run smoothly, on-device AI feels much better integrated than with Windows 11 laptops, and the screen looks fantastic. However, Googlebook OS feels a little underbaked at the moment, though some of the Android ecosystem features show promise. As long as Google remains commited to Googlebooks, and continues to improve the software, then the Acer Googlebook 14 will be an excellent investment for Android users looking for a slick MacBook Air-like experience. However, the limitations of Googlebook OS mean it might not be for everyone, and battery life is a little disappointing.
Reasons to buy
- + Premium design
- + 2-in-1 form factor
- + Excellent screen
Reasons to avoid
- - Googlebook OS needs work
- - Battery life is merely OK
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
At a glance: Acer Googlebook 14
What is it?
The Acer Googlebook 14 is one of the first Googlebook devices on the market. Unlike budget Chromebooks, Googlebooks are premium laptops that run Googlebook OS, an operating system based on Android, and Acer’s model is the most affordable variant and the only one that currently offers a 2-in-1 form factor.
What does it cost?
Googlebooks aren’t budget devices like Chromebooks — they come with premium price tags. That said, the Acer Googlebook 14 is the cheapest model you can get right now, starting at $899 / £999 (around AU$1,300). This entry-level model comes with an Intel Core Ultra 5 Series 3 processor, a 14-inch OLED screen, and 16GB RAM, and in some markets, you can also get it with a more powerful Intel Core Ultra 7 processor.
Alternatives
The Acer Googlebook 14 launches alongside four other Googlebooks: the Asus Googlebook 14, HP Googlebook 14, Lenovo Googlebook 15, and the Dell XPS Googlebook. These laptops all have superficially similar specs, such as starting with 16GB of RAM and 512GB storage, but each one has a different selling point, be it a larger screen, thinner design, or, in the Acer Googlebook 14’s case, a 2-in-1 design.
