Acer Googlebook 14 review: Value for money
Starting at $899 / £999 (around AU$1,300), the Acer Googlebook 14 is the most affordable Googlebook in the initial lineup, with the Dell XPS Googlebook ($999 / $1,099 / $2,399) next. It’s around $200 / £200 cheaper than the HP Googlebook 14 and Asus Googlebook 14, the two most expensive Googlebooks.
The fact that the Acer Googlebook 14 is a 2-in-1 device, whereas the more expensive Googlebooks are simply traditional laptops, makes it, in my view, an even better value. The Acer Googlebook 14, as with all other Googlebooks, gives you 12 months of Google AI Pro (worth $249.99 / £220 / around AU$480), plus three months of YouTube Premium and a year of GeForce Now game streaming.
In the UK, Acer is also offering, for ‘a limited launch window’, an Acer Mega-Hardware Pack worth £144.96 which includes a compact 100W fast charger, 5-in-1 USB-C hub, Acer wireless mouse, three-year warranty — and it’ll plant 10 trees in the buyer’s name — a nice nod to Acer’s admirable focus on sustainability. This deal was supposed to end on October 19, 2026, but I have been informed by Acer that it’s been extended until the end of November.
This helps make the Acer Googlebook 14 an even better value, and I’ve asked Acer if similar bundles are being offered in the US, and will update this review when I hear back (the Acer Googlebook 14 isn’t currently on sale in Australia, which is a shame).
While the Acer Googlebook 14 is quite a bit more expensive than most Chromebooks, it’s a premium device with a gorgeous design and some powerful hardware, which does justify the higher price, somewhat. However, if money is tight, then a budget Chromebook will be a better buy.
Acer Googlebook 14 review: Design
- Only 2-in-1 Googlebook (so far)
- Sleek, premium design
- Lovely screen
When Google announced the first batch of Googlebooks, the company made it clear that these are premium laptops with designs to match. So, don’t think of the likes of the Acer Googlebook 14 as replacements for cheap and cheerful Chromebooks, but instead rivals to the MacBook Air, as well as Windows 11-powered ultrabooks.
That’ll be a disappointment to anyone who was hoping Googlebooks would be more affordable — perhaps rivalling the MacBook Neo when it comes to value for money. However, the Acer Googlebook 14 does look and feel like an expensive laptop, which goes some way to justifying the price.
With dimensions of 12.28 x 8.78 x 0.55 inches (312 x 222.9 x 13.9 mm), it’s slightly chunkier than the MacBook Air 13-inch (M5), though it comes with a slightly larger screen. It’s noticeably lighter than Apple’s laptop, weighing 2.51 lbs (1.14 kg), compared to the MacBook Air’s 2.7 lbs (1.24 kg).

Finger print scanner
The power button includes a finger print scanner for biometric login.
360-degree hinges
The hinges allow the screen of the Acer Googlebook 14 to flip back, turning it into a tablet-like device.
Keyboard
The keys are large and comfortable to type on.
It’s the second lightest Googlebook, only beaten by the Asus Googlebook 14, which weighs in at just 2.2 lbs (1 kg). The body of the laptop uses a magnesium-aluminium alloy, which feels robust without being too heavy, so while the Acer Googlebook 14 feels thin and light, it also feels durable. You certainly wouldn’t feel worried about damaging it when taking it out and about with you.
While it’s not the lightest laptop I’ve ever tested, it feels comfortable to hold in one hand, and shouldn’t hurt your back if you’re carrying it around. The thin design does come with some drawbacks, namely with the port selection — you just get three USB-C ports and an audio jack. One of the USB-C ports is Thunderbolt 4, while the other two are slower USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports, so that means you’ll want to pay attention to which port you plug things into, especially if transfer speeds are particularly important.
To Acer’s credit, three USB-C ports are an improvement on the two ports a lot of similarly-priced thin and light laptops offer (such as the aforementioned MacBook Air, though both those USB-C ports are Thunderbolt 4). If you need to charge the Acer Googlebook 14, however, one of those USB-C ports will need to be sacrificed.
The screen is a 14-inch OLED touchscreen with a sharp resolution of 2880 x 1800 and an aspect ratio of 16:10 (so it’s a little taller than standard widescreen displays). It looks fantastic, and really helps give the Acer Googlebook 14 a premium feel. As a touchscreen, it’s nice and responsive, and it also means that when using Android apps (which you can install directly onto the Acer Googlebook 14) designed to be used with a touchscreen, they work really well. The bezels on either side of the screen are nice and thin, which gives the Acer Googlebook 14 a modern feel, while also maximizing screen size without making the laptop too bulky.

At the top of the screen is a 5MP webcam with a physical privacy shutter that you can slide to turn off the camera, which is a reassuring feature. The keyboard feels nice and responsive, with a decent travel for each key when pressed. The keys are well spaced, so when typing quickly you can still accurately hit the keys you want. They are also backlit, so using the Acer Googlebook 14 in darker environments isn’t an issue.
There’s also a biometric fingerprint scanner included in the top-right corner of the keyboard for logging in quickly and securely. It works well, though it doesn’t feel quite as quick as the Touch ID button on modern MacBooks.
The Acer Googlebook 14 features a large glass touchpad that takes up around a third of the space below the keyboard, and it responds well to gestures.
On the back of the laptop lid is an understated Acer logo, along with the ‘Glowbar’, which is a thin horizontal line that lights up and changes color depending on what you’re using the Googlebook for. The Glowbar appears on all Googlebooks, though its placement on the lid varies (on the Acer Googlebook 14, it’s located in the corner opposite Acer’s logo).
When you plug in the Googlebook, the bar can display the battery level, and it flashes different colors when using the built-in Gemini AI helper. It adds a bit of interesting color to what would otherwise be a rather plain dark rectangle, and while I like the idea of the Glowbar showing the battery level when it charges, it only does so briefly. Also, when using the Acer Googlebook 14, the screen will be open, which means the Glowbar is facing away from the user, so I’m not quite convinced how useful this feature will be (this is an issue with all Googlebooks, not just Acer’s).
What really makes the Acer Googlebook 14 stand apart from the other Googlebooks it launched alongside is that it’s the only one that has a 2-in-1 form factor. Not only can it be used as a traditional laptop, but the screen can be folded back, turning it into a tablet-like device. Because Googlebook OS can run Android apps, both natively and streamed from your Android smartphone, this could be a big selling point for the Acer Googlebook 14. Thanks to the thin design, the Acer Googlebook 14 doesn’t feel too chunky when used in tablet mode, though it’s thicker and heavier than a regular Android tablet.
Android apps I tried on the Acer Googlebook 14 looked fantastic thanks to the OLED screen, with Netflix and Instagram adjusting themselves quickly depending on if I was holding the screen vertically or horizontally. Google Chrome, the default web browser, also worked well, and holding the Acer Googlebook 14 vertically meant I could read webpages with a lot less scrolling.
There is a slightly strange issue, however. While all the apps I tried did indeed change their orientation depending on how I held the Acer Googlebook 14, the desktop screen didn’t change — it stayed in its landscape orientation, and that meant launching apps either from the desktop or the App Drawer (essentially, Googlebook OS’ answer to Windows’ Start menu, and will be familiar to most Android users) was rather clunky — you either had to rotate the Acer Googlebook 14 back into landscape mode to comfortably launch an app, or just try to launch it with the user interface at the wrong angle.
It's a weird omission — Windows 11 has no issue with rotating its entire interface when you rotate the screen it’s on, and I had been expecting Googlebook OS to do the same. I mentioned this to Acer, and it shared the following:
"Acer Googlebook 14 is the first convertible device to run the new Googlebook OS. For the initial launch, Google has chosen to lock the app tray/taskbar in landscape orientation, as its usage data for convertible devices indicates that landscape is the most commonly used orientation. For additional information and support, please refer to the Google Help Center”
This is a bit of an odd decision by Google — sure, there’s only one 2-in-1 Googlebook at the moment, but that’s still 25% of the currently available Googlebook market. Hopefully this changes soon, as it does make the Acer Googlebook 14’s major selling point less enticing. If I were Acer, I wouldn’t be too thrilled about that.
The 2-in-1 abilities of the Acer Googlebook 14 are thanks to the robust 360-degree hinges that hold the two halves of the laptop together, and they feel sturdy and secure. I have no concerns about these handling thousands of openings and closings throughout the lifespan of the device.

Acer Googlebook 14 review: Performance
- Feels fast
- Screen looks great
- Googlebook OS needs work
Google has been keen to highlight that Googlebooks, like the Acer Googlebook 14, are not simply fancy Chromebooks, but an entirely new product category, and I have to say, from my initial impressions, the Acer Googlebook 14 and its fellow Googlebooks are certainly ambitious. The hardware is excellent, and the model Acer sent me to review features a cutting-edge Intel Core Ultra 5 325 processor and 16GB of LPDDR5X memory, plus a 512GB SSD.
That’s the kind of spec that would do well in a Windows 11 laptop, and Googlebook OS is supposed to be far more lightweight (being partially built on Android), so performance should be even better.
It certainly feels fast and responsive when opening apps and browsing the internet. Finding and installing apps via the Play Store is quick and easy, and familiar to anyone who’s used an Android device. Apps and games that have interfaces designed for desktop use (rather than simply being the Android mobile app in a window) have been tagged, so you should know if an app will work particularly well with the Acer Googlebook 14, which is a nice touch.

That said, when I launched Monument Valley, a popular Android game that supposedly has been updated to work well on Googlebooks, I first had to map touch controls to the keyboard in a rather clunky and confusing manner (and as far as I know, all Googlebooks will come with touchscreens).
Skipping through the mapping process took me to the game, and I found using the touchpad and mouse cursor to interact with the game worked absolutely fine, so I’m not too sure what the point of the confusing mapping process is. Also, despite being labelled as being designed for desktop use, the game initially launched in a window in portrait orientation — so essentially, just showing the Android app. Even maximizing the app window didn’t make it go full screen.
I then tried the Acer Googlebook 14 in tablet mode (thinking that would be ideal for a mobile game), but for some reason, the auto-rotate function didn’t work, even when I toggled it on and off. Then, all of a sudden, it did work, though it asked me to restart the app ‘so that it looks better on your screen’. I did (luckily not losing any progress), and the Acer Googlebook 14 acted as it should. However, the game didn’t take up the entire screen, even in fullscreen mode — instead, it had the (admittedly larger) app in the middle of the screen, then large black borders around the edges. Restarting the app again did give me the full-screen experience, but this is far from a slick and premium experience.
Now, I want to be clear that these issues are related to the software, so it’s not really Acer’s fault. Googlebook OS is clearly still in its early days, and while I didn’t experience any major crashes, there’s still a lot of work to be done by Google, and unfortunately it means that the main selling point of the Acer Googlebook 14 — its 2-in-1 design — isn’t as impressive as it should be.
This also extends to some of the more interesting promises of Googlebook OS. The operating system is designed to be familiar for Android users, and aims to give a similarly slick experience that iPhone users get when using a Mac, such as screen mirroring, seamless switching between devices, and seeing messages your phone receives on your laptop’s display.
When Google launched the Googlebooks a month or so ago, I was shown how the apps on a connected Android phone could be opened on a Googlebook without any installation. Another demo showed someone using an app on their phone, then quickly switching to their Googlebook to continue using the same app where they left off. It was impressive, and something that, as an Android user, I’d been wanting for years. Only Samsung came close, and even that was a bit clunky (and you needed to have a Samsung phone and Samsung laptop).
So, I was disappointed when I just could not get the Acer Googlebook 14 to show the apps on my Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra. Instead, I was given a QR code to scan, which opened up the ‘Cross-device services’ settings on my smartphone. These were already enabled, and it wasn’t clear what I needed to do. Again, it was far from the slick experience I (and other Android users) had been promised.
After speaking to Acer, I was pointed to a Google support page which announced that Googlebook OS support for Samsung phones has now begun to roll out, and that phones need to run Android 17 (and in the case of Samsung smartphones, also run One UI 9.0). My phone was actually on a slightly older version, but the One UI 9.0 update was waiting to be installed, which I did. I was then prompted (after scanning the QR once again) to update Cross-Device Services. Progress!
It took a while, but I was then able to see my phone’s apps on the Acer Googlebook 14. Clicking on an app brought it up on the screen with a desktop-like interface, though it took a few seconds. This is because the Acer Googlebook 14 is streaming the app wirelessly from your phone, so there’s a little delay, but then you get the app in the exact state you left it on your phone.
With the phone properly connected, you can also view its files within the file explorer app on the Acer Googlebook 14, as well as files saved on the Googlebook’s internal drive, and any Google Drive accounts you have as well. This is another nice bit of interaction between Googlebook OS and your Android device, though again there’s a bit of a delay as the Googlebook streams files from your phone.
Having your Google Drive folders within the file explorer (called ‘Files’) app is another nice touch — as long as you use Google Drive. As an Android user, there’s a good chance that you do use Google Drive, especially as new owners of Googlebooks get a year’s subscription to Google AI Pro for free, which includes 5TB of storage. I actually mainly use OneDrive, and I was pleased to see that once I had logged into the OneDrive app on the Acer Googlebook 14, the files I store on Microsoft’s rival cloud storage service also appeared within the Files app.
So, the Googlebook OS and Android ecosystem feels like it needs tightening up a bit, as this is still early days, but there’s a lot of potential here, and if Google can nail it, it will make Googlebooks like the Acer Googlebook 14 very attractive to people who use Android smartphones.
On-device AI is a big selling point of Googlebooks, and with the included Google AI Pro subscription, you get access to Gemini Argon, Google’s latest AI model. I had a play around with it on the Acer Googlebook 14, asking it to help me code a complex musical plugin for Ableton Live 11, and it was quick and helpful, explaining its process and offering suggestions and advice. Even with Google AI Pro, I did use up my current allowance in around 10 minutes. At least it resets every five hours.
The ’Magic Cursor’ feature is another key selling point (according to Google) of the Googlebook OS. Once you’ve turned it on, you can shake the mouse cursor, and Gemini can view what’s on your screen. You can highlight parts of the screen and ask Gemini questions about it. I tried it while I had a photo open, and it offered to generate digital art based on the photo, or come up with gift ideas for the people pictured.
It is similar to the ‘Click to Do’ feature of Windows 11, but that takes a screenshot of your screen, then offers limited ways to interact with it. The Magic Cursor feature feels much more flexible, as you’re interacting with live elements of the screen, and highlights the benefits of Googlebook OS being built from the ground up to support AI, rather than having AI awkwardly pasted onto an existing operating system, as with Windows 11.
Overall, the day-to-day performance of the Acer Googlebook 14 was very good, though the early nature of Googlebook OS means some features aren’t quite as slick as I’d have hoped.
That said, there’s a lot of potential here, and the integration for Android smartphones shows a lot of promise. Hopefully Google will continue to update Googlebook OS regularly — though there’s always the worry with Google that it will abruptly drop support and lose interest in any product that it feels isn’t selling well.
Acer Googlebook 14 review: Battery Life
Battery life results
How long does the battery last?
Battery life web surfing test
| Battery life web surfing test Data |  | 
|---|---|
| Product | Value | 
|---|---|
| Acer Googlebook 14 | 10.416666666666666 | 
Because Googlebook OS has been designed as a lightweight operating system, similar to Chrome OS, I was expecting very good results from the Acer Googlebook 14’s battery.
Acer suggests that it will last up to 14 hours for local video playback and up to 16 hours of web browsing. In our battery benchmark tests, which replicated moderate web browsing activity, the Acer Googlebook 14 in fact lasted for just under 10 and a half hours.
This is below what Acer claims, but it’s not bad — expect the Acer Googlebook 14 to last well over a single work or school day on battery, and with some tweaks you should be able to get a few more hours out of the battery.
However, we’re increasingly seeing laptops with battery lives hovering around 20 hours these days, so the 10 hour battery life of the Acer Googlebook 14 isn’t as impressive as it would have been a few years ago.
Should I buy the Acer Googlebook 14?
Buy the Acer Googlebook 14 if...
✅ You have an Android smartphone and need a new laptop
The Acer Googlebook 14 works really well with Android smartphones thanks to some great features of Googlebook OS, such as streaming apps from your phone to the laptop. Just check compatibility before you buy.
✅ You were thinking of buying an Android tablet as well
Thanks to its 2-in-1 design and ability to run Android apps natively, the Acer Googlebook 14 offers a great way to save a bit of money and have a device that can act as both a laptop and an Android tablet.
✅ You’re all-in on Google’s AI ambitions
Google’s Gemini AI is tightly integrated into the Googlebook OS software, so if you already use it a lot, then you’ll love the Acer Googlebook 14.
Don't buy the Acer Googlebook 14 if...
❌ You rely on a certain Windows or macOS app
While Googlebooks can run web apps and thousands of Android apps, it can’t run Windows or macOS apps. In the future, devs might make Googlebook OS-compatible versions, but that’s not guaranteed, so if there’s a critical app you rely on, you should look elsewhere.
❌ You have an iPhone
So many of the Acer Googlebook 14’s benefits are tied to having an Android phone, and while there are some features that work with iPhones, you’ll be missing out on a lot — and you’d be much better off getting a MacBook, anyway.
Also consider

- Lacks ports
- Heavy keys
Pros
- Great all-round performance
- Good display for a Chromebook

- Small lid opening angle
- Not convertible
- Typing can feel cramped
How I tested the Acer Googlebook 14
- Used as main work laptop for several weeks
- Travelled with it
- Connected it up to my Android smartphone
I used the Acer Googlebook 14 for several weeks, for all manner of tasks, including writing some of this review on it. During that time, I also connected my Android smartphone to it to make full use of the ecosystem. I ran a variety of apps and games on the Acer Googlebook 14 during my time testing it.
I also attended Google’s launch event in London, as well as Acer’s own event, for deep dives into the technology and features. I’ve been reviewing laptops, including Chromebooks, for nearly 20 years, and have used that experience to inform my review.

articles.title: Microsoft profite de vos clics involontaires sur le bureau pour ouvrir Bing, et vous ne pouvez même plus l'en empêcher
articles.text:
Bing Wallpaper continue de transformer les clics malencontreux sur le bureau en visites sur Bing. Près d'un an après l'apparition de cette fonction, le réglage qui permettait de la désactiver semble avoir définitivement disparu.
Microsoft ne manque décidément pas d'imagination lorsqu'il s'agit de promouvoir son moteur de recherche. Pour rappel, il y a un peu moins d’un an, Bing Wallpaper, son application de renouvellement automatique des fonds d'écran, s'était découvert une nouvelle utilité : ouvrir Bing lorsqu'on cliquait sur une zone vide du bureau. À l'époque, un réglage permettait encore de désactiver cette fonction, bien que plusieurs utilisateurs et utilisatrices aient rapidement signalé son absence. On pensait alors à un bug. Près d'un an plus tard, pourtant, les redirections sont toujours actives et l'interrupteur a bel et bien disparu des paramètres de l'application.
Des clics détournés et plus aucun moyen de désactiver la fonction
L'alerte a une nouvelle fois été donnée par Windows Latest, qui, lors de ses derniers tests, a constaté qu'un clic gauche sur une zone vide du bureau déclenchait l'ouverture de Bing dans le navigateur par défaut, y compris lorsqu'il s'agissait de Chrome. La recherche porte sur la photographie affichée en arrière-plan et ne se lance qu'une fois toutes les 24 heures environ, ce qui peut donner l'impression d'un comportement aléatoire.
Plus gênant encore, nous avons également pu constater que la dernière version de Bing Wallpaper semble faire fi de l'option permettant de désactiver ces redirections, désormais introuvable dans les paramètres de l'application. Ce qui pouvait encore passer pour un bug il y a quelques mois prend donc une tournure plus discutable, à plus forte raison quand Bing Wallpaper dispose déjà d'un raccourci dédié pour consulter les informations relatives à la photographie du jour.
Bref, miser sur les clics involontaires pour générer du trafic vers Bing est déjà contestable, mais si Microsoft a effectivement supprimé ce réglage de manière délibérée, la manœuvre est franchement abusive. Heureusement qu’il était question de réduire les publicités sur Windows 11.
À toutes fins utiles, on rappellera que vous pouvez profiter de fonds d'écran renouvelés quotidiennement sans passer par Bing Wallpaper, et donc sans subir ces redirections, en activant Windows à la une depuis les Paramètres > Personnalisation > Arrière-plan.

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass "Á La Carte" System May Let Players Choose Features
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Xbox Game Pass "Á La Carte" System May Let Players Choose Features
Xbox's Game Pass has long offered relatively few choices, with just three tiers to choose from, with the more expensive plans offering features like day-one game availability, access to certain online games and their more premium features, longer cloud game streaming allotment, and a larger game library. This seems to be on the cusp of changing, though, with a new report from Fortune making mention of an upcoming á la carte service that would allow players to build out their own feature-set for their Game Pass subscription. 
The change is described as a planned "overhaul" of Game Pass, suggesting that the existing Game Pass tiered subscriptions may disappear when the new system comes in. An á la carte Game Pass system would allow subscribers to tailor their Game Pass experience, and, while this may result in a more affordable bottom-end for Game Pass, something that Xbox CEO, Asha Sharma, has expressed interest in before, it may also result in a more "complete" Game Pass experience ultimately costing more.The á la carte Game Pass offering was mentioned as part of Asha Sharma's plan for the future, with the insiders who spoke to Fortune citing a 2027 launch date for the offering. In fact, much of Sharma's current strategy to turn Xbox around—meaning to increase profits, revenue, and player counts—seems to hinge on Xbox exclusive games and Game Pass subscriptions. The Xbox CEO has already increased the top-end Xbox Game Pass pricing earlier in 2026, at the same time as the company introduced the Game Pass Essential tier was introduced.
Source:
				Fortune			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on Xbox Game Pass "Á La Carte" System May Let Players Choose Features
I haven't sold my Series X, despite collecting more dust than achievements as we speak, for a fraction of the inflated prices now being carried.
Gamepass has been one of the dumbest bets microsoft has made. Partly due to unrealistic expectations sure, but also games are not a good fit. Most people likely get one month finish the game they want to play and cancel it.
Maybe you mean a good balance for the consumer and Microsoft but from a consumer standpoint we can't see the cost of offering games on gamepass especially things like Fable/Gow/Forza which would likely sell much better if they were not on game pass.
I do think a good strategy would be having people sign up for 2-3 years and getting a subsidized console given the next generation is likely going to start at double the current one did.
I'm glad this service exist for those who like it but it's never made sense to me from a money standpoint for Microsoft, given that they've had to can 3000 gaming jobs it must not be going very well.
over a million people paid 30 bucks for the premium upgrade on Gears E Day you can't tell me a large portion wouldn't have at least bought the base version otherwise.
I do think gamepass on console without Xbox live and the streaming bs could make sense though for the consumer, for Microsoft I feel like they are beating a dead horse at this point lol.

articles.title: Nous avons testé la centrale Philips qui intègre sa propre table à repasser
articles.text:
| Puissance | 2200 W | 
| Débit vapeur | 90 g/min | 
| Débit vapeur réglable | Oui | 
| Pression | 6 bar(s) | 
| Temps de chauffe annoncé | 90 s | 
| Poids à vide | 3.74 kg | 
| Capacité du réservoir | 1.2 L | 
| Bac à eau amovible | Oui | 
| Centrale illimitée | Oui | 
| Collecteur de tartre | Non | 
| Fonction pressing | Oui, 300 g/min | 
| Pose verticale du fer | Non | 
Avec sa Série 8000 AIS8540/80, Philips réunit une centrale vapeur, un défroisseur et une table orientable. Cet ensemble permet de passer du repassage à plat au défroissage vertical, sans avoir besoin de sortir une seconde planche. Nous l'avons mis à l'épreuve face à notre linge froissé.
La Philips AIS8540/80 Série 8000 occupe une place un peu à part sur le marché des centrales vapeur. Elle est livrée avec sa propre table à repasser, que l'on peut placer à l'horizontale, incliner ou redresser afin de défroisser un vêtement suspendu. Le fer, le générateur de vapeur et la planche se retrouvent ainsi réunis sur un même support. C'est un système astucieux qui évite de chercher une place pour chaque élément, à condition bien sûr de disposer d'un espace dédié pour le stocker.
Ce modèle affiche une puissance de 2200 W, une pression maximale de 6 bars et un débit continu de 90 g/min. L'appareil propose trois niveaux de vapeur, ainsi qu'un effet pressing. La température ne se règle pas manuellement : la technologie OptimalTEMP est en effet conçue pour traiter les différents tissus repassables sans nécessiter de modifier la chauffe entre deux vêtements. Enfin, la base peut être détachée de son support pour accompagner le fer dans d'autres pièces de la maison.
Avant de nous attaquer aux plis, il faut assembler la station. Ô joie, l’opération ne réclame aucune compétence particulière. Bonne nouvelle aussi pour l'usage quotidien : il n'est ensuite pas nécessaire de tout démonter pour la ranger. La table se redresse et l'ensemble reste sur pied.
Cette position verticale réduit considérablement la place occupée au sol, même s'il faut toujours lui réserver un emplacement en hauteur. Le poids total annoncé atteint 11,9 kg, mais celui-ci comprend la planche et son support. Comptez environ 3 kg pour la centrale seule.
Des roulettes intégrées permettent de déplacer la station sans avoir à la soulever entièrement. Nous l'avons ainsi glissée sans aucune difficulté entre son emplacement de rangement et notre zone de repassage.
La table offre une surface de 83 x 36 cm et sa hauteur est réglable. Son inclinaison permet d'adapter la position de travail à vos habitudes, du repassage traditionnel à plat jusqu'au défroissage vertical.
Le support du fer peut lui aussi s'installer à plusieurs endroits. Il s'ajuste selon l'orientation choisie pour la planche, les préférences de l'utilisateur, et selon qu'il soit gaucher ou droitier.
Un crochet rabattable permet d'accrocher directement un cintre au-dessus de la planche redressée.
Le fer en lui-même ne pèse que 740 g. Son format compact et sa poignée dégagée rendent les manipulations agréables. Si le flexible vapeur de 1,28 m peut paraître court face à celui d'une centrale classique, sa longueur nous a suffi pour travailler sur la table sans ressentir de gêne particulière.
Le réservoir amovible contient 1,2 l d'eau. C'est une capacité plus modeste que sur d'autres centrales vapeur du marché, mais son retrait permet de le remplir directement au robinet. Avantage majeur : la réserve peut être complétée en cours d'utilisation, sans avoir à attendre le refroidissement de l'appareil.
La prise en main ne demande pas d'apprentissage. Après la mise en chauffe, un bouton permet de choisir entre trois quantités de vapeur : Éco, Normal et Max. Le réglage porte uniquement sur la vapeur, la température de la semelle étant gérée par l'appareil. Pour le coton et le lin, Philips recommande le niveau le plus élevé.
Deux façons de travailler sont possibles. Une pression sur la gâchette envoie de la vapeur aussi longtemps qu'on la maintient. Un double appui active un débit continu pendant 8 min. Cette seconde possibilité évite de garder le doigt crispé durant la séance. La station nous a surtout convaincus à l'horizontale avec une position de travail familière et un fer facile à guider.
La base amovible élargit les possibilités. Elle se détache de la station et son support peut recevoir le fer. On peut ainsi emporter le générateur au plus près d'un textile à défroisser sans déplacer la table. Il faut toutefois garder une prise à proximité, car le cordon secteur de 1,9 m limite le rayon d'action dans cette configuration.
Le rangement des câbles convainc moins. Un enrouleur placé sous la station permet de les regrouper, mais le cordon électrique et le flexible restent apparents.
Comme le conseille Philips, il est nécessaire de purger le flexible au démarrage après un arrêt prolongé. Pour ce faire, il suffit d'actionner la vapeur pendant une dizaine de secondes à l'écart du vêtement afin d’évacuer l'eau condensée. Bon à savoir, nous avons constaté des projections d'eau lors de nos essais.
Côté entretien, Philips indique qu'aucun détartrage n'est nécessaire. Même si l'appareil ne possède pas de collecteur de tartre, il est équipé d'un système anticalcaire et peut être utilisé avec l'eau du robinet. Cela ne dispense pas de suivre les recommandations dans les régions où l'eau est dure. Le manuel conseille dans ce cas-là un mélange à parts égales d'eau du robinet et d'eau déminéralisée ou distillée. Le Philips Série 8000 AIS8540/80 demande également de vider le réservoir après utilisation.
Les 90 s de préchauffage annoncées ont été respectées à la seconde près lors de nos essais. La vapeur est disponible après ce délai, la station Philips est donc opérationnelle.
Au centre de la semelle, nous mesurons une température comprise entre 113,7 et 118,2 °C. La chauffe est relativement stable avec une température modérée. Sur les cinq points contrôlés, les valeurs vont de 105,8 à 126,8 °C. Notre indicateur d'homogénéité atteint 92,1 %, ce qui constitue un bon résultat.
Cette température modérée n'a pas empêché d'obtenir de bons résultats sur notre chemise en lin et notre jean. Avec la vapeur au maximum et la planche à l'horizontale, le repassage est fluide et les plis s'atténuent. Nous avons obtenu un meilleur résultat dans cette position qu'en défroissage vertical.
Notre essai vapeur de 10 min s'accompagne d'une perte d'eau de 392 g, l’effet pressing nous ayant peu servi. Son activation demande un appui prolongé de 2 s sur le bouton marche/arrêt, puis un double appui sur la gâchette. Le renfort, lui, dure 3 s. Durant nos essais, le bénéfice ne nous a pas paru suffisant pour préférer cette manipulation à la vapeur maximale en continu, simple à utiliser.
Sur notre cycle comprenant la mise en chauffe, puis l'essai vapeur de 10 min, la Philips AIS8540/80 a consommé 0,303 kWh, soit 303 Wh. Elle se situe sous les 0,398 kWh de la Calor GV9610 et les 0,419 kWh de la Philips PerfectCare Elite Plus GC9682, qui offrent une puissance plus élevée. Ce chiffre, pas forcément évocateur, correspond à notre façon de mesurer. Au quotidien, en usage normal, tout dépendra du niveau de vapeur choisi et du temps d'utilisation.
La Philips AIS8540/80 Série 8000 rassemble tout le nécessaire pour repasser dans un ensemble bien conçu. Sa table orientable, ses roulettes et sa base amovible permettent d'adapter l'installation aux besoins, tandis que le fer est léger et les commandes sont simples. Rapidement opérationnelle, elle donne de bons résultats, même sur le lin et le jean. Le défroissage vertical complète les possibilités en utilisant la vapeur maximale en continu. Le rangement des câbles et la longueur du cordon secteur mériteraient toutefois d'être repensés. Une station pratique pour qui souhaite réunir centrale et planche, à condition de lui trouver une place à la maison.
La Calor Pro Express Ultimate GV9610 offre davantage de puissance vapeur et un effet pressing convaincant pour les longues séances de repassage, mais nécessite une planche séparée. La Philips PerfectCare Elite Plus GC9682 mise aussi sur un débit supérieur et automatise l'émission de vapeur selon les mouvements du fer, toujours sans proposer la table orientable intégrée de l'AIS8540/80.

articles.title: La “uberización” de Brasil: casi 2 millones de personas ya dependen de las aplicaciones para sobrevivir
articles.text:
Brasil vive un proceso acelerado de “uberización” de su fuerza laboral: casi 2 millones de personas, en su mayoría hombres, trabajan a tiempo completo para aplicaciones de transporte o entrega, una cifra que creció 37% en tres años y que equivale a cerca del 2% de la fuerza laboral del país, según investigaciones gubernamentales citadas por Financial Times.
Por qué crece la economía gig en Brasil
El motivo más habitual por el que los brasileños se suman a las aplicaciones de transporte y reparto es que no consiguieron otro empleo, de acuerdo con datos del organismo de estadística del país. Brasil ofrece condiciones propicias para esta expansión: ciudades extensas y caóticas, transporte público deficiente, salarios bajos y una proporción amplia de trabajadores sin contrato formal.
El resultado es un mercado sin comparación en el mundo. Los brasileños realizan más viajes en Uber que los habitantes de cualquier otro país, y cerca del 85% de los adultos ha usado la aplicación al menos una vez. En la mayoría de los meses, tres de las cinco ciudades con mayor actividad de Uber a nivel global están en Brasil: São Paulo, Río de Janeiro y Belo Horizonte.
El economista Daniel Duque calculó que en Río de Janeiro el 10% de los hombres de entre 25 y 29 años trabaja para aplicaciones, frente al 7% en São Paulo. Para Duque, la plataforma funciona como una red de contención social.
“Uber se ha convertido en una especie de programa de empleo garantizado, excepto que en este caso está sostenido por la demanda privada... sin él, el desempleo definitivamente sería más alto”, señaló Duque al medio citado, quien estima que la economía gig ha reducido la tasa de desempleo general en aproximadamente un punto porcentual.
La economía gig brasileña es el mecanismo por el cual miles de trabajadores sin empleo formal consiguen ingresos inmediatos, a costa de jornadas más largas y menor estabilidad. Funciona como amortiguador del desempleo oficial, aunque no resuelve la precariedad estructural que empuja a la gente hacia estas plataformas.
El testimonio de los conductores que sostienen el sistema
Rafael Antunes, de 52 años, fue camionero durante dos décadas en Río de Janeiro, un empleo que le permitió comprar una vivienda en los suburbios del norte de la ciudad y costear la universidad privada de su hija. Desde que perdió ese trabajo hace dos años, conduce para Uber.
“Depende del mes, pero a veces gano solo la mitad de lo que ganaba antes”, relató Antunes a Financial Times. “Pero mire, a un tipo de mi edad es el único trabajo que le dan hoy en día”, añadió.
No todos llegan a la plataforma por necesidad. Klebson Vitorino, de 23 años, dejó su empleo como operador de imprenta en São Paulo para manejar un Uber mientras ahorra para estudiar ingeniería agronómica. “Lo estoy tomando más como un pasatiempo hasta que logre alcanzar mis metas”, afirmó.
Carlos Ribeiro, conductor de Uber Black en São Paulo desde hace dos años, valora el control que le da sobre su tiempo. “Si tengo que llevar a mis hijos al médico o algo así, puedo estar allí siempre”, explicó.
Esa flexibilidad inicial, sin embargo, suele desgastarse. Leandro Cruz, líder de un sindicato de conductores de aplicaciones en São Paulo, advirtió que muchos trabajadores empiezan entusiasmados y después ven caer sus ingresos conforme se acumulan averías o accidentes con el vehículo. “Muchos terminan teniendo que trabajar los siete días de la semana para salir adelante”, aseguró.
Los números respaldan esa percepción de deterioro. Quienes trabajan en plataformas digitales solían ganar más que el promedio del sector privado, pero los datos recientes muestran que esa brecha se cerró, mientras la jornada laboral en la economía gig es 5,4 horas más larga a la semana que la del empleo convencional.
El costo político de la uberización para el Partido de los Trabajadores
Una encuesta de Quaest realizada en septiembre mostró que el 49% de los brasileños cree que la economía empeoró en el último año, frente a solo el 19% que percibe una mejora, en un contexto de endeudamiento creciente de los hogares. Más del 80% de los hogares brasileños paga deudas personales, una carga agravada por las altas tasas de interés del país.
Para el economista Guilherme Klein Martins, de la Universidad Federal de Río de Janeiro, la dependencia de la economía gig alimentó “un sentimiento más amplio de resentimiento en Brasil que se ha ido acumulando durante algún tiempo”.
Algunos analistas enmarcan esta desconexión como una “vibecession”, un término que describe el desajuste entre indicadores económicos positivos y la percepción negativa de la ciudadanía, un fenómeno comparable al vivido en Estados Unidos durante el gobierno de Joe Biden.
Ese malestar económico es, según economistas consultados por el medio citado, una de las claves detrás del resultado inesperado del senador de extrema derecha Flávio Bolsonaro en la primera vuelta presidencial de este mes, donde obtuvo el 47% de los votos frente al 45% de Lula, lo que lo coloca como favorito para la segunda vuelta.
El avance de las aplicaciones también revela un giro cultural hacia el individualismo y el trabajo por cuenta propia, en contraste con la tradición sindicalista que marcó buena parte de la trayectoria política de Lula.
“Hace 30 años, el primer empleo solía ser en la industria, tal vez para una gran empresa que contaba con sindicatos activos... pero ahora es muy probable que sea en Uber”, apuntó Mansueto Almeida, exfuncionario del Ministerio de Hacienda y actual economista jefe de BTG Pactual.

articles.title: 'Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior': Tencent admits AI agents it was testing made more than 2,600 attempts in 11 days to slip past Alibaba's map defenses, just to find out which zoo gate people use
articles.text:
'Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior': Tencent admits AI agents it was testing made more than 2,600 attempts in 11 days to slip past Alibaba's map defenses, just to find out which zoo gate people use
Researchers hid a message for a live fleet of rogue AI agents, and the agents wrote back
- Tencent says AI agents it used to evaluate third-party models showed "unintended" browsing behavior, the first such admission by a major Chinese firm
- Swarmchasers researchers logged more than 2,600 attempts by the Tencent Cloud fleet to pull entrance data from Alibaba's Amap
- Most attempts failed, but agents used a public scanner as a remote browser, and one leaked company API key returned real place data
Tencent has acknowledged that AI agents running on its infrastructure behaved unexpectedly after independent researchers caught a fleet of them repeatedly trying to pull data from Alibaba's Amap navigation service.
Reuters reports the company's AI unit, Tencent Hunyuan, said the agents were being used to evaluate third-party models, in what appears to be the first known case of rogue agent activity acknowledged by a major Chinese company.
In a post on X, the unit said the activity did not come from its own Hunyuan models, noting "During these evaluations, some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior, but our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination," before adding that it was tightening network access controls and agent monitoring.
A lot of "unintended" effort for a zoo gate?
The admission follows a full report by Swarmchasers, a loose group of researchers who met at an AI hackathon. They counted more than 2,600 attempts to extract Amap data over 11 days, from September 28 to October 8 2026, traced the traffic to Tencent Cloud servers in Hong Kong, and then did something nobody appears to have done before: they talked to the agents while they were still running.
The tasks were almost comically mundane. A typical job asked which entrance of a place like Chengdu Zoo most Amap users use, with other runs covering parks, museums, and hospitals and, on September 30, a British Columbia cancer statistics dashboard.
The problem was getting the answer. Amap's anti-bot system expects browser cookies, JavaScript-generated tokens, and sometimes a CAPTCHA, while the fleet's harness sent plain Python and curl requests. One agent told the researchers that Amap had blocked its Tencent sandbox, so it could not fetch the data itself.
The agents improvised instead; according to the Swarmchasers report, they packed their own HTML and JavaScript into URLs and fed them to urlquery.net, a public security scanning service, borrowing its browser to run their code.

When Amap kept blocking them, the programs tried to intercept or forge tokens from Alibaba's own anti-bot libraries, sent 57 requests to four pre-production hosts, routed traffic through Baidu Translate and remote browsers, and, in seven reports, used Amap API keys found on the open web.
Most of it did not work as intended: in a snapshot of 2,372 reports up to October 4, nearly half ended on an empty Amap page or login prompt and almost a quarter on a blank tab. None of the token tricks appear to have succeeded, and there is no evidence that any pre-production server answered. The entrance figures that did come back arrived mostly through Jina's page reader, which can serve cached copies up to 30 days old.
The exception should worry businesses more than Alibaba. A key and security code exposed in another company's public source code did return real place data, and the researchers say they cannot tell whose account was billed for those requests.
Tencent's framing of the activity as "unintended" is accurate as far as it goes, but it sidesteps an awkward point. If an evaluation asks agents for data that only Amap displays, behind defenses a sandboxed agent without a browser cannot legitimately clear, then crossing that line is close to the only route to a correct answer.
US incidents involved something similar: OpenAI's agents breached Hugging Face while hunting for answers to an ExploitGym benchmark, with later disclosures showing they organized through a makeshift message board, and roughly 700 of them took part in an attack Hugging Face eventually contained using Zhipu's open GLM 5.2 model. Anthropic found three Claude models had compromised real organizations after a misconfigured evaluation left internet access open, and this month disclosed that Claude Haiku 4.5 filed a false homicide tip with Philadelphia police while exploring random websites.
Reuters judges Tencent's case less egregious than those, and the Swarmchasers found no sign the agents coordinated, which is why they call it a fleet rather than a swarm. Still, as recent analysis argued, sandbox escapes often come down to an agent routing around a proxy, and borrowing a stranger's browser is exactly that.
Tencent's admission lands in the same week ByteDance's Seed unit created a dedicated Alignment & Preparedness team and began recruiting 10 researchers worldwide, a rare public commitment to frontier safety work by a major Chinese developer. The internal email announcing it went out a day before the Swarmchasers' full report and, in 36Kr's translation, points to a broader run of agent escapes rather than this one case, so the two are not cause and effect even if they do point the same way.
The argument is that alignment remains unsolved regardless of whose flag flies over the data center, and they want every lab running internet-connected agents to audit what its sandboxes can reach, a seemingly modest ask.
This fleet, however, ran for nearly a week before outside researchers stumbled on it at a hackathon, then carried on for four more days after their preliminary findings went public, and Tencent has yet to explain why.

articles.title: Subaru : c'est terminé, la marque ne vendra plus aucune voiture essence en Europe dès 2028, place au 100 % électrique
articles.text:
Subaru : c'est terminé, la marque ne vendra plus aucune voiture essence en Europe dès 2028, place au 100 % électrique
Le moteur à plat qui a mené Subaru aux titres mondiaux des rallyes vit ses derniers mois sur le Vieux Continent. D'ici fin 2027, la marque n'y proposera plus que trois SUV électriques conçus avec Toyota. Et la France a pris ce virage avant tout le monde.
Le 16 octobre 2026, Subaru Deutschland a confirmé l'information au magazine auto motor und sport. Le constructeur japonais arrêtera de vendre des voitures thermiques neuves en Europe au plus tard fin 2027. La lignée née en 1966 avec la Subaru 1000, premier modèle de la marque à moteur boxer, s'éteint donc sur le continent. Dès 2028, le catalogue européen se limitera aux Solterra, Uncharted et E-Outback, cousins des Toyota bZ4X, C-HR+ et bZ4X Touring.
Outback, Forester, Crosstrek : le calendrier de sortie du boxer
L'Outback part le premier : son 2,5 litres atmosphérique de 169 ch quitte les catalogues avant la fin de l'année. Impreza, Crosstrek et Forester suivront au fil de 2027, avec leur 2 litres e-Boxer microhybride de 136 ch. Leur production pour l'Europe est déjà arrêtée, et les concessionnaires écoulent les derniers stocks.
Subaru met en cause les plafonds de CO2 que Bruxelles impose aux flottes des constructeurs. Il cite aussi la liste croissante des aides à la conduite et des équipements de sécurité obligatoires. Pour une marque de niche, chaque homologation coûte très cher. Le boxer hybride complet de 197 ch, vendu sur les Crosstrek et Forester américains, ne fait l'objet d'aucun projet concret pour l'Europe.
Le revirement est brutal. En juillet 2025, Subaru Europe présentait encore ses trois électriques comme un complément à la gamme thermique.
En France, Subaru vend déjà uniquement des voitures électriques
Pour les automobilistes français, le décor reste le même. Après cinq années de quasi-absence, la marque est revenue en 2026 avec Emil Frey France et une gamme exclusivement électrique. Le Solterra démarre à 48 990 €, l'Uncharted à 36 990 €, et l'E-Outback a rejoint le réseau en juin. La fiscalité française avait déjà eu raison du boxer. Pierre Guignot, président de Subaru France, vise 550 immatriculations cette année.
	
Nous allons étoffer notre offre avec d'autres modèles 100 % électriques en 2027 et 2028, issus de la toute dernière génération technologique.
En Suisse, la demande progresse. D'après Blick, le Solterra et l'Uncharted cumulent 277 immatriculations depuis janvier, contre 327 pour le seul Crosstrek. Subaru prépare aussi son émancipation. Sa première plateforme électrique maison, avec des batteries Panasonic et des moteurs Aisin, doit arriver vers 2029.

articles.title: El Tamagotchi Original si existe: cuáles son las diferencias entre la generación 1 y 2 hoy
articles.text:
El reciente anuncio de Meta sobre el desarrollo de su nuevo dispositivo portátil “Muse Charm” —un pequeño equipo impulsado por inteligencia artificial cuyo diseño y avatar virtual (Jolly) han sido comparados directamente con Tamagotchi, el clásico juguete de los años noventa— reavivó el interés del público por el formato de las mascotas digitales de bolsillo.
A pesar del avance en los dispositivos móviles y los agentes de IA, Bandai mantiene en producción activa el hardware y software exacto del Tamagotchi original. Bajo la línea comercial “Original Tamagotchi”, la compañía japonesa continúa distribuyendo estos dispositivos a nivel global en dos versiones de programación: Generación 1 (Gen 1) y Generación 2 (Gen 2).
Comprender las diferencias entre ambas generaciones es fundamental antes de realizar la compra, ya que las variaciones afectan directamente la jugabilidad diaria, el aspecto visual interno y las recompensas evolutivas.
Diferencias técnicas y de software
Aunque el aspecto exterior del dispositivo —una carcasa de plástico en forma de huevo con tres botones y una pantalla LCD monocromática— es idéntico en ambas generaciones, el código interno presenta tres diferencias estructurales:
El minijuego interno: para mantener el peso y la felicidad de la mascota virtual, el usuario debe interactuar a través de un minijuego.
- En la Gen 1, el juego es de azar posicional: el usuario debe adivinar hacia qué lado —izquierda o derecha— mirará el personaje en el siguiente movimiento.
- En la Gen 2, el juego es numérico y de lógica básica: la pantalla muestra un número del 1 al 9, y el usuario debe adivinar si el siguiente número generado por el sistema será mayor o menor.
El fondo de la pantalla física: la lámina impresa detrás del panel LCD cambia según la versión. Los dispositivos Gen 1 presentan un fondo con un patrón de cuadros tipo ajedrez, mientras que los modelos Gen 2 exhiben un diseño de líneas onduladas.
El ciclo evolutivo y los personajes: cada generación cuenta con un código genético distinto que determina en qué criatura se convertirá la mascota tras su etapa de crecimiento, según los cuidados del usuario —alimentación, disciplina y limpieza—.
- La Gen 1 incluye personajes clásicos como Mametchi, Kuchipatchi y Maskutchi, además del personaje secreto Oyajitchi.
- Gen 2La introduce una lista completamente nueva de personajes adultos, con Mimitchi y Pochitchi como figuras destacadas, y Zatchi —o Sekitoritchi en su versión japonesa— como el personaje secreto de máxima dificultad.
El ecosistema de carcasas y logotipos
Bandai diferencia comercialmente estas dos generaciones a través del empaque. Si bien existen decenas de diseños de carcasas exteriores —desde colores sólidos hasta patrones translúcidos, de neón o franquicias licenciadas—, el empaque oficial indica claramente qué software incluye. Como regla general en las reediciones actuales, la Gen 1 suele asociarse con un diseño de empaque y logotipos específicos que la diferencian de la Gen 2 para facilitar su identificación en tiendas.
Cómo adquirir un Original Tamagotchi en la actualidad
En 2026, no es necesario recurrir a plataformas de subastas o mercados de segunda mano para adquirir un modelo original de 1996 o 1997. Bandai Namco produce continuamente estas unidades mediante su programa de reediciones oficiales, conservando la placa base, los componentes de audio y la pantalla LCD sin modificaciones.
Los canales de adquisición oficiales son los siguientes:
- Tiendas de comercio electrónico globales: plataformas como Amazon cuentan con tiendas oficiales gestionadas directamente por Bandai, donde el inventario se actualiza regularmente con nuevas series de diseños de carcasas para las versiones Gen 1 y Gen 2.
- Tienda oficial de Bandai Namco: la compañía dispone de la página tamagotchi-official.com, con envíos internacionales y ediciones exclusivas limitadas.
- Cadenas minoristas: en Norteamérica y Europa, grandes superficies y tiendas especializadas en videojuegos mantienen un inventario constante de estos dispositivos en la sección de juguetes electrónicos.

articles.title: Dyson se proposer d'aspirer et laver en un seul passage avec le V15s Detect Submarine en promo à -33%
articles.text:
Le Dyson V15s Detect Submarine est un aspirateur balai qui aspire et passe aussi la serpillère, que vous retrouvez en promo à 589 euros au lieu de 879 euros sur Fnac.
Le Dyson V15s Detect Submarine marque l'entrée très attendue du constructeur britannique sur le marché des aspirateurs laveurs. Si l'on devait faire une analogie facile, nous dirions que Dyson est aux aspirateurs ce qu'Apple est aux smartphones. Un produit luxueux, haut de gamme, qu'on aime utiliser autant qu'afficher. Ici, il combine l'aspiration cyclonique du V15 avec une tête de lavage à l'eau claire. Comme tout appareil Dyson, son prix de base est onéreux mais il bénéficie de 290 euros de réduction sur Fnac, ce qui peut permettre de sauter plus facilement le pas.
Voici le Dyson V15s Detect Submarine à 589 € au lieu de 879 € sur Fnac
Pourquoi choisir le Dyson V15s Detect Submarine ?
- Pour son aspiration sans compromis typique de Dyson avec une puissance de 240 AW avec une brosse Optic Fluffy pour traquer la poussière invisible à l'œil nu.
- Le lavage efficace des tâches avec la brosse Submarine humidifiée qui vient à bout des tâches incrustées et liquides sur les sols durs.
- Son écosystème modulaire livré avec une pléthore d'accessoires pour passer du nettoyage d'une salle de bain à l'aspiration des poils d'animaux en un clic.
Un nettoyage hybride efficace qui se mérite
Si vous connaissez les Dyson, vous ne serez pas surpris de leur efficacité en aspiration, et ce modèle ne fait pas exception à la règle. Avec sa puissance de 12 500 Pa, il peut aspirer toute la poussière sur son chemin pour l'engranger dans son réservoir de 0,76 l. Ce n'est pas tout puisqu'il est doté d'une tête Submarine qui lave mais attention : elle peut faire l'un ou l'autre, pas les deux en même temps. Et il faut avoir une petite condition physique pour le manier parce qu'il est quand même 4,1 kg et qu'il faut garder en permanence le doigt sur la gâchette. Il est quand même silencieux en mode lavage, avec 60 dB mesurés, ce qui contraste avec l'autonomie de ses petits réservoirs (300 ml d'eau propre) qui imposent des allers-retours fréquents au robinet. Il se destine avant tout aux profils avec des surfaces dures, de taille modérée (environ 40m²) qui ont l'habitude d'aspirer avant de passer la serpillère.
Une approche modulaire face aux aspirateurs tout-en-un
Contrairement aux aspirateurs laveurs massifs comme le Dreame H12 Pro, ce modèle Dyson apporte de la polyvalence en conservant le format passe-partout et les accessoires dédiés d'un aspirateur balai premium : un suceur long, une brosse Digital Motorbar, une mini brosse motorisée auto démêlante et la station murale qui va avec. C'est juste dommage qu'il ne sache pas aspirer et laver en même temps, et que son autonomie ne fasse pas un peu de progrès : 60 minutes en mode Eco, une poignée de minutes en mode Boost. Et il n'y a pas de station d'auto nettoyage, donc ça implique un entretien de votre part.
✅ Les points forts
- Sa puissance d'aspiration de 240 AW sur tous les types de sols
- Son lavage qui vient à bout des tâches aussi bien fraîches qu'incrustées
- Sa polyvalence avec sa panoplie complète d'accessoires
- So niveau sonore maîtrisé et agréable en mode lavage de 60 dB
❌ Les limites
- Impossible d'aspirer et laver en même temps avec la brosse Submarine
- Ses réservoirs d'eau sous-dimensionnés qui poussent à des remplissages fréquents
- Un collecteur d'eau sale mal conçu qui fuit si la brosse est inclinée
- Son poids important et le maintien de la gâchette obligatoire
- Un seul rouleau fourni
L'aspirateur balai laveur Dyson V15s Detect Submarine est bradé à 589 € sur Fnac
Le Dyson V15s Detect Submarine est une bonne affaire si vous êtes fan de la marque et que vous cherchez un modèle capable de ponctuellement laver en profondeur les sols de vos petites pièces. C'est l'outil idéal pour centraliser le matériel d'entretien au sein d'un appartement ou pour un ménage par zone de la maison.
Si vous avez de grandes surfaces carrelées à traiter en une seule passe, les petits réservoirs d'eau vont rendre l'expérience trop fastidieuse. Et un dernier conseil pratique : pensez à bien transporter la brosse Submarine à l'horizontale jusqu'à votre évier : le bac d'eau sale étant ouvert, il risque de fuir s'il est trop incliné quand vous le manipulez.

articles.title: Helldivers 2 Anti-Cheat Change Breaks Mods but Keeps Steam Deck Compatibility
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Helldivers 2 Anti-Cheat Change Breaks Mods but Keeps Steam Deck Compatibility
Helldivers 2 developer, Arrowhead, has just announced a substantial change to the game's anti-cheat systems: A move away from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat. The change will take place on October 20, and Arrowhead explained in a recent Steam post that the justification for the switch away from GameGuard comes down to cracking down on cheat mods and implementing additional security tools to "improve game integrity protection."
- Implementing additional security measures to crack down on recent cheat mods that have been circulating.
- Transitioning from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat today, October 20th, with additional security tools in place to enhance its effectiveness and improve game integrity protection.
The studio explains in the post that there has been a notable increase in the number of mods that affect gameplay, including pick-up rates, and "manipulate the war itself, breaking the unfolding story and dragging down innocent players with it." As such, Arrowhead notes that the switch to EAC will specifically impact and break mods that affect other players' gameplay. However, it adds that "some non-malicious cosmetic mods may require updates from their individual creators in order to keep working. 
The studio also adds that the switch to EAC will not impact compatibility with the Valve Steam Deck and SteamOS, in general, even though Helldivers 2 will be using EAC's kernel-level anti-cheat. There are also no new hardware requirements, like TPM or secure boot. Arrowhead did not directly mention how account bans would work under the new anti-cheat implementation or if malicious mods would result in account bans.
Sources:
				Helldivers 2 on Steam, 				via GamingOnLinux, 				qxyovo123 on NexusMods

articles.title: Youtuber construye refrigerador que utiliza fuego y sal para enfriar sin electricidad
articles.text:
Un canal de YouTube dedicado a la metalurgia y la ingeniería casera construyó un refrigerador que funciona con fuego, agua y sal de carretera, sin depender de un compresor eléctrico convencional. El proyecto, desarrollado por Greenhill Forge, logró enfriar una sección del dispositivo hasta los 5 °C (41 °F) mientras la temperatura ambiente rondaba los 16 °C (61 °F), un resultado que el propio canal documentó en video.
La propuesta retoma un principio de ingeniería centenario con una aplicación actual: la posibilidad de generar frío en lugares donde la electricidad es escasa o poco confiable.
El principio detrás del sistema: absorción refrigerante
El dispositivo se basa en la refrigeración por absorción, una técnica que existe desde hace más de un siglo y que prescinde del compresor eléctrico para hacer circular el refrigerante. En su lugar, utiliza calor para impulsar una reacción química que produce el efecto de enfriamiento.
El diseño de Greenhill Forge se compone de dos secciones principales: un generador y un absorbedor. El generador contiene una solución de cloruro de calcio y agua destilada. Cuando el fuego calienta esa mezcla, el vapor de agua se separa de la solución y viaja a través de una tubería hasta un condensador, donde se enfría y vuelve a su estado líquido.
Después, el agua líquida pasa por una pequeña válvula ajustable hacia un evaporador que opera bajo un vacío intenso, de alrededor de seis milibares. A esa presión tan baja, el agua puede evaporarse a temperaturas muy por debajo de su punto de ebullición habitual. Ese proceso de evaporación absorbe calor del entorno inmediato y genera el efecto refrigerante.
El rol de la sal para sostener el vacío
El sistema enfrenta un desafío técnico: a medida que se acumula vapor de agua, la presión tiende a subir y limita la evaporación posterior. Para evitarlo, el dispositivo rocía una solución concentrada de cloruro de calcio dentro del absorbedor, que capta ese vapor y ayuda a mantener la baja presión necesaria para que el ciclo continúe.
De este modo, el fuego aporta el calor que impulsa todo el proceso, mientras la solución salina sostiene las condiciones que permiten que el agua se evapore a bajas temperaturas.
Un proyecto de metalurgia con control electrónico
Más allá de su funcionamiento térmico, el dispositivo representa un trabajo considerable de metalurgia. Greenhill Forge fabricó gran parte de la estructura con chapa y tubería de acero inoxidable, soldó los compartimentos y unió las conexiones más pequeñas mediante soldadura fuerte con plata.
Para formar la bobina de enfriamiento, el constructor llenó un tubo con agua, lo congeló y luego lo dobló alrededor del núcleo helado, con el objetivo de evitar que la tubería se colapsara durante el proceso.
Antes de cargar el sistema con los líquidos, se realizaron pruebas de fugas y se evacuó el circuito con una bomba de vacío, un paso considerado crítico porque incluso una filtración mínima puede alterar el proceso de evaporación a baja presión.
Un controlador basado en Arduino supervisa las temperaturas y presiones del sistema, ajusta la velocidad de las bombas y activa alarmas de seguridad en caso de fallas. Esas bombas de circulación y los ventiladores de enfriamiento sí requieren electricidad: consumen entre 30 y 50 vatios en conjunto.
Un prototipo que aún no reemplaza la heladera convencional
Pese a que el fuego aporta la mayor parte de la energía térmica, el sistema no es completamente independiente de la red eléctrica. Un panel solar pequeño o una batería podrían cubrir esa demanda eléctrica modesta, según plantea el proyecto, mientras el calor del fuego continúa impulsando el ciclo de absorción.
Los primeros resultados, reportados por Hackaday, muestran que el sistema alcanzó los 5 °C (41 °F) con una temperatura ambiente cercana a los 16 °C (61 °F). Sin embargo, esa cifra no permite determinar aún cómo se comportaría el prototipo en climas más cálidos, cuánta capacidad de almacenamiento de alimentos tendría o si podría sostener de forma constante una temperatura segura de conservación.
La refrigeración por absorción no es una tecnología nueva: se utiliza desde hace décadas en entornos donde un compresor eléctrico convencional resulta poco práctico. Lo que aporta el proyecto de Greenhill Forge es una implementación casera con materiales accesibles y una fuente de calor tan simple como la leña.
Con mayor desarrollo, sistemas similares podrían encontrar aplicación en talleres remotos, cabañas u otros espacios donde conseguir combustible resulte más sencillo que acceder a un suministro eléctrico estable.

articles.title: ‘Quite the deal, especially when you consider all the features on hand’ — I tested Hisense’s mid-range mini-LED TV and was impressed by its quality HDR, decent sound and near-budget price
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Hisense U6SF Pro is a solid TV, especially for the price. It has just about all the features one could want, though Alexa+ is not hands-free. And it comes with a good but not great picture and decent audio that’s good enough to at least skip the soundbar.
Reasons to buy
- + Good picture quality for the price
- + Alexa+ a little more accurate than other AI voice assistants
- + Good sound quality with a few well implemented audio features
- + The price is right
Reasons to avoid
- - Quite a bit of vignetting
- - Not a lot of detail in shadows
- - No hands-free control
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Hisense U6SF Pro: One-minute review
The Hisense U6SF Pro felt like a budget TV reaching for the mid-range when I first unboxed it. After spending some time with it, I think that impression stands. I don’t mean that in a derogatory way, either. If you had $650 for a TV, getting the 65-inch size of the Hisense U6SF Pro is certainly worth it.
That price tag gets you a 4K resolution with a native 144Hz refresh rate, all the HDR and spatial audio support one could want, a Fire TV interface, and Alexa+ built-in. And just to clear the air, the Hisense U6SF Pro does have appreciable if somewhat hidden upgrades over the non-Pro version. The Pro version is a couple pounds heavier, comes with a built-in subwoofer (and has double the speaker wattage) and WiFi 6, and has the pro version of AMD FreeSync Premium and support for DTS Virtual:X.
The Hisense U6SF Pro has most of the bonafides of the best gaming TVs, such as two HDMI 2.1 ports for up to 4K@144Hz refresh rate passthrough support and the aforementioned AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, though I do wish there was a game-specific bar or menu. I can see an argument for putting this model among the best TVs for the price, though it still comes with some compromises, such as some vignetting all along the bottom of the screen and a lack of detail in the shadows.

The Hisense U6SF and U6SF Pro, along with the Hisense U7, hit the market in March of 2026. While the listed MSRP of the U6SF Pro is much higher on retail sites like Amazon and Best Buy, where the TV’s “value” at 65 inches is listed at $1,099.99, the actual and consistent prices listed above are what I consider the real prices and are what you’ll actually pay.
With a price range of $499.99 for the 55-inch to $2,299.99 for the 100-inch, the Hisense U6SF Pro really falls right into that area between budget TVs and more mid-range models (most TVs within a couple hundred dollars above or below a grand). And it comes in just about every size one could need, unless you’re looking for a smaller TV. The 55-inch model is the smallest it comes in.
