Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: Features
- Supports all the necessary HDR and spatial audio formats
- Alexa+ works well but isn’t hands-free
- Ambient mode includes options to load personal photos or AI art
Let’s get the basics in terms of features out of the way. The Hisense U6SF Pro supports the litany of HDR formats one would need including Dolby Vision IQ. It also comes with Dolby Atmos and DTS: Virtual X for anyone wanting or needing spatial audio support. And you can connect to the TV via Bluetooth (whether that’s playing music or connecting a device like a game controller), Apple AirPlay, and Smart Home integration.
Since the Hisense U6SF Pro is a Fire TV, it comes with Alexa+, Amazon’s AI-powered version of the company’s long-standing voice assistant. One of the places where this TV’s limitations are a little more obvious than slightly more expensive TVs like the Hisense U7 is the fact that, while there is an actual voice assistant on hand, I have to press the mic button on the remote to use it. In essence, there’s no hands-free control here.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As far as using Alexa+, it’s conversational and does one thing that I’ve had issues with on Google TVs and Google Gemini and that is actually play content directly from the home screen when asked instead of bringing me to an intermediary landing page. Sometimes, I don’t want more info. Sometimes, I just want to watch Psych.
Since it is 2026, AI is implemented throughout this TV and not just with Alexa+. For one, it comes with what Hisense calls “Hi-View AI Engine,” which from what I can tell is the same thing as Dolby Vision. Also worth noting that this TV is said to support Dolby Vision IQ but doesn’t have any Dolby-Vision-related settings in its menu (it only pops up as a picture mode when watching certain media), but it does have more generic sounding settings that do the same thing. I assume this is Hisense’s Hi-View AI Engine.
Also implemented on this TV is an AI-powered Ambient mode, a neat feature that I personally don’t get a lot out of, but you might. You can use premade art, create AI-generated art, or upload pictures using the Amazon Photos app.
- Features score: 4.5 / 5
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: picture quality
- Not a lot of detail in shadows
- Smooth action; little blooming
- Quite a bit of vignetting
The interesting thing about a TV like the Hisense U6SF Pro is that the picture quality is generally decent but looks a little two-dimensional compared to more expensive TVs. Whether I’m watching Coco, Top Gun: Maverick, or The Batman, the colors are vibrant enough — this TV has around 96% P3 color coverage — for me to feel like I’m seeing everything as intended. Of course, I have Filmmaker Mode and Imax Mode available along with Dolby Vision IQ.
And the action is smooth — something I noticed with my gaming tests as well. The Hisense U6SF Pro has a 144Hz refresh rate that applies to any content capable of taking advantage, including sources coming through the two 2.1 HDMI ports.
Considering that this TV has all the HDR formats one could need as well as a peak brightness of over 1200 nits (at 10% in Filmmaker Mode) in our benchmarks, I was surprised that the screen felt a little flat. That’s because I consider that flatness to be an issue with the contrast.
While a Hi-QLED mini-LED TV, the Hisense U6SF Pro doesn’t have as much separation of detail in shadows, something I noticed most sharply when gaming but I think contributed to the more two dimensional quality of the picture.
That said, the TV did a good job with blooming, as I didn’t notice any of that halo effect show up when watching a bright subject against a dark background.
The one other issue that I noticed with this TV is vignetting, not just in the corners as I’ve seen with TVs in this range, but along the bottom of the screen as well.
- Picture quality score: 4 / 5
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: sound quality
- Sounds good enough to skip a soundbar
- Soundstage is pretty narrow
- Dialog enhancer and night mode work well
The Hisense U6SF Pro’s sound quality is pretty good. With a 50 watt 2.1 built-in system, it should be good enough to skip a soundbar. And I think it is, within reason. I can hear dialog clearly with whatever I’m watching and there’s a bit of a sound stage where I can hear audio elements go from one side to the other, though it’s only as wide as the TV itself.
Since there’s a built-in sub, you do get some low-end information. For instance, one of the scenes I use to test is the Penguin chase scene in The Batman and explosions had a bit of that low-end rumble that you want when watching an action-packed movie.
I will say that the sound quality won’t reach home theater levels, however, so using a soundbar system with a subwoofer (and surrounds) will still sound better. The sound here, with its crisp highs and balanced mids, will do the job if you don’t want to also invest in a full system.
When deep diving into the settings, I noticed that Devialet has licensed its name to Hisense for this model so you can thank the company for the sound quality here. I also noticed that there’s some Atmos and surround sound virtualization, the latter of which completely removes any stereo separation when on.
There’s also a dialog enhancer that works as intended while not sounding too hinky (this feature can sometimes do that since it’s basically boosting the frequencies where voices typically sit). And there’s also a night mode that does a good job of compressing audio so that you can watch at night without loud sections of audio waking someone up. A five-band EQ is also available, as well as a handful of sound modes.
- Sound quality score: 4 / 5
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: Design
- Uses feet instead of stand but are width-adjustable
- Plenty of ports including two 2.1 HDMI
- Anti-glare screen
The Hisense U6SF Pro comes in the usual sizes one would expect from most models these days with its smallest size at 55 inches and its biggest at 100. There are also 65, 75, and 85 inch sizes available.
As far as stands go, the Hisense U6SF Pro has two feet on the outer ends of the TV instead of the center base. While this means that the TV isn’t height adjustable (some stands can be screwed in at different heights), there are a couple places to screw in the feet so that one can have the feet wider or narrower. This is helpful if you have a smaller entertainment console. Just be aware that this particular feature is not available on the 55-inch model.
The ports on the TV are more than enough for most people. There are the usual four HDMI ports — two 2.1 that support 4K@144Hz — a single LAN, two USB (one USB 3.0 and one USB 2.0), an optical port, and an RF Antenna port.
While I don’t want to talk too much about the screen here, Hisense does use an anti-glare screen that makes this TV a little easier to watch in a bright room. Also worth noting is that there’s a 2.1 50 watt built-in sound system with an included subwoofer.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: Smart TV & Menus
- Amazon-focused content and ads in interface
- Less free content than expected
- Some menu settings only accessible when playing content
Being a Fire TV, using the Hisense U6SF Pro is going to be a little Amazon-focused. The layout, which is composed of a banner of rotating content followed by rows of suggested content and apps, is littered with ads and content on Prime. Of course, this isn’t new nor is it unique. Whenever I review a Google TV, it’s the same except with Youtube-related suggestions instead of Prime.
The layout itself is one that I think has been broadly adopted because it’s intuitive and lets you navigate to content without having to open an app just to see what’s locked in there. Interestingly, maybe because Amazon wants everyone on Prime, there’s less free content here than I typically find included in an OS. Sure, there’s a Guide app that looks like an old school cable interface with plenty of free content, but that’s about it.
The OSD menu, integrated into the Fire TV OS, seems intuitive to use. However, certain settings, particularly for picture and sound settings, are not accessible through the settings menu in the interface. Instead, you have to press the settings button on the remote when some content is playing to get access to advanced settings. So, if I want to turn on “Intelligent Picture” or change to Filmmaker Mode or Imax Mode (both of which are available on this TV), I need something to be playing first.
- Smart TV & menus score: 4 / 5
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: Gaming
- Screen holds gaming back a little, especially with shadows
- No gaming-related menu settings or game bar
- Smooth action thanks to fast refresh rate and a few key features
There are only two things that really hold the Hisense U6SF Pro back as a gaming TV. The first are the limitations of the screen that I’ve covered above. For instance, because the Hisense U6SF Pro’s HDR support is good but not up to the standards of a mid-range $1,000+ TV (let alone a flagship TV), there’s less differentiation in shadows so games that are overall just darker or have a lot of shadow are harder to make out what’s happening. On top of that, the colors aren’t quite as vibrant as they are on something like the Hisense U7 that I keep comparing this TV to.
That said, without being able to A/B the way I am, the colors probably won’t bother you, as they still look good. You might have to compensate in the settings for the shadows, however.
The other is the fact that, outside of a Game Picture Mode, there aren’t any gaming specific menus. There certainly isn’t a gaming bar. I would appreciate being able to make more specific adjustments based on the type of game or to bring up an FPS counter.
That said, I do appreciate that AMD FreeSync Premium Pro is on offer (non-Pro version for the 100-inch) that uses a variable refresh rate along with an auto low-latency mode. I also appreciate the Motion Rate 480 feature, which gives a virtual representation (though not a true one) of having a 480 Hz refresh rate. The end result is smooth action no matter the game.
- Gaming score: 4 / 5
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: Value
- Occupies that mid-range performance at budget price point
- Strong value but can find slightly better TVs for slightly more
- The competition has at best similar value
When I think of the Hisense U6SF Pro, I think of a few other specific TVs. The Hisense U7 is a natural comparison since they came out at the same time and is the next step up. Interestingly each TV has a slightly different issue. Whereas the U6SF Pro has more vignetting and a flatter picture, the U7 has some color bleed. But the Hisense U7 is a slightly better TV at just $150 more at the 65-inch size and the 75-inch model has even been cheaper in the past. While this is a rarity, the U7 is generally worth the higher price.
I also think of the TCL QM6K, which came out in 2025 and only got a mild refresh in 2026. It occupies a similar mid-range at almost budget price space, especially since its prices have come down since first reviewed last year. Originally, a 65-inch size would have cost $999.99, but it now goes for $649.99 just like the U6SF Pro. And it’s basically the same or similar prices at the various other sizes as well. That’s for a TV with a slightly better picture quality and slightly worse audio and brightness.
- Value score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV?
| Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Features | This TV has all the features you could want from HDR and spatial audio support to the inclusion of Alexa+, though you can’t use that last one hands-free. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Picture quality | There could be a little more detail in the shadows and there’s more vignetting than I would like, but the picture quality is very good for the price. | 4 / 5 | 
| Sound quality | You can skip the soundbar with this TV as its 2.1 system has enough detail and low-end rumble for casual use. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design | The port selection is good including two 2.1 HDMI ports and the screen is anti-glare. While the TV uses feet instead of a stand, they are width-adjustable. | 4 / 5 | 
| Smart TV and menus | I don’t like how some of the settings are separated. It makes adjusting the screen a bit counter intuitive. But the OS is generally easy to use. | 4 / 5 | 
| Gaming | The Hisense U6SF Pro comes with some nifty features like AMD Freesync Premium Pro for smooth action, but there’s no game-specific menu and no game bar. | 4 / 5 | 
| Value | The price for what you get the Hisense U6SF Pro for is quite the deal, especially when you consider all the features on hand. | 4.5 / 5 | 
Buy it if...
You want mid-range quality at budget prices
With all the features and good quality picture and sound, this TV almost reaches the heights of mid-range TVs at a lower price point.
You don’t want to buy a soundbar
It won’t be home theater level, but for casual use, the 2.1 Devialet-branded system sounds good enough that you won’t feel compelled to buy an external soundbar.
You’re in the Alexa Smart Home ecosystem
Being a Fire TV, it comes with Alexa+ so you can ask it all sorts of questions, not just to play content. And being a Fire TV, you can integrate it into an Alexa-based smart home.
Don't buy it if…
You want hands-free control
There’s something to being able to just talk to your TV, and, unfortunately, that’s just not a feature on this TV. For some, it’s not a big deal. For others, it might be as vital as any of the accessibility ones that usually come stock in a smart TV.
You can stretch your budget a few extra hundred dollars
The Hisense U6SF Pro is a good TV for the price and comes at a good price. But for just a few hundred dollars more, there are slightly better TVs, including ones from Hisense.
Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV review: Also consider
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Hisense U6SF Pro | TCL QM6K | Hisense U7 | Roku Pro Series (2025) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price (65-inch) | $649.99 | $649.99 | $999.99 | $899.99 | 
| Screen type | Hi-QLED Mini-LED | Mini-LED | Mini-LED Pro | QLED | 
| Refresh rate | 144Hz | 144Hz | 165Hz | 120Hz | 
| HDR support | Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10, HDR10+, HDR10+ Adaptive, HLG | Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG | HDR10, HDR10+, HDR10+ Adaptive, HLG, Dolby Vision | Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+ Adaptive, HLG | 
| Smart TV | Fire TV with Alexa+ | Google TV | Google TV | Roku | 
| HDMI ports | 4 (2x HDMI 2.1) | 4 (2x HDMI 2.1) | 4 HDMI 2.1 | 4 (2x HDMI 2.1) | 
TCL QM6K
The TCL QM6K is just as good value if you’re looking for a mid-range TV for almost budget prices. It has a relatively great picture quality with vibrant colors, and good contrast, but suffers a little bit in the audio department and comes with lower brightness. Read our full TCL QM6K review.
Hisense U7
While the audio on the Hisense U7 has a little less low end and the picture has some color bleed, this TV outperforms its price by a wide margin making it an even better deal than the Hisense U6SF Pro here. However, it is at a slightly higher price point. Read our full Hisense U7 review.
Roku Pro Series (2025)
The Roku Pro Series (2025) is a little more expensive, but comes with a lot of the same features, has a similarly fast refresh rate for gamers (though no game bar), and has a unique shadowbox design that makes it sit flush on the wall when mounted, making it the better TV for that situation. Read our full Roku Pro Series (2025) review.
How I tested the Hisense U6SF Pro Series MiniLED TV
- I used the TV for a couple weeks
- Tested with both TV, movies, music, and games
I used the Hisense U6SF Pro MiniLED TV regularly for a couple weeks. I tested it using streaming shows, movies, music, and games (via PS5). I went through the various features, particularly Alexa+. I also spent time listening to the audio as well as paying attention to the picture quality.
After spending some time with this TV, it’s my humble opinion that this TV is ideal for those who are looking for a mid-range TV but wanting to pay closer to budget prices.
I’ve tested a lot of tech gear over the years from laptops to keyboards and speakers, and so have been able to use my expertise towards giving an honest and fair opinion, not to mention a critical eye, to any product I test.

articles.title: Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 se faufile partout pour faire le ménage : pour moins de 550€ vous êtes tranquille
articles.text:
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un aspirateur robot laveur qui s'occupe de vos sols pour vous laisser du temps libre, que vous pouvez avoir contre 549,99 euros au lieu de 889,99 euros jusqu'au 25 octobre 2026.
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un aspirateur robot laveur plutôt classé dans le haut de gamme, qui s'occupe donc de la poussière mais aussi des tâches, avec ses serpillères. Il est livré avec une station multifonction qui est plutôt massive, ce n'est pas un modèle discret, mais ça permet d'automatiser son entretien, ne vous laissant que le strict minimum à faire. Vous lui déléguez l'entretien des sols, comme ça vous avez du temps libre pour faire autre chose, et en plus vous le payez moins cher avec la réduction actuelle sur Amazon puisqu'il perd 38% de sa valeur.
Voici le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 à 549,99 € au lieu de 889,99 € sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 ?
- Pour sa finesse extrême avec son LiDAR rétractable qui réduit sa hauteur globale à 7,98 cm, ce qui lui permet de se glisser sous les meubles, canapés et lits inaccessibles aux autres modèles.
- Sa grande capacité d'aspiration de 25 000 avec un bras mécanique FlexiArm qui garantit des sols durs impeccables et des angles parfaitement dépoussiérés.
Un nettoyage automatisé pour les grands espaces
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un aspirateur robot laveur comme on peut en trouver beaucoup sur le marché, qui se démarque par sa puissance d'aspiration brute de 25 000 Pa. Elle est couplée au système intelligent DirTect qui détecte optiquement le niveau de saleté au sol pour adapter instantanément l'intensité des passages. Le fait qu'il puisse soulever ses patins de 12 mm sur les moquettes ou relever l'intégralité de sa brosse principale sur une trace de liquide fait qu'il passe facilement d'une surface à l'autre chez vous. C'est un appareil fait pour les habitations de grande surface ou si vous possédez des animaux, puisqu'il a une brosse faite pour ça. Il peut enchaîner 160m² de nettoyage et ne pas être gêné grâce à sa brosse DuoDivide.
Face au Qrevo Curv 2 Pro, un choix de raison
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est plus fin que la concurrence, et son rapport qualité/prix avec la promotion du moment fait qu'il est vraiment intéressant. Mais il montre sa limite technique sur le franchissement des seuils : il ne peut pas grimper plus de 2,5 cm. Là où le Qrevo Curv 2 Pro peut allègrement grimper des obstacles de 4 cm d'épaisseur. Un de ses compromis majeurs qui le rend moins adapté aux logements anciens qui ont d'importantes barres de seuil surélevées entre chaque pièce.
✅ Les points forts
- Son format fin de 7,98 cm pour passer sous les meubles bas
- Le bras FlexiArm pour le nettoyage des angles et le suivi des plinthes
- La puissance d'aspiration de 25 000 Pa avec la brosse anti enchevêtrement DuoDivide
- La station multifonction autonomie avec lavage, séchage et vidange automatisés
- La gestion des poils d'animaux et des tapis avec le relèvement de 12 mm des patins
❌ Les limites
- Le franchissement des seuils limité à 2,5 cm
- La détection d'obstacles par IA perfectible sur les petits objets du quotidien
- La station d'accueil est assez volumineuse
- L'absence de réservoir interne dédié au détergent
Jusqu'au 25 octobre 2026, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est à 549,99 € au lieu de 889,99 €
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un appareil qui permet d'automatiser le ménage chez vous, avec des caractéristiques premium et une traque de la saleté le long des murs pour un tarif bien maîtrisé, surtout avec la promo chez Amazon. Il s'adresse directement à celles et ceux qui veulent un appareil qui passe tout seul. Vous le programmez pour qu'il passe plusieurs fois par semaine ou vous le faites intervenir sur une tâche qui vient de se faire et vous allez gagner un temps fou.
Par contre si votre logement est très compartimenté, avec des seuils de portes qui sont haut, il faudra passer sur un modèle à châssis élévateur sinon vous n'arrêterez pas d'avoir des messages d'erreur. Et un petit conseil avant de craquer : pensez à lui réserver une belle place chez vous, car pour pouvoir stocker sa station de charge, il faut anticiper ce besoin précis.

articles.title: Xbox Helix Console Reportedly Headed for Holiday 2028 at $1,200 to $1,800
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Xbox Helix Console Reportedly Headed for Holiday 2028 at $1,200 to $1,800
Microsoft's next-gen Xbox console could cost a lot more than anyone hoped. A new Fortune profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says the Project Helix console has internally been projected to cost consumers between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft decides to subsidize it. For reference, the current Xbox Series X with a disc drive sells for $799.99, and that is after the recent price hikes. The report also says Sharma plans to release a next-gen handheld by the 2027 holiday season, followed by the console in time for the 2028 holidays. Apparently, Helix engineering deadlines have been moved up by at least several months, according to people familiar with the matter, which is putting extra pressure on development teams.
The handheld has also caused some friction inside Microsoft. Windows leaders reportedly wanted it to run a trimmed-down version of Windows Home, while Sharma's team wanted its own software for better gaming performance. It got heated enough that a senior Xbox executive reportedly threatened to scrap the handheld rather than ship the Windows build, though Xbox now seems to be steering the OS. Sharma, for her part, says the teams still work together, noting, "We can't build Helix on our own." Microsoft hasn't confirmed any pricing, and a subsidy could bring the final number down a bit. However, Fortune puts Xbox's profit margin at around 3%, which probably doesn't leave much room for one. Elsewhere, memory makers expect supply to get even tighter in 2027 and 2028, while rival Sony also struggles with rising costs, so a cheap next-gen console looks unlikely from either side.
Source:
				Fortune			
	
	
	
		
	
		
12 Comments on Xbox Helix Console Reportedly Headed for Holiday 2028 at $1,200 to $1,800
Having it with a Windows base OS tells me two things:
- They're not expecting Xbox as an exclusive platform to last.
- Microsoft is sort of okay that this hardware runs whatever OS so as long as Game Pass is compatible.
Xbox is failing as it is, a console over $1,200 would be a failure even if MS made a pro-consumer decision like letting users have a OS that isn't locked down to gamepass games.

articles.title: Investigadores hallaron más de 6.800 chats privados de la IA Muse de Meta expuestos en internet
articles.text:
Claroc, una firma de ciberseguridad encontró más de 6.800 conversaciones que usuarios compartieron con Muse, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, accesibles para cualquiera en internet sin que nadie les hubiera enviado el enlace.
La empresa, especializada en ciberseguridad, llegó a esas conversaciones mediante una búsqueda de DNS pasivo, una técnica que registra los nombres de dominio que ya circularon en internet. Abrió solo algunos cientos de los enlaces hallados y dejó el resto sin revisar.
El problema nace del propio diseño de Muse. Cuando un usuario pide compartir una charla con el asistente, Meta genera una página pública y arma la dirección web con el título que el usuario le puso a esa conversación. Ese nombre queda registrado en los servidores de DNS, visibles para cualquiera que sepa buscarlos.
Eso significa que no hace falta recibir el enlace para entrar a la página: alcanza con rastrear los nombres de dominio del servicio, algo que Claroc hizo con una sola consulta a una base de datos comercial. El sitio urlscan.io, que cualquiera puede usar, ya guardaba más de 75 capturas de esas páginas.
Qué se encontró en los datos de Muse
Entre los enlaces revisados, Claroc halló un documento con los apuntes de una persona que se preparaba para una entrevista confidencial con un laboratorio de inteligencia artificial, con el nombre del contacto interno y el horario exacto de la reunión.
Asimismo, encontró la revisión interna de ingresos de una empresa de marketing, dirigida a su director ejecutivo; una solicitud de préstamo con el monto pedido por su dueño; una lista de tareas con una alerta de fraude bancario y un número de cuenta parcial; y un informe de un inversor inmobiliario con direcciones de propiedades y cifras de rentabilidad.
Claroc también accedió al calendario anual de vacaciones de una empresa, con el nombre de cada empleado junto a la semana en la que estaría ausente. La firma aclaró que no identificó a ninguna de las personas ni empresas afectadas en su publicación.
No se trató de un ataque informático clásico. Muse respetó exactamente lo que cada usuario le pidió: compartir esa conversación puntual. El fallo está en que la dirección de esa página terminó siendo pública y fácil de reconstruir a partir de su propio título.
Claroc recordó un problema similar ocurrido en 2025, cuando conversaciones compartidas de ChatGPT aparecieron en los resultados de Google y OpenAI tuvo que retirar la opción que las hacía indexables. Después, Google ya había indexado más de 370 mil conversaciones de Grok, el chatbot de xAI.
Meta no respondió a los reclamos
La firma de seguridad informó el hallazgo al programa de recompensas por errores de Meta el 8 de octubre de 2026 y, según contó su cofundador y director de tecnología, Asaf Aproszper, no recibió ninguna respuesta de la empresa. Meta tampoco contestó las preguntas que le envió Ars Technica por correo electrónico.
Claroc dijo no tener pruebas de que alguien haya usado esa información de forma maliciosa, aunque aclaró que solo monitoreó un canal de búsqueda entre varios posibles.
El último día que revisó el sistema, aparecieron 27 páginas nuevas generadas por usuarios que seguían compartiendo conversaciones.
Muse se lanzó el 8 de septiembre de 2026 y rápidamente se ubicó entre las aplicaciones más descargadas de la tienda de Apple. El asistente puede completar formularios, hacer compras y gestionar cuentas de correo y calendario en nombre de sus usuarios.
La filtración se suma a una serie de tropiezos de seguridad que atravesó Muse desde su lanzamiento. A fines de septiembre del mismo año, un investigador descubrió una falla que permitía a cualquier aplicación instalada en la computadora tomar el control total de una cuenta de Muse, algo que Meta corrigió horas después de conocerse el caso.
Semanas más tarde, la revista Time reveló que Muse arma perfiles detallados sobre los contactos de cada usuario a partir de sus mensajes y correos, y un usuario denunció públicamente que el asistente compartió su dirección particular con un desconocido durante una venta en Facebook Marketplace.

articles.title: DeepSeek AI tools banned from US government agency systems as rift with China grows
articles.text:
DeepSeek AI tools banned from US government agency systems as rift with China grows
Federal civilian agencies are no longer allowed to use DeepSeek and must remove it from their tech stack
- US civilian agencies have been ordered to stop using DeepSeek and remove it from government systems
- DHS cited data security, user tracking, and potential national security risks tied to the AI model
- The move expands broader US restrictions on Chinese technology across government infrastructure
The Donald Trump administration has banned Chinese Artificial Intelligence model DeepSeek from all civilian government agencies and ordered them to stop using it and remove it from its tech stack immediately.
Earlier this week, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) issued a new notice, notifying government agencies of the change:
“The Department of Homeland Security is publishing notice of the Secretary of Homeland Security’s issuance of an order (1) excluding information technology products and services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd (DeepSeek), to include affiliated entities as defined in applicable regulations, from federal civilian agency procurements; and, (2) removing all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.”
Multiple threat vectors
Apparently, this is not the first time the Trump administration made moves against Chinese AI tech. According to CNBC, the order was originally issued in late July this year, and applies to federal civilian agencies including the Treasury, State and Justice departments, but excluding the Department of Defense. The publication also said the US Congress restricted the use of DeepSeek in intelligence community systems late last year, and even earlier - in March - the US Commerce Department told its staff not to use DeepSeek. The Defense Information Systems Agency banned it in January 2025.
In the latest DHS order, it was said that DeepSeek’s models “present multiple threat vectors”. To use the tool, users need to provide all sorts of data - from personally identifiable information (PII) to other business or proprietary information, which the company can use to “track and digitally fingerprint users”. Furthermore, China’s laws allow the government to easily access and collect the data created and stored by private companies, meaning information on US citizens can easily fall into the government’s hands. That, in turn, “could produce actionable intelligence on US persons and/or government programs,” the DHS explains.
“The models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities,” it stressed. “Indeed, open-source security research has found that the DeepSeek iOS mobile application contains multiple critical vulnerabilities.”
When asked for a comment, China’s foreign ministry told the Reuters news agency it would safeguard the rights of its companies: “China consistently opposes the over-generalization of national security as well as the politicization of science, technology and trade issues,” Mao Ning, a ministry spokesperson, told the agency.

China trade war
US President Donald Trump has openly talked against using Chinese technology and has banned multiple companies and solutions already. In his first term, he blacklisted hundreds of Chinese companies and affiliates, including telecommunications giants Huawei and ZTE, semiconductor manufacturer SMIC, drone maker DJI, and surveillance technology firms Hikvision and Dahua Technology. ZTE almost went bankrupt over it, and Huawei ended up building its own mobile phone operating system, Harmony OS, after losing access to Google and Android. At the time, the US was upgrading its mobile network to 5G, something Chinese companies were interested in working on. However, Trump argued that the Chinese government could force these companies into installing backdoors, which could allow China to eavesdrop on US communications.
In August 2026, during his second term, Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency and banned all foreign bulk-power systems from being imported, installed, or used in the country. He also said the government would analyze existing systems to isolate and remove any foreign-built hardware or software. The same ban was issued during his first term but was revoked by the Biden administration.
Later this month, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will vote to prevent all Chinese labs from testing hardware used in the US, Reuters reported. Last year, four in five (82%) of all US electronics were tested in China.

articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro et Pro Max : les prix fuitent et rendent l'iPhone 18 Pro Max finalement pas si cher
articles.text:
Attention au portefeuille, ça risque de piquer. Les Xiaomi 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max devraient être annoncés prochainement en Europe. Leur prix de départ pourrait titiller celui des modèles d'Apple, quitte à le dépasser.
Xiaomi a présenté ses smartphones 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max en Chine le mois dernier, deux smartphones qui se distinguent notamment par leur autonomie, en plus de leur écran dorsal. Alors que leur lancement international se fait toujours attendre, des informations récemment divulguées apportent des précisions sur leurs caractéristiques, mais aussi sur le prix en Europe.
Des batteries revues à la baisse par rapport à la version chinoise
Des fiches publiées sur le registre européen EPREL (European Product Registry for Energy Labeling) révèlent les capacités des batteries prévues pour les versions européennes de ces deux appareils. Le Xiaomi 18 Pro serait ainsi équipé d'une batterie de 6 000 mAh, tandis que le 18 Pro Max disposerait d'une batterie d'une capacité de 7 050 mAh.
Ces capacités restent inférieures à celles annoncées pour les modèles commercialisés en Chine. Elles restent toutefois convenables pour des smartphones haut de gamme.
- Design toujours réussi
- Un objectif principal très lumineux
- Les performances dingo
D'après ces mêmes fiches, le Xiaomi 18 Pro pourrait offrir une autonomie allant jusqu'à 66 heures et 30 minutes, contre 70 heures et 40 minutes pour le Pro Max. Ces chiffres correspondent à des estimations issues de tests standardisés. Les deux smartphones seraient par ailleurs dotés de batteries garanties pour conserver 80 % de leur capacité d'origine après 1 000 cycles de charge.
Un tarif en Europe très élevé ?
C'est sur le plan tarifaire que ces informations suscitent des interrogations. Toujours selon le rapport cité, le Xiaomi 18 Pro pourrait être proposé à partir de 1 449 euros pour la version 256 Go, et à 1 649 euros pour la version 512 Go. Le Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, dans sa configuration 512 Go, serait quant à lui annoncé à 1 849 euros.
À titre de comparaison, le prix d'un iPhone 18 Pro en version 256 Go est de 1 479 euros, soit trente euros de plus. Idem pour le tarif d'un iPhone 18 Pro Max en version 512 Go, dont le tarif devrait être attendu à 1 879 euros. Cependant, Xiaomi ne semblerait pas proposer de version 256 Go de son 18 Pro Max.
Ainsi, l'appareil le moins cher de la gamme, 1 849 euros dépasserait le tarif de départ de 1 629 euros demandé pour un iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Une proposition qui devra convaincre
L'autonomie élevée promise par ces deux modèles pourrait séduire les utilisateurs cherchant à limiter la fréquence de charge de leur smartphone. Cependant, le positionnement tarifaire du modèle Pro, proche de celui du Xiaomi 17 Ultra, pourrait inciter les acheteurs à patienter davantage.
Ces prix européens restent pour l'instant non confirmés par Xiaomi. S'ils venaient à se vérifier, la marque devrait démontrer que ses nouveaux modèles haut de gamme justifient ce positionnement tarifaire. En effet, les alternatives à des prix inférieurs ne manquent pas.
Contrairement à la marque à la pomme, Xiaomi est cependant adepte des promotions de lancement, pouvant parfois atteindre plusieurs centaines d'euros. Si les tarifs indiqués sont avérés, il y a donc fort à parier que l'appareil devrait coûter moins cher à son lancement, à grands coups d'offres promotionnelles.
Source : AndroidAuthority

articles.title: Mozilla y Google bloquearon ocho certificados digitales que podían falsificar cualquier sitio web
articles.text:
Mozilla y Google bloquearon ocho certificados digitales de la empresa india eMudhra después de que un investigador anónimo, identificado solo como Wayne, demostró que podía falsificar la identidad de cualquier sitio de internet.
Los certificados digitales son las credenciales que permiten a un navegador confirmar que una página es quien dice ser y cifrar el tráfico mediante el protocolo HTTPS. Quien controla la clave privada de uno de esos certificados puede hacerse pasar por cualquier sitio web.
Seis de los ocho certificados comprometidos se usan para asegurar conexiones web y los otros dos para firmar programas de software. Todos están respaldados por los programas de confianza de Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple y Google, de los que dependen la mayoría de los navegadores y sistemas operativos del mundo.
El problema no estuvo en el cifrado sino en cómo eMudhra generó las claves. Una clave de ese tipo debería tener alrededor de 384 bits de aleatoriedad, miles de billones de combinaciones posibles. Las ocho claves filtradas tenían apenas entre tres y ocho bits, lo que las hacía recuperables en segundos.
Un ingeniero de Mozilla recuperó las ocho claves por su cuenta en menos de dos horas, sin conocer el método del primer reportante, y confirmó así que la falla era real. Otros investigadores le pidieron a asistentes de inteligencia artificial que resolvieran el problema como si fuera un desafío de seguridad informática, y lo lograron en el primer intento.
Un error que recuerda al desastre de Heartbleed
Filippo Valsorda, ingeniero de criptografía y uno de los mantenedores del lenguaje de programación Go, le dijo a Ars Technica que la limpieza sería “más grande que Heartbleed”, la falla de 2014 que tardó años en repararse por completo.
Según explicó, el problema ahora se repetirá en dispositivos de internet de las cosas, contenedores de software y computadoras con Linux que nadie actualiza, sistemas mucho más difíciles de alcanzar que un navegador.
El riesgo mayor es para quienes usan redes privadas virtuales, conocidas como VPN, y para las personas que viven bajo gobiernos dispuestos a interceptar el tráfico de internet. Aplicaciones como Signal y WhatsApp no dependen de estos certificados para proteger sus mensajes, por lo que no están expuestas.
Los usuarios no pueden revisar por sí mismos si sus programas ya bloquearon los certificados comprometidos, porque esa protección depende de que cada fabricante distribuya su propia actualización. Mantener el navegador y el sistema operativo al día es, por ahora, la única medida al alcance de la mayoría de las personas.
Hasta el momento no hay evidencia en los registros públicos de transparencia de certificados de que alguien haya emitido certificados falsos con las claves filtradas, según un aviso que Mozilla envió a otros fabricantes de navegadores y sistemas operativos. El mismo aviso advirtió que el abuso de esas claves es probable en el corto plazo.
Una limpieza que involucra a toda la industria del software
La reparación definitiva depende de actualizar decenas de sistemas distintos, desde distribuciones de Linux como Ubuntu y Debian hasta lenguajes de programación como Python, Rust y Go, además de navegadores, sistemas operativos móviles y programas como Electron. Cada uno debe eliminar o marcar como no confiables los certificados afectados.
Ante la posibilidad de que varias personas hubieran recuperado las mismas claves y difundido la información en público, Mozilla decidió ir un paso más allá: retiró por completo la confianza en uno de los certificados raíz de eMudhra, llamado emSign ECC Root CA - G3, en lugar de bloquear solo los certificados intermedios comprometidos.
eMudhra es una autoridad certificadora con sede en India, habilitada para emitir credenciales de seguridad aceptadas por los principales navegadores del mundo. Las ocho claves comprometidas formaban parte de un lote de 24 certificados intermedios generados en abril de 2025.
Mozilla le pidió a eMudhra que deje de emitir certificados desde cualquier cadena vinculada a esa raíz y que ayude a migrar a sus clientes hacia alternativas. La actualización de paquetes para sistemas como Debian y Node.js todavía seguía pendiente al cierre de esta nota.
.

articles.title: GTA 6 Digital Pre-Orders Climb to 6.45 Million, PlayStation Holds 74% Share
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
GTA 6 Digital Pre-Orders Climb to 6.45 Million, PlayStation Holds 74% Share
GTA 6 has now racked up an estimated 6.45 million digital pre-orders worldwide, worth roughly $630 million net of returns, according to the latest weekly update from Sensor Tower's sales tracker. PlayStation accounts for 74% of the total, or about 4.80 million copies and $468 million, while Xbox sits at 1.66 million copies and $162 million. The tracker's October 13 figures had GTA 6 at 6.08 million pre-orders and $594 million, so around 370,000 more people locked in their copy in about a week. In the US, Sensor Tower says GTA 6's digital pre-orders are 148% ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2022) at the same point before launch, the best performer among the big releases it tracked over the past six years.
Of course, these are third-party estimates covering digital copies only, and Take-Two hasn't confirmed any figures. CEO Strauss Zelnick did say in August that pre-orders were skewing toward the $100 Ultimate Edition, and Sensor Tower now says the vast majority of buyers went for that version. PlayStation has led since tracking began in June, and in late August Sensor Tower had it at about 77% of 4.86 million pre-orders. The firm tweaked its estimation model on October 5, however, so those older numbers aren't a perfect like-for-like comparison. Xbox's smaller share probably isn't helped by US Xbox hardware sales sitting at an all-time low this year. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, so expect these numbers to keep climbing.

articles.title: Russia drafted plans for AI that could block 95% of VPNs — but the idea has quietly vanished from its national roadmap
articles.text:
Russia drafted plans for AI that could block 95% of VPNs — but the idea has quietly vanished from its national roadmap
The machine-learning filter it would have relied on is funded separately
- A draft of Russia's national AI plan proposed using AI to analyze 70% of blocked VPN services and lift blocking effectiveness to 95%
- The Digital Development Ministry says the measure is absent from the current draft, but Roskomnadzor's separately budgeted and arguably crucial ML filtering project remains
- The 95% is an effectiveness target, not accuracy, and sources expect AI to raise false positives, with corporate VPN, cloud and voice traffic most exposed
Russia's Digital Development Ministry considered using artificial intelligence to push the effectiveness of its VPN blocking to 95%, according to a front-page report in Kommersant.
The measure appeared in a draft of the country's national plan for implementing AI through 2030; the ministry now says it is not in the current version.
This isn't the first time such a move has been reported, but some earlier coverage might have been overzealous, to say the least, when it reported that "Russia Eyes AI-Powered VPN Crackdown With 95% Blocking Accuracy." The problem with that headline is that not only was that proposal dropped, but the 95% accuracy figure was never actually in play.
A draft that proposed AI use
None of the above reporting should reassure an estimated 57 million Russians who rely on circumvention tools.
Roskomnadzor (the Federal agency tasked with "Supervision of Communications, Information Technology and Mass Media") has its own machine-learning filtering project budgeted outside the national AI plan, and the money for Russia's blocking infrastructure is set to double next year.
Kommersant, which reviewed the draft, reports that the ministry wanted AI to analyze the characteristics of 70% of all the VPN services Russia blocks. The drafters reckoned that would lift blocking effectiveness to 95%.
Asked about it, the ministry said the current draft of the plan "contains no such information," in Meduza's translation. A source familiar with the discussions told Kommersant that agencies had pitched a range of measures for the plan, some of which may never be implemented, and that the traffic-analysis algorithms already in service are a form of intelligent analysis but do not count as AI.
An AI layer would behave fundamentally differently; rather than matching known signatures, models would weigh packet sizes and timing, session length, and the balance of inbound to outbound traffic, then flag likely VPN servers from indirect clues: how a node behaves, which host it sits on, and what its neighboring IP addresses look like. The payoff is speed, catching new servers before they reach any blocklist.
Kommersant uses the word effectiveness, and the distinction matters: a blocking-effectiveness figure describes how much targeted traffic it stops. It says nothing about how much legitimate traffic gets stopped with it, and that is what the catch is; the solution proposed does not account for any mistakes, just how effective it would be at its job of blocking out VPN traffic.
The 95% target is also less of a leap than some headlines suggest, because Russia already has 92% on paper, at least by its own estimates. A Roskomnadzor subsidy decision for its Main Radio Frequency Center (GRChTs), dated January 2025 and surfaced in May 2026 by journalist Maria Kolomychenko, sets an "average level of effectiveness" of 92% for restricting VPNs via signatures by the end of 2030. Verstka reports that the AI proposal was meant to lift that same indicator to 95%.
The more consequential point is that striking a line from a draft strategy does not strike the capability. Forbes Russia reported in January 2026 that Roskomnadzor planned to spend 2.27 billion rubles (around $29 million) in 2026 on a machine-learning-based traffic-filtering mechanism, a project we flagged when Windscribe saw a roughly 90% drop in its Russian traffic that same month.
The false-positive risk is not hypothetical in Russia, because the government has already learned how hard it is to separate good VPNs from bad ones. When the ministry ordered major platforms in April to block users with VPNs switched on, its guidance promised a whitelist for corporate VPNs.
Telegram founder Pavel Durov claimed the crackdown had "triggered a massive banking failure," and outage-tracking data showed bank disruptions on April 3 2026. A source told RBC at the time that no reliable technical method existed to tell permitted corporate VPN traffic from the rest.
For now the picture on the ground is unchanged: blocking is intensifying with or without an AI mandate. At least 10 VPN providers reported tighter restrictions in the week after September's State Duma elections, and VPN Guild chairman Alexey Kozlyuk described it to Meduza as "a continuation and gradual intensification" of a campaign that began in August.
The Kommersant report also landed a day after RBC revealed a draft ministry order requiring phones on Russia's 5G networks to support the FSB-developed Kuznyechik cipher from March 1, 2032.
Providers keep adapting. "In Russia, VPNs face pressure almost every month; it is a new norm," an Amnezia VPN spokeswoman told TechRadar Pro. But Sarkis Darbinyan of RKS Global and the VPN Guild warned TechRadar that for users, the end result is "an ever-shrinking number of services that actually work."
The 95% target may be gone from one document. The infrastructure, the money, and the intent behind it are not.

articles.title: Pillages du 17 octobre : les iPhone et autres smartphones Samsung déjà en train d'être bloqués
articles.text:
Des pilleurs du 17 octobre ont cru pouvoir faire un bon bénéfice avec leurs vols de matériels électroniques. Mais les blocages de ces appareils ont déjà commencé !
Aujourd'hui, les grandes enseignes et plateformes s'organisent pour faire en sorte que les pillages consécutifs aux manifestations du 17 octobre rapportent le moins possible aux délinquants. On a ainsi Leboncoin, Vinted et eBay qui mettent en place une stratégie pour contrer ces reventes. Et du côté des géants comme Apple, on se met à bloquer en masse les appareils volés.
Des iPhone volés le week-end dernier déjà bloqués (avec un petit message menaçant au passage)
Parmi les magasins qui ont été pillés le week-end dernier, on retrouve des Apple Store, comme celui de Lille. Mais les iPhone qui ont été dérobés au passage ne feront pas la fortune des voleurs, comme vous pouvez le voir sur la petite vidéo ci-dessous.
Apple a pu en effet commencer à bloquer les iPhone dérobés, et serait même en train de géolocaliser les appareils. C'est ce qui permet à la marque américaine de pouvoir gentiment intimer l'ordre à l'individu tenant le téléphone volé de rapidement le rapporter là où il devrait être. « Cela vaut aussi pour Samsung, les Google Pixel, ou encore des appareils Xiaomi et Honor » indique une source anonyme de BFM Tech.
Apple a un système particulièrement robuste pour contrer les pillages
Cette action est possible grâce au numéro IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) qui, associé au numéro de série du produit, est envoyé au fabricant, qui peut alors bloquer l'appareil quand il se connecte à internet. Il est par ailleurs ajouté sur une liste noire nationale et internationale, avec, derrière, une plainte qui suite. La justice peut alors exiger une géolocalisation de l'appareil.
À noter que même si le blocage empêche l'appareil de se connecter à un réseau mobile, il peut toujours passer par le Wifi… sauf chez des marques comme Apple. La firme de Cupertino a en effet développé une stratégie anti-pillage au fil des années. Les appareil mis en vitrine sont dans ce cadre dotés d'un système d'exploitation différent, rendant impossible de changer le mot de passe ou d'ajouter un compte iCloud. Une fois connectés au Wifi, il se verrouille, et devient inutilisable. Samsung dispose d'un système similaire avec sa suite Know Mobile Enrollment, capable de verrouiller à distance un modèle d'exposition. De quoi limiter les dégâts ?
Source : L'Indépendant, BFM Tech

articles.title: Atlético Nacional vs, Cúcuta por Roja Directa y Tarjeta Roja: opciones que debes evitar
articles.text:
El encuentro de este 20 de octubre entre Cúcuta Deportivo y Atlético Nacional por la Liga BetPlay concentra una alta atención mediática, impulsada por el regreso de James Rodríguez a su ciudad natal para disputar este compromiso. Ante la expectativa por sintonizar el partido, un sector de la audiencia recurre a motores de búsqueda para acceder a plataformas de transmisión no autorizadas, como Roja Directa o Tarjeta Roja.
Sin embargo, la utilización de estos portales gratuitos expone a los espectadores a riesgos informáticos críticos que comprometen la integridad de sus dispositivos y datos personales.
Interfaz engañosa, ingeniería social y descargas silenciosas
El modelo de rentabilidad de los sitios de piratería deportiva se basa en la publicidad maliciosa (malvertising) y la ingeniería social. La vulnerabilidad principal para el usuario radica en el diseño de la interfaz del reproductor de video. Estas páginas superponen capas invisibles sobre los botones legítimos, un método conocido como clickjacking. Al intentar pausar la imagen, activar el sonido o cerrar un anuncio superpuesto para ver el partido de Atlético Nacional, el usuario desencadena secuencias de comandos no autorizadas.
Además, estas plataformas despliegan alertas falsas que exigen la actualización de componentes del sistema —como reproductores de video inexistentes o códecs de audio— para permitir la visualización del contenido.
Aceptar estas solicitudes o interactuar con la interfaz alterada ejecuta descargas en segundo plano. Esto facilita la infiltración de software espía (spyware), secuestradores de navegador (browser hijackers) y troyanos que logran eludir las advertencias de seguridad, modificando la configuración del equipo para inyectar publicidad de forma permanente incluso cuando el portal deportivo ya ha sido cerrado.
Secuestro de recursos (cryptojacking) y degradación del hardware
Más allá de los virus tradicionales que requieren una instalación manual, plataformas como Tarjeta Roja integran a menudo secuencias de código JavaScript diseñadas para la minería de criptomonedas directamente desde el navegador (cryptojacking).
Mientras el usuario visualiza el encuentro en Cúcuta, la página web secuestra la capacidad de procesamiento de su dispositivo para resolver algoritmos matemáticos complejos a favor de los administradores del sitio, sin necesidad de que el espectador descargue ningún archivo.
Durante los más de noventa minutos que dura la transmisión, el procesador (CPU) y la tarjeta gráfica (GPU) son forzados a operar a su máxima capacidad. El usuario puede identificar este ataque mediante síntomas físicos y técnicos: los ventiladores del equipo giran a máxima velocidad para disipar el calor excesivo, el sistema operativo presenta lentitud extrema y las baterías se agotan rápidamente.
Esta exigencia térmica ininterrumpida provoca un estrés estructural que degrada irreversiblemente la vida útil de los componentes de hardware, especialmente en computadoras portátiles y teléfonos móviles.
Exposición de credenciales, robo de sesión y fraude financiero
La infección inicial mediante descargas ocultas suele tener como objetivo final la sustracción de información confidencial de alto valor. El código malicioso inyectado desde estas plataformas de streaming está diseñado para implementar registradores de pulsaciones (keyloggers) que capturan cada tecla presionada por la víctima. A esto se suman los ataques de secuestro del portapapeles, los cuales monitorean y copian automáticamente contraseñas o direcciones de billeteras de criptomonedas cuando el usuario utiliza la función de “copiar y pegar”.
Adicionalmente, los troyanos bancarios distribuidos por estas vías ejecutan ataques de superposición de pantallas (overlay attacks) en dispositivos móviles o extraen las cookies de sesión almacenadas en el navegador del ordenador.
A través de estas técnicas avanzadas, los atacantes logran evadir los sistemas de autenticación en dos pasos (2FA) y capturan credenciales de acceso a correos electrónicos, redes corporativas y aplicaciones financieras. En consecuencia, el supuesto ahorro al evitar el pago de una suscripción oficial se traduce en un alto riesgo de sufrir fraudes económicos directos y suplantación de identidad.

Points faibles

- S Pen sans Bluetooth.
Le Galaxy S24 Ultra avait rempli tous les critères attendus d'un smartphone très haut de gamme, et Samsung fait aussi bien, sinon mieux, avec son Galaxy S25 Ultra. Le terminal est une réussite incontestable sur le plan technique et se paie le luxe de gagner en puissance comme en endurance, tout en conservant son talon d'Achille (minime, il faut bien le dire), à savoir sa charge pas vraiment rapide. Son seul véritable problème n'en est un que pour les plus férus de téléphonie : si l'on excepte son volet logiciel dopé à l'IA, il n'apporte pas de véritable nouveauté à son prédécesseur. Il se frotte dès lors à la même difficulté que ses concurrents ; alors que la téléphonie a atteint un plateau technique, comment se démarquer, si ce n'est par des fonctionnalités logicielles ? Pour résumer, il manque peut-être au Galaxy S25 Ultra ce que l'on pourrait qualifier de petit supplément d'âme pour non seulement convaincre (ce qu'il fait sans peine), mais aussi séduire. Mais tout cela n'est que chipotage, puisqu'à notre sens, c'est l'efficacité qui prime.

articles.title: Xbox Is Asking Inactive Owners to Sell Their Consoles to Best Buy
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Xbox Is Asking Inactive Owners to Sell Their Consoles to Best Buy
Microsoft is reportedly emailing Xbox Series X|S owners who haven't touched their consoles in a while, nudging them to trade those consoles in at Best Buy. The email, first shared by Nintendeal on X, opens with "Haven't played on your console in a while?" and tells owners who have moved to other platforms that they can get "up to $375 back." Per Gizmodo, Xbox has confirmed the email is genuine. That $375 applies to a Series X in good condition with its cables and controller, while a Series S apparently tops out at $200. Payment comes as a Best Buy eGift Card, and the campaign seems limited to the US for now.
It looks like this is the trade-in program Microsoft promised in June, when it announced another round of price hikes and said traded-in consoles would be resold at lower prices. Those hikes pushed the 1 TB Series X with a disc drive to $799.99, and the 512 GB Series S to $499.99. Unsurprisingly, Circana data later showed US Xbox hardware sales hit an all-time low through August. Stock is the other problem, as new units are reportedly scarce in mainland Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and South America, while GTA 6's November launch is expected to drain shelves even further. Owners thinking about trading in should note that used Series X consoles have recently sold for over $500 on eBay, so Best Buy's offer is more about convenience than value.
Sources:

articles.title: Just Eat's AI food photos are a disaster — but why are we letting AI invent pictures of things we're paying for?
articles.text:
Just Eat's AI put bacon and eggs in a glass of cola — and it's exposed a much bigger problem with AI
Mmm tasty!
Just Eat has apologized after its new AI service designed to auto-generate images of food items got confused and put an image of bacon and eggs swimming in a glass of cola on the menu for a Northern Ireland restaurant. The restaurant, which offers a range of soda breads, ended up with sausages, bacon and fried eggs floating in pints of fizzy drinks instead of the Irish breakfast sandwiches they were supposed to represent.
These AI-generated images were part of a Just Eat trial for a new AI-powered system. The bacon and egg cola wasn’t the only hilarious image that the trial produced. You can see many other examples on the uknewestfoods Instagram page:
Referring to the AI photos, one Just Eat user on X said, “I swear if my salt and pepper chips come like this I’m going to cause murder”
But while these AI-generated disasters are easy to laugh at, the real problem might be the images that look perfectly believable.
It's the realistic images you need to worry about
Talking to The Independent, a Just Eat spokesperson said, “We've been trialling AI-enhanced images and as with any new technology, it isn't always quite right the first time. We're sorry for any inaccurate images that have been posted. We're in the process of removing them and have paused rolling this out while we further develop the tool to ensure it best serves our partners and customers."
Just Eat isn’t the only food delivery service trialling AI-generated images. Last week DoorDash opened its text-to-order AI agent for testing: you text what you want, it picks the dish and texts back a photo of it. Bloomberg News testers found several errors during testing, including “photos that didn’t match the recommendation”.
The wider question is, why are Just Eat and DoorDash trialling using AI to generate images of food that people are ordering anyway? While obvious mistakes like this are easy to spot, what about the smaller inaccuracies that are easily missed, like a wrong-sized dish or missing topping?
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Michael Bortinger, Director of Marketing and Partnerships at Tastewise, explains: "An image model has no concept of a specific dish. It renders the average of everything labeled 'burger', and better tools just make that average more convincing. There are pages of brand rules for how a logo sits on a cup and nothing at all for what's in the burger."
Is this a good use of AI?
I can understand why using AI could save the time required to take and then upload individual photos of each menu item; however, food images would seem to be a case where accuracy of what you’re ordering is of supreme importance. Outsourcing this job to AI is not only fraught with problems, but surely wouldn't produce a faithful representation of the food anyway.
There are many good uses for AI; I’m just not sure this is ever going to be one of them. AI-generated food photos might make life easier for delivery platforms and restaurants, but it's hard to see what benefit they offer customers if they can't be trusted to show what's actually being sold.
After all, when I’m ordering a bacon sandwich, I want to see a picture of the item I’m actually going to get, not AI’s interpretation of what a bacon sandwich looks like.

Graham is the Senior Editor for AI at TechRadar. With over 25 years of experience in both online and print journalism, Graham has worked for various market-leading tech brands including Computeractive, PC Pro, iMore, MacFormat, Mac|Life, Maximum PC, and more. He specializes in reporting on everything to do with AI and has appeared on BBC TV shows like BBC One Breakfast and on Radio 4 commenting on the latest trends in tech. Graham has an honors degree in Computer Science and spends his spare time podcasting and blogging.

articles.title: Trop petit le HomeView ? Apple préparerait une seconde version avec un écran plus grand
articles.text:
Avec son nouvel écran connecté, Apple répond enfin à une demande grandissante des utilisateurs. Cependant, sa taille compacte suffit-elle à convaincre les adeptes de la marque à la pomme ? Un modèle plus grand serait déjà en préparation.
La semaine dernière, Apple a lancé le HomeView, son premier écran domestique intelligent fixé à une enceinte. Ce produit vise clairement à concurrencer l'Echo Show d'Amazon et le Nest Hub de Google. Avec cet appareil, Apple répond à une nécessité de présence sur ce segment de marché, refusant de le laisser entièrement à ses concurrents. Cependant, cet écran connecté n'est pas parfait, il semble comporter certaines limites que la marque à la pomme souhaiterait dépasser, avec une nouvelle version.
Un écran plus grand monté sur bras robotisé ?
Cette prochaine version, qui pourrait être commercialisée sous le nom de HomeView Ultra, Max ou 360, serait dotée d'un écran de 9 pouces fixé à un bras robotisé, répondant ainsi au problème d'absence de pivotement du modèle actuel.
Mark Gurman, analyste chez Bloomberg et source de cette information, précise que le HomeView actuel serait en réalité un produit relativement ancien, resté stocké en entrepôt pendant près d'un an, le temps que le logiciel soit mis à niveau. Cette information expliquerait les larges bordures de l'écran, ainsi que l'utilisation d'une puce A18 associée à 8 Go de RAM, des caractéristiques techniques déjà dépassées au moment du lancement.
Le lancement du produit aurait été reporté à plusieurs reprises : initialement prévu pour le printemps 2025, il aurait ensuite été repoussé à l'été, puis à l'automne, avant d'être de nouveau fixé au printemps de cette année, et ainsi de suite.
Un plus grand modèle envisagé pour 2027 ou 2028
Quant au futur modèle à écran de 9 pouces, désigné en interne sous le nom de code J595, sa sortie serait actuellement envisagée pour 2027 ou 2028, toujours selon Mark Gurman. Cet appareil serait capable d'identifier la personne qui s'adresse à lui, l'écran suivant alors les mouvements de l'utilisateur grâce à son bras motorisé.
Ce nouveau modèle devrait logiquement être proposé à un tarif supérieur à celui du HomeView actuel, sans estimation toutefois disponible à l'heure où nous écrivons ces mots.
Source : GSMArena

articles.title: PS5 Firmware 14.10 Reportedly Jailbroken in Private, Hypervisor Still Holding Up
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
PS5 Firmware 14.10 Reportedly Jailbroken in Private, Hypervisor Still Holding Up
PS5 homebrew developer Gezine has shown a working exploit on firmware 14.10, the latest PlayStation 5 software, just a month before GTA 6 launches. In a short video posted on X with the caption "Hello 14.10," Gezine opens the console's debug settings, and apparently it gets past the protections Sony added with the 14.10 update on October 1. The jailbreak is private for now, and there's no word on whether Gezine plans to release it. The timing is what makes this interesting. Sony's 14.00 update in mid-September disrupted the Relapse exploit that had been working on firmware 13.60, and 14.10 followed with more security fixes. Players are also reporting that Sony now requires 14.10 to sign in to PSN. 
On top of that, datamining account PlayStation Game Size found that GTA 6 needs firmware 14.10 to run, though neither Rockstar nor Sony has confirmed this. However, this doesn't mean pirated copies of GTA 6 are around the corner. The hypervisor bypass that the scene uses to dump and run game backups doesn't work on 14.10 yet, and Gezine reportedly said a separate hypervisor exploit may be needed. Until then, backups, and by extension apps like Overdrive that allegedly hand out free games and DLC, seemingly aren't an option on the latest firmware. Some people in the community have asked Gezine to hold off on a release until after GTA 6 launches, since going public now would likely prompt Sony to patch it.
Sources:
				Gezine on X, 				PlayStation Game Size on X, 				via Notebookcheck

articles.title: Nokia 1100 y Tamagotchi, los dos dispositivos preferidos de los 90’s: cuánto valen hoy
articles.text:
El mercado de la tecnología retro experimenta una demanda constante impulsada tanto por el coleccionismo como por la búsqueda de una desconexión digital funcional. Dos de los dispositivos más representativos de esta tendencia son el Tamagotchi (icono definitivo de la década de 1990) y el Nokia 1100 (lanzado a principios de los años 2000, pero consolidado como el estándar de resistencia para la generación noventera).
A diferencia de otros aparatos de su época que hoy son obsoletos, ambos equipos mantienen un valor comercial específico en 2026.
El Tamagotchi: producción activa y precios estandarizados
Mientras la mayoría de los juguetes electrónicos de hace tres décadas solo se consiguen de segunda mano, la mascota virtual de Bandai mantiene una línea de producción ininterrumpida. La compañía comercializa el “Original Tamagotchi”, conservando la programación original (Generación 1 y 2), la pantalla monocromática y los componentes de hardware clásicos.
En Estados Unidos, el precio oficial y general de estos modelos es de $19.99 dólares. Esta tarifa estándar aplica para la mayoría de los diseños distribuidos en grandes cadenas minoristas como Walmart y Amazon. Dependiendo de la disponibilidad de inventario o si se trata de carcasas con diseños de edición especial, el valor en estas plataformas puede presentar variaciones menores, situándose entre los $19.99 y los $22.97 dólares.
Por otro lado, Bandai también comercializa reediciones de modelos más avanzados que incorporan conectividad infrarroja y mayor complejidad en el ciclo de vida de la mascota. Las versiones como Tamagotchi Connection o Tamagotchi Paradise registran precios que oscilan entre los $32.99 y $44.97 dólares, dependiendo del canal de distribución.
Nokia 1100: el mercado de segunda mano y el estado de conservación
A diferencia del Tamagotchi, el Nokia 1100 dejó de fabricarse oficialmente en 2010. Con 250 millones de unidades vendidas, sigue siendo el teléfono celular más distribuido de la historia. Hoy, la adquisición de este dispositivo depende exclusivamente de plataformas de subastas o mercados digitales de segunda mano, siendo eBay uno de los canales principales para su comercio a nivel internacional.
El valor actual de un Nokia 1100 no está estandarizado y fluctúa significativamente en función de su estado de conservación. Las unidades usadas que presentan desgaste visible en la carcasa antideslizante, marcas en la pantalla y que no incluyen accesorios originales, suelen comercializarse por debajo de los 50 dólares. Estos dispositivos generalmente son adquiridos por usuarios que buscan un teléfono secundario de máxima resistencia y autonomía de batería para realizar llamadas básicas o mensajes de texto.
El impacto del coleccionismo en el valor del teléfono
El precio se incrementa drásticamente cuando el equipo ingresa en la categoría de colección. Un Nokia 1100 que conserva su caja original, el cargador de fábrica y los manuales impresos puede superar los 100 dólares en sitios de subastas. Los modelos sellados de fábrica, los más demandados en el mercado retro, alcanzan importes aún más elevados, sujetos directamente a la competencia de pujas entre coleccionistas.
Quienes adquieren este equipo en la actualidad deben considerar un factor técnico fundamental antes de la compra: el dispositivo opera en bandas de telefonía de generaciones anteriores (2G). Su utilidad como herramienta de comunicación depende enteramente de que los operadores de telecomunicaciones locales mantengan activa la infraestructura de redes compatible con este estándar, un aspecto que varía según el país o la región de uso.
Para aquellos usuarios que buscan la fiabilidad del clásico teclado físico y la resistencia extrema, pero con componentes de hardware actualizados, la marca ha mantenido vivo el legado de este icónico modelo a través de reediciones modernas como el Nokia 300 Charge en septiembre de 2026: un dispositivo sin conexión a internet ni redes sociales, pero equipado con una batería que promete hasta 40 días de autonomía en modo de espera, linterna integrada y el diseño robusto que definió a la telefonía móvil de la década de los noventa.

articles.title: AI infrastructure management software startup ASI hits $3B valuation after raising $325M in funding - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI infrastructure management software startup ASI hits $3B valuation after raising $325M in funding
An artificial intelligence startup called ASI Inc., which builds complex models of air traffic and energy grids, said today it has scored $325 million in a Series C funding, bringing its valuation to a cool $3 billion.
The round was led by Spark Capital and joined by participants including Citadel Securities, Craft Ventures, Meritech Capital, Energy Impact Partners and Andreessen Horowitz.
The startup, which used to be known as Air Space Intelligence, is an AI company that develops frontier models designed to model physical reality and simulate future scenarios, so that its customers can plan and orchestrate how they operate critical infrastructure in real time.
It caters to companies in the aviation, defense and energy industries. For instance, it works with the Federal Aviation Administration and airlines such as United Airlines Inc. and Delta Air Lines Inc. to simulate and predict what’s happening in air space, so they can plan their flight operations. It gives pilots and air traffic controllers a way to plan ahead, reduce delays and increase flight safety and efficiency.
In addition, ASI works with the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force and others, providing them with AI-driven command-and-control software that’s used to manage their daily operations. It also helps companies in the energy sector, including grid operators, enabling them to simulate their grid operations and plan for surges in demand.
ASI founder and Chief Executive Phillip Buckendorf (pictured) said he believes that future economic growth will be dependent on giving the people who run the country’s most critical infrastructure the ability to predict and forecast scenarios ahead of time, so they can avoid failures. “While the broader tech ecosystem spent hundreds of billions teaching AI to manipulate words and generate text, ASI is deeply focused on AI systems that can manage and control physical assets,” he stressed. “This capital ensures ASI scales as America’s engine: the automated nervous system keeping the country running.”
While hundreds of billions have been spent teaching AI to manipulate words and generate videos, ASI builds AI systems that can manage and control critical physical infrastructure – where there is zero margin for error.
Today we announced our $325M Series C to scale America’s… pic.twitter.com/l133h8H92E
— ASI (@AirSpaceIntel) October 20, 2026
The round follows a significant customer win for ASI. In June, it signed an $875 million multiyear agreement with the FAA to manage future air traffic across the U.S. with its AI platform. Impressively, it won the 12-year contract ahead of bigger and better known rivals such as Palantir Technologies Inc. and Thales SE, which both made aggressive bids, according to Bloomberg.
In air traffic scenarios, ASI’s system combines data from flight paths, real-time air traffic, weather and controller staffing to predict congestion and devise ways to get around problems and avoid delays. The FAA implemented the software at Dulles International Airport in Washington DC last month, and plans to expand it to all major U.S. airports in future.
The contract was a significant win for ASI, making the startup one of only four technology companies to land a federal contract of that size since 2000. Since then, ASI has secured another big contract with the U.S. Army. Earlier this month, it announced it had agreed a five-year deal worth $99 million to supply the military with AI software for its command-and-control program. Another big customer is National Grid USA Service Company Inc., which uses ASI’s software for planning purposes.
Going forward, ASI said the money from today’s round will help it expand further into the aviation, defense and energy sectors and also target new industries such as logistics. It’s also planning to grow its research and engineering teams with an eye to expanding the capabilities of its software.
