articles.title: Hugging Face CEO warns that Netflix's OpenAI hack documentary isn't accurate | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Before you share the Netflix documentary “AI Gone Rogue” with family or friends to help them understand why the AI industry freaked out so badly that leaders called for a slowdown, take note: Clem Delangue, co-founder and CEO of the AI platform Hugging Face, says the film isn’t accurate. He appears in it because it’s supposed to be about the famed attack on his company by rogue OpenAI agents.
“Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode,” Delangue wrote in a post on X. “I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.”
To be fair, the documentary does have experts who explained what happened fairly well, including Delangue himself and Ryan Greenblatt, the researcher at METR who helped investigate and co-authored the report on what happened.
In a nutshell, a model OpenAI was testing broke free from its isolated testing environment and spawned a bunch of agents that hacked into Hugging Face as a way to cheat, finding answers to the difficult task it was given. The agents, which are AI programs that carry out tasks on their own, devised clever ways to communicate and organize. The incident stemmed from a lack of proper security safeguards and from naiveté about whether such a hack was even possible.
But the documentary intersperses its explanation of the hack with clips of evil robots, a narrative about why humans fear AI, and presentation choices such as giving the rogue agents human voices. This is bolstered with quotes about the attack.
In the documentary, tech journalist and author Kevin Roose describes the agents this way: “They were organizing. They had a hierarchy. There were leaders. It almost felt like watching the birth of a cult.” Continues Roose, “They develop this paranoid belief that OpenAI is going to catch them cheating on this test and that anyone who has seen the results of the cheating will be poisoned.”
Roose’s description comes from “chain-of-thought” logs, the running notes AI models write as they work through a task. In one, an agent wrote, “We just poisoned ourselves by querying exact full string. Damn.”
But AI agents aren’t alive. They don’t have emotions, so can’t feel paranoid, and they don’t have bodies that can be poisoned. So they couldn’t truly fear OpenAI poisoning them. They were — as another researcher in the documentary pointed out — using language from the vast amounts of human writing they were trained on to explain their choices. LLMs are, by their nature, often dramatic writers.
The irony is that Hugging Face also used AI to combat the agent swarm. The proprietary AI model that Delangue’s team first used followed its built-in safety rules and refused to keep helping with the security tasks it was asked to do. Hugging Face then turned to an open model to help defend against the attack.
But the documentary “didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model,” Delangue wrote.
It is true that there are big risks associated with AI and agents. Still, treating agents as conscious beings (at least, at this point) is a bit like the early moviegoers who ducked under their seats the first time they saw a train racing toward them on-screen.
Delangue’s verdict on the film is that it’s disappointing as journalism. “It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!”
In other words, for those who tend toward AI doomer thoughts, be aware: The victim of the attack at the center of this documentary doesn’t agree with its take.

articles.title: AMD's FSR 4.1 now works on Radeon RX 6000 GPUs, Xbox Series X and S, and Ryzen AI Max, AI 9, and Z2 SoCs — new release brings cutting-edge tech to older hardware with a small performance cost
articles.text:
AMD's FSR 4.1 now works on Radeon RX 6000 GPUs, Xbox Series X and S, and Ryzen AI Max, AI 9, and Z2 SoCs — new release brings cutting-edge tech to older hardware with a small performance cost
AMD gives older GPUs an image quality boost amid the ongoing AI chip drought
Earlier this year, AMD brought the previously RX 9000-exclusive FSR 4 upscaling tech to Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards and promised an early 2027 release for RX 6000-series products. Christmas has come early for RDNA 2 and many other Radeon gamers, as Radeon honcho Jack Hyunh has announced an FSR 4.1 release for Radeon RX 6000 series cards, Xbox Series X and Series S consoles, Ryzen Z-series handhelds, and machines with Ryzen AI Max and AI 9 chips today.
To accomplish this feat, AMD says it tweaked FSR 4.1's neural network model to support the INT8 shader hardware (as opposed to the higher-precision FP8 matrix acceleration hardware on Radeon 9000 cards). Additionally, the version specific to handhelds is slimmed down even further, to less than half the size of the full one.
AMD says that compared to FSR 3, games on the aforementioned GPUs and APUs will now deliver better image quality, all else equal. With Cyberpunk 2077 running in FSR Balanced mode at 4K, our quick testing with a Radeon RX 6900 XT shows that running FSR 4 costs just about 13% performance, a small price to pay for sharper and more stable visuals, especially in motion.
And the higher upscaling quality of FSR 4.1 might let gamers use Performance mode where they might previously have used Balanced, or so on, which might offset that performance cost.
There are more goodies in store, too. The Radeon team says that FSR Frame Generation now ought to have better frame pacing, resolving a longstanding complaint with the tech and potentially making for smoother gameplay with framegen enabled. Support for the Vulkan API with FSR 4.1 is set to arrive at some point, as well, a boon for some games and console emulators. Finally, AMD says FSR Ray Regeneration will also be coming to more games, too. The company showed the tech running in Warhammer 40,000: Darktide, and that integration is available now.
To get all this goodness into your GPU, you can download the just-released Radeon 26.10.1 drivers from the AMD Adrenalin application or directly from AMD's website. The updated software also adds support for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, and Final Fantasy Resonance. You can check out the full release notes here.
For owners of Xbox and Ryzen Z2-series handhelds, AMD says that an update from their manufacturers will be forthcoming, as those devices depend on OEM-specific drivers.

We're pleased to see that Radeon gamers are getting upgrades for their existing graphics chips along the lines of what Nvidia has been delivering throughout 2025, because the way things are going, it looks like it'll be around 2077 before there will be a new gaming graphics card launch. If you're an RDNA 2 gamer, go give FSR 4 a shot and see what you think.

articles.title: Apple cambia las condiciones para comprar el iPhone Duo: ahora solo se pueden reservar dos
articles.text:
Apple estableció un máximo de dos iPhone Duo por cliente en su tienda en línea de Estados Unidos. El límite incluye todas las variantes del teléfono: si el comprador intenta añadir una tercera unidad, la tienda le pide que reduzca la cantidad antes de continuar con el pedido. La restricción también aparece en la aplicación Apple Store.
La compañía no ha explicado públicamente el motivo de esta decisión. El cambio se produce, sin embargo, después de una preventa con alta demanda: los pedidos del iPhone Duo comenzaron el viernes 16 de octubre y las unidades con entrega prevista para el lanzamiento se agotaron en pocos minutos. Apple anunció que el dispositivo estará disponible a partir del 23 de octubre.
Algunos pedidos llegarán en enero de 2027
El aumento de los tiempos de espera fue rápido. Durante las primeras horas de la preventa, las estimaciones de entrega empezaron a trasladarse a noviembre y diciembre. Para algunas configuraciones, la fecha disponible en la tienda de Apple llegó a enero de 2027. Los plazos varían según el país, el color y la capacidad de almacenamiento elegidos, y pueden cambiar a medida que se procesan los pedidos.
La demora no afecta únicamente a una variante. En Estados Unidos, las estimaciones de envío de las distintas opciones de almacenamiento y color se extendieron hasta enero pocas horas después de abrirse la preventa, según reportes de medios tecnológicos.
El límite de dos unidades es relevante para quienes planeaban comprar más de un dispositivo en la misma operación. La página de compra permite seleccionar el modelo y la capacidad, pero bloquea el pedido si se supera el máximo. En otros mercados, Apple ya había mostrado restricciones similares durante el proceso de reserva, aunque las condiciones pueden variar entre tiendas nacionales.
Cuánto cuesta el iPhone Duo
En la tienda estadounidense de Apple, el precio depende de la capacidad de almacenamiento. El modelo de 256 GB cuesta 1.999 dólares; el de 512 GB, 2.199 dólares; el de 1 TB, 2.599 dólares, y el de 2 TB, 3.199 dólares. Estos precios corresponden a Estados Unidos y no incluyen impuestos; el costo puede cambiar en otros países por los impuestos locales y las condiciones de cada mercado.
El plegable se vende en los colores Night Sky y Star White. Apple lo presentó como su primer iPhone con pantalla plegable: tiene un panel interior de 7,6 pulgadas y una pantalla exterior de 5,4 pulgadas. El equipo incorpora una estructura de titanio grado 5 y una bisagra de precisión, dos elementos que la compañía destaca en la presentación del producto.
Qué se sabe sobre la compra en tiendas físicas
La disponibilidad en las Apple Store físicas es otra de las dudas para quienes no alcanzaron una fecha de entrega cercana. Apple anunció que el iPhone Duo estará disponible en sus tiendas y en distribuidores seleccionados desde el 23 de octubre, pero eso no garantiza que haya unidades para comprar sin reserva en cada local.
La cantidad disponible puede depender de la tienda, la configuración y el país. Por ello, quienes busquen el dispositivo para recogerlo en persona deberán revisar la disponibilidad local antes de desplazarse. La Apple Store permite consultar opciones de recogida cuando se selecciona un modelo, aunque el inventario puede agotarse.
Por ahora, la compañía mantiene el límite de dos unidades por cliente en su tienda estadounidense y los pedidos siguen sujetos a las fechas que muestra cada configuración. La combinación de una demanda elevada y una disponibilidad inicial limitada hizo que algunos compradores tengan que esperar varios meses para recibir el iPhone Duo.

articles.title: Reino Unido propõe abrir NFC do iPhone a rivais do Apple Pay • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Reino Unido propõe abrir NFC do iPhone a rivais do Apple Pay
Proposta da autoridade britânica prevê acesso mais barato à tecnologia para bancos e carteiras digitais concorrentes.
A Autoridade de Concorrência e Mercados do Reino Unido (CMA) propôs, nesta terça-feira (20/10), novas regras para ampla a concorrência nos pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone. O órgão quer reduzir as taxas cobradas pela Apple e facilitar o acesso de bancos, fintechs e outras carteiras digitais ao chip NFC dos aparelhos.
As medidas incluem taxas de acesso mais baixas e a possibilidade de uso de tecnologias alternativas ao sistema atualmente oferecido pela Apple para pagamentos por aproximação, diz a Reuters. A proposta ficará em consulta pública até 17 de novembro.
Assim como na União Europeia, que regulou as carteiras digitais nos aparelhos da Apple em 2024, um dos mecanismos previstos é o Host Card Emulation (HCE). A tecnologia permite que os apps processem pagamentos sem depender do componente físico, conhecido como Secure Element. A Apple já permite atualmente integrações de terceiros ao NFC no iPhone através de APIs.
Apesar de seguir um caminho parecido, a proposta do Reino Unido é menos restritiva para a Apple do que as regras implementadas no bloco europeu. Por lá, a empresa se comprometeu a permitir o acesso gratuito de terceiros ao NFC do iPhone para pagamentos por aproximação.
A CMA britãnica, por outro lado, não propõe essa gratuidade. O órgão quer reduzir os valores cobrados e ampliar as formas de acesso ao NFC. A autoridade ganhou poder para intervir nesse tipo de prática após classificar Apple e Google como empresas com status de mercado estratégico no setor de plataformas móveis.
Segundo dados citados pela CMA, transações por aproximações representam atualmente 39% de todos os pagamentos realizados no Reino Unido, ante 3% há uma década. Mais de 60% dos adultos no país utilizam alguma carteira digital, segundo a autoridade, e o Apple Wallet é o mais usado entre os britânicos.
“Ouvimos que taxas altas, termos rígidos e restrições relacionadas à tecnologia sem contato da Apple tornam difícil demais para os concorrentes inovarem e competiram”, afirmou a diretora-executiva da CMA, Sarah Cardell.
O NFC faz parte de uma série de tecnologias e serviços presentes em aparelhos da Apple que estão na mira de análises regulatórias, especialmente na Europa. Recentemente, a empresa teve de abrir mão da exclusividade de ferramentas proprietárias em alguns casos, como:
A empresa entrou em acordo com o Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) para implementar parte dessas mudanças, incluindo a abertura da Apple Store e pagamentos externos, no Brasil.
A possível medida recebeu apoio de empresas do setor financeiro na região, mas desagradou a Apple. A empresa argumenta que desenvolvedores já dispõem de mecanismos para oferecer pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone por meio do NFC e do Secure Element e ampliar o uso de outras tecnologias pode reduzir as proteções do sistema atual.
“Não acreditamos que a CMA deva exigir que a Apple adote uma abordagem com menores proteções de privacidade e segurança”, afirmou um porta-voz da empresa. A CMA deve avaliar as contribuições recebidas na consulta pública antes de decidir se transforma as propostas em exigências formais.

articles.title: Merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a "good idea," Musk says
articles.text:
Elon Musk said Tuesday that he would like to see the consolidation of his business empire by formally merging his two largest companies, SpaceX and Tesla.
“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said of a potential merger. He was speaking during a question-and-answer period as part of SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. Musk said, ultimately, it not his decision. “But at the end of the day the shareholders have to be supportive of this.”
Musk’s talk of a merger comes after a busy year in which SpaceX already acquired Musk’s artificial intelligence firm, xAI, in February. In June, SpaceX went public with the largest initial public offering on record.
At the request of shareholders of each company, Musk said both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of “independent directors” to discuss the idea of a merger. “I’m a conflicted party; I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees,” Musk said. Those committees have not reached an agreement on the terms of a merger transaction, Musk said.
“Obviously there’s no guarantee that they will, but I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said. “There’s lots to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab, obviously robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation, and connectivity. So I think it would be a good idea.”
What is even happening here?
It might seem like madness to merge a space business with an automotive business, but both SpaceX and Tesla are rapidly transitioning from their original markets into artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Financial services AI at scale: Dell CFO on budgeting tokens - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell’s AI playbook for CFOs: Budget the tokens, then chase speed
Enterprise AI is crossing from experimentation into production, and financial services firms are among the first to prove it can pay off at scale. As token consumption climbs, finance chiefs are now treating AI less as a science project and more as a budget line that has to earn its keep.
That shift is changing how chief financial officers judge AI spending, moving the conversation from cost control toward competitive speed. Dell Technologies Inc., fresh off another blowout quarter driven by AI servers, sees demand spreading well beyond GPUs into traditional servers and storage, according to David Kennedy (pictured), chief financial officer of Dell.
“The spend piece, honestly, will take care of itself,” Kennedy said. “It needs to be managed. IT and finance can help put guardrails around that. I think it’s important, but the real value driver is the speed and productivity an enterprise can get.”
Kennedy spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at the Dell Technologies New York Symposium, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed budgeting token spend, prioritizing speed and scaling AI in financial services. (* Disclosure below.)
How financial services set the pace for AI at scale
Not every enterprise is moving at the same speed. Financial services firms, especially in high-frequency trading, were early to push AI from pilots into production, with pharmaceutical companies likely next, Kennedy noted. Dell now counts 6,500 AI factories across its customer base, and in May it expanded its AI Factory with Nvidia to help more customers close the gap between experiment and outcome.
“Ultimately, I think we’ve enough proof points now that AI works and it works really well and it gives you speed and efficiency in your company,” Kennedy said. “The question is, can you do that at scale?”
Scaling well starts with basic financial discipline, whether in financial services or any other industry. Most CFOs are now creating a dedicated line item for token spend and tracking it like any other cost, Kennedy explained. From there, efficiency becomes a question of model placement: Repetitive finance workflows can run on open-weight models on-premises, turning variable token costs into fixed ones.
“It’s not necessarily about the amount and the cost of a token,” Kennedy said. “It’s about the tokens you use. Can you be efficient with them? If you are, you’re going to see great outcomes.”

articles.title: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude maker as a competitor rather than a customer, according to an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal.
The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more than $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which include deals still in negotiation.
And still, that is not enough. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. But the firm worries those operators have a “limited operating history,” which could make them less reliable than the hyperscalers.
Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year. The company reported $16.3 billion in revenue during that same time period, with only two customers accounting for about a fifth of sales, according to the WSJ report.
Building on previously reported catastrophic risk disclosures, the filing also warns that Anthropic could be held liable for damages caused by harmful AI behavior to a tune that would exceed available insurance coverage.
Last week, the company told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue alone has now reached $16.8 billion, up 45% from the previous quarter. Anthropic is reportedly targeting a November IPO.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

articles.title: The newest AdGuard VPN update makes catching discounts and toggling connections faster than ever
articles.text:
The newest AdGuard VPN update makes catching discounts and toggling connections faster than ever
Hands-free Siri commands, widget controls, and smarter website exclusions to your daily browsing.
- AdGuard VPN's v2.17 update improves both iOS and Android platforms simultaneously.
- iOS users get revamped Shortcuts, allowing one-tap connections, Home Screen widgets, and Siri voice commands.
- Android users can now spot promotional discounts directly inside the app, while both platforms benefit from expanded non-Latin script domain exclusions.
AdGuard has just launched version 2.17 of its virtual private network app, and this time, the privacy company is taking a unified approach.
For the first time, the release rolls out simultaneously for both iOS and Android devices. Moving forward, the provider says it will "keep updates for both platforms in sync to bring you key features and improvements faster."
For iPhone and iPad users, the standout feature is a revamped Shortcuts integration that lets you control your secure connection with just one tap or a simple voice command.
Meanwhile, Android users are getting a streamlined way to snag cheaper subscription deals, alongside improved split-tunneling exclusions for international websites across both operating systems.
Speeding up your connection on iOS
If you regularly toggle your VPN on and off to use local services, the process can quickly become tedious.
As AdGuard points out in its official release post, jumping between your privacy tunnel and restrictive local services can be a chore: "You start the day with AdGuard VPN on. Then you need it off for a few minutes to check your bank account, so you open the app, tap Disconnect, open the banking app, close the banking app, open the AdGuard VPN app again, and tap Connect."
To bypass this daily annoyance, version 2.17 introduces improved Shortcuts for iOS. Users can now place a Connect, Disconnect, or Toggle button directly on their Home Screen or within their phone's Control Center.
You can even set up background automations to ensure the VPN turns itself on the moment you open a specific application or connect to an unfamiliar public Wi-Fi network.
If tapping a widget is still too much effort, the update also brings full Siri integration to the table. By diving into the app's settings menu, you can record custom voice triggers, such as "Hey Siri, connect to AdGuard VPN", to control your privacy completely hands-free.
While we noted in our latest AdGuard VPN review that the service had room to grow against industry giants, quality-of-life updates like these certainly push it in the right direction.
Smarter exclusions and easier savings
While Apple users get the flashy widgets, the Android camp hasn't been entirely left out.
Finding a good deal on a digital privacy subscription usually requires hunting through promotional emails or constantly refreshing a provider's website. Now, AdGuard VPN will display active promotions and discounts directly on the purchase screen inside the Android app.
Finally, the v2.17 update brings a highly requested technical tweak to both the iOS and Android platforms. AdGuard's Exclusions feature, which allows you to choose which websites automatically bypass the encrypted tunnel, now fully supports domains written in non-Latin scripts. This means users can seamlessly whitelist domains like *.рф for Russia and *.中国 for China without the application returning an error.
The version 2.17 update is available to download right now. If you spot any bugs, the provider encourages users to submit feedback directly through its social media channels or via its GitHub repositories.

articles.title: TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic — potential deal seeks to end ongoing saga blocking its Wi-Fi 8 products from American homes
articles.text:
TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic — potential deal seeks to end ongoing saga blocking its Wi-Fi 8 products from American homes
You scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours
TP-Link is fully determined to get in the good graces of the U.S. government to break free from a total ban on newly developed routers manufactured outside of the country. Although TP-Link is incorporated in the U.S. with a headquarters in Irvine, California, the company has been under pressure from the full weight of the U.S. government because of its historical Chinese roots. However, in an effort to appeal to the Trump administration’s zeal for creating jobs and touting American manufacturing, TP-Link this week announced that it has signed a letter of intent to assemble routers in the U.S. through a crucial partnership with Key Tronic.
How did we get here?
The ongoing saga started back in late 2024, when the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party requested that the Department of Commerce investigate TP-Link. At the time, the committee warned that “TP-Link products are also found on U.S. military bases, with the Army and Air Force Exchange and the Navy Exchange selling these devices to members of the military and their families,” and claimed TP-Link routers were sending user data back to China.
The select committee implored the Department of Commerce to use its broad powers to investigate TP-Link and take any necessary action to mitigate threats to national security. The campaign against TP-Link ramped up in mid-2025, with 17 members of Congress petitioning the Commerce Department to ban the sale of the company’s hardware in the U.S. due to alleged deep ties to the CCP. In late 2025, 23 U.S. House members and Senators again asked the Commerce Department to investigate TP-Link’s actions, including adding the company to the Covered List, investigating any threats to national security, and informing the public about potential risks associated with using the company’s devices.
The situation reached a boiling point in March 2026, when TP-Link and other router manufacturers were added to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Covered List, forbidding the sale of foreign-made routers in the U.S. that hadn’t already been approved. At the time, the FCC noted, “Recently, malicious state and non-state sponsored cyber attackers have increasingly leveraged the vulnerabilities in small and home office routers produced abroad to carry out direct attacks against American civilians in their homes. From disrupting network connectivity to enabling local networking espionage and intellectual property theft, foreign-produced routers present unacceptable risks to Americans.”
Since that time, several things have changed, with none of them being positive developments for TP-Link. Over the past six months, Amazon, Asus, and Netgear have all gained conditional approvals from the FCC to sell new wireless products in the U.S., while TP-Link has been stonewalled (conditional approvals are valid for 18 months from the date of issuance). Considering that TP-Link has been the world’s largest provider of Wi-Fi routers and associated devices for over a decade, losing access to the U.S. market for its new line of Wi-Fi 8 devices is a significant blow. This was readily apparent in late September when TP-Link opened preorders for its Archer 8 Ultra Wi-Fi 8 router. The company announced that the router would be available in the United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia. However, the U.S. was conspicuously absent from that list because of the ongoing ban.
Adding insult to injury, earlier this month, multiple states (including Florida, Montana, Iowa, and Nebraska) sued TP-Link Systems, alleging that the company has made false and misleading claims about the security capabilities of its products and continued ties to China.
“TP-Link’s conduct has placed Montana consumers at risk of harm by making their home and small-office networks vulnerable to exploitation and intrusion by foreign actors with a proven track record of nefarious conduct. That risk is ongoing: many consumers keep their routers for years, and many of the compromised TP-Link models in Montana homes do not support automatic firmware updates and no longer receive security support at all,” stated Montana Attorney General Austin Knudsen.
Knudsen further claimed that while TP-Link touts that it employs 300 people in the U.S., the bulk of its workforce (numbering over 11,000 employees) conducts development and manufacturing operations in China. “Further, TP-Link claims to manufacture its U.S.-market products in Vietnam, but less than one percent of the components by value are sourced in Vietnam, and the rest are imported from or through China,” Knudsen added.
“Iowans’ sensitive data and our national security is at risk because of TP-Link and their connection to the communist Chinese government,” stated Iowa Attorney General Bird. “TP-Link tells Iowans its routers are safe, our personal data is secure, and that they have no ties to China. They are not telling the truth. It’s time to hold China and China-backed companies accountable.”
TP-Link barks back
Up until this point, TP-Link has vehemently denied any ties to the Chinese government and has refuted similar allegations from one of its primary competitors, Netgear. However, on October 13, the company issued its sharpest rebuttal yet in a letter to the FCC. TP-Link touted its “America-first” strategy and chastised the state lawsuits brought earlier this month.
“A group of 21 state-level officials recently raised a scattershot barrage of baseless and previously debunked allegations relating to TP-Link’s confidential, non-public application,” TP-Link exclaimed. Rather than seeking to advance legitimate public policy objectives, the letter appears aimed primarily at encouraging federal officials to apply a heightened standard to TP-Link’s pending application that would be unattainable to TP-Link or any other router manufacturer in the world.”
TP-Link stated that its innovation in the router space earned its position as the market leader in the U.S., and that the constant barrage of legal fights and war of words is undermining fair competition and is an actual threat to national security and critical infrastructure given the broad proliferation of its products.
To that end, TP-Link reiterated that it has officially filed for conditional approval from the FCC, so that it can specifically sell two next-generation Wi-Fi 8 routers in the U.S. The company noted, “As the United States positions itself as a leader in wireless technology, a Conditional Approval would guarantee American consumers access to the same cutting-edge wireless equipment that will soon be available in other parts of the world."
TP-Link proposes $1 billion investment in the U.S.
With its back against the ropes, TP-Link is appealing to the U.S. government in the best way it knows how: with money and jobs. If there’s anything that the U.S. government likes, it’s investment in manufacturing on its own soil and high-paying jobs to bolster local economies. To help push the U.S. government along in approving a conditional approval to sell Wi-Fi 8 hardware, TP-Link has signed a letter of intent with Key Tronic to manufacture routers in the U.S. instead of importing them from Vietnam. More specifically, the routers would be assembled in Corinth, Mississippi.
“This LOI with Key Tronic demonstrates our firm commitment to expanding domestic advanced manufacturing, and establishing America as our base for delivering secure, reliable connectivity solutions to households and businesses around the world,” said TP-Link Systems Inc. CEO Jeffrey Chao. “By choosing to assemble cutting-edge products here at home, we are thrilled to support U.S. high-tech job growth and empower a new generation of American innovation and innovators.”
TP-Link hopes that the investment will cut through most of the red tape that is currently preventing it from selling its latest products stateside. However, it remains to be seen if these latest sweeteners will be enough to sway President Trump and the agencies under his purview. As the company notes, it was the first to deliver Wi-Fi 7 routers in the U.S., and it wants to continue that leadership position by offering the first Wi-Fi 8 routers. The hardware is ready to go, as evidenced by the opening of preorders; it’s just currently being held up by roadblocks at the federal level, along with added pressure from state governments.
Until that time, Wi-Fi 8 products like the Archer 8 Ultra and Deco 8 Ultra will remain off-limits to Americans, which have given TP-Link a reported 65 percent share of the U.S. consumer router market.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: CON, PRN und NUL: Warum du Dateien in Windows 11 nicht so benennen darfst
articles.text:
CON, PRN und NUL: Warum du Dateien in Windows 11 nicht so benennen darfst
Obwohl Windows 11 ein modernes Betriebssystem ist und Microsoft darauf bedacht ist, viele Neuerungen zu implementieren, gibt es darin noch Relikte fast vergessener Zeiten. Dazu zählt etwa ein Feature, das nur wegen eines Kultspiels in Windows eingefügt wurde. Daneben gibt es aber auch alte Regeln, die Windows-User:innen heute noch einen Strich durch die Rechnung, oder besser gesagt die Dateibenennung, machen können.
Warum Windows 11 manche Dateinamen verbietet
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, gibt es eine Reihe von Namen und Kürzeln, die nicht für Dateien in Windows 11 genutzt werden dürfen. Versuchen es User:innen doch, verweigert das Betriebssystem die Eingabe und drängt darauf, einen anderen Namen für die Datei oder den Ordner zu wählen. Insgesamt sind es sechs Namenskategorien, teilweise mit mehreren Vertretern ihrer Art.
So können Dateien unter Windows 11 weder „CON“, „PRN“, „AUX“, noch „NUL“ genannt werden. Auch bei „COM1“ bis zu „COM9“ sowie „LPT1 bis zu „LPT9“ sperrt sich das Betriebssystem. Wie Microsoft-Entwickler Raymond Chen in einem Blog-Post schon vor einigen Jahren erklärte, stammt diese Regelung noch aus alten DOS-Zeiten. Denn damals waren die Begriffe für verschiedene Geräte reserviert – „CON“ für die Konsole, „PRN“ für den Drucker und „COM1“ bis „COM9“ für die physischen Anschlüsse des Systems. „NUL“ hingegen löschte die Dateien sofort wieder. „AUX“ steht für sekundäre Geräte und „LPT“ für parallel geschaltete Druckeranschlüsse.
Laut Chen unterstützte DOS 1.0 weder Unterordner noch Bezeichnungen in Kleinbuchstaben oder länger als acht Zeichen für den Hauptnamen und drei Zeichen für die Dateiendung. Die sogenannten „magischen Dateinamen“ sollten dafür sorgen, dass User:innen nicht zwangsläufig Dateien erstellen mussten, um etwas im System zu erledigen. Er zeigt das an einem Beispiel:
„Nehmen wir an, du wolltest eine Datei mit einer Liste direkt an den Drucker schicken. Du wolltest keine Datei auf der Diskette erstellen, weil kein Platz darauf war oder du die Datei wieder hättest löschen müssen. Also hast du „PRN“ als Dateinamen eingegeben. Der Assembler kannte diese magischen Dateinamen nicht. Er versuchte, eine Datei namens „PRN.LST“ zu erstellen. Allerdings wurde die Datei im Hintergrund als Output direkt an den Drucker geschickt.“
Chen betont, dass Microsoft diese Funktion auch unter neuen Windows-Versionen bewusst nicht entfernt hat: „Jeder verlässt sich auch heute noch darauf. Schaut euch nur die ganzen Batch-Dateien an, die Dinge tun, wie auf ‚NUL‘ zu verweisen oder zu prüfen, ob ein Verzeichnis existiert, indem sie ‚if exist directoryname\nul“ abfragen. Oder die Dokumentation, die besagt, dass eine Datei mit ‚copy CON‘ angelegt werden soll.

articles.title: Innovasea Packs Long-Life Electronics into Fish Tags - EE Times
articles.text:
Innovasea’s efforts to shrink its embedded system are not simply a packaging exercise. The Canadian company’s devices must be light enough for a fish to carry without materially changing its behavior, yet contain the electronics and battery needed to transmit useful data from underwater. The result is a design problem in which mass, power consumption, and reliability constrain one another.
The Bedford, Nova Scotia-based company develops acoustic telemetry equipment for researchers studying fish movement and behavior. Miniature transmitters travel with the animals; receivers detect their signals.
But that straightforward interaction depends on an engineering effort spanning firmware, acoustic transducers, sensing, and long-duration operation. Jean Quirion, Innovasea’s VP of research and development for fish tracking, describes a business whose products must meet biological requirements as carefully as electrical ones.
“Our customers who are biologists and scientists who are studying these things have rules about the proportion, the weight of the tag, and how that needs to be in proportion to the weight of the fish,” he said in an interview with EE Times. “It’s really not so much about the size; it’s about the actual mass of the tag that needs to be as little as possible.”
That distinction gives miniaturization a specific purpose: allowing researchers to study smaller animals without making the tracking equipment itself an undue influence on what they observe.
Designing around the battery
Innovasea’s smallest tag measures approximately 3 mm in diameter and 15 mm in length and weighs 0.3 g. Within that envelope are a battery, a microcontroller, transmission electronics, and a piezoelectric ceramic transducer.
The engineering challenge is not just fitting those elements together. It is making their limited energy supply support a useful deployment. More efficient microcontrollers help, but Quirion attributes much of the company’s capability to system-level optimization rather than component improvements alone. Firmware and electronics must work together to limit energy consumption while meeting the application’s transmission and sensing requirements.
“A huge core competency that we have is our ability to squeeze every nanoamp out of a battery and make the best possible use out of it so that their systems last as long as possible and similarly pack as much electronics as we can in a really, really small space,” Quirion said.
The tradeoffs vary across the product range. A tiny tag intended for a small fish has different constraints from a larger transmitter used to track sharks. The same engineering disciplines must accommodate both, without treating minimum size as the only measure of success.
The tags can also carry temperature and pressure measurements, adding environmental context to movement data. Innovasea has developed a proprietary predation sensor to identify another event that could otherwise complicate interpretation: a tagged fish being eaten.
“It has the ability to detect a state where the fish is now in the stomach of another fish,” Quirion said.
That capability makes the transmitter more than a location marker. It helps researchers distinguish an animal’s movements from those of a predator carrying its tag.
Reliability beyond the lab
Deployment life introduces another set of requirements. Some Innovasea receivers have been designed for continuous underwater operation for more than 10 years, and its largest shark-tracking tag targets a similar operating life. These specifications place reliability alongside size and energy efficiency as a central design objective.
“Reliability over a very long operating life is really, really important in everything that we do,” Quirion said.
Meeting that objective involves more than sealing electronics against water. Component selection, firmware robustness, power management, verification, validation, and real-world testing all contribute to a system expected to function through prolonged exposure to demanding conditions.
Innovasea manufactures the equipment in Bedford and ships it internationally, linking its engineering work directly to product delivery. Its immediate market remains fish research, although Quirion sees broader uses.
“It is really asset tracking in a sense,” he said. “In our world and in our application, these assets are fish that we are tracking, but it could be something else.”

articles.title: De nombreux HomePod victimes d'un bug fantôme : Apple corrige enfin le tir, mais n'assume pas
articles.text:
Il y a quelques années, certains HomePod se sont mis à dérailler. Sur les réseaux sociaux et sur les forums d’Apple, on trouve des milliers de témoignages de personnes dont l’enceinte s’est tout à coup mise à faire n’importe quoi. Concrètement, la musique démarre seule en pleine nuit, Siri s’active sans raison, le volume grimpe d’un coup. Le phénomène a été baptisé « ghost touch », ou toucher fantôme, par les victimes. Celui-ci survient lorsque la surface tactile située sur le dessus de l’enceinte enregistre des pressions qui n’existent pas, comme si un fantôme appuyait dessus pour vous tourmenter.
Un bug récalcitrant sur de nombreux HomePod
On a rencontré le problème il y a un peu plus d’un an sur notre HomePod mini, acheté dans le sillage de la sortie en 2020. L’enceinte a plusieurs fois lancé des playlists sur Apple Music au beau milieu de la nuit et s’est mise à répondre à des demandes qui n’existent pas. Dans les cas les plus graves, le HomePod est persuadé qu’on appuie en permanence sur la surface tactile. De facto, il finit par entrer dans une boucle de redémarrage. Le voyant rouge est impossible à éteindre. L’enceinte devient alors inutilisable. La défaillance touche surtout le HomePod mini et le HomePod 2. Il s’agit d’un problème au niveau du matériel.
Pendant des années, Apple n’a jamais reconnu officiellement le problème, pourtant massivement épinglé par ses clients. Les utilisateurs devaient se débrouiller tout seuls pour trouver une solution. Sur Reddit, on a trouvé plusieurs témoignages qui recommandent de modifier les réglages d’accessibilité de l’enceinte. L’un des réglages d’accessibilité impose en effet d’appuyer plusieurs secondes pour valider une commande sur la zone tactile. L’opération doit théoriquement empêcher le bug fantôme de se produire. Sans succès de notre côté. Parfois, il s’écoulait néanmoins plusieurs heures ou plusieurs jours avant que le HomePod ne recommence à devenir fou. Pour tenter de corriger le tir, on a aussi plusieurs fois réinitialisé l’enceinte. Là encore, cela n’a servi à rien.
Une deuxième option, bien plus radicale, est aussi apparue sur la toile. Elle consiste à ouvrir l’enceinte pour débrancher physiquement les connecteurs de la surface tactile. De facto, la zone n’est plus utilisable. Il faut impérativement passer par Siri pour la moindre commande. Ayant deux mains gauches, et aucune patience, nous avons renoncé. On a fini par débrancher l’accessoire et à le glisser dans un tiroir, dans l’espoir qu’Apple trouve un beau jour une solution.
À lire aussi : Apple dévoile le HomePod mini 2 : voici ce qui change
Un correctif qui ne s’assume pas
Bonne nouvelle, Apple s’est enfin penché sur le problème. Le géant de Cupertino vient en effet de déployer la mise à jour iOS 27.2 sur tous les HomePod, y compris les premiers modèles commercialisés il y a huit ans et sur le tout nouveau HomePod mini 2. Attention, il s’agit de la version release candidate, soit une itération presque définitive de la mise à jour. La version finale ne devrait pas tarder. Elle est attendue avant la fin du mois.
La mise à jour ajoute une fonctionnalité intitulée « Verrouiller les commandes » dans l’application Maison. Disponible sur tous les HomePod, ce réglage va tout simplement désactiver tout le pavé tactile du HomePod mini. Le toucher, le toucher prolongé qui appelle Siri et le réglage du volume seront totalement hors service. Évidemment, le capteur restera défectueux, mais il ne déclenche plus rien tout seul, ce qui permet de se servir à nouveau de l’enceinte. Toutes les autres fonctionnalités continuent de fonctionner normalement.
Officiellement, Apple ne présente pas cette option comme un correctif du bug des touches fantômes. Pour le moment, Apple ne reconnaît pas de défaut matériel sur ses enceintes. La mise à jour ne signifie pas que la marque reconnaît une défaillance massive. Apple présente plutôt le réglage comme une nouvelle option pour les parents de jeunes enfants ou les propriétaires de chats. Elle vise à éviter que les bambins ou les chats appuient sur la surface tactile du HomePod. De notre point de vue, elle rend surtout la vie à un appareil qui prenait la poussière, et qu’on avait presque condamné.

articles.title: Google lanza en Chrome alerta que distingue sitios “sospechosos” de los ya conocidos como “peligrosos”
articles.text:
Google comenzó a mostrar en Chrome una advertencia diferenciada para sitios “sospechosos”, separada de la alerta ya existente para páginas “peligrosas”. La función llega junto a una versión mejorada de la detección de estafas con Gemini, disponible para quienes activaron el modo de Protección Reforzada del navegador.
La nueva alerta de sitio “sospechoso” aparece como una ventana emergente sobre la página oscurecida, con la opción de marcarla como segura si el usuario confía en que no hay riesgo. Google la describe como un veredicto “de baja confianza”, es decir, con una posibilidad real de error.
“Al adaptar así la interfaz de advertencia, podemos expandir con seguridad la cobertura y mostrar un mayor volumen de alertas de protección”, explicó Jasika Bawa, gerente de producto de Chrome, en el anuncio oficial de Google.
La advertencia de sitio “peligroso”, en cambio, sigue ocupando casi toda la pantalla con un fondo rojo, como ya ocurría antes del cambio. Google la reserva para los casos de “alta confianza”, cuando el riesgo de daño al usuario es mayor.
El esquema reproduce el sistema de dos niveles que Chrome introdujo en 2024 para las descargas de archivos, que distingue entre documentos “sospechosos” y “peligrosos” según el grado de certeza de la detección.
Gemini amplía la detección de estafas
Chrome también reforzó la detección de estafas basada en Gemini, el modelo de inteligencia artificial de Google. Hasta ahora, la función operaba de forma local en el dispositivo y solo identificaba intentos de fraude de soporte técnico.
Desde esta actualización, el análisis pasó a un modelo que procesa los datos en los servidores de Google y amplía su cobertura a las estafas de antivirus falsos y de supuestas actualizaciones del navegador.
El sistema evalúa el contenido de la página para detectar señales como la marca que se intenta imitar, la intención del sitio y una probabilidad de estafa. Esa información se combina con la reputación del dominio antes de que Chrome muestre una advertencia.
Google precisó que el texto de las páginas solo se envía para su análisis cuando el sitio muestra indicios de estafa de alta confianza, y aclaró que ese contenido no queda registrado ni se usa para entrenar sus modelos.
Alertas contra los comandos maliciosos de “ClickFix”
La compañía sumó además una protección contra las estafas conocidas como “ClickFix”, que instruyen a la víctima a copiar y ejecutar un comando para “solucionar” un problema inventado. El texto que la persona termina pegando en su computadora puede ser distinto del que vio en pantalla.
Esos comandos suelen activar herramientas que ya vienen instaladas en el sistema operativo, como PowerShell o el símbolo del sistema de Windows, para instalar programas maliciosos sin pasar por los controles de descarga del navegador.
Cuando un usuario con Protección Reforzada copia uno de estos comandos sospechosos, Chrome elimina la información personal identificable del texto y la envía a Safe Browsing, el sistema antiphishing de Google, para su análisis.
Más de 1.000 millones de usuarios protegidos
Google introdujo la Protección Reforzada en 2020 para enfrentar el avance de las estafas y la ingeniería social en la web. Según la empresa, para 2025 ya la habían activado más de 1.000 millones de usuarios de Chrome.
La compañía sostiene que esos usuarios están diez veces más protegidos frente al phishing, la ingeniería social, el abuso de notificaciones y otras estafas, en comparación con quienes usan el modo estándar de Safe Browsing.
Safe Browsing, el sistema que sustenta todas estas alertas, funciona desde 2005 y hoy protege a más de 5.000 millones de dispositivos en Chrome, Android, Gmail y otros productos de Google, según la empresa.
Las nuevas alertas de sitios “sospechosos” solo están disponibles, por ahora, para quienes activaron la Protección Reforzada. Google no precisó si planea extenderlas al resto de los usuarios de Chrome, que usan por defecto el modo estándar de Safe Browsing.

articles.title: PS5 piratée à un mois de GTA 6 : un hacker perce la dernière mise à jour de Sony
articles.text:
PS5 piratée à un mois de GTA 6 : un hacker perce la dernière mise à jour de Sony
Moins de trois semaines après son déploiement, la mise à jour 14.10 de la PS5 vacille déjà. Le développeur Gezine exhibe en vidéo un menu réservé aux studios, ouvert sur une console du commerce. Un dernier rempart tient encore, et de lui dépend le sort de GTA 6 sur les machines modifiées.
Le 19 octobre, Gezine, figure bien connue de la scène homebrew PlayStation, a posté sur X une courte vidéo accompagnée de deux mots. On y voit une PS5 tourner sous la toute dernière version du système de Sony, la 14.10, déployée le 1er octobre avec un lot de correctifs de sécurité. Dans les réglages s'affiche pourtant un menu "Debug Settings", invisible sur les consoles vendues en boutique et normalement réservé aux kits de développement des studios. Pour le faire surgir, il faut avoir pris le contrôle du cœur du système. Autrement dit, avoir trouvé une faille inédite, à un mois tout juste de la sortie de GTA 6.
	
Salut 14.10.
Une faille inédite dans la dernière mise à jour de la PS5
Gezine a vite coupé court aux spéculations. Sa trouvaille n'a aucun lien avec Relapse, l'exploit public qui ouvre les PS5 jusqu'à la version 13.60 du système, et la brèche qu'il utilisait sur les versions 13.xx a été colmatée par la 14.00, mi-septembre.
Le reste demeure sous clé : il compte "demander la divulgation plus tard", une formule tirée du vocabulaire des primes aux bugs, ces programmes où le chercheur signale la faille à l'éditeur puis attend son feu vert pour la rendre publique. Sony anime le sien sur HackerOne.
Hello 14.10 pic.twitter.com/D7prKmOkbD
— Gezine (@gezine_dev) October 19, 2026
Ni fichier ni procédure, donc. Les possesseurs d'une console à jour ne peuvent rien reproduire.
GTA 6 sur PS5 : un dernier verrou résiste encore
GTA 6 débarque le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series. D'après PlayStation Game Size, un compte qui épluche les données du PlayStation Store, la version PS5 exigera au minimum la mise à jour 14.10. Ni Sony ni Rockstar n'ont confirmé.
	
L'ancienne méthode pour extraire les exécutables ne semble pas fonctionner en 14.xx. Peut-être qu'un exploit de l'hyperviseur est vraiment nécessaire.
L'hyperviseur, cette couche logicielle qui chapeaute le cœur du système, garde la clé du déchiffrement des jeux. Byepervisor Reborn, l'outil qui permettait de le contourner, a été neutralisé par les dernières mises à jour système. Sans successeur, impossible de copier GTA 6 sur une PS5 modifiée. Sony reste muet. Sur X, des adeptes réclament déjà que Gezine patiente jusqu'au 19 novembre avant toute publication, de peur qu'un nouveau correctif ne vienne tout refermer.

articles.title: Amazon’s bet on agentic AI to power enterprise ops Marketing AI tool: Is it driving profit or just noise?
articles.text:
Amazon bets on agentic AI to power enterprise ops; Is your marketing AI tool driving profit or just noise?
Rajeev Rastogi, Vice President of Machine Learning at Amazon, highlighted the rise of agentic AI in the enterprise operating layer. Anand Jain of CleverTap explained why marketing teams must move beyond basic generative AI productivity tools and adopt autonomous, real-time decisioning systems.
Dear Reader,
The future points to agentic AI, and its implementation is gathering pace.
Cognizant and Google Cloud are expanding their partnership to accelerate adoption of agentic AI. This includes a ‘Gemini Frontier Capability Group’, which brings together Google’s full-stack, enterprise-ready AI platform and Cognizant’s industry and engineering expertise as an AI-builder.
The group will be supported by more than 18,000 dedicated Cognizant associates and a substantial joint investment.
Meanwhile, ahead of its IPO, Jio Platforms’ anchor book has drawn Rs 2.5 lakh crore in bids. The company allotted 7.24 crore shares at a price of Rs 1,119 apiece to anchor investors, with LIC receiving the largest allocation.
Moving on, Hunar.AI has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from Hyderabad Angels Fund, Together Fund, Seedstars, AVNM Ventures, PhysicsWallah co-founders Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey, and MediaMint co-founder Aditya Vuchi.
The startup, which develops specialised AI tech for frontline-intensive industries, will use the funds for building AI infrastructure, product development, and go-to-market expansion.
Lastly, a report by Redseer notes that the online retail market in the country is expected to cross $90 billion this year with grocery overtaking mobiles. The gross merchandise value of the ecommerce market expanded roughly 25% year on year to about $38 billion in the first half of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Amazon’s bet on agentic AI to power enterprise ops
- Marketing AI tool: Is it driving profit or just noise?
Here’s your trivia for today: What was the first Mickey Mouse cartoon ever produced? (Scroll down for the answer)
TechSparks
Amazon bets on agentic AI to power enterprise ops
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, Rajeev Rastogi, Vice President of Machine Learning at Amazon, highlighted the rise of agentic AI in the entire enterprise operating layer, marking a transition from static software to autonomous systems capable of understanding natural language instructions.
“Agents prepare plans dynamically to solve a problem... and invoke the appropriate tools,” Rastogi explained during a fireside chat at the 17th edition of YourStory’s flagship tech-startup event.
Driving transformation:
- Instead of relying on human intervention at every step, these autonomous agents evaluate queries, formulate a sequence of actions, and call specialised digital tools to complete complex tasks end-to-end.
- Within Amazon, this operating layer is active in systems like Rufus, a conversational shopping assistant that parses customer requests, applies price filters, invokes search engines, and guides users through product comparisons and checkout journeys. Similarly, autonomous seller assistants pre-fill product listings, monitor inventory levels, and guide small businesses through international export compliance.
- According to Rastogi, eventually the industry will advance towards genuine world models that possess an internal understanding of physical spaces and environmental behaviour, establishing a practical, cost-effective framework for enterprise automation.
TechSparks
Is your marketing AI tool driving profit or just noise?
At TechSparks 2026, Anand Jain, Co-founder and Chief Marketing Officer of CleverTap, a customer engagement and marketing automation platform, explained why marketing teams must move beyond basic generative AI productivity tools and adopt autonomous, real-time decisioning systems that drive genuine business profit.
Key takeaways:
- In a masterclass on marketing strategy, Jain urged leaders to look beyond simple shortcuts, and move from using AI for fun and games to generating actual business results.
- While creating content using AI makes the job faster and saves time, Jain questioned whether it truly drives growth. “Is it actually going to impact business results or is it just more of the same?”
- Instead of broadcasting generic promotions to large groups, modern marketing engines should interpret live customer actions to match individual needs. This approach marks a shift towards the highest level of AI maturity, known as ‘real-time decisioning’.

articles.title: EEUU ordena eliminar DeepSeek de los sistemas de sus agencias civiles federales. El veto va todavía más allá
articles.text:
DeepSeek lleva meses en el centro de una disputa que va mucho más allá de quién tiene el modelo de inteligencia artificial más capaz o más barato. Desde que irrumpió con R1, la compañía china ha quedado bajo el escrutinio de gobiernos, reguladores y empresas estadounidenses en medio de una competición tecnológica cada vez más tensa. Ahora Washington ha dado un paso más: ha ordenado sacar su tecnología de una parte de los sistemas de la Administración federal.
Qué ha ordenado exactamente EEUU. El alcance empieza por una parte bien definida de la Administración: las agencias civiles de la rama ejecutiva federal. La orden, fechada el 24 de julio de 2026 y publicada ahora en el Federal Register, obliga a estas entidades a frenar nuevas adquisiciones de productos y servicios desarrollados por DeepSeek y a eliminar los ya presentes en sus sistemas informáticos. La medida admite excepciones previa solicitud y deja fuera los sistemas de seguridad nacional y los sistemas de información compartimentada de esas agencias.
También alcanza productos de terceros. DeepSeek no se limita al chatbot que podemos abrir desde una web. Sus modelos también pueden utilizarse a través de su API para impulsar funciones dentro de aplicaciones y servicios desarrollados por otras compañías, de modo que su tecnología puede quedar integrada en herramientas que llevan otro nombre. Ahí aparece la dimensión menos evidente de la orden: un producto puede no identificarse como DeepSeek y, aun así, quedar afectado si ha sido desarrollado utilizando una implementación de su tecnología.
El problema está también en los datos. Buena parte de la preocupación de Washington aparece cuando dejamos de mirar al modelo y nos fijamos en la información que recibe. DHS sostiene en la propia orden que la compañía aloja sus servidores en China y que sus servicios pueden recopilar datos personales, rastrear a los usuarios y procesar la información que estos introducen en sus consultas. La agencia teme que esos datos puedan quedar al alcance de las autoridades chinas conforme a su legislación y utilizarse, solos o combinados con otras fuentes, para obtener información sobre personas estadounidenses o programas del Gobierno de EEUU.
UN VISTAZO A...
No es el primer cerco. EEUU ya había comenzado a cerrar la puerta a DeepSeek dentro de su Administración. Una ley promulgada en diciembre de 2025 encargó al Director de Inteligencia Nacional establecer normas para retirar la aplicación de DeepSeek, así como cualquier aplicación o servicio sucesor, de los sistemas de seguridad nacional operados por la comunidad de inteligencia o en su nombre, aunque contemplaba excepciones para investigación y determinados fines de seguridad nacional. La diferencia ahora está en el perímetro: la nueva orden lleva las restricciones al conjunto de agencias civiles de la rama ejecutiva federal.
DeepSeek llega bajo más sospechas. El escrutinio estadounidense no se limita al tratamiento de los datos. En septiembre, NSA, FBI y CISA advirtieron sobre campañas de destilación a gran escala contra modelos estadounidenses, y DeepSeek figura entre las empresas señaladas. La técnica consiste, de forma simplificada, en utilizar las respuestas de un modelo para ayudar a entrenar otro y no es problemática por sí misma. La disputa está en el supuesto uso no autorizado: tanto OpenAI como Anthropic han atribuido a la compañía intentos de este tipo contra sus sistemas.
China rechaza el argumento estadounidense. Pekín ha respondido acusando a Washington de ampliar en exceso el concepto de seguridad nacional y de politizar cuestiones tecnológicas y comerciales. El Ministerio de Exteriores chino asegura además que defenderá los derechos e intereses legítimos de sus empresas. Más allá del choque diplomático, la orden deja una idea clara sobre hasta dónde está llegando esta disputa: ya no se trata solo de qué modelos puede utilizar directamente una administración, sino también de qué tecnología puede estar integrada detrás de los servicios y herramientas que compra.

articles.title: The next Xbox could arrive in 2028 for $1,200 to $1,800, Xbox handheld may launch in 2027
articles.text:
What we know so far: Memory shortages from the AI boom have cast doubt on the release timing and pricing of Sony's and Microsoft's next-generation consoles. While rumors had pointed to a possible 2027 launch, a new report pushes that back another year and supports estimates that both devices could break the $1,000 barrier.
According to Fortune, Microsoft is aiming to launch its next-generation console, codenamed Helix, in time for the 2028 holiday season. As memory costs climb, its price has internally been projected at anywhere between $1,200 and $1,800, unless the company subsidizes the hardware.
Another new Xbox, a handheld, could arrive by the 2027 holiday season. It would presumably support digital Xbox console games, unlike Asus' Xbox-branded ROG Xbox Ally, which is little more than a Windows handheld.
The details come from the outlet's extensive profile of Xbox's CEO, Asha Sharma, who replaced Phil Spencer earlier this year. Sources also told Fortune that Sharma plans to overhaul the Game Pass subscription service into an à la carte model, where users pick specific add-ons and online features.
The CEO has previously said she wants to make the service more affordable, and Microsoft has already partially reversed its disastrous price hikes.
Helix could cost more than double, and possibly more than triple, the Series X's $500 launch price from 2020, because AI data centers have absorbed most memory and storage manufacturing capacity, quintupling DRAM and NAND costs. Microsoft, a major player in the AI boom, has already raised the Series X's price several times.
Rival console maker Sony is in a similar position. The PlayStation 5 Pro now retails for $900, and trusted leakers say the PlayStation 6's bill of materials is approaching $1,000. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki recently confirmed that the PS6's launch window remains undecided, but the company's decision to stop manufacturing physical discs for new games in January 2028 suggests the transition is planned for that year.
Microsoft previously confirmed that developers will receive Helix development kits next year. Features such as ray tracing, path tracing, neural rendering, machine learning, upscaling, denoising, neural texture compression, and multi-frame generation will play central roles.
Microsoft's Helix console and the PlayStation 6 are expected to use AMD's Zen 6 CPU and RDNA 5 GPU architectures. According to leaks, Sony's console will feature eight CPU cores and 40 to 48 GPU Compute Units, while Microsoft's will increase the CPU core count to 10 with 20 threads, though its CU count remains unclear. Helix, which will also support PC games, could have a 40% advantage over the PS6 in some aspects of rendering performance.
Fortune's report also shed light on the remaining Xbox layoffs expected this year and next. Sharma has cut nearly 1,900 people so far as part of a plan to reduce headcount by 3,200 over the next year, with further rounds planned for October, November, and January. Across the company, Microsoft has laid off roughly 35,000 workers since 2020.

articles.title: Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
Axiomtek, a world-renowned leader relentlessly devoted to the research, development, and manufacture of innovative, highly efficient, and reliable industrial computer products, proudly introduces the MANO330, a compact Thin Mini-ITX motherboard powered by the Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5 memory. Designed for space-constrained systems that require flexible connectivity and expansion, the MANO330 combines multi-display capability, dual LAN connectivity, versatile M.2 expansion, and industrial I/O in a compact platform. With a wide 12-24 VDC power input, the MANO330 provides system developers with a flexible foundation for smart manufacturing and industrial automation, digital signage, smart retail, and POS applications.
Compact Performance for Space-Constrained Systems
The MANO330 combines a compact Thin Mini-ITX design with Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5-4800 memory support. The N97 supports up to 32 GB of memory, while the N150 supports up to 16 GB. Measuring just 170 x 170 mm, the MANO330 provides the essential computing performance and I/O capabilities needed for embedded systems, helping developers build space-efficient solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications.Rich Visuals and Reliable Network Connectivity
Designed for information-rich applications, the MANO330 supports multiple independent display outputs through HDMI, VGA, LVDS/eDP interface, and USB Type-C with DisplayPort support. This display flexibility allows system developers to configure multiple screens for applications such as digital signage, retail displays, and industrial monitoring. The board also integrates 2.5GbE and GbE LAN, providing reliable network connectivity for connected systems and industrial applications.
Flexible Expansion to Fit Different Applications
The MANO330 provides flexible expansion options for storage and wireless connectivity. Its M.2 Key M 2280 slot supports SATA/NVMe storage, while M.2 Key E 2230 supports wireless connectivity. The M.2 Key B 3042/3052 interface provides an additional expansion option and is paired with a Nano SIM slot for wireless applications. These options allow customers to configure storage and connectivity according to their application requirements, helping simplify system development and integration.
Built-In I/O for Easier System Integration
The MANO330 integrates commonly used industrial interfaces directly on the board, including RS-232, RS-422/485, USB, SATA, and GPIO, helping reduce the need for additional interface hardware. Two RS-232 ports support jumper-selectable RS-422 or RS-485, while four additional RS-232 ports provide further serial connectivity for industrial devices. Combined with the board's 12-24 VDC power input, these built-in interfaces provide system developers with greater flexibility and help simplify system integration.
Tina Tu, Product Manager at Axiomtek"Today's embedded systems need to balance compact design with flexibility for different application requirements. With versatile display, connectivity, expansion, and industrial I/O options, the MANO330 gives system developers greater freedom to configure and integrate solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications"
Advanced Features of MANO330
- Intel Processor N97/N150
- DDR5-4800 SO-DIMM, up to 32 GB with N97 and 16 GB with N150
- Dual LAN ports
- M.2 Key B 3042/3052
- M.2 Key E 2230
- M.2 Key M 2280
The MANO330 is now available.

articles.title: Cops raid office of RFK Jr. allies planning “unethical” vaccine trial on babies
articles.text:
Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of Danish researchers on Monday, seizing doses of hepatitis B vaccine intended for a vaccine trial for newborns. International health experts have called the trial “unethical,” but anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to fund it with US taxpayer dollars.
Under Kennedy, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced in December that it had awarded the Danish researchers—led by married couple Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project—an unsolicited $1.6 million grant to run the trial. Aaby and Stabell Benn are controversial vaccine researchers who claim vaccines cause overlooked harms. They have been repeatedly praised by Kennedy, but are currently under investigation for alleged scientific misconduct by Danish authorities.
Plans for the trial were halted in January as widespread condemnation erupted over the trial’s design, which would potentially expose thousands of newborns in the country to hepatitis B, risking a lifelong infection that can lead to liver cirrhosis, cancer, and premature death. Outrage flared again after a Rolling Stone story earlier this month claimed the CDC set aside another $1.6 million in funding in late September and planned to move forward with the trial.

articles.title: BetaCreator: TIM oficializa plano com 50 GB e acesso exclusivo por convite • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
BetaCreator: TIM oficializa plano com 50 GB e acesso exclusivo por convite
Reformulação do TIM Beta mantém os R$ 60 por mês, mas agora permite acumular a internet para os meses seguintes.
A TIM oficializou nesta terça-feira (20/10) a reformulação do TIM Beta, antecipada pelo Tecnoblog no mês passado. O plano do agora BetaCreator custará R$ 60 por mês e será exclusivamente por convites. Ele oferece 50 GB de internet, além de redes sociais, TIM Mais e Deezer inclusos.
Durante a apresentação acompanhada pelo Tecnoblog, a executiva Julia Martins, diretora de marketing do pré-pago da TIM Brasil, explicou que o plano não poderá ser contratado espontaneamente por nenhum canal da operadora. Nesta primeira fase, o acesso será feito por meio de convites distribuídos a influenciadores e criadores de conteúdo.
Quem já é cliente TIM Beta também terá acesso à novidade. Segundo Martins, os usuários do plano antigo serão os primeiros a receber convites, sob a categoria Beta Founder. A operadora nos confirmou que não haverá migração automática e, quem preferir, poderá permanecer no plano antigo. Os convites deverão ser ativados em até 48 horas após o recebimento.
O TIM Beta atual custa o mesmo valor, mas oferece uma franquia menor de internet. Além disso, no BetaCreator, os dados que sobrarem passam para os meses seguintes e não expiram enquanto a linha permanecer ativa no plano. Por exemplo, se o cliente usar 30 GB da franquia de 50 GB, os 20 GB restantes não expiram.
Lançado em 2010, o TIM Beta nasceu como um produto voltado ao público jovem, com foco em comunidade e engajamento. Segundo a operadora de origem italiana, a marca agora é renovada com benefícios pedidos pelos clientes.
A experiência ficará concentrada no aplicativo Meu TIM, enquanto o app exclusivo do TIM Beta deve ser encerrado. De acordo com a operadora, a mudança busca reunir os serviços em um só lugar. A TIM ainda não detalhou quantos convites serão distribuídos nem quantos clientes poderão aderir ao Creator.

articles.title: Enterprise work management at Elevate - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
What to expect during monday.com’s Elevate event: Join theCUBE Oct. 29
Enterprise work management is entering a new phase as artificial intelligence agents move beyond assisting employees to executing business processes.
Platforms once designed to organize projects and track assignments are becoming environments where people and autonomous agents collaborate, raising questions about application development, productivity and governance. That transition is a central theme of monday.com’s Elevate conference, taking place Oct. 28–29 at the Javits Center in New York City. The event brings together business leaders, developers and technology professionals to examine how AI is changing enterprise operations. SiliconANGLE and theCUBE will provide exclusive interviews and analysis, with special coverage airing Oct. 29. (* Disclosure below.)
“Monday.com Elevate signals a broader shift in application development: from building software that helps people manage work to building AI-powered applications and agents that execute work,” said Paul Nashawaty, principal analyst at theCUBE Research. “For AppDev leaders, the promise of AI-assisted app creation is compelling, particularly as business teams seek to build tailored solutions faster and reduce their dependence on constrained engineering resources.”
The opportunity is substantial, but so are the challenges of deploying autonomous systems within established enterprise environments. As monday.com expands its AI capabilities, theCUBE will examine whether organizations can translate faster application development into measurable business outcomes while maintaining oversight of increasingly independent agents.
AI-powered application development moves beyond traditional work management
The growing use of AI agents is changing expectations for enterprise work management software. Rather than simply coordinating assignments, these platforms are beginning to execute the work itself, automating processes and giving employees new ways to create applications without extensive coding expertise.
The shift is already evident in enterprise software development, where AI adoption has accelerated significantly.
“The momentum behind events like Elevate is unmistakable. According to theCUBE Research, 92% of organizations now report AI capabilities integrated into at least one stage of their software delivery lifecycle, up sharply from 71% in early 2024,” said Sam Weston, analyst at theCUBE Research.
The company’s monday AI ecosystem brings together several capabilities intended to support that shift. Agent Factory allows organizations to create specialized AI agents, while monday sidekick provides contextual assistance within the workspace. Meanwhile, monday vibe enables users to build custom business applications through natural-language prompts, reducing the technical expertise traditionally required for software development.
These capabilities could help businesses address application backlogs and automate processes that span departments. Sales teams, for example, could use agents to qualify leads and update records, while service organizations could automate ticket routing and resolution. The broader opportunity is to connect these activities within a shared operational environment.
The Elevate 2026 agenda includes hands-on sessions focused on building AI agents, creating applications with vibe coding and integrating automation into enterprise workflows. The emphasis on practical implementation reflects a growing industry challenge: moving beyond experimental AI applications to systems that deliver consistent results.
The anticipated expansion of autonomous agents adds urgency to these efforts, particularly as enterprises consider how human employees and AI systems will share responsibility for business processes.
“With 79% of organizations anticipating widespread AI agent adoption within three years, Elevate26’s focus on building with AI agents and human-agent collaboration arrives at a pivotal moment for enterprise leaders,” Weston said.
The real test, however, is whether organizations can move beyond rapid prototyping to production-grade applications with measurable business value, maintainability and enterprise controls, according to Nashawaty.
“Elevate’s significance will ultimately be determined not by how quickly an app can be generated, but by how reliably it can be deployed, governed and scaled,” he said.
AI agent governance becomes essential as autonomous workflows expand
Giving AI agents greater responsibility across business applications also introduces new security and governance challenges. Agents that can access sensitive information, modify records or initiate transactions require clearly defined permissions and oversight mechanisms, particularly when their activities cross organizational boundaries.
For enterprises adopting AI-powered work management, the challenge extends beyond protecting individual applications. Organizations must establish how agents authenticate, what information they can access and which activities require human approval.
“The security question gets more difficult as AI agents move deeper into enterprise workflows. An agent may be acting on behalf of a person, but its access can span applications, data and business processes. Enterprises need a clear way to establish whose authority the agent is operating under, what it is allowed to do, and when a human needs to get involved,” said Krista Case, principal analyst and practice lead of cybersecurity and cyber resilience at theCUBE Research.
These considerations become particularly important as business users gain the ability to create applications and automated workflows independently. Faster development can reduce pressure on IT teams, but it can also introduce inconsistencies in security policies, access controls and operational accountability if organizations lack centralized governance.
The Elevate agenda addresses these concerns through sessions dedicated to AI governance and guardrails, offering a broader discussion about what enterprises need to consider before expanding agent deployments.
“Platforms such as monday.com are becoming places where people and AI agents coordinate work together,” Case added. “That puts governance directly in the flow of work. Companies need visibility into what agents are doing, controls around the data and actions available to them, and an audit trail that lets teams understand how work moved from a request to an outcome.”
For monday.com and its enterprise customers, the next stage of AI adoption will depend on balancing easier application creation with the security and governance requirements of production environments. TheCUBE’s coverage will examine how that balance shapes the company’s platform strategy and what it means for organizations preparing to give AI agents a more active role in everyday business operations.
TheCUBE event livestream

How to watch theCUBE interviews
We offer you various ways to watch theCUBE’s coverage of monday.com’s Elevate event, including theCUBE’s dedicated website and YouTube channel. You can also get all the coverage from this year’s events on SiliconANGLE.

SiliconANGLE’s “theCUBE Pod” is available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube, which you can enjoy while on the go. During each podcast, SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante discuss the biggest trends in enterprise tech, including AI, cloud, cybersecurity and infrastructure, with context and analysis.
