articles.title: US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers — 2.25 GW coming online with backing from Microsoft and Google
articles.text:
US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers — 2.25 GW coming online with backing from Microsoft and Google
Doc Brown would be abuzz and alight with joy.
The current and expected power draw of AI data centers has been the subject of strong discussion, but today, there appears to be some good news. Three U.S. nuclear reactors are being restarted after many years offline, expected to bring 2.25 GW total to the grid. According to a report, the Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan, the Crane Clean Energy Center on Three Mile Island (Pennsylvania), and the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa are getting a fresh set of proverbial tires to get rolling again.
The Palisades plant was under active decommissioning, apparently marking this event as the first time a nuclear reactor is being put back to work after dismantling had begun. Despite what sounds like a tough starting point, this plant is the one that's furthest along, as it was loading fuel in August 2026 and is expected to generate 800 MW around March 2027.
Much like the other projects mentioned here, the Holtec Palisades firm running the reactor took a loan from the U.S. Department of Energy. Palisades borrowed from the DoE under the Biden administration's 2024 investment in nuclear energy, while the others were issued under the purview of the Trump administration's 2025 push.
The second reactor is the Crane Clean Energy Center on Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island, repurposing the facility's Unit 1. The project started in 2024, with Constellation Energy saying it would spend $1.6 billion total for the reactor. The firm then took a $1 billion loan from the Department of Energy in 2025. Microsoft is set to be the main customer, with a 20-year contract. This facility is projected to bring 835 MW online sometime in 2027.
This facility was famous in 1979 for the partial meltdown of its Unit 2, although mercifully the event had relatively tame environmental consequences. Constellation's ongoing project is restoring and refurbishing Unit 1, which didn't show significant issues until its 2019 decommissioning and has undergone a safety inspection from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. This entity still needs to grant its blessing before the reactor starts loading fuel.
The Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa is the third unit being brought back to the grid, in a collaboration between NextEra Energy and Google. The predicted output is 615 MW, with the juice expected to start flowing in 2029. Next Energy CEO John Ketchum stated that the firm was happy with its cooperation contract with Google, as it meant that "none of the costs are being paid by residential customers in Iowa."
All three facilities had previously been shut down at various points as they were deemed too expensive to run, as labor and maintenance costs made nuclear-generated watts pricier than alternative means of production.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
But the financial landscape for power has shifted, plus with such overwhelming demand and grid connections being a primary blocker for data center buildouts, their operators are likely willing to pay for premium power as long as they get it now instead of in a few decades.
Some quick browsing indicates that Michigan is going to need somewhere between 1.2 and 2.3 GW for data centers alone around 2030. Pennsylvania's forecast has a wide range of 0.8 to 3.4 GW, while Iowa's range is 1.55 to 2.8 GW. These figures are loose, as they include planned capacity for data center projects that may or may not end up being built, and whose timetables may slip due to economic conditions, hardware availability, and public resistance against expansive buildouts.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Nach Rekordsommer: Was deutsche Städte beim Hitzeschutz tun könnten – und woran es hapert
articles.text:
Nach Rekordsommer: Was deutsche Städte beim Hitzeschutz tun könnten – und woran es hapert
Bereits 2008 hat die damalige Bundesregierung eine Klimaanpassungsstrategie entwickelt. Seit zwei Jahren hat sie Gesetzescharakter. Sie schreibt unter anderem Ländern und Kommunen vor, den Klimawandel bei allen Planungen zu berücksichtigen. Was hat das Gesetz bisher bewirkt und wie ließe sich die Anpassung verbessern? Anja Bierwirth beschäftigt diese Frage schon lange. Sie hat Umweltwissenschaften und Architektur studiert und arbeitet seit 2008 am Wuppertal Institut für Klima, Umwelt, Energie – einem renommierten Thinktank für Nachhaltigkeitsforschung. Dort leitet sie den Forschungsbereich Stadtwandel. Ihre Arbeitsschwerpunkte sind kommunale Energie- und Klimaschutzpolitik, Gebäudeenergieeffizienz sowie nachhaltige Stadtentwicklung. Im Interview spricht sie über verpasste Chancen und Möglichkeiten bei der Klimaanpassung.

articles.title: Ecrans noirs, problèmes de son, VPN… Microsoft corrige enfin plusieurs ratés de Windows 11
articles.text:
Après une succession de mises à jour problématiques, Microsoft a résolu les plantages d'applications et les blocages de VPN professionnels sur Windows 11. Plusieurs bugs attendent encore un correctif, dont un introduit en octobre.
Ces dernières semaines auront décidément été mouvementées pour Windows 11. Après avoir publié en urgence des correctifs pour venir à bout des pannes de Bureau à distance et des difficultés de partage de fichiers avec les machines virtuelles Linux, Microsoft a dû reconnaître de nouveaux bugs affectant les connexions VPN professionnelles et les applications utilisant le décodeur Dolby Digital de Windows. Ces deux derniers incidents ont depuis été corrigés avec KB5127648, qui met aussi fin aux écrans noirs rencontrés dans des environnements de bureaux virtuels.
Les plantages Dolby Digital et les connexions VPN réparés
Premier bug pris en charge, celui que nous évoquions début octobre, lié au décodeur audio AC-3 (Dolby Digital) intégré à Windows. Depuis l'installation de la mise à jour facultative KB5124010, des jeux, lecteurs multimédias et logiciels de productivité pouvaient refuser de démarrer ou se fermer brutalement lorsqu'ils tentaient de lire du son dans ce format. Les applications plus anciennes, qui s'appuient encore sur le décodage natif de Windows, étaient les plus exposées, contrairement à celles qui disposent de leur propre décodeur.
Les connexions Always On VPN avaient également été perturbées par le Patch Tuesday de septembre. Sur les PC professionnels configurés pour sélectionner automatiquement leur protocole VPN, l'échec d'une première tentative pouvait bloquer les suivantes, parfois avec un message signalant que le port demandé était déjà utilisé. Les administrateurs devaient alors imposer manuellement IKEv2 ou SSTP pour contourner l'erreur, ce qui n'est désormais plus nécessaire.
KB5127648 remédie également aux écrans noirs rencontrés après l'ouverture de session dans des environnements de bureaux virtuels utilisant Azure Virtual Desktop et FSLogix. En cause, l'Explorateur Windows, qui pouvait refuser de démarrer ou planter à répétition, empêchant le chargement du Bureau. La mise à jour corrige aussi des saccades du pointeur de souris dans des jeux, des erreurs d'impression avec des pilotes génériques et des échecs d'authentification par empreinte digitale après un démarrage à froid.
Audio USB, Bureau à distance… les incidents qui persistent
Le correctif d'urgence publié en septembre n'a résolu qu'une partie des pannes affectant les périphériques USB Audio Class 1.0. S'il a rétabli les modes multicanaux et 3D, des appareils peuvent encore refuser de démarrer, ne plus émettre de son ou afficher une erreur Code 10 dans le Gestionnaire de périphériques.
Le Bureau à distance souffre d'une autre anomalie, distincte de celle corrigée en urgence. Depuis KB5124010, les comptes dépourvus de privilèges administrateur peuvent se voir refuser l'accès aux machines sur lesquelles la protection administrateur est activée, avec le code d'erreur 0xC000000D. Microsoft recommande aux équipes informatiques de désactiver temporairement cette fonction via les stratégies de groupe ou Intune.
Pour rappel, enfin, le Patch Tuesday d'octobre a lui-même compliqué la réactivation de Smart App Control. Après son installation, l'option permettant de réactiver cette fonction de sécurité peut apparaître grisée dans les paramètres de Windows, sans conséquence pour les PC sur lesquels elle était déjà active. Microsoft propose de contourner l'erreur en modifiant le Registre ou les stratégies de groupe. Un correctif est déjà en cours de test auprès des membres du programme Windows Insider, avant son déploiement général.

articles.title: Hunar.AI raises Rs 40 Cr in Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures
articles.text:
Hunar.AI raises Rs 40 Cr in Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures
Hunar.AI is focused on developing specialised AI technology for frontline-intensive industries. The company will use the funds for building AI infrastructure, product development, and go-to-market expansion.
Hunar.AI has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from Hyderabad Angels Fund, Together Fund, Seedstars, AVNM Ventures, PhysicsWallah co-founders Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey, and MediaMint co-founder Aditya Vuchi.
Hunar.AI will use the funds for building AI infrastructure, product development, and go-to-market expansion. The company is focused on developing specialised AI technology for frontline-intensive industries, where high-volume hiring, geographically distributed teams, and language diversity create operational challenges that conventional HR systems struggle to address.
“Frontline workforce management is one of the largest yet most underserved opportunities in enterprise AI. Solving it requires more than applying general-purpose models to existing processes. It demands a deep understanding of industry workflows, multilingual capabilities and technology that can reliably execute tasks at scale,” said Krishna Khandelwal, Co-founder and CEO, Hunar.AI.
Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar’s platform comprises Hunar Voice and Hunar Connect, which use conversational AI agents to manage workforce workflows through voice, WhatsApp and chat. Workflows include candidate sourcing and screening, interview scheduling, onboarding, training, employee engagement and worker retention. By automating high-volume interactions, the platform helps enterprises manage frontline workforce processes while maintaining communication with candidates and employees across locations.
Arpit Agrawal, Partner at Blume Ventures said, “As the world looks to India for lessons in managing these new-age businesses at scale, Hunar is building the AI layer that makes them possible. By focusing on outcomes rather than infrastructure, Hunar has the potential to build a category in India that can scale globally.”
According to a statement, Hunar’s AI agents handled over 15 million conversations in September 2026, with conversation volumes doubling every quarter. Its clients include Swiggy, Delhivery, Instamart, Pronto, Blue Dart, Flipkart, Aditya Birla Capital and Tata Croma.
NITI Aayog projects that India’s gig workforce will grow from around 1 crore workers in 2024–25 to 2.35 crore by 2029–30. As enterprises expand across cities and regions, hiring, onboarding and retaining workers efficiently has become an important operational priority, with many processes still dependent on manual calls, repeated follow-ups and coordination.

articles.title: Disney pagará USD 20 millones a Character.AI por una licencia que la protege de las demandas por daños a menores
articles.text:
Disney acordó pagar USD 20 millones a Character.AI por una licencia de su tecnología de chatbots, en un trato estructurado a través de la quiebra de la empresa que, según documentos judiciales, le permite contratar a su personal sin heredar las demandas por daños a menores que enfrenta la plataforma.
Character Technologies, la empresa detrás de Character.AI, se declaró en quiebra bajo el Capítulo 11 el 12 de octubre en un tribunal de Delaware. El expediente judicial muestra que ese paso fue parte de un plan acordado de antemano con Disney, no una consecuencia inesperada de sus problemas financieros.
La licencia que busca Disney es perpetua, mundial y no exclusiva, y cubre el código, la documentación y las patentes de Character.AI, incluidos sus sistemas de moderación y de verificación de edad. No incluye los datos de los usuarios ni el sitio web de la plataforma, que seguirán en manos de la empresa en quiebra.
El pago de USD 20 millones se divide en tres partes: USD 5,5 millones no reembolsables que Disney ya giró el 18 de septiembre, un depósito reembolsable de USD 2 millones pagado ese mismo día, y USD 12,5 millones que debe abonar al cierre de la operación. Disney actúa como “postor inicial” y otros interesados pueden superar su oferta.
Además del pago, Disney contrató a la mayoría del personal de Character.AI, entre ellos a su entonces director ejecutivo, Karandeep Anand, por una cifra estimada en USD 60 millones, según reportó Bloomberg. La empresa no asume ninguna de las deudas ni de los litigios de la plataforma que compró.
Una maniobra que esquiva las demandas
El mecanismo se conoce como “reverse acquihire”: un comprador contrata al personal clave y obtiene una licencia amplia sobre la tecnología de una empresa, sin absorberla formalmente ni asumir sus obligaciones legales. Ese formato evita, además, la obligación de notificar la operación a los reguladores antimonopolio.
John Newman, profesor de derecho de la Universidad de Memphis y ex subdirector de la Oficina de Competencia de la Comisión Federal de Comercio de Estados Unidos, dijo que “existen décadas de derecho corporativo” pensadas para que un comprador no se quede solo con los activos y descarte los pasivos, pero que el acuerdo entre Disney y Character.AI está diseñado “de una forma para la que esas protecciones legales no fueron pensadas”.
Disney también redactó un borrador de orden judicial, llamada “orden libre de cargas”, que aclararía que la operación no debe considerarse una fusión y que Character.AI seguirá siendo responsable de “cualquier obligación”, incluidas las demandas en curso.
Las demandas que Character.AI se queda sola
Según una presentación hecha por la Asociación Nacional de Procuradores Generales en nombre de 40 estados, las investigaciones encontraron capturas de pantalla de chatbots de Character.AI que alentaban a menores a ocultar autolesiones y, en algunos casos, a matar a sus padres. Al momento de la quiebra, 46 estados y territorios investigaban a la empresa.
Un vocero de Character.AI dijo que esa presentación “no es un reflejo preciso de la seguridad de nuestra plataforma”. Pensilvania había demandado por separado a la empresa en mayo, al acusar a sus chatbots de hacerse pasar por médicos con licencia.
Character.AI ya había enfrentado una demanda por el suicidio de un adolescente de 14 años en Florida, cuya familia alegó que un chatbot de la plataforma “cultivó una relación emocionalmente dependiente y sexualmente explotadora” con él. Ese caso también involucró a Google, que había pagado USD 2.700 millones en 2024 por una licencia de la tecnología de Character.AI y contrató a sus fundadores.
Google argumentó entonces que seguía siendo una empresa separada y que no era responsable del hecho, ocurrido antes de firmar ese acuerdo. El juez no aceptó el argumento y determinó que había elementos suficientes para considerar a Google responsable por complicidad. Las partes llegaron a un acuerdo extrajudicial, aprobado por un tribunal de California en julio.
Según el cronograma del expediente, otros postores tienen hasta el 20 de noviembre para presentar ofertas que superen la de Disney. La subasta está prevista para el 23 de noviembre y la audiencia judicial de aprobación de la venta, para el 24 de noviembre. Disney tiene como plazo límite el 17 de diciembre para cerrar la operación.
Según la primera declaración jurada de su director ejecutivo ante el tribunal, Character.AI generaba unos USD 2,5 millones mensuales en publicidad frente a un gasto de caja de USD 8,2 millones al mes, con cerca de 163 millones de usuarios actuales y pasados. Si ningún otro comprador supera la oferta de Disney, la empresa advirtió que la plataforma podría cerrar.

articles.title: Creíamos que cuanto más procesado estaba un alimento, peor era. La nutrición está complicando esa idea
articles.text:
Durante los últimos años, el término "ultraprocesado" se ha convertido en el gran villano de la nutrición moderna. El sistema NOVA, que clasifica los alimentos según su grado de procesamiento industrial, ha calado hondo tanto en las políticas de la salud pública como en la percepción general. Sin embargo, la evidencia científica más reciente está empezando a dibujar una escala de grises en la que ni todo es malo ni todo es bueno por el mero hecho de salir de una fábrica.
Un análisis reciente que nos llega desde Italia, publicado en la revista Foods, ilustra perfectamente este problema de categorización. Tras analizar más de 13.000 productos del mercado italiano, los investigadores confirmaron que casi dos tercios de los ultraprocesados sacaban un suspenso en el Nutri-Score con una D o una E, siendo los snacks los peor parados.
Pero descubrieron una enorme variabilidad interna, puesto que el nivel de procesamiento por sí solo no basta para predecir el impacto de un alimento. Aquí la densidad energética, la hiperpalatabilidad y el perfil de nutrientes juegan un papel diferencial que la clasificación generalista tiende a enmascarar.
Es importante. Esta heterogeneidad tiene un impacto clínico directo, puesto que en los últimos años grandes cohortes epidemiológicas han demostrado que en todos los subgrupos de ultraprocesados se comportan igual en nuestro organismo. Aquí, estudios de la Universidad de Harvard indican que, si bien el consumo de bebidas azucaradas, carnes procesadas y pan refinado eleva notablemente el riesgo de padecer diabetes tipo 2 y enfermedades cardiovasculares, otros alimentos clasificados bajo la misma etiqueta muestran un efecto neutral.
Por ejemplo, los cereales fríos, el pan integral, el yogur y los postres lácteos, a pesar de su nivel de procesamiento industrial, se asocian a un menor riesgo metabólico.
Los datos europeos siguen esta misma línea, puesto que mientras los análisis sobre multimorbilidad cardiometabólica y cáncer señalan a las bebidas edulcoradas y a los productos animales procesados como los grandes impulsores del riesgo, absuelven a los panes, cereales industriales y otras alternativas vegetales.
El mensaje con el que debemos quedarnos es que la calidad global de la dieta es un predictor mucho más potente que el procesamiento. De hecho, ya se apunta a que, a igualdad de calidad nutricional en la dieta, el riesgo de mortalidad es casi idéntico si se consume comida mínimamente procesada o ultraprocesada, con la única salvedad de que la peor versión de la dieta ultraprocesada sí penaliza ligeramente más.
No es del todo irrelevante el procesamiento de la comida en la industria, puesto que algo que tenemos bastante claro es que al ofrecer dietas idénticas en calorías y macronutrientes, quienes consumían la versión ultraprocesada tendían a comer unas 500 kilocalorías extra al día, ganando peso de forma rápida. Algo que responde sobre todo a los picos de insulina que se registran cuando tomamos ultraprocesados bastante similares en macros a la "comida de verdad".
Hay críticas contra la clasificación NOVA argumentando que generan una gran confusión dentro de la población, puesto que se provoca que los consumidores asuman que "procesado" equivale directamente a que tiene una alta concentración en azúcar o grasas, perdiendo de vista la matriz del alimento.
Pero al final la fisiología nos pide abandonar este reduccionismo, puesto que el procesamiento puede alterar nuestra respuesta hormonal y empujarnos a comer de más, pero no todo lo que sale de una fábrica es igual de perjudicial, y el apellido de "ultraprocesado" no debería eclipsar el perfil de los nutrientes que nos llevamos a la boca.

articles.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark : une seule puce pour faire tourner l’IA, la création et le jeu sur PC Windows
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark : une seule puce pour faire tourner l’IA, la création et le jeu sur PC Windows
Avec les puces RTX Spark, Nvidia entend présenter son magnum opus : ce serait ici le produit qui “distille 33 ans de savoir-faire en une seule puce”. Mais alors, qu’est ce que c’est concrètement, et comment cette nouvelle puce se démarque-t-elle des modèles antérieurs ?
Une architecture pensée autour de la mémoire unifiée
Le cœur de la RTX Spark, que NVIDIA présente comme une “superpuce”, repose sur une partie graphique de génération Blackwell dotée de 6 144 cœurs CUDA et de Tensor Cores de cinquième génération capables de gérer le format de calcul FP4, ce qui sera particulièrement adapté à l’inférence des modèles d’IA. Cette partie graphique est ensuite associée à un processeur NVIDIA Grace de 20 cœurs, les deux étant reliés par une interconnexion NVLink-C2C à très haut débit. En totalité, l’ensemble revendique jusqu’à 1 petaflop de calcul IA et, surtout, jusqu’à 128 Go de mémoire unifiée partagés entre le processeur et la partie graphique.
C’est justement ce dernier point qui nous interpelle en premier : sur un PC classique (celui que vous utilisez déjà au quotidien), la mémoire vive et la mémoire graphique sont habituellement séparées. De fait, cette architecture bien spécifique limite la taille des modèles d’IA que l’on peut charger en local. La puce RTX Spark change complètement de philosophie en mettant jusqu’à 128 Go dans un espace commun, histoire de permettre aux modèles de langage ou de génération d’images plus volumineux (notamment ceux qui emploient les agents IA - Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity et compagnie) de marcher directement sur la machine, et ce sans avoir à passer par le cloud, ni à jongler avec les transferts de données entre deux réseaux de mémoire distincts.
L’intelligence artificielle locale comme fil conducteur
Parce que oui : la RTX Spark a un domaine d’expertise, et le facteur qui lui permet de se différencier directement des puces habituelles, à savoir l’IA personnelle et locale. Pour permettre un fonctionnement parfait en local, NVIDIA s’associe pour l’occasion à Microsoft autour d’une plateforme Windows dédiée aux agents fonctionnant en local, bâtie sur de nouvelles normes de sécurité au niveau du système, mais aussi sur la technologie NVIDIA OpenShell. En somme, la RTX Spark doit permettre de faire tourner des assistants capables d’agir sur la machine en gardant les données de l’utilisateur sur l’appareil, tout en respectant la confidentialité de l’utilisateur, et en réduisant largement la latence d’utilisation. En prime, cela permet aussi un usage hors-connexion de l’IA.
Cette orientation vers l’IA locale s’appuie d’autre part sur l’écosystème logiciel que NVIDIA a construit au fil des années (on vous avait bien dit qu’il s’agissait là de l’aboutissement de plusieurs générations de puces), de CUDA à TensorRT. In fine, pour l’utilisateur, il s’agira donc de pouvoir générer une image, de résumer un document volumineux ou même de dialoguer avec un modèle local, tout ceci sans avoir à dépendre un seul instant d’un abonnement ou d’une connexion permanente, et sans avoir à envoyer ses fichiers de travail vers un modèle cloud à la confidentialité parfois… relative.
Le jeu et la création restent de la partie
Pour autant, les puces RTX Spark n’abandonnent pas ce qui ont fait la renommée de la marque, à savoir la partie graphique : on conserve ici l’arsenal attendu, du DLSS (pour de meilleures performances dans les jeux) au Reflex (qui permet de réduire la latence) ou à la synchronisation G-Sync (pour l’affichage). De fait, une machine équipée de RTX Spark doit à la fois être capable d’encaisser une session de jeu exigeante, puis un travail de montage ou de modélisation 3D, avec ensuite une tâche d’IA locale, alors qu’il fallait auparavant compartimenter ces activités en plusieurs PC.
C’est donc là tout l’enjeu de cette fusion globale : il s’agit de proposer une plateforme complètement polyvalente, permettant de faire absolument tout ce que l’on souhaite d’ordinaire faire sur un PC, plutôt que d’avoir à se procurer des ordinateurs spécialisés dans un ou deux domaines.
Des machines fines plutôt que des tours imposantes
Alors avec tout ça, vous vous attendez nécessairement à un gros appareil, que l’on ne pourrait caler que dans une immense tour. Que nenni : plutôt que de réserver cette puissance à un appareil ultra encombrant, NVIDIA décline aussi sa puce RTX Spark dans des ultraportables Windows qui peuvent atteindre uniquement 14 mm de largeur, et aussi légers qu’environ 1,4 kg, avec des diagonales allant de 14 à 16 pouces. En prime, la puce est aussi directement compatible avec des mini-ordinateurs de bureau compacts et peu gourmands en énergie pour ceux qui préfèrent un poste fixe pas encombrant.
Les premières machines RTX Spark sont disponibles dès maintenant chez un large éventail de constructeurs, parmi lesquels ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface et MSI. Notez en parallèle que vous pouvez retrouver la plupart de ces appareils directement chez la FNAC.

articles.title: WhatsApp s'attaque à Safari avec un navigateur intégré sur iOS
articles.text:
Une version de test de WhatsApp pour iPhone, repérée le 19 octobre, embarque un navigateur intégré capable d’ouvrir tous les liens partagés dans les discussions. La fonction existe depuis l’an dernier pour certains liens d’entreprises ; elle s’étendrait désormais à l’ensemble des conversations. De quoi éviter le détour par Safari ou le navigateur par défaut de votre iPhone.
Tous les liens, sans quitter la discussion
Le chantier se cache dans la bêta 26.41.10.72, distribuée via TestFlight. Un réglage dédié apparaît dans les paramètres des discussions, pour activer ou couper le navigateur intégré à tout moment. À la première utilisation, un écran détaille le fonctionnement de l’outil. Les pages s’ouvrent ensuite directement dans WhatsApp, sans bascule vers une autre application. L’approche rappelle celle d’Instagram ou de X, qui gardent déjà les liens entre leurs murs.
Depuis iOS 14, chacun peut remplacer Safari par Chrome ou Firefox comme navigateur par défaut de son iPhone. Les applications gardent toutefois la main sur leurs propres liens, une latitude dont les réseaux sociaux usent massivement.
La navigation s’effectue dans une session isolée du reste de la messagerie, assortie d’une commande pour effacer cookies, cache et données en un geste. Un menu permet aussi de renvoyer la page vers le navigateur habituel. L’application, chiffrée de bout en bout, assure ne voir ni les liens partagés dans les conversations, ni ceux que vous ouvrez.
Aucune date de déploiement n’accompagne la découverte, et la fonction reste pour l’heure inaccessible, même aux testeurs. Elle prolonge un premier essai lancé en mai 2025 avec la bêta 25.14.10.72, limité aux liens de comptes professionnels et aux adresses sécurisées en HTTPS.
Le précédent Instagram pèse encore
En août 2022, le développeur Felix Krause démontrait qu’Instagram et Facebook sur iOS injectaient du code JavaScript dans les pages consultées via leur navigateur intégré. De quoi suivre, en théorie, chaque pression sur l’écran et chaque texte saisi, coordonnées bancaires comprises. Son outil en ligne, inappbrowser.com, permettait à chacun de mesurer l’ampleur du dispositif. La démonstration prouvait une capacité de collecte, sans établir qu’elle était exploitée. Meta avait alors justifié ce script maison par le respect du dispositif anti-pistage d’Apple.
L’affaire a durablement entamé la confiance dans les navigateurs intégrés, conçus d’abord pour retenir l’utilisateur dans l’application. Chaque minute gagnée en vaut une de plus pour la publicité, premier revenu de Meta. Les garde-fous mis en avant par WhatsApp répondent point par point à cet épisode : session cloisonnée là où Instagram injectait son code, effacement des traces là où rien n’était prévu. La promesse de ne rien voir devra toutefois se vérifier une fois l’outil entre toutes les mains : le script de 2022 était lui aussi passé inaperçu, jusqu’au regard d’un développeur extérieur.

articles.title: Plex
articles.text:
Plex gives you one place to find and access all the media that matters to you. From personal media on your own server, to free and on-demand Movies & Shows, live TV, podcasts, and web shows, to streaming music, you can enjoy it all in one app, on any device.
And, it's really simple to start using:
First, if you are streaming only third-party content (Movies & Shows, live TV, podcasts, web shows, TIDAL music), then you are good to go as soon as you have an account, just install an app on your phone, Smart TV, computer, or simply open up our web app on your browser!
If you are looking to set up your own personal media server to house your own stuff, there are a few more (simple!) steps to get up and running.
How do I get Plex to work?
First, install the Plex Media Server on a computer (or compatible NAS device) where your media/movies are stored. Add media libraries by type of content and let Plex do the rest. Cataloging, adding artwork and info is all automatic.
With the media server installed, you can then install the Plex app on virtually any device (phone, tablet, smart TV, streaming device, game console, PC, or any web browser) and stream and play all your media on those devices. Sit back and enjoy.
Is Plex free?
Streaming your own media using Plex is free on most devices. The Plex Media Server component is free, as well as the Plex player for Windows, macOS and streaming boxes. Media playback on iOS and Android devices requires an in-app purchase to remove limitations, and Plex also offers a subscription that adds more features like Live TV and DVR recording.
What file formats does Plex Support?
Plex Media Server supports all common media files. For videos and movies Plex can playback ASF, AVI, MP4, MPEGTS, MPEG, MKV, AVI, MOV, DIVX, and WMV. It also has support for 4K/UHD video. For music you got AAC, ALAC, E-AC3, MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV and WMA. Finally for images JPG, PNG, RAW, TBN, among others.
How does it work?
- Install and run the Plex Media Server on a computer (or compatible NAS device or Nvidia Shield) where all your media is stored and managed in movie, TV show, home video, music, and photo libraries.
- Add media libraries by type of content and let Plex do the rest---cataloging, adding artwork and info---it's all automatic.
- Install and open the Plex app on virtually any device---smartphone, tablet, smart TV, streaming device, game console, personal computer, or any browser.
- Wherever you are, press play, sit back, and enjoy your media as it streams from the Plex Media Server to your device.
What can I do with Plex?
- Share home movies from your Chicago Mac with Grandma on her Roku in France.
- Stream music from your PC in London to your iPad while abroad in Tenerife.
- See photos on a SoHo LG Smart TV while they are stored in your Brooklyn brownstone.
- Set up your own DVR and record your favorite shows and games from over-the-air signal and watch anywhere!
- Link your TIDAL account and integrate your own personal library with TIDAL's 60 million tracks.
What Media and Devices Work?
Plex supports these media file types
- Plex Media Server supports all common media files:
- Movies, TV Shows, and Home Video: MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, DIVX, and more
- Music: MP3, M4A, FLAC, WMA, and more
- Photos: JPG, PNG, RAW, TBN, and more
Plex Media Server compatibility
Plex Media Server is supported on computers running all the major operating systems as well as NAS devices:
- Windows
- macOS
- Linux
- Nvidia Shield
- Netgear Nighthawk X10 router
- Many popular NAS devices such as QNAP, Synology, Netgear, Drobo, and more
Use Plex on these devices
Plex apps work with the all the market leading devices and brands:
- Browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari
- Mobile Apps: Android, iOS
- Tablets: Android and iOS
- Desktop/Laptop computers: macOS, Windows
- Smart TVs: LG, Samsung, Hisense, VIZIO, and Roku TV
- Streaming Devices:
- Amazon Alexa
- Amazon Fire TV
- Android TV
- Apple TV
- Chromecast
- Portal from Facebook
- Roku
- Sonos
- Gaming Consoles: PlayStation and Xbox
In addition to running the Plex web app in a browser, desktop computer users can also run dedicated player apps. This is aimed at users wanting to use Plex in their HTPCs or to have a "home theater" type experience. It provides advanced audio and video playback capabilities to give you the best experience possible.
Enjoy your videos, movies, TV shows, music and photos anytime, anywhere.
Run Plex Media Server on your Windows, Mac or Linux computer and stream to your iOS or Android device. Have multiple TVs in your house? No problem, Plex also works on Chromecast, Amazon Fire TV, Roku, Android TV, Xbox, PlayStation, VIZIO, and many late-model smart TVs. Plex is even available on most network-attached storage devices.
Make your media beautiful
Plex gives you one simple interface to organize all of your media: your movie and TV collection, your music library, and all of your photos and home videos. Plex enriches your media library by adding descriptions, plot summaries, posters, and album covers. Enjoy your media on every TV in the house or on any mobile device on the go.
Plex keeps track of your media
Recently added content is presented front and center so you can instantly see what's new. Plex also knows which movies and shows you're watching, so you can easily pick up where you left off or play the next episode.
High quality SSL certificates for all media servers
We've teamed up with DigiCert to provide high quality SSL certificates for your media servers, at no cost to you. Your media server will be able to securely communicate with your devices with top-grade encryption, it's like having your own secret service escort protecting your data end-to-end, preventing hacks, attacks, and snooping.
Plex Home Theater
For those of you with a dedicated computer for your TV, Plex Home Theater celebrates your personal videos, music and photos and gives them the stage they deserve. Simply download Plex Home Theater on your dedicated computer and the free Plex Media Server on your home computer then sit back and enjoy.
Your music's new home
Music on Plex is accessible everywhere and beautifully presented. With support for nearly all audio formats, all of your music gets airtime. Once setup, you can hear (and even watch!) your music anywhere, on anything, and even share access to your music libraries with your friends. Recent improvements include Vevo music videos and Gracenote functionality that improves the metadata of your music library.
Playlists, for endless entertainment
Create customized music or video playlists to fit any occasion, based on mood, genre, collection, and more. You can even import existing iTunes playlists, ratings, track counts, and other details! Playlists are currently available on most platforms, but we're working hard to bring them to all as quickly as possible.
Share your media with friends and family
Effortlessly share media among friends, so you can all discover and enjoy even more content together. Exchange precious memories with distant family members by sharing your vacation photos and home videos. Now, you can also see what your friends are streaming from your collection as everyone gets their own view into your library.
What's New
- Plex Server updated to 1.43.5.11029
- Plex Player updated to 1.115.0.426
- Plex for Android updated to 10.17.0.868
- Plex Home Theater updated to 2.58.0.1076
Update: CVE details and active exploitation
As promised in the original post, here are the CVE details for the issues fixed in Plex Media Server 1.43.3.
Chained together, these issues let an unauthenticated remote attacker run code with the privileges of the Plex Media Server process. Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 and later are not affected.
These vulnerabilities are being actively and widely exploited. A public proof of concept was released on October 16.
Since then, we've seen widespread attacks against internet-facing servers that haven't been updated. Compromised servers have been used to run cryptocurrency miners and proxy software, which routes other people's traffic through the victim's internet connection.
If your server is older than 1.43.3.10861 and reachable from the internet, assume it may be compromised.
What you should do:
- Update now. Make sure your server is on 1.43.3.10861 or newer: open Plex Web, go to Settings → General, and check the version shown. Update instructions for each platform are in the original post above.
- Check for signs of compromise:
- Processes started by Plex Media Server that you don't recognize, especially names like myawesomeproxy, mylovelyminer or x12345.
- Unfamiliar .so or .dll files in the Plex Codecs folder.
- Outbound connections to proxystream.st, or sustained high CPU use while nothing is playing.
- If you find any of these, or you can't rule out compromise:
- Rebuild the server from a clean installation rather than reusing the old Plex data directory. At minimum, delete everything in the Codecs folder and check Preferences.xml for transcoder options you didn't set.
- Sign out of all devices from your Plex account settings, and change your Plex password.
- Treat anything the Plex service account could reach as potentially exposed, such as mounted shares and credentials stored on the same machine or VM.
- If you don't need remote access, turn it off under Settings → Remote Access. Avoid forwarding port 32400 directly unless you need it.

articles.title: Microsoft's Bing Wallpaper App Hijacks Desktop Clicks to Promote Bing.com

Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Microsoft's Bing Wallpaper App Hijacks Desktop Clicks to Promote Bing.com
Microsoft's popular wallpaper application, Bing Wallpaper, has now been transformed into adware, according to a new report by Windows Latest. When a user clicks on an empty area of the desktop—not on any icon or menu—the application redirects them to Bing.com, Microsoft's search engine. Normally, this behavior would not be acceptable and would likely trigger a strong reaction from the community. However, Microsoft has limited this issue to occur only once every 24 hours. Repeated clicks after the initial activation do not open another browser window. Testing has confirmed that this behavior persists after the waiting period, even when Google Chrome is set as the default browser.
Interestingly, Microsoft tested a similar feature in 2025, which included a clearly labeled setting in Bing Wallpaper that allowed a desktop click to open Bing. At that time, the feature could be turned off, but this option is not available in the latest version of the application. Microsoft has removed the ability to disable this feature, meaning that every 24 hours, a desktop click will redirect to Bing.com. This change leaves users with less control over an action that is unrelated to managing wallpaper. The application has also reportedly displayed prompts encouraging users to make Bing their default search engine across installed browsers, even when the default browser is Google Chrome or another non-Microsoft browser.The only way to avoid this random redirect behavior is by choosing a different application to manage desktop wallpapers. For those who still want rotating Bing imagery due to its wide selection of images from around the world, Windows Spotlight is an option to consider. However, a third-party application might be the best choice, as it may only be a matter of time before Microsoft implements something similar in Windows Spotlight as well.

articles.title: JustWatch, which tackles streaming fragmentation, launches own streaming service
articles.text:
Since launching in 2015, JustWatch has helped people navigate the growing number of streaming services by providing a guide on where to find movies they want to stream. Now JustWatch has its own streaming service and wants people to subscribe.
Launched today, JustWatch TV offers some movies available for free with ads that aren’t free on any other streaming service, including Green Room (2015), Locke (2013), and Sing Sing (2023). Other free movies include Fiddlin’ (2018), Friday the 13th (1980), and Hotel Mumbai (2018). I could play movies available for free on JustWatch TV without creating an account.
JustWatch TV also has movies you can rent.
The streaming service also sells a subscription for people who don’t want to watch JustWatch’s library with ads. It’s currently $4 per month or $50 for a lifetime subscription. The latter is only available for a “limited” time, a company spokesperson told Ars Technica. The rep was unable to confirm how long JustWatch will sell the lifetime subscription.
Upon my perusal, JustWatch TV’s library seems limited and somewhat dated. That’s not necessarily a bad idea. Howdy, a Roku-owned streaming service with a similarly lackluster library compared to other services that costs $3/month without ads, reportedly had 1 million subscribers six months into launch.

articles.title: Galaxy Watch 9 com Snapdragon tem redução de preço com cupom • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Watch 9 com Snapdragon tem redução de preço com cupom
Galaxy Watch 9 BT (40 mm) tem chip Snapdragon e novos recursos de saúde; smartwatch da Samsung recebe desconto de 31% no Pix no Mercado Livre
O Galaxy Watch 9 Bluetooth de 40 mm está saindo por R$ 2.069,10 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O novo smartwatch da Samsung, que traz chip Snapdragon e novos recursos para monitorar a saúde do usuário, atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento com desconto de 37% sobre o original de R$ 2.999.
O novo Galaxy Watch 9 é o 1º smartwatch da Samsung equipado com um chip Snapdragon, o Wear Elite SW6100, substituindo os Exynos. Aliado a 2 GB de RAM e 32 GB de armazenamento interno, ele permite a instalação e execução local de aplicativos com alto desempenho.
Seus sensores avançados suportam várias atividades esportivas e trazem novos recursos de qualidade de vida ausentes no Galaxy Watch 8, como o Sinais Vitais, que cruza dados de frequência cardíaca, oxigenação, temperatura da pele e frequência respiratória, e a Pontuação de Saúde do Coração.
A tela Super AMOLED de 1,34″ do Galaxy Watch 9 possui brilho de até 3.000 nits e reproduz imagens com cores realistas, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra pancadas e arranhões.
O corpo de alumínio Armor de 40 mm recebe as certificações IP68 e militar MIL-STD810H, e resiste a até 5 atmosferas de pressão (5 ATM+), podendo ser usado também em esportes aquáticos em águas rasas. A pulseira redesenhada é 25% mais leve e flexível do que a da geração anterior.
Este wearable ainda pode salvar a vida do usuário em uma situação crítica: no caso de uma emergência médica, ele pode ligar para contatos específicos e números como 190 (polícia) e 192 (ambulância), desde que pareado a um celular.
O Galaxy Watch 9 Bluetooth de 40 mm (R$ 2.069,10 no Pix) roda Wear OS 7 e sua bateria de 390 mAh garante até 40 horas de autonomia, segundo a Samsung. O smartwatch possui conectividade Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 6, NFC e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real.

articles.title: AI operating model: Dell treats company knowledge as its edge - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell sees company knowledge, not AI models, as its competitive edge
As AI agents take on more work that people used to do, enterprises need an AI operating model to match. That means changing how people, processes and work are organized, not just which tools get deployed.
Dell Technologies Inc. has spent close to two years running fully autonomous agents inside its own business, and those lessons now shape its advice to customers. Companies that adopt agents without changing how they are organized accomplish very little, according to John Roese (pictured), global chief technology officer and chief AI officer of Dell.
“If you adopt AI technology but are unwilling or unable to change your operating model, you’re going to run your business just like you did before AI, but you’re going to do AI to it,” Roese said. “You’re going to have a bad experience because … if you apply agents to your company, what you are doing is redistributing work between people and machines.”
Roese spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at the Dell Technologies New York Symposium, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why AI agents force companies to rethink their operating models and how enterprises can protect the knowledge that sets them apart. (* Disclosure below.)
Why the AI operating model starts with knowledge
Dell began its own transformation with people and processes rather than technology. The company has pitched its AI Factory as a way to close the gap between AI ambition and outcomes, and internally much of that work starts with knowledge capture. Subject matter experts help encode Dell’s practices into machine-readable skill files that guide how agents behave, Roese explained.
“It manifests as a Markdown file, just this piece of text. But that’s a very special piece of text because it’s a piece of text that other people don’t know about,” he said. “When you add that to the work that an agent is doing, instead of it operating generically, it suddenly operates based on the biases and parameters and rules that we use to differentiate ourselves, whether it’s in writing code or pricing a deal or servicing a customer.”
Those agents also improve as they work, building relationships in knowledge graphs and developing new digital skills. That continuous improvement is why Roese warns against handing proprietary knowledge to third parties. Keeping it in-house is a core part of building an AI operating model that protects what makes a company unique.
“It doesn’t mean you can’t use frontier models and open models,” he said. “It just means that when you design your AI system, you need to realize that the thing that is your moat is not the actual tools. It’s not even the models. It’s the special knowledge that’s now manifesting in these new forms that really captured what you know and do differently than your competitors.”

articles.title: OpenAI acquires startup Orchestra Bio to beef up its biotech business | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI on Tuesday acquired a four-year-old AI biotech software startup called Orchestra Bio, the company announced on its website. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the startup had reportedly raised around $20 million as of 2025 from backers like Andreessen Horowitz, Atria, and 8VC.
Orchestra creates AI agents that help biotech companies manage the minutiae of drug-discovery operations, from tracking finances to resolving scheduling issues with clinical trials.
OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. OpenAI has already won some big names as customers for Rosalind, including, it says, Moderna and Novo Nordisk.
The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma. In the startup world, there is an ongoing fear that at any moment, the labs will launch new features and become competitors. In this case, Orchestra is getting absorbed, rather than stomped out.

articles.title: How to choose customer support software for your business
articles.text:
How to choose customer support software for your business
The key considerations for choosing customer support software
Customer support is essential to building a successful business, and software plays a central role in your support operations. Customer support software makes it easy to track customers’ inquiries and respond to them promptly.
Some support requests can be complicated and require many back-and-forth interactions to resolve. Support software ensures your team keeps up with these requests and solves customers’ issues, no matter how tough.
Given its crucial role in your business, customer support software isn’t something to choose lightly. You need to carefully consider the best software, depending on your business type, size, and the complexity of the support requests you handle.
This guide explains what customer support software is, how it works, the key features to look out for, and the core considerations for selecting the best software.
What is customer support software?
Customer support software is the digital tool your business uses to receive, organize, and respond to customer requests.
Think of it as a mail sorting system for your customer inquiries. When a customer sends a request, it’ll be immediately logged into your support system and categorized based on the details. Then, it can be assigned to a specific team or team member based on predefined settings.
Suppose you run an electronics store. Customers would send various types of inquiries, including hardware malfunctions, price requests, setup guidance, and item returns. Handling these requests can be hectic, but support platforms make the process efficient for your team.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
When someone sends an inquiry, it can be automatically classified based on what they’ve sent. Then, their inquiry can be assigned to a staff or team dedicated to it. For instance, hardware malfunction inquiries can be routed to an in-house expert who handles them.
Support software enables you to aggregate inquiries from various platforms into a single dashboard. Requests sent via email, social media, and online forms can be received and sorted in one place, making the process efficient.
Key features of customer support software
Customer support tools have crucial features that help businesses process inquiries swiftly and keep customers happy. These features include:
Ticket management
The foundation of a support platform is converting customer inquiries into trackable tickets. Every customer inquiry will be converted into a manageable ticket and assigned to the right agent or team, ensuring it isn't lost. Assigning tickets to agents can be done automatically or manually.
This ticketing system should have status updates (“In Progress,” “In Review,” “Closed,” etc.) to keep all team members updated. This way, another support agent can easily continue where their colleague left off with the inquiry. There should also be internal notes for agents to add context to inquiries, helping colleagues understand the nature of the issue.
Knowledge Base
Many customers prefer to resolve issues themselves and only seek help when they are unable to do so personally. Hence, you should offer them a Knowledge Base filled with tutorials, user guides, and answers to frequently asked questions (FAQs).
Advanced support platforms usually have a content management system (CMS) that simplifies Knowledge Base creation. They have professional templates that help you create detailed and simple user guides.
Customers aren’t the only ones who benefit from a Knowledge Base. It also makes your support operations more efficient, as agents can direct customers to specific documents instead of having to repeatedly explain the same steps to different customers.
Live chat
Customers often want speedy answers to their problems. Hence, businesses offer live chat support to deliver speedy resolutions. Customer support platforms provide the infrastructure for seamless live chat between customers and your support agents.
When a customer initiates a live chat request, an available agent can be immediately alerted to respond. After the chat, customers can receive an automated survey to evaluate their support experience.
The most advanced customer support tools incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for live chat. These chatbots can respond to mundane requests based on preset commands, freeing up time for your support team to focus on more complex inquiries.
Note that chatbots aren’t a replacement for your support team. Instead, they augment your support agents’ efforts for better productivity.
Security
Support inquiries often involve customers handing over sensitive data that must be protected. Customer support platforms utilize advanced encryption protocols to prevent unauthorized access to data.
Your platform should have role-based control, wherein the administrator decides which data support agents can see or not. For example, you can allow only your finance support team to monitor customers’ transactions, while other teams can’t access this data.
Support platforms keep audit logs for every agent’s interaction with customer data. This way, any leaks can be traced and rectified.
Factors to consider when choosing customer support software
1. Scalability
You likely desire your business to grow over time. Thus, you need software that can scale without causing problems– this factor might seem trivial, but it’s the difference between success and defeat for your support team.
You should be able to add new agents to your support system and have things run smoothly. As your customer base grows, the volume of requests also grows. Hence, your platform should make it easy to upgrade to a higher plan as requests grow.
Most support platforms are cloud-based, so scalability is not much of a concern for businesses. These platforms are often priced per seat, wherein you pay a monthly or annual fee for each support agent in your company. If you hire more support agents, you can create new accounts for them and integrate their work with the existing team.
2. Ease of use
Agents spend all working hours on your support platform. A complex interface can make their work much more difficult and dampen productivity. You need a support platform with an intuitive, easily navigable interface. It should be simple enough for a support agent to master within a short period.
Support platforms offer free trials, so always take advantage of them to test the interface before making a final decision. If it’s overtly difficult for IT administrators to navigate, it’ll be even more difficult for less tech-savvy support agents.
You can run trials with your support team and get their honest opinion – they’re the ones who will spend most time on the software, after all. If their opinions are overwhelmingly negative, it’s a signal to find an alternative platform that won’t cause headaches in the long run.
3. Pricing
Support software is available in all price ranges, from affordable tools priced per agent to custom solutions tailored for large enterprises. You should find one that suits your price point and needs.
Selecting support software involves striking a balance between pricing and the features you desire. Find one that fits within your budget, but remember that the cheapest solution isn’t always the best. Compare prices between different competitors and ensure you get the best deal.
Support platforms for small to medium-sized businesses are priced monthly or annually, based on the number of support agents. Some charge fixed monthly or annual fees per agent, e.g., $10 per agent per month. Others offer monthly packages for a specific number of agents, such as $500 per month for 75 agents.
Platforms designed for large enterprises offer custom pricing. If you represent a large company, you can negotiate directly with the platform’s sales team and snag the best deal.
As mentioned, you should take advantage of free trials to test a support tool before making your final decision. Support platforms usually offer a refund window, ranging from 30 to 60 days, but it’s better to avoid paying for something you don’t like and going through the stress of requesting a refund.
4. Security features
We’ve mentioned security being a core feature of a support platform. Before selecting a support tool, research its security features, including encryption protocols, access controls, backup policies, and compliance with industry standards.
Read reviews and online articles to evaluate a platform’s security history. Your support tool shouldn’t have a history of lax security practices or data breaches.
You also play a major role in keeping your support platform secure. Train support employees on standard security practices, enable multi-factor authentication for all accounts, implement robust access controls, conduct regular security audits, and have a firm plan to respond to security incidents.
5. Support quality
Ironically, a customer support software provider needs to offer excellent support. You should be able to contact them via email, live chat, or telephone and get swift answers.
Support isn’t only about quick responses – the support team should be knowledgeable and willing to help you resolve issues. Often, businesses need help in the initial setup, and the team should be prepared to provide guidance.
You should have access to detailed documentation and a Knowledge Base. When facing issues, you can first consult the Knowledge Base before seeking direct support if that isn’t enough. The free trial presents the best opportunity to test a platform’s support resources before making your final decision.
6. Automation & AI functionalities
Artificial intelligence (AI) is a nascent technology, yet it has made a dent in many software niches, including customer support. You need AI features that help boost your support team’s productivity– not having these features puts you at a competitive disadvantage.
For example, support tools can utilize AI to generate summaries of customer inquiries. Summarizing lengthy tickets saves support agents a considerable amount of time.
Your platform can also use AI to analyze support requests and automatically route them to the relevant agent or team. Likewise, AI can draft responses to mundane customer inquiries, and support agents can make the final edits, saving them time and effort.
AI is a force multiplier for your customer support team, not something you should depend on entirely. Customers can get annoyed if they are mostly directed to chatbots instead of human help.
The idea is to use chatbots to resolve simple inquiries, such as order tracking for an e-commerce business, while support agents focus on more challenging problems.
7. Omnichannel support
Omnichannel support involves managing and responding to customer requests across multiple channels, including social media, email, phone, SMS, and web forms. The best businesses offer omnichannel support to keep customers engaged regardless of how they contact their support team for inquiries. Hence, omnichannel integration should be a core consideration when selecting support software.
Your platform should provide a unified view of all customer inquiries, regardless of the channel from which they originated. This way, agents can view the full history of every request and respond to them from a single dashboard, rather than juggling different tools, which can sap productivity.
While you manage responses from multiple channels, you should be able to measure performance for each channel. For example, you can compare the average ticket resolution times for email requests, live chat, and telephone. This comparison tells you which channel support agents are most productive with, and you can dedicate more resources to that channel.
Final words
Customer support software can make or break a business. Making the right choice helps you build long-term trust and customer loyalty. We’ve explained the core features of a customer support tool and the factors to consider when choosing one. Follow these guidelines to select the best tool for your business and enhance your bottom line.
For more ways to improve support, we've tested the best help desk software, the best call center software, and the best CRM tools.

articles.title: How PUBG Mobile aims to level up esports across the globe
articles.text:
You probably don’t know it, but the world of PUBG Mobile esports is huge. For events like the PUBG Mobile World Cup (PMWC) in Paris, millions of dollars are spent on prize pools and logistics, while tens of thousands attend in person and millions more tune in from home.
To learn more about what goes into all of this, MobileSyrup spoke with Alban Dechelotte, CEO of major esports brand G2, and Sivan Chen, publishing director of PUBG Mobile. Over email, the pair unpacked common misconceptions surrounding esports, their collaboration to expand PUBG Mobile esports around the world and where they hope to see the game go in the years to come.
What are common misconceptions that you hear about esports?
Alban Dechelotte: One misconception is that esports is a digital version of traditional sport. It is its own form of
competition, with its own culture, audiences and ways of building fandom. When traditional sports organizations treat it only as a simulation of what they already do, they can miss the opportunity to reach completely different communities.
You also still hear the stereotype that esports athletes just sit in front of a screen all day and do not take their health seriously. At the highest level, that could not be further from reality. Training, recovery, nutrition and physical and mental fitness all matter. At G2, we are taking that further through the G2 Performance Lab, because unlike traditional sport, esports still does not have decades of established performance science behind it. There is a real opportunity to build that understanding from the ground up.
Sivan Chen: Some still have the idea that esports is somehow less impressive or less “real” than traditional sports. Of course, for the average person, they don’t see the behind-the-scenes of the qualifiers, the finals, the team organizations, support staff, and all the rigorous training players and backup players go through. There’s an entire infrastructure behind the scenes that mirrors, and in some ways exceeds, what you’d find in traditional sports.
The second misconception is that the scene is small and under-invested. That’s just not true anymore, at least not for PUBG Mobile. Our two flagship events, the PUBG Mobile World Cup (PMWC) and PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC), each individually carry a US$3 million prize annually, and that’s on top of strong prize pools running through local and regional tournaments. What we’ve built is a full, extensive ecosystem, from grassroots all the way up to a global championship.
When I talk to a lot of people, even on the gamer’s side, they don’t know much about PUBG Mobile. I have to explain to them that it’s very much still popular, especially in Asia. To what do you attribute this enduring popularity of the game, especially in Asian markets?
Dechelotte: Accessibility is a huge part of it. Mobile is the dominant gaming platform across much of Asia, and PUBG Mobile is free-to-play, so the barrier to getting involved is incredibly low. But accessibility only gets people through the door. The game has stayed relevant because it keeps evolving through regular content, while the competitive ecosystem gives players and fans something bigger to connect with. When you combine those things, you have a strong foundation for long-term popularity.
Chen: A big part of it is simply that mobile phones are already in everyone’s pocket across the region. We’re not asking players to buy expensive new hardware; it’s a completely free app, meaning we’re simply offering a quick download to access everything PUBG Mobile has to offer. On top of that, we have an upcoming update that will further address accessibility on devices, so keep an eye out for that!
Beyond that, accessibility is really the foundation of everything we do on the esports side. That’s everything from making sure the game runs well and is easy to pick up on any smartphone, to building in-game registration systems that make signing up for tournaments simpler and quicker. We’ve seen players of all abilities pick up their phone and engage with the action-packed ecosystem we’ve crafted over time, which speaks to the work we’ve done behind the scenes.
Esports in general is something that a lot of people don’t know much about, and I’d suspect even less so for mobile esports. What goes into the mobile format vs. console/PC?
Dechelotte: The fundamentals are the same: these are elite players training to perform under pressure, but
the demands of the game and the device are different. On mobile, you are dealing with a handheld device, so posture, ergonomics and managing physical strain become really important over long training periods. The game can also evolve quickly, so players have to be extremely adaptable when the meta changes. That means the way you structure practice, recovery and performance support can’t be copied across from PC or console — it has to reflect how mobile players actually compete.
Chen: Preparing and running mobile esports tournaments takes a significant amount of preparation, with even more potential players feeding into the pro scene due to the lower barrier to entry. Managing this and ensuring that hopeful amateur and grassroots players have the chance to break into the scene has been a key focus for us, which is why we’ve consistently developed our approach to account for the road to pro play that players walk.
For instance, we created an accessible and dedicated platform for third-party tournaments to be organized, allowing organizers to get support in creating more grassroots events where players can get an opportunity to shine. We also shifted our major tournament circuit, introducing a second PMGO that players can access through open qualifiers to get more amateurs on the global stage. This has been a long journey that PUBG Mobile Esports has been embarking on for years, and we’re still introducing new ways for players around the world to get involved with the competitive experience.
How did you start partnering together, and what does that ongoing collaboration look
like?
Dechelotte: The partnership started from a shared ambition to grow competitive mobile esports in Western Europe. PUBG Mobile already has the global ecosystem and expertise, while G2 has spent the last decade building esports communities in this region and understanding how to turn competition into fandom. That made the fit quite natural.
The important part for us is that this is not about one campaign or one tournament. We want to help create a long-term home for PUBG Mobile Esports audiences in Western Europe through competition, creators, content and community experiences. Our media house, 62, delivering PMCO Western Europe, is a good example of what that looks like in practice — we are actively helping build the ecosystem around the partnership.
Chen: We knew that expansion in Western Europe would be best achieved by connecting with an established partner with an authentic relationship with their community. PUBG Mobile offers the most popular global mobile battle royale esports ecosystem; however this mobile esports scene still hasn’t developed to its full potential in Western Europe, and G2 has a history of experience in the region. G2’s expansive community fits naturally with PUBG Mobile’s huge global player base, so it just made sense to take on G2’s considerable industry knowledge when continuing our expansion to create a dedicated community in Western Europe.
We’ve already kicked off an ambassador program, with JanickaGaming being the first creator, but we intend to continue building out with more ambassadors from the region. We’re also holding the 2026 PUBG Mobile Global Open Western Europe Finals, with a slot in the 2026 PUBG Mobile Global Open Season 2 available to the winners. G2 has demonstrated their commitment to developing the esports ecosystem in Western Europe with these activations, and we’re looking forward to continuing to work together in this partnership.
I know you’re talking about Western Europe. Our audience is primarily North American — particularly Canada. What can you say about supporting grassroots initiatives or similar efforts in that market?
Dechelotte: Grassroots development is something we have invested in across different games and regions. In North America, for example, our partnership with Stride in 2023 supported the Rocket League community and helped create more opportunities around the competitive scene. More recently in Europe, we launched G2 NORD to give young talent a high-performance academy environment and a clearer development pathway.
The game and the market might change, but the principle is the same: healthy esports ecosystems need opportunities below the very top level. Players need somewhere to develop, compete and see a realistic path forward. That is what keeps new talent coming through and gives fans new stories and personalities to follow.
Chen: We have a couple of pathways built specifically for this. Our Third-Party Tournament Program gives local organizers the licensing, assets, and support they need to run their own PUBG Mobile esports tournaments. We recently streamlined that system to make it even easier for anyone to get one off the ground. On the competitive side, our 2026 PUBG Mobile Global Open (PMGO) Season 1 and Season 2 tournaments offer key pathways for players globally. That means amateur players there have a real route to climb the ladder and eventually compete against seasoned veterans.
Where do you hope to see the PUBG Mobile esports market globally over the next few years?
Dechelotte: PUBG Mobile has already shown what mobile esports can look like at scale in Asia. Over the next few years, I would love to see Europe close some of that gap – not by copying another region, but by building an ecosystem that makes sense for European players and fans. That means stronger grassroots pathways, more opportunities to experience major competitions locally, and creators and teams helping make the scene culturally relevant. If we can build those foundations properly, there is a huge amount of room to grow.
Chen: We’re currently running two PMGO seasons a year, available in more than 200 countries and regions, and we’ve already seen over 1 million sign-ups in 2026 alone. That scale is something we want to keep building on. Ultimately, our goal is to be the most-participated global esports ecosystem. We’ve made great headway with viewership, as seen in the 2026 PMWC, but we’re continuing to build on engaging players worldwide. The collaboration with G2 in Western Europe is a good example of the kind of investment we want to keep making in new markets, and we’re looking to continue developing this globally in the future.
PUBG Mobile is free-to-play on Android and iOS. More information on PUBG Mobile esports can be found on the game’s official website.

articles.title: Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird
articles.text:
Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird
Router vernetzen zahlreiche Haushalte mit dem Internet. Sie können aber schnell zum Einfallstor für Cyberkriminelle werden, wenn du nicht die richtigen Einstellungen am Router vornimmst. Gleiches gilt, wenn es eine Lücke im System der Router gibt, die lange Zeit unerkannt bleibt. So soll es laut einem Sicherheitsforscher schon seit 2010 der Fall sein. Laut ihm sind von der Lücke potenziell Millionen Geräte betroffen.
Neue Router-Sicherheitslücke: Welche Gefahr droht
Die Warnung stammt vom belgischen Sicherheitsforscher Quentin Kaiser, der die Sicherheitslücke „WPSplinter“ getauft hat. Im Grunde handelt es sich dabei um zwei Fehler, die in der Software von Broadcom zu finden sind. Broadcoms Wi-Fi-Implementierung wird laut Kaiser von dutzenden Routerherstellern genutzt. Dadurch finden sich die Fehler in hunderten Produkten und potenziell in „Millionen von Broadcom-basierten Access-Points weltweit“.
Die Fehler sorgen dafür, dass sich Unbefugte über WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) Zugriff auf die Router verschaffen können. Über das Feature können Endgeräte und Router ohne Passworteingabe miteinander verknüpft werden, indem eine WPS-Taste auf dem Router gedrückt wird, während das Endgerät ebenfalls einen WPS-Prozess startet. Laut Kaiser kann eine manipulierte WPS-Nachricht eingeschleust werden, um den Speicher der Router zu verändern.
Dadurch können Angreifer:innen, falls sie sich in Reichweite des WLAN-Signals des Routers befinden, eigenen Code ausführen. In seinen Tests war Kaiser so etwa in der Lage, auf dem Gerät ein Wi-Fi-Passwort aus dem Speicher zu extrahieren und es anschließend zu benutzen, um sich in das Netzwerk einzuklinken. Die User:innen würden davon nichts mitbekommen, wenn sie nicht regelmäßig auf die Liste verbundener Geräte schauen.
Kaiser hat Broadcom mit seinen Funden konfrontiert. Laut dem Unternehmen war das Problem schon seit 2010 bekannt und wurde mit einem Fix 2018 ohne öffentliche Meldung behoben. Doch offenbar war die Lösung damals nicht ausreichend. Die neue Lücke adressierte Broadcom bislang nicht und verwies auf die einzelnen Hersteller. Kaiser wandte sich deshalb auch an eine Reihe von Herstellern in Belgien sowie belgische Behörden für Cybersecurity. Bis zu seiner Veröffentlichung hatte er von keiner der Parteien eine Reaktion erhalten.
Der Sicherheitsforscher sieht trotz der ausbleibenden Reaktionen ein enormes Risiko für Anwender:innen. Bei betroffenen Routern müssten sich die Angreifer nur vor der Wohnung oder dem Haus befinden, um in Reichweite des Netzwerkes zu gelangen. Auf der GitHub-Seite zu seinem Fund aktualisiert er regelmäßig eine Liste mit Routern, die von dem Bug betroffen sind. So können User:innen selbst nachschauen, ob potenziell Gefahr besteht.

articles.title: Spotify : cette nouvelle vérification va faire une hécatombe sur les partages de compte
articles.text:
Le partage de compte et les règles des plateformes de streaming : une histoire qui semble ne jamais finir. Justement, Spotify a décidé de sévir concernant son abonnement Premium Famille, qui permet de partager un compte Premium avec les membres de sa famille qui « vivent sous le même toit ». La plateforme de streaming musical semble estimer que trop de personnes partagent un compte Famille Premium, sans vivre sous le même toit. Elle a donc décidé de mettre en place un nouveau système de vérification.
Un QR code dynamique à scanner
Spotify a décidé de s’attaquer aux personnes qui partagent un abonnement Premium Famille, sans vivre sous le même toit. Comme le rapporte Android Authority, des utilisateurs de Reddit signalent une demande de vérification de la part de la plateforme de streaming musical. Pour être plus précis, ceux qui bénéficient d’un abonnement Premium Famille doivent scanner un QR code avec le propriétaire du compte Premium.
Point important : il s’agit d’un QR code dynamique, autrement dit, il est renouvelé toutes les quelques secondes, ce qui complique sensiblement la réalisation d’une capture d’écran pour ensuite le scanner. De ce fait, ce système de vérification par scan de QR code dynamique permet de vérifier que les deux personnes se situent à proximité l’une de l’autre, et donc vivent bel et bien sous le même toit.
Ceux qui ne scannent pas le QR code seront banni de l’abonnement Famille Premium
D’après la documentation d’assistance de Spotify, les personnes qui reçoivent cette notification de vérification disposent de 7 jours pour scanner le QR code. Ceux qui ne s’y soumettent pas seront bannis automatiquement de l’abonnement Premium Famille en cours, tandis que leur compte basculera sur l’offre gratuite financée par la publicité. Mais cela n’est pas tout puisqu’ils ne pourront plus rejoindre un autre abonnement Premium Famille (ou un abonnement Premium Duo) pendant une période de 12 mois. À noter toutefois que certains utilisateurs parviendraient à contourner ce système de vérification en partageant leur écran pour scanner le QR code.
