articles.title: Jio Platforms' anchor book draws Rs 2.5 lakh crore in bids ahead of IPO
articles.text:
Jio Platforms' anchor book draws Rs 2.5 lakh crore in bids ahead of IPO
Jio Platforms allotted 7.24 crore shares at a price of Rs 1,119 per share to the anchor investors and LIC received the largest allocation
Jio Platforms has allotted shares worth Rs 8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at the top end of its price band, after institutional demand for the offering exceeded Rs 2.5 lakh crore, more than 30 times the amount available in the anchor book, according to a stock exchange filing and people familiar with the matter.
The allotment of 7.24 crore shares at Rs 1,119 apiece comes ahead of the initial public offering that opens for public subscription on Wednesday.
The strong demand underscores institutional investor interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO, although the extent to which it translates into broader public demand will become clearer once the offer opens.
Life Insurance Corporation of India received the largest allocation, worth Rs 499.98 crore, accounting for 6.17 per cent of the anchor portion.
New World Fund Inc was allotted shares worth Rs 486.27 crore, followed by the Government of Singapore at Rs 340.93 crore, SBI Focused Fund at Rs 315 crore and BNP Paribas Financial Markets - ODI at Rs 303.25 crore.
Domestic mutual funds received 2.489 crore shares worth Rs 2,784.96 crore, representing 34.34 per cent of the anchor book, through 95 schemes across 25 fund houses. Life insurers and pension funds received 97.4 lakh shares worth Rs 1,089.95 crore, or 13.44 per cent of the total.
Both categories exceeded the allocations reserved for them under the red herring prospectus dated October 14, which earmarked 33.33 per cent of the anchor portion for mutual funds and 6.67 per cent for insurers and pension funds.
Global investment firms participating in the anchor book include BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson.
Sovereign and public investment institutions include the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and the Monetary Authority of Singapore, alongside other long-term institutional investors.
Some large overseas and domestic institutions bid for allocations worth $750 million to more than $1 billion each, people familiar with the matter said.
Jio Platforms is seeking to raise about Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, at a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece. The offering values the company at around USD 108 billion, according to the offer documents.
The IPO will open on October 21 and close on October 23.

articles.title: Panne mondiale chez Revolut : des millions de personnes ont perdu leur moyen de paiement
articles.text:
Panne mondiale chez Revolut : des millions de personnes ont perdu leur moyen de paiement
Depuis ce mardi 20 octobre au matin, la banque en ligne Revolut subit une panne mondiale, empêchant ses clients de régler leurs achats. La firme assure être sur le coup.
C'est un coup très dur depuis ce matin pour les millions de clients de Revolut. La banque en ligne rencontre une panne depuis plusieurs heures dans le monde entier, empêchant les utilisateurs grand public et les sociétés d'accéder à leur argent, ou même de régler leurs achats. La firme assure travailler sur un correctif, tandis que le véritable coupable ne serait autre que Google Cloud.
Revolut en panne, Google en cause ?
D'après les premiers témoignages sur Downdetector, les problèmes ont commencé autour de 8h ce matin. Plusieurs pays européens et ailleurs dans le monde, dont la France, sont concernés. Revolut aurait aujourd'hui 80 millions de clients.
Sur X, la néobanque indique depuis 10h ce matin :“Nous rencontrons actuellement une interruption de service qui affecte plusieurs de nos services. Nous pouvons vous assurer que l'argent et les données de tous nos clients sont en sécurité. Nous travaillons à la résolution du problème depuis qu'il a été identifié ce matin et nous présentons nos excuses à toutes les personnes concernées pour les désagréments occasionnés.”
We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe. We’ve been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience…
— Revolut (@Revolut) October 20, 2026
Sur la page dédiée au statut de ses différents services, c'est l'hécatombe : les 31 services de la banque en ligne sont en panne. Pas étonnant donc que de très nombreux clients ne puissent pas utiliser l'application de Revolut ou encore payer. Nul doute que bon nombre de clients ont dû être incommodés aujourd'hui par ce dernier fait, toujours en cours en milieu d'après-midi.
Selon certaines informations, provenant notamment de Sky News, le problème viendrait d'un prestataire tiers, et pas des moindres : Google Cloud. Sur Downdetector toujours, une panne semble bel et bien toucher le service de Google utilisé par de nombreuses personnes et applications. Il ne s'agit donc probablement pas d'une cyberattaque, tandis que la situation semble doucement revenir à la normale chez les services impactés.
L'origine de cette panne reste cependant à confirmer, tandis que les clients de Revolut ne peuvent que prendre leur mal en patience pour le moment.

articles.title: La Guardia Civil compra por 2,5 millones un sistema para acceder de forma remota a móviles Android y iPhone
articles.text:
La Guardia Civil ha comprado una herramienta diseñada para registrar de forma remota los móviles de las personas que se encuentren bajo investigación, sin necesidad de incautar los dispositivos. El contrato, publicado en el BOE, ofrece pocos detalles técnicos, pero sí revela lo que el sistema es capaz de hacer.
Espionaje a distancia. Según el contrato, la herramienta funciona tanto en Android como en iOS. La idea es que el sistema pueda ser capaz de alojar software en los teléfonos objetivo y proporcionar un “acceso transparente” a sus contenidos y comunicaciones. O lo que es lo mismo, que las autoridades puedan acceder a toda la información del teléfono sin que la persona se de cuenta.
Normalmente, la forma de proceder es incautar un teléfono móvil y proceder al análisis del mismo, una vez confiscado. Sin embargo, esta herramienta se ahorraría bastantes pasos.
El acuerdo. Tal y como señala la publicación en el BOE, el contrato fue adjudicado el 26 de marzo de 2026 a Fortier Europe, una empresa con sede en Boadilla del Monte, Madrid. El precio por el que la Guardia Civil compró el software fue de 2.066.115,70 euros antes de IVA (unos 2,5 millones de euros incluyendo impuestos).
El contrato se negoció sin licitación pública y solo se recibió una oferta. Tiene sentido teniendo en cuenta que el anuncio dice que el fabricante había concedido los derechos exclusivos de suministro y distribución a la empresa mencionada.
Lo que no sabemos. Los documentos publicados no mencionan al fabricante ni detallan las características específicas del producto. Tampoco explican cómo se instalaría el software en un teléfono, ni si se llegaría a necesitar acceso físico al dispositivo. Que no contemos con esta información nos deja dudas acerca del alcance de la herramienta.
Lo que dice la ley. Disponer de la herramienta no significa que los agentes puedan registrar el teléfono de cualquier persona. La Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal (LECrim) de España permite registros remotos únicamente con autorización judicial. Tal como cuenta El Confidencial Digital, la ley permite a un juez aprobar un software que examine un dispositivo de forma remota y sin el conocimiento de su propietario, pero solo para una lista cerrada de delitos:
- Delitos cometidos en el seno de organizaciones criminales.
- Terrorismo.
- Delitos contra menores o personas con capacidad modificada judicialmente.
- Delitos contra la Constitución, traición y delitos relacionados con la defensa nacional.
- Delitos cometidos a través de tecnologías informáticas o de telecomunicación.
Los límites. La orden judicial debe especificar qué dispositivos se ven afectados, cómo se accederá a los datos y se incautarán, qué agentes pueden llevar a cabo la medida y cómo se protegerá la integridad de los datos. Esta medida dura como máximo un mes, prorrogable por periodos iguales hasta un máximo de tres meses, según cuentan desde el medio.
Quién es el proveedor. Fortier Europe fue fundada en marzo de 2011 y aparece regularmente en los contratos del Ministerio del Interior. El Digital de Albacete informa de al menos 13 contratos por valor de unos 15,6 millones de euros antes de IVA. En sus adjudicaciones de este año se incluyen un contrato de 743.802 euros para dos sistemas portátiles para localizar dispositivos móviles y extraer información de ellos, y un contrato de 495.570 euros para dispositivos de captura de audio y GPS. Los registros también muestran un acuerdo de mantenimiento de la Guardia Civil en 2020 para la plataforma EGOBOX.

articles.title: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to backdoor WordPress sites
articles.text:
A threat actor breached TeamUpdraft's website, a developer of popular WordPress backup and security plugins, potentially compromising UpdraftCentral connection keys that can send commands to connected websites.
TeamUpdraft detected unauthorized access to its infrastructure over the weekend and believes that the hacker accessed the customer database.
The developer offers several WordPress tools for backup, storage, and site management:
- UpdraftPlus: website backup and restoration plugin with more than 4 million downloads
- UpdraftCentral: for managing multiple sites remotely
- UpdraftVault: for cloud backup storage
- UpdraftClone: for creating staging websites
"Over the weekend of 17-18 October we identified unauthorised access to the teamupdraft.com website," TeamUpdraft said in an advisory yesterday.
"Our team responded straight away and worked through the night to contain it – we closed the access route, signed out every account and replaced the keys and credentials that could have been affected."
The vendor says it believes the threat actor accessed its customer database, which included details about the customer and billing, order history, as well as more sensitive information:
- password hashes
- two-factor authentication settings
- connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone services
The vendor said it did not store any payment details and noted that UpdraftPlus plugin files and downloads remain unaffected. Self-hosted UpdraftCentral instances are not impacted.
Even if backups in customers' own remote storage are unaffected, the company recommends that users rotate storage credentials and reauthorize connections if they accessed their site through UpdraftCentral.
Massive blast radius
An estimated 10% of sites using UpdraftPlus have an UpdraftCentral or Migrator key, potentially exposing around 400,000 websites to the attack.
According to Patchstack lead researcher Oliver Sild, attackers have begun using stolen access keys to backdoor sites connected to UpdraftCentral, saying the campaign may be more severe than the "wp2shell” attack.
The WordPress plugin security company says that the attacks started on October 18 at 15:32 UTC to execute arbitrary code and add accounts with full administrator privileges.
The researchers logged at least 99 malicious backdoor plugins with distinct names disguised as WordPress maintenance and optimization tools, such as “Site Health Cache.”
Although Patchstack describes an early variant of the backdoor plugin that is broken due to a coding error, a report from web application security firm Nethemba documents a newer version that lets attackers create privileged accounts or log in as existing administrators.
Nethemba says three of its own WordPress websites were targeted through UpdraftCentral, with malicious plugins successfully installed on two of them.
“All three sites ran the current WordPress 7.1.3 and UpdraftPlus 2.26.11, which is patched against the June vulnerability CVE-2026-10795,” Nethemba says.
“The attacker did not break into our servers and did not exploit any weakness in our configuration. The attacker came in through the UpdraftCentral remote management channel and signed the commands with valid private dashboard keys”
Nethemba reports that the vendor's initial 1.26.12/2.26.12 release was meant to remove UpdraftCentral Cloud keys, but a bug prevented it from doing so.
Users are recommended to update UpdraftPlus to 1.26.13 (free) / 2.26.13 (Premium) or later.
After updating, it is recommended to log into each WordPress site and delete the UpdraftCentral connection keys from Settings → UpdraftPlus Backups → Advanced Tools → UpdraftCentral → Manage existing keys.
Administrators should inspect logs and files for indicators of compromise provided by TeamUpdraft, Patchstack, and Nethemba.
If compromise is confirmed, it is recommended to restore sites from clean backups, change the TeamUpdraft account password, revoke all sessions, and reset the two-factor authentication protection method.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked

articles.title: Revolut, Lloyds, HSBC… les banques britanniques dans la tourmente, un incident Google Cloud ?
articles.text:
Outre Revolut, d’autres banques britanniques comme Lloyds, HSBC ou NatWest enregistrent ce mardi une vague de signalements. Au même moment, Google Cloud reconnaît un incident d’ampleur sur ses serveurs de Londres, sans en préciser l’origine.
La panne de Revolut, qui bloque depuis ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 les cartes et application de nombreux clients jusqu'en France, pourrait bien n'être que la partie visible de l'immense iceberg qui cache les banques… britanniques. Oui, Outre-Manche, les signalements grimpent aussi chez Lloyds, HSBC, NatWest ou Santander, pour une matinée du 20 octobre 2026 franchement agitée. En coulisses, un nom revient avec insistance, celui de Google Cloud, qui admet de sérieux déboires dans ses installations londoniennes.
Après Revolut, plusieurs grandes banques britanniques en panne
Chez Revolut, la journée a mal débuté. Dès 8 heures, l'application affichait un message d'erreur, la carte était refusée au supermarché ou dans un taxi, et les virements impossibles. Les plaintes ont afflué du Royaume-Uni, son pays d'origine, mais aussi de France où la banque compte plus de 8 millions de clients, d'Espagne, d'Allemagne ou de Grèce, et l'offre Revolut Business n'est pas épargnée. L'entreprise a reconnu une interruption touchant plusieurs fonctionnalités, sans avancer ni cause ni horaire. Sa page de statut, restée au vert une bonne partie de la matinée, affichait au dernier relevé ses 31 services comme indisponibles, même si certains clients arrivent encore à payer en magasin.
Sur Downdetector, le site qui agrège les signalements d'internautes, la version britannique affiche en tête de sa page d'accueil un trio éloquent avec Revolut, Lloyds Bank, HSBC et, un peu plus loin, Google et Google Cloud. Bank of Scotland est aussi passée au rouge, tout comme Halifax, Scottish Widows, MBNA, NatWest et Santander UK, qui présentaient encore tout à l'heure des pics suspects. Or Lloyds, Halifax, Bank of Scotland, Scottish Widows et MBNA appartiennent toutes au même groupe bancaire.
Les opérateurs télécoms (BT, EE, Vodafone, O2) ne présentent aucune anomalie. Ce ne serait donc pas l'internet britannique qui cale, mais plutôt des services hébergés quelque part. Le désordre dépasse d'ailleurs le cadre bancaire, avec des signalements chez Royal Mail, Rightmove ou sur le portail gouvernemental GOV.UK.
Le cloud de Google sous les projecteurs
Ce « quelque part » pourrait bien s'appeler europe-west2, la région londonienne de Google Cloud, autrement dit un ensemble de centres de données où les entreprises louent serveurs et stockage. Google y signale un incident depuis 8h08, heure de Paris, et liste une trentaine de produits touchés, avec les machines virtuelles, bases de données, stockage et réseau. La seule consigne concrète, ajoutée à 11h24, est destinée aux entreprises clientes : déplacer, si elles le peuvent, leurs applications vers une autre zone ou une autre région. Une région se découpe en effet en plusieurs « zones », des compartiments isolés les uns des autres pour limiter la casse en cas d'incident, et Google ne précise pas lesquelles sont touchées. Sur Reddit, un administrateur système affirme que les problèmes se concentrent sur l'une d'elles, europe-west2-b, les autres restant accessibles.
Or ces briques forment les fondations de n'importe quelle application. Une banque dont les serveurs tournent à cet endroit peut perdre d'un coup l'accès à ses données et la capacité de valider un paiement, ce qui expliquerait une carte refusée en caisse. Le calendrier coïncide à peu de chose près avec les premiers déboires de Revolut, et une panne cantonnée à une seule zone éclairerait aussi pourquoi tous les clients ne sont pas logés à la même enseigne.
Attention toutefois, car ni Google ni les banques concernées n'ont officiellement établi de lien, et rien ne garantit qu'elles soient toutes hébergées chez le même fournisseur. Downdetector a aussi ses biais, comme en témoignent les pics affichés par AWS ou Azure, parfois signalés par simple réflexe un jour de grosse panne. Google, qui n'a toujours livré ni cause ni horaire de rétablissement, promet un nouveau point vers 13 heures. Sa région londonienne avait déjà vacillé en 2020 puis en 2024, rappel assez cru qu'une seule région cloud peut suffire à gripper une partie du système bancaire, surtout quand le plan B consiste à déménager en pleine tempête.

articles.title: Console portable Xbox : pourquoi elle n'utilisera pas Windows — Frandroid
articles.text:
Malgré des vagues de licenciement sans fin et des chiffres de vente décevants, Xbox tient toujours debout et ne compte pas se laisser devancer dans la course aux consoles de nouvelle génération. D’après le magazine Fortune, qui a interviewé sa PDG, Asha Sharma, une console portable serait prévue pour 2027, avec des petites surprises côté logiciel.
Si la ROG Xbox Ally tournait avec une version sur-mesure de Windows, la prochaine console 100 % Microsoft pourrait arriver avec son propre système d’exploitation, faisant la nique au reste de la firme.
Une guerre fratricide
Le futur gadget aurait en effet ravivé une certaine rivalité entre les équipes responsables de Windows et celles travaillant chez Xbox. Les premières auraient fait pression sur les secondes pour que l’appareil embarque une déclinaison « light » de Windows Home. En face, l’idée était plutôt de construire son propre système d’exploitation afin de coller au mieux aux exigences techniques de la console et d’en tirer les meilleures performances.
Le conflit aurait tant gonflé que des responsables du projet auraient carrément menacé d’enterrer la future console portable si on les forçait à y installer Windows. Une menace qui a porté ses fruits, puisque les équipes de Xbox auraient désormais carte blanche pour développer leur propre solution logicielle, explique Fortune. Histoire d’arrondir les angles, la PDG explique tout de même que les équipes collaborent, puisque Xbox « ne peut pas s’attaquer au projet Helix seul ».
Cette guerre qui a failli coûter la vie à la prochaine console Xbox rappelle les grandes heures de Microsoft, où chaque équipe regardait les autres en chien de faïence en développant les choses de son côté. L’autonomie qu’a gagnée Xbox ces derniers mois (à tel point qu’une scission de la branche gaming semble possible) n’a rien dû arranger de ce point de vue-là.
La supériorité de Linux
Pour autant, les inquiétudes de l’équipe Xbox ne venaient pas de nulle part. Sur les consoles portables actuelles, Linux a prouvé sa supériorité en termes de performance, à tel point que beaucoup ont entrepris d’installer SteamOS sur leur ROG Ally afin d’en tirer pleinement parti.
    Pour aller plus loin
J’ai installé SteamOS sur ma ROG Xbox Ally : pourquoi je ne reviendrai plus en arrière
            
Si Windows est encore considéré comme le système d’exploitation par défaut pour les joueurs et joueuses convaincues, Linux lui grignote gentiment des parts de marché pendant que Microsoft tente désespérément d’alléger l’empreinte mémoire de son OS pour le maintenir pertinent sur un marché plus concurrentiel que prévu.

articles.title: Un agricultor halló en su campo de maíz en Minnesota los restos de un cohete chino de 3,35 metros
articles.text:
Un agricultor del condado de Stevens, en Minnesota, encontró un objeto metálico circular de 3,35 metros de diámetro mientras cosechaba maíz el 14 de octubre. El análisis de Ars Technica concluyó que se trata de la etapa superior de un cohete chino Zhuque-2E.
La Oficina del Sheriff del condado de Stevens recibió el aviso ese mismo día y confirmó el hallazgo en Scott Township, una zona rural al oeste del estado. “Los agentes confirmaron que había un objeto metálico grande, de unos 3,35 metros de diámetro, presuntamente un objeto espacial”, informó la oficina en un comunicado.
Las autoridades trabajan junto a agencias estatales y federales para identificar al dueño del objeto y coordinar su retiro del campo, aunque no precisaron una fecha para completar esa tarea. Según informaron, el objeto no representó ningún peligro para la población mientras permaneció en el terreno.
Un cohete que recorrió medio planeta antes de caer
El 15 de septiembre, un cohete Zhuque-2E de la empresa china LandSpace despegó desde Dongfeng, una zona de lanzamientos comerciales ubicada junto al centro militar de Jiuquan, en el noroeste de China. Media hora después del despegue, liberó diez satélites en una órbita polar circular de unos 900 kilómetros de altitud.
Los satélites pertenecen a la red Qianfan, también llamada “Mil Velas”, el proyecto con el que China busca competir con Starlink, la constelación de SpaceX. Desde 2024, el país lanzó 258 satélites Qianfan, con el objetivo de llegar a 1.296 unidades y, a largo plazo, superar los 15.000.
Después de soltar su carga, la etapa superior del cohete encendió otra vez su motor para reducir la velocidad y salir de órbita, sin completar una vuelta entera a la Tierra. El vuelo duró entre 75 y 80 minutos y recorrió medio planeta: despegó en el desierto de Gobi, sobrevoló la Antártida y cruzó América.
Esa misma noche, usuarios de redes sociales registraron estelas de fuego que cruzaban el cielo sobre Kansas rumbo a Minnesota, visibles también desde Wisconsin. Según Ars Technica, el horario, la trayectoria y la dirección de esos registros permitieron vincular la caída con el lanzamiento del Zhuque-2E.
El diámetro de la etapa superior del cohete coincide de forma exacta con el del objeto hallado en el campo de maíz.
Un diseño pensado para caer en el océano
Lo inusual del caso, según el sitio especializado, es el tamaño del resto recuperado, mayor al de la mayoría de los objetos que sobreviven a la reentrada, y el hecho de que haya caído el mismo día del lanzamiento.
Nunca antes una persona sufrió heridas graves por la caída de basura espacial, aunque sí existen antecedentes de daños materiales. El derecho internacional establece que el país responsable de un lanzamiento debe responder por los daños que un objeto espacial cause en tierra.
La práctica habitual para desechar una etapa de cohete es dirigirla hacia una reentrada controlada sobre el océano, lo que sugiere que lo ocurrido el 15 de septiembre fue resultado de una maniobra de desorbitado fallida. LandSpace no se pronunció públicamente sobre la caída del resto en Minnesota.
En teoría, deshacerse de una etapa gastada apenas termina su misión es una práctica responsable que limita la generación de basura espacial. Pero los cohetes chinos ya habían generado inconvenientes similares.
La etapa superior del vuelo anterior del Zhuque-2E, en junio, se fragmentó tras cumplir su misión y dejó decenas de piezas de basura en una zona de la órbita baja terrestre muy transitada, donde operan la Estación Espacial Internacional y buena parte de los satélites Starlink.
Los cohetes estadounidenses que cumplen misiones en órbita baja suelen reservar combustible para una disposición guiada hacia el reingreso, algo que no ocurrió con el vuelo de septiembre del Zhuque-2E.

articles.title: A judge lets Denuvo subpoena Discord, Reddit, and Steam to unmask the cracker Voices38
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: Denuvo has spent the past few weeks trying to uncover Voices38's true identity. The mysterious cracker has been wreaking havoc on the company's notorious DRM and anti-tamper technology, and Denuvo is now turning to lawyers in a bid to unmask the skilled coder.
Denuvo's first attempt to uncover Voices38's real identity was unsuccessful because the company tried to obtain too much data at once. Now, a California federal judge has granted the Irdeto-owned DRM maker's revised subpoena requests. Several internet companies will soon have to respond to Denuvo's lawyers, but Voices38 could still remain a John Doe in the end.
Denuvo's latest legal assault began earlier this month, when the company asked a judge to help identify the unnamed cracker operating under the "Voices38" moniker. The request was part of Denuvo's lawsuit against Voices38, which centers on the cracker's alleged violations of the DMCA's anti-circumvention provisions.
Denuvo initially asked the judge to approve 46 separate subpoena requests targeting Discord, Valve, Reddit, and other internet companies. The subpoenas sought potential names and email addresses, along with additional data related to payments and financial transactions, login logs, comment histories, and more.
According to Judge Haywood S. Gilliam Jr., Denuvo's requests went too far. Although the company was seeking to uncover Voices38's identity, the subpoenas extended well beyond the information needed to identify the individual or individuals involved. Given the potentially significant privacy implications, the judge decided to narrow the scope of the requests.
Denuvo was given two options: revise its subpoenas or provide detailed explanations justifying each request. The DRM maker chose the former, reducing the number of requests from 46 to nine. Judge Gilliam has now approved the revised requests, allowing Denuvo to serve subpoenas on Discord, Valve, and Reddit.
Specifically, the company is seeking identifying information associated with the "voices38" Discord account, Reddit user voices38, and seven different Steam profiles. So far, Denuvo has been able to target only an online pseudonym. The subpoenas could help the company obtain further information about Voices38's identity, including names, government-issued identification documents, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses.
Despite being targeted by a company known for pursuing DRM crackers, Voices38 recently indicated that things would be fine regardless. The coder released their latest crack just a couple of days ago. However, over the past few hours, Voices38 has reportedly deleted their official Reddit account, one of the main channels the cracker used to share releases and updates.
Could Voices38 become the next Voksi, the cracker whom Denuvo successfully forced into early retirement several years ago? The developer was instrumental in removing Irdeto's anti-tamper technology from recent games, including Doom: The Dark Ages and Resident Evil Requiem.

articles.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
articles.text:
Hoping to quell criticism, Meta has dropped the word “train” from its “streamlined” commercial terms of service that kick in on October 30.
Last week, Meta faced backlash after legal experts warned that the tech giant’s sweeping new commercial terms of service seemed to give Meta permission to endlessly scrape websites linked on business pages. Talking to Nieman Lab, experts suggested that Meta could possibly use the policy to avoid millions in licensing fees from news organizations by requiring all business users to share a wealth of AI training data simply for running a business page.
A Meta spokesperson confirmed that Meta did not alert users to the changed language following backlash. This potentially only adds to confusion ahead of the policy rollout. In response to backlash, Meta’s spokesperson provided a statement to Ars, acknowledging Nieman Lab’s initial report but not its follow-up report reiterating experts’ concerns:
“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”
The same experts who sounded the initial alarms were not impressed by Meta’s updates, which they told Nieman Lab do not go far enough to protect business page users from invasive scraping. Matt Topic, a media and intellectual property attorney at Loevy & Loevy, told Nieman Lab that “publishers should remain concerned.”

articles.title: Galaxy Watch Ultra cai 59% para quem busca relógio para aventuras • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Watch Ultra cai 59% para quem busca relógio para aventuras
Galaxy Watch Ultra tem corpo de titânio e monitora diversos esportes; smartwatch da Samsung sai por menos da metade do preço original, no Pix no Mercado Livre
O Galaxy Watch Ultra LTE de 47 mm está saindo por R$ 2.068,64 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch da Samsung lançado em 2025, que possui corpo de titânio e sensores que suportam diversos esportes, recebe desconto de 59% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.999.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra é um dos melhores smartwatches da Samsung, equipado com o mesmo kit de sensores do novo Ultra 2. Ele oferece suporte a diversas modalidades esportivas, como corrida e ciclismo, e traz funções de qualidade de vida, como eletrocardiograma (ECG), monitores do sono e da oxigenação do sangue.
Seu corpo em titânio de 47 mm resiste a até 10 atmosferas de pressão (10 ATM) e traz certificações IP68 e militar MIL-STD-810H, podendo assim ser usado em esportes aquáticos em águas rasas, enquanto resiste a altas temperaturas.
Graças à conectividade 4G/LTE, este wearable pode salvar a vida do usuário em uma situação de risco. No caso de uma emergência médica, ele pode disparar alertas para contatos pré-programados e ligar para números como 190 (polícia) e 192 (bombeiros), sem depender de um celular.
A tela Super AMOLED de 1,5″ com brilho de até 3.000 nits do Watch Ultra pode reproduzir imagens nítidas com cores vibrantes e oferece visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra arranhões, pancadas e quedas.
O gadget traz o chip Exynos W1000, 2 GB de RAM e 64 GB de espaço interno, um kit interno que o permite instalar e rodar apps localmente. Sua bateria de 590 mAh resiste até 100 horas de uso no modo economia de energia, segundo a fabricante, podendo ser usado por um dia inteiro sem descarregar.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra de 47 mm (R$ 2.068,64 no Pix) suporta redes Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.3, o já mencionado 4G/LTE e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real, recurso essencial para a prática de esportes e outras aventuras.

articles.title: Carriers ask CRTC to scrap several consumer protections
articles.text:
The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) is currently looking at ways to harmonize and improve the various consumer protection codes governing wireless and internet services. But some of Canada’s largest carriers are using the process to push for changes that could hurt consumers in the long run.
In interventions filed in mid-August and reviewed by MobileSyrup, Rogers, Bell, and Telus responded to various proposed changes to the Wireless and Internet codes, and added their own requests as well. However, some of the proposed alterations would see existing consumer protections gutted or removed. Proposals include removing caps on roaming overage charges, bringing back phone locking, extending financing terms, and more. We highlight some of the biggest ones below:
Clawbacks for sign-up benefits
Telus stood alone with this one. It suggested to the CRTC that economic inducements, such as “gift cards, retail
credits, promotional gifts, discounts or other financial benefits,” should be paid back if customers cancel early:
“These should all be treated consistently: regardless of form, if a customer receives a financial benefit in exchange for a term service commitment, early cancellation should trigger an obligation to repay the unamortized portion of that benefit.”
Further, Telus suggested that the CRTC should lump these economic inducements in with device subsidies in the Wireless Code. Specifically, Telus said it should “replace ‘subsidized device’ with the more inclusive and technologically-neutral term ‘economic inducement'” to “reflect modern retail realities.”
Removing roaming caps
Telus and Rogers both proposed changes to roaming fees, though with some subtle differences. Telus asked the CRTC to eliminate the $100 roaming cap entirely, while Rogers suggested limiting the cap to pay-per-use roaming. Rogers also asked the CRTC to remove the $50 roaming usage notification.
Notably, roaming costs are quite expensive, and these caps were introduced to prevent bill shock from people inadvertently racking up hundreds of dollars in roaming charges. With roaming being something of a cash cow for carriers, it’s hardly a surprise to see them advocate for removing caps.
Phone locking
Rogers, Bell, and Telus all proposed that the CRTC add a 60-day phone-locking rule instead of the current rules that prohibit locking phones entirely.
Phone locking, as a reminder, locks phones to a carrier’s network, preventing use on other networks. For context, the CRTC banned locking phones back in 2017 and eliminated unlocking fees, which enabled Canadians to more easily switch between carriers.
The phone locking push shouldn’t come as much of a surprise to anyone who’s been following Canadian telecom. Both Bell and Telus have previously called on the CRTC to change its stance on locking phones over theft concerns, with both carriers pushing ahead with implementing 60-day locks despite rules prohibiting the practice. Telus also previously claimed Bell’s 60-day phone lock made its unlocked phones a bigger target for theft.
Extended financing periods
Another request made by all three providers was to extend device financing beyond the current 24-month limit. Rogers, Bell, and Telus all argued that customers are seeking longer financing terms because of factors like rising device costs and improved durability.
Rogers wrote that the 24-month limit “has a direct impact on affordability for consumers” by restricting carriers’ ability to spread the cost of a device over a longer period. Further, Rogers noted that because “device durability and functionality has improved, many consumers are retaining their devices for longer and are therefore interested in options that would allow longer-term financing.”
On one hand, I actually kind of agree with the carriers on this one, at least to the extent that longer terms should be available for customers who want one. Part of the reasoning behind the 24-month limit was to prevent people from being trapped into lengthy phone contracts, so I think as long as the spirit of that is preserved, I don’t see a major issue with allowing people to choose longer contracts if they want.
At the same time, several providers have come up with ways to work around the 24-month rule. Rogers, Bell, and Telus all offer device return options, which discount the monthly financing costs if customers agree to return their phone or pay the difference after 24 months. Notably, Bell has started offering customers a second 24-month financing term as another way to spread out the cost of phones.
Other suggested changes

articles.title: Financial transformation: Why slow AI adoption is the top risk - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dell’s security chief warns AI is lowering the barriers to sophisticated cyberattacks
Financial transformation powered by artificial intelligence now runs as two races at once. Banks and other financial institutions are racing to turn data into action with AI, while their security teams scramble to prepare for a wave of agentic AI-driven threats.
That second race is being shaped by how cheaply attackers can now obtain advanced capabilities. Agentic AI hasn’t erased the old hierarchy of hacktivists, criminal gangs and nation-states, but it has handed lower-tier actors tools once reserved for the top, according to John Scimone (pictured), president and chief security officer of Dell Technologies Inc.
“I think the pyramid still exists, but undoubtedly the cost of entry and the barriers to entry have crumbled,” Scimone said. “Said another way, the least sophisticated attack tomorrow is more sophisticated than the world will have ever seen a year ago.”
Scimone spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at the Dell Technologies New York Symposium, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed financial transformation and using AI to defend against AI threats. (* Disclosure below.)
Securing financial transformation in the agentic era
Dell is already putting frontier models to work on its own defenses. The company is a partner in Anthropic PBC’s Project Glasswing, which gives vetted organizations access to powerful AI tools to secure critical systems, Scimone noted. The program has drawn in new members and was recently folded into a broader verification program. The fundamentals of identity, access management and detection still apply, but attacks now arrive at a speed and scale that make yesterday’s practices insufficient, he explained.
“We as cybersecurity professionals are going to have to use AI to defend against AI,” Scimone said. “There’s a huge opportunity really to be able to leverage this capability for good.”
That opportunity could matter most to organizations that have never been able to staff a full security team. Agents can deliver scale and expertise that smaller companies could never hire or build on their own, according to Scimone.
“Our future security program might be a security program of one person, but it might have 10,000 agents, all of which are the best security practitioners in the space and the roles in which they’re assigned,” Scimone added.

articles.title: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products.
The company said Tuesday it’s upgrading Gemini in vehicles with a personal intelligence feature that can draw on information from Gmail, Google Calendar, YouTube, Maps, Google Search history, and other connected Google services to understand your preferences, activities, and past experiences.
Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in, software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle.
The feature will launch in Android Auto, starting today, and expand to cars with Google Built-in in the coming months.
Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto. Meanwhile, Gemini’s “Personal Intelligence” feature rolled out across the U.S. in March and is now in beta in global markets.
This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps.
Drivers will have to opt in for Personalized Intelligence to work. Once a user does so, they should expect all sorts of cross-pollination. For instance, a driver who is navigating to the airport may be alerted that the flight on their calendar is delayed.
Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language. Returning to that airport example, a user might ask the AI assistant for their flight gate before quickly following up with a question about whether it’s still on time. Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said.
That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence. The feature can be turned on or off at any time, and users can selectively choose which apps they’d like to connect, Google said.

articles.title: Oblivion gamer uses Claude AI to boost average FPS gains up to 48%, stutters slashed by 90% — performance mod doesn't change game assets or alter visuals
articles.text:
Oblivion gamer uses Claude AI to boost average FPS gains up to 48%, stutters slashed by 90% — performance mod doesn't change game assets or alter visuals
Yes, this mod is just about 100% vibe-coded.
The revelation that there was a ton of performance lying on the table in the remastered The Elder Scrolls Part IV: Oblivion won't be a surprise to people who have played the game, which is notorious for its hitching and stuttering. The reason primarily lies in its poor utilization of hardware, and that's a big part of what LTSharpe and Claude have addressed in the new Oblivion Remastered Performance Fix that changes nothing about the game's visuals yet increases performance by as much as 68% in the worst case. (h/t to ComputerBase)
Yes, this mod is just about 100% vibe-coded, and yet, rather than hacking Minecraft into GTA V on iPhone, or hacking CoD Black Ops 2 maps into Minecraft, this mod is a binary code modification for Oblivion Remastered that seeks to improve performance and stability considerably, and according to numerous jubilant and thankful posts on NexusMods, it seems to do exactly that, with one user proclaiming that the performance increase was "dramatic" and that the overworld stuttering that plagues the game is "completely gone."
The story goes like this: gamer and mod creator LTSharpe has a slightly older system with a Ryzen 7 5800X CPU. Not the newest chip on the block to be sure, but Zen 3 isn't so old that it should be crumpling under the weight of games just yet. Frustrated with the verifiably awful performance of the remaster of The Elder Scrolls Part IV: Oblivion, he paid for a subscription to Anthropic's Claude AI agent and started working with the assistant to diagnose and fix the performance problems.
"Diagnose" is a critical keyword here, because it isn't like Claude was hallucinating an engine.ini tweak somebody else published for the original game 20 years ago. The partners, with Claude doing the hard work and LTSharpe directing, reverse-engineered the game to the point that they were able to build a repeatable benchmarking framework. That allowed them to systematically diagnose the causes of the performance problems and then test fixes against the real behavior of the game with modified machine code.
That's the thing; this was done without source code. Neither TES4 Oblivion nor the remaster's Unreal Engine is open-source software. The sheer magnitude of the task would be incredibly daunting to a team of human engineers, much less a single person. According to LTSharpe, over the course of two weeks Claude successfully diagnosed and fixed bugs in not only the Remaster's Unreal Engine code, but also in the underlying Gamebryo original engine, in AMD's frame generation code, and even in the Unreal Engine itself, improving performance and avoiding crashes.
The developer—or perhaps we should say, coordinator?—is careful to acknowledge that the performance tweaks were created with his system specifically in mind and that they may not work well for others. Indeed, he has a Radeon graphics card, which puts him within a surprisingly small minority of PC gamers, and some portion of his fixes were aimed at making sure AMD's FSR upscaling and frame generation remain in effect despite a long-standing game bug that disables them when you task-switch (Alt+Tab) out of the game. The good lieutenant invites other gamers to try out the fix and report back, and he's even helping out with support requests on NexusMods, too. Head over there if you're keen to grab the fix and try it for yourself.

articles.title: ‘Self sabotage by Spotify’: The music platform is cracking down on Family plan sharing, and it does nothing except reveal Spotify’s true colors
articles.text:
Spotify’s crack-down on Family plan sharing could land you a 12-month ban, and it could be the final straw for users — myself included
A very narrow definition of 'family'
- Spotify is rolling out a new verification process for Premium Family members
- Users must now scan the account manager's QR code to confirm they're part of the same household
- Spotify will boot you back to the free tier and give you a 12-month Premium Family ban if you fail to verify
The Netflix password-sharing crackdown is rubbing off on one of the best music streaming services — now Spotify is taking its own approach to putting a stop to Premium Family plan sharing.
Spotify is enforcing this via a new QR code verification system, which has started rolling out to a number of users if they’re not at the same address as the account manager. The QR code appears on the account holder’s device, requiring those under the plan to scan it in order to verify that you’re living in the same household. This code updates every few seconds, making it harder for users to use screenshots to bypass the process.
The platform goes into the verification process in detail on its support page, clarifying that it doesn’t use location tracking but instead checks your address to verify it’s the same one as the account manager’s. Additionally, Spotify states that ‘both the manager and member need to be in the same place to complete the scan’.
If you receive a verification prompt, you’ll have a 7-day window to complete the scan, but failure to comply comes with consequences. Spotify will boot you back to ad-listening on the free tier as well as banning you from joining another Premium Family or Duo plan for 12 months. It really does feel like a prison sentence.
As you can imagine, users are beyond frustrated with Spotify’s latest move, and despite not being on the Premium Family plan myself, even I can’t fathom the ridiculousness of it all.
We don’t know if this is region-specific, but a number of users on Reddit have received verification prompts despite there being no formal announcement from the company. ‘Self sabotage by Spotify. If I have to do this more than once for my kids that live at home I'm shutting it down,’ an angry Redditor posted.
One of the many users' frustrations is with, of course, money. By limiting Premium Family as a solely household plan, Spotify will drive a huge number of users out of the grouped plan and leave them with no option but to sign up to Premium Individual.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This plan is priced at $12.99 / £12.99 / AU$15.99 a month, while Premium Family is $21.99 / £21.99 / AU$25.99 a month and includes up to six individual accounts — which is roughly $3.665 / £3.665 / AU$4.331 per individual account. The more users Spotify can force into Premium Individual accounts, the more subscription revenue it can generate, but it’s so much more than money.
For me, the most ridiculous part is Spotify’s narrow definition of what a ‘family’ is, as a large majority of Premium Family users are members who have moved out of their parents’ home but are still on the same plan — for example, students who move away from home to study. So, in Spotify’s eyes, these types of families are essentially considered lesser than a family whose members still live under the same roof.
Equally, Spotify’s Premium Family plan has been helpful for adults to guide their not-so-tech literate elderly parents through navigating digital streaming, as another Redditor highlights. Someone takes control of the account, sets up a profile for their parents, shows them the ropes, and lets them listen away. Not only does the verification remove this, it also gets rid of the novelty of families comparing their music tastes and reminiscing about their old favourites together.
It has to be said that until now, Spotify has been on its best behavior and even rolled out helpful tools to exclude your kids’ music from your recommendations, which has been welcomed by Premium Family members — but the new verification process just feels like one step forward, three steps back. In that case, Spotify should rebrand Premium Family to 'Premium Household' to avoid confusion.
We’ve reached out to Spotify for further comment, and will update this story if/ when we hear back.

articles.title: How Singapore Connects Chip Research, Startups, and Manufacturing - EE Times
articles.text:
As competition in the semiconductor industry expands beyond conventional process scaling to encompass photonics, power devices, advanced packaging, and heterogeneous integration, Singapore leverages its established R&D and manufacturing base to explore ways to bring deep tech to market.
Singapore is advancing technologies including advanced packaging, silicon photonics, power electronics, RF GaN, piezoMEMS, flat optics, and IC design. A pathway from research through technology translation to startups and industrial commercialization is gradually taking shape. Research platforms such as the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) play a key role in connecting research outcomes with industry needs.
Three examples illustrate this journey: silicon carbide (SiC) power device research at A*STAR’s Institute of Microelectronics (A*STAR IME); metalens technology being commercialized by Singapore-based startup MetaOptics; and silicon photonics foundry Advanced Micro Foundry (AMF), which emerged from A*STAR’s technology translation efforts before being acquired by GlobalFoundries. Together, they show how deep-tech innovations can progress from research and technology translation to industrial scale.
SiC research: from device development to technology translation
Chien Yu-Chieh (Jack), a senior scientist at A*STAR IME originally from Taiwan, focuses on SiC power MOSFETs, including device structures, process development, electrical characterization, and reliability. He aims to take his research beyond device development toward technology translation.
SiC is already an established material for commercial power semiconductors, but next-generation devices still face significant technical challenges. Chien noted, for example, that trench MOSFETs can reduce on-resistance but introduce challenges related to gate oxide integrity, defects at the SiC/SiO₂ interface, and long-term reliability.
Chien is therefore working on next-generation SiC device structures and fabrication processes. Because device design, fabrication, measurement, and reliability testing require repeated validation, access to a comprehensive research platform with the necessary equipment and cross-disciplinary expertise is critical. At A*STAR IME, he said, researchers can conduct device design, process development, and electrical characterization within the same R&D environment, shortening development cycles.
For Chien, the next step is to advance his research toward technology translation, potentially by establish a startup to turn the results into commercial applications and valuable IP.
MetaOptics: from metalens research to manufacturing
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Singapore, MetaOptics specializes in manufacturing metalenses on glass substrates. Its technology uses nanoscale structures to directly control light waves, enabling thin optical elements to perform some of the functions traditionally achieved with multiple conventional lenses.
MetaOptics applies semiconductor manufacturing techniques to form nanoscale pillar structures on 12-inch glass wafers. By incorporating processes such as deep ultraviolet (DUV) immersion lithography, the company is advancing wafer-level metalens manufacturing. The approach could help shrink optical modules for smartphone cameras, wearables, machine vision, and other sensing systems.
For MetaOptics CEO Aloysius Chua, the real challenge is not simply demonstrating that a metalens can form an image, but convincing customers that the technology works in real-world applications. For a deep-tech startup, developing a prototype is only the beginning. As Chua put it, “I need to show customers that my lens is working.”
Chua said MetaOptics must also complete customer validation and address process consistency, yield, and manufacturing scale. As nanoscale structures, optical design, and semiconductor lithography move toward volume production, process control becomes a key determinant of commercial competitiveness. A*STAR provides research resources and an R&D environment to help technologies bridge the gap between laboratory development and industrial applications.
AMF: scaling silicon photonics for industry
While MetaOptics and Chien’s work remain at the startup or technology validation stage, AMF offers a concrete example of deep tech advancing toward industrial-scale operations.
AMF is a Singapore-based silicon photonics foundry that grew out of A*STAR’s technology translation efforts. It operates a 200-mm manufacturing platform and provides silicon photonics prototyping, fabrication, and testing services. In November 2025, GlobalFoundries announced its acquisition of AMF, bringing the foundry’s manufacturing capabilities, silicon photonics IP, and talent into its global operations. GlobalFoundries said AMF was expected to contribute more than $75 million in revenue in 2026, helping the company target more than $1 billion in annual silicon photonics revenue by the end of the decade.
For GlobalFoundries, the acquisition brings more than a silicon photonics manufacturing platform. It adds AMF’s accumulated expertise, IP, and talent to the company. Yew Kong Tan, senior VP of GlobalFoundries APAC Manufacturing and general manager of the Singapore site, said the company’s silicon photonics collaboration with A*STAR dates back to 2015. The acquisition also creates an opportunity to bring 300-mm silicon photonics capabilities developed in the U.S. to Singapore, complementing A*STAR’s research capabilities.
“The acquisition actually allows us to combine capabilities on both sides,” Tan said. “From the research technology standpoint, AMF’s talent can also support 300-mm research. At the same time, the acquisition allows us to expand the capacity that the market needs in Singapore.”
GlobalFoundries also announced plans to establish a silicon photonics R&D center of excellence in Singapore in collaboration with A*STAR. The work will include developing next-generation silicon photonics technologies and materials for data transmission at 400 Gbps. GlobalFoundries plans to use AMF’s existing 200-mm platform to serve markets such as long-haul optical communications, computing, LiDARs, and sensing, with the potential to expand to 300-mm manufacturing as demand grows.
AMF illustrates another critical stage in deep-tech commercialization. Once research has been taken up by a startup and validated in the market, further growth requires an established manufacturing platform, accumulated expertise, and IP. Integrating these assets into a larger semiconductor company can extend the technology’s reach and expand its market potential.
A*STAR: bridging research and industry
This is the essence of what Yeo Yee Chia, A*STAR’s assistant chief executive for innovation and enterprise, calls “technology translation.” He emphasized that research institutions must go beyond conducting research: They need to work backward from industry needs to determine which equipment, talent, and technical capabilities to build.
This kind of platform support is particularly important for deep tech. Metalenses require nanoscale fabrication and wafer-level manufacturing; SiC power devices need device design, process development, and reliability validation; and silicon photonics involves optical devices, CMOS-compatible processes, wafer fabrication, packaging, and testing. These technologies often require years of capital-intensive R&D, while initial market demand may be too limited to justify a startup investing in a full set of production tools or building a complete R&D team on its own.
As Yeo noted, the value of a research institution extends beyond publishing academic papers or filing patents. More importantly, it lies in establishing the infrastructure and capabilities needed to validate, refine, and commercialize emerging technologies. For startups, this can lower early-stage barriers by allowing them to access research and development resources without bearing the full upfront capital expenditure. For larger enterprises, it provides access to technology platforms, IP, and expertise that have already progressed through technical validation and are better positioned for industrial deployment.

articles.title: Mysteriöse Nachricht in Super Mario 64: Wurde sie nach 30 Jahren endlich entschlüsselt?
articles.text:
Super Mario 64: Ist ein 30 Jahre altes Rätsel endlich gelöst?
Schon 1996 haben Zocker:innen auf der ganzen Welt in Super Mario 64 auf ein seltsames Detail geschaut. In einem Hinterhof des Schlosses steht die Statue eines Sterns. Darunter ist eine Plakette mit einer Inschrift angebracht. Die Auflösung von 32 x 32 Pixeln hatte es bisher aber unmöglich gemacht, die genauen Wörter zu entziffern. Doch das hat Gamer:innen nicht aufgehalten, Theorien aufzustellen.
Super Mario 64: Theorien zur Plakette
Seit Jahrzehnten hält sich hartnäckig die Theorie, dass die obere Zeile der zweizeiligen Inschrift „L is real 2401“ zeigen würde. Die kryptische Nachricht soll laut einigen Gamer:innen ein versteckter Hinweis der Entwickler:innen sein, dass Luigi (also „L“) sich doch im Spiel befindet. Die Zahl 2401 soll indes ein Hinweis sein, wie er freischaltbar ist.
Im Laufe der Jahre hatte Nintendo diese Theorie aber schon zerstört. Damals hieß es in einem Schreiben an einen Fan, dass die Nachricht bewusst unleserlich ist und niemand genau wüsste, was da überhaupt steht. Doch jetzt will ein Fan endlich Licht ins Dunkel gebracht haben. Unter dem Nicknamen „Supermochi64“ hat er auf GitHub eine ausführliche technische Analyse der mysteriösen Plakette veröffentlicht.
Was sagt die Inschrift wirklich?
Um das herauszufinden, hat der Mario-Fan nicht einfach KI genutzt, um die niedrigaufgelöste Plakette hochzurechnen. Er hat den umgekehrten Ansatz gewählt und eigene Plaketten erstellt, die er dann auf die Größe von 32 × 32 Pixeln geschrumpft hat. So konnte er Font und die geschriebenen Wörter mit dem Original vergleichen und die Phrasen mit der höchsten Wahrscheinlichkeit finden. Das ist möglich, weil die Buchstaben trotz der geschrumpften Größe ein Muster hinterlassen. Die Plakette benutzt insgesamt 32 verschiedene Grautöne.
Am Ende bekam „Supermochi64“ für eine Reihe von Phrasen einen Mismatch-Score. Je niedriger dieser ist, desto besser stimmen die Ergebnisse mit dem Original aus Super Mario 64 überein. Allein für das erste Wort ließ der Mario-Fan mehr als 1,2 Millionen Optionen vom System analysieren. Dabei kristallisierte sich „Eternal“ als klarer Sieger heraus. Andere Wörter dahinter waren lediglich Varianten von „Eternal“ mit Schreibfehlern. Erst auf dem 13.217. Platz landete das nächste fehlerfreie englische Wort „Sternal“.
Denselben Vorgang wiederholte er auch für die anderen Wörter und Phrasen. Am wahrscheinlichsten steht auf der Plakette in Super Mario 64 demnach „Eternal Star / We hope so“. Bei der zweiten Zeile gibt es noch andere Kandidaten mit ähnlichen Resultaten wie „We hope he“ oder „We hope as“. Da sie mit dem Rest aber keinen Satz ergeben, geht „Supermochi64“ davon aus, dass sich lediglich das Schriftbild ähnelt.
Um sein System zu überprüfen, versteckte der Mario-Fan anschließend noch 50 andere Wörter in der Plakette und ließ sie analysieren. Bei 38 von ihnen befand das System aus über 1,2 Millionen Kandidaten das korrekte Wort als bestmögliches Ergebnis. Bei den anderen zwölf Wörtern schnitten Varianten mit Schreibfehlern (wie „Dnration“ bei „Duration“) nur geringfügig besser ab.
Zu guter Letzt prüfte „Supermochi64“ auch noch andere Theorien, die sich im Laufe der Jahre angesammelt hatten. Seine Phrase erreichte einen Gesamt-Mismatch-Score von 1.129 über beide Zeilen. „L is real 2401“ hat einen deutlich höheren Mismatch-Score von 2.031, der auch nur die erste Zeile umfasst. Denn die Theorie hat nie eine Phrase für die zweite Zeile geliefert. Und auch der Satz „A Secret Star / lie here“, der seit Jahren in der Community kursiert, kommt auf einen hohen Mismatch-Score von 4.304.

articles.title: Fiat Koala : une voiture électrique à 10 000 € conçue sur la base de la nouvelle 2CV ?
articles.text:
Chantre de la voiture populaire, Fiat n’entend pas se laisser faire face à une concurrence chinoise déboulant en nombre. La marque entend ainsi casser le marché avec une nouvelle proposition extrêmement agressive. Une citadine électrique placée sous la Grande Panda est ainsi dans les cartons. Celle qui s’appellerait Koala devra s’afficher autour des 10 000 €, aides comprises, ce qui en fera l’une des voitures à batterie les moins chères du marché.
La Grande Panda ayant sensiblement grandi par rapport à la Panda originelle, l’idée serait de retrouver les valeurs essentielles de l’automobile avec un équivalent électrique de la petite Pandina hybride. Pour ce faire, Fiat n’hésitera pas à tirer parti du groupe Stellantis en utilisant la plateforme qui servira de base à la future 2CV prévue pour 2028. Voici la parfaite candidate pour entrer dans la catégorie des voitures électriques économiques voulue par l’Europe.
Pourquoi Fiat a préféré cacher sa Koala au Mondial de l’Automobile
Interrogé par Autocar au Mondial de l’Automobile, Arnaud Belloni, le nouveau patron de Fiat, a lui-même confirmé l’arrivée de cette nouvelle auto : « nous travaillons sur plusieurs voitures basées sur la plateforme E-Car. Nous préparons une petite voiture dérivée de la 2CV, et elle va faire sensation ». Devrons-nous attendre longtemps avant d’en voir la couleur ? Pas vraiment, d’après François Leboine, directeur du design Fiat.
Selon lui, la Koala est aussi « prête que la 2CV ». Pourquoi la marque garde-t-elle alors son nouveau bijou sous protection ? Selon la transalpine, le Mondial n’était « pas le bon moment pour nous de montrer ce que nous faisons ». Il ne fallait forcément pas impacter la française qui a d’ailleurs fait le plein sur son stand. Et il serait risqué de voir la Koala complètement abandonnée par le public dans ce fourre-tout de concepts créés par Stellantis.
Un design inédit : pas de néo-rétro, mais un vrai nom plein de fraîcheur
Fiat prépare donc activement son retour sur les petites voitures. Leboine explique que « nous sommes en train de repenser l’entrée de gamme [avec] la Pandina, mais aussi la 500. La maturité du concept 2CV est indéniable, et nous suivrons la même voie. Nous dévoilerons la Koala au moment opportun ». Concernant ce nom adorable, Belloni a confirmé que Fiat a bel et bien déposé la marque Koala.
Contrairement à la 2CV, l’italienne ne prendra pas totale inspiration sur son ancêtre. Des codes stylistiques pourront se retrouver, mais le reste résultera « d’une approche très différente, et non néo-rétro ». Cela justifierait alors le nom Koala, complètement inédit chez Fiat. Seule la technique sera identique à celle de la 2CV, avec un ensemble moteur/batterie aux chiffres semblables. La Fiat Koala devrait débarquer en 2028, peu après la 2CV.

articles.title: OYO-parent PRISM to nearly halve IPO fresh issue size to up to Rs 3,350 cr: Sources
articles.text:
OYO-parent PRISM to nearly halve IPO fresh issue size to up to Rs 3,350 cr: Sources
People familiar with the matter said the reduction in the issue size follows continued strong cash generation and an improving balance-sheet position, which has lowered the amount of capital the company needs to raise compared with what was originally envisaged.
OYO parent PRISM is planning to nearly halve the size of the fresh issue in its proposed initial public offering (IPO) to up to Rs 3,350 crore from almost Rs 6,650 crore, sources said.
People familiar with the matter told PTI the reduction in the issue size follows continued strong cash generation and an improving balance-sheet position, which has lowered the amount of capital the company needs to raise compared with what was originally envisaged.
"The original issue was sized before the company's more recent financial performance came through. With cash generation remaining strong and the balance sheet improving, the funding requirement has come down, allowing the company to reduce the amount of primary capital it raises.
"The objective is to raise what the business needs while keeping the capital structure efficient. The plan is to repay the residual debt over the next two to three years through cash flows generated by the business," a person familiar with the matter said.
Earlier, OYO had planned to raise up to Rs 6,650 crore through an IPO, of which around Rs 5,000 crore was intended for debt repayment.
The revised issue size comes with PRISM continuing to focus on reducing its outstanding debt.
Under the revised structure, most of the issue proceeds are proposed to be used towards repayment or prepayment, in part or full, of certain borrowings.
The revised issue comes as PRISM moves towards the next stage of its proposed IPO following its earlier filing of the uUpdated draft herring prospectus.
Moody's Ratings has revised the outlook on PRISM to 'positive' from 'stable', while reaffirming the travel tech unicorn's B2 corporate family rating.
Explaining the rationale behind ratings, Moody's said, "We expect OYO's EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) to grow to around Rs 3,000 crore ($315 million) over the next 12-18 months as the company continues to scale and add new storefronts to its platform.
For FY26, OYO's EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 2,630 crore from Rs 1,080 crore in FY25.
OYO was founded in 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal, who currently holds a 30.52 per cent stake in the company. SVF India Holdings (Cayman) Ltd, a subsidiary of SoftBank Group Corp is the largest shareholder in the company, with a 40.04% stake.

articles.title: Chauffer sans soufflerie et régler la température depuis son téléphone : le Dreo 711S est à 129,99 €
articles.text:
Le radiateur connecté à convection Dreo 711S de 2 000 W est à 129,99 € (-13 %)
Le radiateur connecté Dreo 711S chauffe par convection naturelle, sans ventilateur, avec un thermostat réglable, une télécommande et une minuterie de 24 heures.
Amazon propose le radiateur connecté Dreo 711S argent à 129,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 149,99 €. L’économie atteint 20 €, soit environ 13 %. Le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours est également indiqué à 149,99 €.
L’appareil est vendu et expédié par Amazon. La livraison est affichée à 6,99 €, soit un total de 136,98 €, avec une date annoncée au 12 novembre. Ces conditions sont à vérifier lors de la commande.
Une chauffe par convection naturelle, sans ventilateur
Le radiateur à convection Dreo 711S développe jusqu’à 2 000 W. Il réchauffe l’air sans soufflerie, ce qui évite le bruit mécanique d’un ventilateur. Ce fonctionnement peut intéresser ceux qui cherchent un chauffage d’appoint pour une chambre ou un bureau.
Trois niveaux de chauffe et un mode Éco permettent d’adapter son fonctionnement. Le thermostat se règle de 5 à 35 °C, par incréments de 1 °C. En mode Éco, l’appareil régule la chauffe selon la température ambiante et la consigne, plutôt que de fonctionner continuellement à pleine puissance.
Des commandes connectées et deux possibilités d’installation
Le radiateur peut se piloter depuis son panneau de commande, avec la télécommande fournie ou l’application Dreo. La minuterie atteint 24 heures et les fonctions connectées permettent de programmer les périodes de chauffage. Un indicateur lumineux renseigne également sur la température ambiante.
Le Dreo 711S peut être fixé au mur ou installé sur les pieds fournis. Il dispose d’une protection contre la surchauffe et d’un verrouillage enfant. Son indice IP24 correspond à une protection contre les projections d’eau ; son emplacement doit respecter les indications de la notice d’installation.

articles.title: Mozilla, Google, Apple block compromised eMudhra CA certificates
articles.text:
Certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers found their private keys were so weak that anyone could recover them almost instantly and use them to forge trusted certificates for legitimate websites.
Major browsers and operating systems trusted the compromised certificates, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites and intercept encrypted communications.
A security researcher known as Wayne discovered the weakness on October 17 while scanning publicly available certificate data.
According to Mozilla's incident report, all eight certificates used P-384 private keys generated in April 2025 that had values smaller than 256, allowing anyone to recover them by testing just 256 possible numbers.
To demonstrate the weakness, security researcher Flüpke published one of the compromised private keys on GitHub, showing that the private key for eMudhra's "EM OV TLS CA - G3C" certificate had a value of just 4.
BleepingComputer independently verified that the published key matches one of the revoked certificates.
In a response to Mozilla, eMudhra blamed the issue on an error in a script used to generate the certificates in April 2025. The company said the error generated a second set of weaker keys that were mistakenly selected for certificate signing because they had labels similar to the properly generated keys.
Some of the resulting certificates were also submitted to Sectigo for cross-signing.
eMudhra said most of the affected intermediate certificates were never used in production and that it had found no evidence they were used to issue certificates to end users.
However, attackers could have recovered and abused the weak keys since their creation in April 2025, though there is no evidence that this happened.
Following the disclosure, eMudhra revoked the eight compromised certificates and stopped issuing new certificates under its G3 root.
Browser makers and software vendors release fixes
Mozilla said it blocked the compromised certificates through Firefox's OneCRL system on October 17, protecting users without requiring a browser update or restart.
Google Chrome also blocked the six compromised intermediates authorized to issue TLS certificates that day, while Apple added protections on October 19.
Mozilla also released Firefox 158.0.1 and updates for its ESR releases on October 20 to protect users whose browser configurations prevented them from receiving the earlier revocation updates.
However, software that uses its own certificate stores or doesn't check certificate revocations may keep trusting the compromised intermediates until it is updated.
The Go development team released versions 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 to address the issue, tracked as CVE-2026-111943.
Mozilla cryptography engineer Dennis Jackson has also published an incident tracking website listing affected software and available security updates.

Administrators can use the advisory's test endpoints and mitigation instructions to determine whether their systems are still affected.

articles.title: Pour 5000 dollars, un hacker s'introduit dans plus de 100 sites d'entreprises grâce à des agents IA
articles.text:
Un hacker a confié à des agents IA le soin de s'introduire dans des sites liés à plus de 100 entreprises, dont Deere, SharkNinja et Cummins. Le coût de la campagne est estimé à environ 5000 dollars.
Le chercheur Snorre Fagerland, de NorForge, a pu suivre cette campagne en direct depuis le début du mois. Pour ce faire, il a cherché des installations de Cairn (un outil open source qui pilote des agents IA) laissées exposées sur le web. Selon Reuters, qui a identifié plusieurs victimes grâce à ces données, le pirate n'a presque rien fait lui-même.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Moins de 100 caractères de consignes, 23 heures d'essais
Cairn n’a pas été conçu pour pirater. Son auteur le décrit comme une architecture multi-agents, c’est-à-dire un logiciel qui fait travailler plusieurs agents IA sur un même problème. Il suffit de donner à Cairn une cible et un objectif, et les agents se mettent au travail. Ils notent leurs trouvailles sur un tableau commun et changent de piste quand une échoue, là où un scanner classique suit un scénario figé. Ici, l’opérateur a rédigé ses consignes en chinois, en moins de 100 caractères.
La campagne a démarré le 25 septembre contre des boutiques en ligne américaines, canadiennes, australiennes et japonaises, avec des tentatives d'intrusion sur plus de 1200 sites. Un outil basé sur Playwright (un logiciel de Microsoft qui pilote un navigateur) vérifiait d'abord que la boutique prenait bien les commandes. Les agents devaient ensuite trouver comment exécuter leurs propres commandes sur le serveur du site sans s’y connecter. Les consignes citaient notamment l’injection SQL, l’envoi de fichiers dangereux que le site accepte sans contrôle, le contournement de l’écran de connexion et le traitement non sécurisé d’objets enregistrés par le site. L'objectif était de s'installer durablement dans les systèmes de paiement pour pouvoir en tirer des revenus par la suite.
NorForge a confirmé une intrusion sur le site d'un vendeur de matériel, où l'adresse donnée par l'agent menait à un "webshell", un script permettant de déposer des fichiers sur un serveur et d'y garder un accès. D’après l’agent, l’attaque combinait trois éléments. Le premier est un accès en écriture non autorisé au stockage des sessions (memcached), l’espace où le site garde les informations de chaque visiteur connecté. Le deuxième est une désérialisation PHP non sécurisée. PHP transforme ses objets en texte pour les stocker, puis les reconstruit en les relisant. Si le site ne vérifie pas ce texte, un attaquant peut y glisser des données piégées. Le troisième concerne d’anciens composants de Zend Framework. Aucun point d’entrée évident n’avait été repéré, et c’est cet enchaînement qui a donné accès au serveur. Dans un autre cas, l'application principale d'une grande entreprise était complètement verrouillée. Les agents ont alors cherché l'infrastructure associée, repéré un panneau d'administration public et, après des heures d'essais, affirmé pouvoir y exécuter des commandes.
Il a fallu en moyenne 23 heures pour orchestrer une intrusion réussie. Fagerland estime les dépenses à 5000 dollars de tokens, soit 50 dollars par intrusion réussie. D’après Reuters, la campagne semblait mêler DeepSeek et Claude Code, même si NorForge n'a pas pu confirmer la configuration exacte. L'entreprise Deere dit avoir pris des mesures correctives et n'avoir aucun signe d'accès à des données sensibles. SharkNinja parle d'un site d'assistance isolé du reste de son infrastructure. Pour sa part, Cummins enquête sur un site géré par un prestataire, et Reuters n'a pas pu savoir si des données ont été extraites.
Le mois dernier, nous rapportions qu'un pirate francophone, seul, avait ciblé une quarantaine d'organisations liées à l'extrême droite française et pénétré dans au moins quatorze d'entre elles, en s'appuyant sur Claude à chaque étape, selon Anthropic.

articles.title: La nouvelle affiche des Anneaux de pouvoir saison 3 montre le changement d'ère pour Sauron
articles.text:
C’est une information qui ne surprendra personne, en tout cas pas celles et ceux qui suivent assidûment la série Les Anneaux de pouvoir sur Amazon Prime Video. La saison 3, attendue le 11 novembre, tourne autour de la fabrication de l’Anneau unique. Son synopsis officiel montre Sauron qui cherche à forger l’anneau qui lui donnera l’avantage dans sa guerre contre les Elfes.
La production communique beaucoup autour de cet artefact, que ce soit dans la bande-annonce, dans des clips promotionnels ou dans des affiches mises en ligne courant octobre. On y voit une forge, puis Sauron, incarné par Charlie Vickers, dans les entrailles de la Montagne du Destin, marteau en main face à la lave.
Une nouvelle affiche sur Les Anneaux de pouvoir
L’Anneau unique apparaît par moments, par exemple tenu par une pince, avec la silhouette de Sauron en arrière-plan. Sur la première affiche de la saison, publiée en juillet avant le Comic-Con de San Diego, Sauron tenait l’anneau dans sa main. Jusqu’ici, aucun visuel ne le montrait au doigt du seigneur des ténèbres. Une nouvelle affiche officielle montre désormais Sauron avec la bague au doigt.
Un éclat très vif apparaît en effet sur l’index de sa main droite. Peter Jackson avait fait le même choix dans La Communauté de l’anneau (2001) : dans le prologue du film, Sauron porte l’Anneau unique à l’index de la main droite. La série reprend donc un code visuel des films. J.R.R. Tolkien, lui, n’a jamais précisé à quel doigt Sauron le portait.
Ce Sauron bagué donne un indice sur la saison 3. L’Anneau unique pourrait être achevé bien avant le dernier épisode, ce qui laisserait le temps de montrer le seigneur des ténèbres en train de s’en servir.
Les huit épisodes de cette saison 3 arrivent en trois fois sur Prime Video : les quatre premiers le mercredi 11 novembre, les épisodes 5 et 6 le 18 novembre, puis les deux derniers le 25 novembre. Toute la saison sera donc disponible avant la fin du mois, alors que la saison 2 avait été diffusée chaque semaine.
