articles.title: Modern software is built on the backs of low-paid maintainers, opening the door to potential threats — report details critically underfunded projects that remain understaffed or unfunded
articles.text:
Nearly half of critical open-source software relies on just one or two low-paid maintainers, opening the door to potential threats — report details critically underfunded projects that remain understaffed or unfunded
Welp, time to bring out that xkcd comic out again.
Modern computing systems and devices typically require pieces of crucial open-source software, typically maintained by unpaid or low-paid volunteers. Recently, a report collated a list of critical open-source projects, noting which of them are chronically underfunded and/or understaffed. The information is sobering: 11 out of 23 of the listed projects currently only have one or two maintainers, and funding is generally scarce and sometimes nonexistent.
The Data Drop's report on open-source maintainers identifies that having only one or two sets of eyes on critical pieces of software means that sooner or later something breaks — and it tends to do so in spectacular fashion, given its ubiquity. So, what happens when these projects, which are widely used across software, go underfunded or understaffed?
Lessons from the past
In 2014, the same year as Heartbleed, Shellshock made waves: a vulnerability in the Bash shell that's present in Linux, macOS, and Unix-type systems. The problem was traced back to a line of code present since 1989, displaying how even software that's thought to have all the bugs hammered out of it can still fall prey to attacks. A quick look at Bash's commit history shows it's almost exclusively maintained by Chet Ramey.
In 2016, ImageMagick was exploited, providing attackers with remote code execution. This library is used for image manipulation across a wide range of software, in webpages, mobile apps, and more. A 2020 analysis revealed that hundreds of security issues had been found over the years in its extensive codebase. Nearly every code contribution in the past couple of years has been done by an individual named Dirk Lemstra.
Contemporary examples include 2021's Log4Shell exploit, a critical vulnerability in the Apache Log4j logging library used in millions of servers. The libwebp image-handling library saw a zero-day vulnerability in 2023, and the xz compression library used across Linux and iOS was compromised in 2024.
Thankless work
Key points in the report mention specific repos, which might be under threat. Somewhat unsurprisingly, the low number of overall maintainers and the unpaid nature of the work make it unattractive to perform.
The main time-zone file used across Linux-based operating systems is maintained pro bono by Paul Eggert, a UCLA teacher. Core-js, a piece of support software that lets new JavaScript work in old browsers and is estimated by the author to be used in half of the busiest websites in the world, is handled by Denis Pushkarev. He once had to endure criticism from the community because he added a command-line message to the library's installer asking for help or a job.
The HarfBuzz library developed by Behdad Esfahbod is a cornerstone in ligatures and text shaping in Middle Eastern languages. In those writings, a letter changes shape and/or orientation according to what's around it. Esfahbod handles that vast majority of the project's code, and doesn't mention public or corporate funding.
Libjpeg-turbo handles JPEG images on Android, Firefox, LibreOffice, and every Chromium-based browser. It's kept ship-shape by D.R. Commander aka DRC, who occasionally is contracted for library-specific work, though at arguably modest values of "3-4 figures rather than 6 or 7." Libxml2, just like the label says, handles XML reading and writing across numerous applications and operating systems. Nick Wellnhofer, the original maintainer, stepped down in September 2025, after years of work with little income.
The SQLite project provides a one-file database that's exceedingly easy to integrate into most software, instead of complicated, resource-heavy databases, while still retaining standard SQL language and accouterments. Thanks to its ease of use, it found its way into an astonishing number of applications. Examples include WhatsApp, Dropbox, Android, Windows, and all major browsers.
The project estimates that there are about a trillion instances of SQLite in use. Just four people keep this critical project together, and they've gone to the length of removing their names and photos from the project's page, as "there are a lot of crazy people in the world who might misuse that information." The project is funded by the offering paid support via the founder's company, though there's no word on effective income, especially when it presumably needs to feed four mouths.
Funding is there, but scarce
It's not all doom and gloom, though. Take curl (the software), for example. Almost every developer has used it, thanks to its URL-fetching abilities and extensive scripting options. The project was started by Daniel Stenberg, who is now paid to work full-time on it. The team has now grown to 11 and has received funding through Open Collective and Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency, among others.
Likely due to the lessons learned from their past respective debacles, both the Log4j and OpenSSL projects are likewise funded by the Sovereign Tech Agency, as are the FFmpeg video file handler and the OpenSSH secure shell software that's ubiquitous in Linux servers.
All things considered, it's easy to argue that the critical importance of all the aforementioned software merits sizable investments from industry players, especially those whose commercial products benefit the most from the community's efforts. Plus, even if the firms feel no moral obligation to contribute, in the day and age where AI agents are finding exploitable vulnerabilities in hours, donations to these open-source projects could also be considered investments.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: “We are not forking TypeScript”: Cloudflare spearheads Rust port written by agents, for agents
articles.text:
“We are not forking TypeScript”: Cloudflare spearheads Rust port written by agents, for agents
Cloudflare is going all-out to ensure that AI coding agents can check their work without exhausting available computing resources, leading a new effort to bring Microsoft’s TypeScript compiler to Rust.
But whatever you do, don’t call it a fork.
Taking to X, Cloudflare’s director of engineering Christoph Nakazawa confirmed that the company is taking ownership of tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that it claims is up to eight times faster, and uses 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0.
Microsoft’s own TypeScript compiler is reaping the benefits, too, with the teams sharing optimizations as they work to keep the two implementations in sync.
“We are not forking TypeScript — we are working with the TypeScript team and as a result 7.1 is already ~2.5x faster, too,” Nakazawa writes.
That “port vs fork” message runs throughout the accompanying blog post, co-authored by Nakazawa and fellow Cloudflare engineers Boshen Chen and Dimitri Mitropoulos, who go to great lengths to explain that they very much see TypeScript as Microsoft’s to continue steering.
“To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction.”
“To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript,” they write. “We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.”
Why Rust, when Microsoft already has Go?
Developed and released by Microsoft back in 2012, TypeScript extends JavaScript with a type system that helps developers catch errors before their applications run. However, checking those types can consume considerable computing resources, particularly in large projects where multiple AI agents may be writing and validating code simultaneously.
Microsoft addressed some of those performance problems in July with TypeScript 7.0, replacing its JavaScript-based compiler with one written in Go and delivering roughly tenfold speed improvements.
As The New Stack previously reported, Microsoft had considered Rust for the rewrite, but concluded that reproducing TypeScript’s existing architecture in Rust would introduce significant complications around memory management and compatibility.
The performance gains reported for tsrs make for an interesting comparison with Microsoft’s own Go implementation. Commenting in a Hacker News discussion about the Rust port, Daniel Rosenwasser, Microsoft’s principal product manager for TypeScript, notes that “a lot of the speed does not just come down to language choice,” adding that “some of what is going to make TS 7.1 faster and leaner… actually comes from optimizations discovered in tsrs.”
“Some of what is going to make TS 7.1 faster and leaner… actually comes from optimizations discovered in tsrs.”
Separately, Rosenwasser announced TypeScript 7.1 beta earlier today, detailing substantial speed and memory optimizations.
Cloudflare, for its part, sees another opportunity in Rust, particularly its compatibility with WebAssembly (Wasm). Go can compile to Wasm, but it has to bring its garbage collector along. Rust offers more direct control over memory, reducing the overhead of running development tools in resource-constrained environments. For Cloudflare, that could make it easier to run complete development environments inside browsers and isolated Workers sandboxes, where AI agents can write, check, and build applications.
The move also fits into Cloudflare’s growing JavaScript ecosystem. As The New Stack reported last week, the company has been assembling an extensive collection of JavaScript tools and expertise, including through its acquisition of VoidZero in June and the recent release of Void, an open-source platform for deploying and managing AI-built applications.
With that in mind, it’s the Cloudflare and VoidZero teams who are are now developing tsrs as part of Oxc, VoidZero’s Rust-based JavaScript toolchain, with plans to integrate it into other developer tools.
Owner and operator: A tsrs origin story
It’s worth noting that the tsrs project began just last month at restaurant software company Owner.com, where head of AI developer experience Max Schwenk says he faced a 37,000-file TypeScript backend. Writing in a blog post published on Monday, he notes that Microsoft’s Go compiler consumed 19 GiB of memory and took 80 seconds for a single-threaded check, restricting how many coding agents could work concurrently.
With multiple agents generating code simultaneously, the resource demands made it difficult for each to check its changes independently, forcing Owner.com to experiment with cloud-based development environments and other compromises.
“For a coding agent to be maximally productive, it needs to be able to validate its work in the tightest possible loop,” Schwenk writes.
After running into limits while trying to improve the Go compiler’s memory usage, Schwenk tried something somewhat more ambitious: use Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 to recreate the compiler in Rust. He would direct the experiment and evaluate the results, leaving the implementation entirely to AI agents.
“I wrote zero code,” Schwenk writes. “Not ‘barely any’. Zero.”
“I wrote zero code. Not ‘barely any’. Zero.”
And the results came remarkably quickly. Schwenk says he deployed more than 20 AI subagents in parallel, waking the following morning to a functioning typechecker. Further optimizations brought Owner.com’s typechecking time down to roughly seven seconds in CI, and across more than a dozen public projects, Schwenk reports tsrs running 2.5 to five times faster than Microsoft’s newer Go compiler nightly, while using about a third as much memory.
Agentic rewrites in Rust
In truth, the tsrs project is just the latest example of AI agents being enlisted for substantial Rust migrations. As The New Stack reported last month, GitHub used its own Copilot agents to rewrite its coding-agent runtime in Rust, while Anthropic had previously used Claude agents to help migrate its Bun JavaScript runtime from Zig to Rust.
Elsewhere, Meta has also used AI to help port the React Compiler to Rust, while in September OpenAI revealed two engineers used Codex and GPT-5.5 to rebuild its Habitat storage service in Rust.
But such rapid, AI-assisted rewrites raise questions about how developers verify that the resulting software behaves as intended. For a TypeScript compiler, that means ensuring it catches the same errors as Microsoft’s implementation. Schwenk says the project uses TypeScript’s conformance tests, deliberately introduces errors into real projects and runs Miri, a tool for detecting memory-safety problems in Rust. Those checks have already uncovered a memory bug that appeared only in an optimized build.
“A faster compiler that finds fewer errors is a broken compiler with good marketing.”
“A faster compiler that finds fewer errors is a broken compiler with good marketing,” Schwenk writes.
Maintaining compatibility, it’s fair to say, will be an ongoing challenge. Cloudflare plans to borrow the AI-assisted approach behind Vinext, its Vite-based reimplementation of the Next.js web framework, where agents monitor Next.js for changes, run compatibility tests, and propose fixes when differences emerge. Some discrepancies remain in tsrs, including the order in which diagnostic messages are displayed.
“We will apply the same process to TypeScript, taking extreme care that we don’t introduce diverging behaviors from upstream TypeScript,” the Cloudflare authors write.

articles.title: ChatGPT's Chrome extension can now control tabs, download files, and fill out forms
articles.text:
In a nutshell: OpenAI has released a major update to its ChatGPT browser extension, bringing deeper integration with Google Chrome. The extension can now access content from open webpages, analyze information, and complete tasks directly in the browser. The update also introduces new voice features and support for several additional languages.
ChatGPT's Chrome extension gained the ability to access content from open tabs last July. The latest update introduces two distinct AI modes, Chat and Work, allowing ChatGPT to interact with browser tabs and perform a wide range of tasks, including filling out online forms using information from documents stored on the device.
In Chat mode, the AI can read content from open tabs to analyze information and answer questions based on the active page context. For example, users can compare prices, delivery times, return policies, and other factors for products listed across different shopping sites.
In Work mode, ChatGPT can control the browser to send messages, download files, and group open tabs by topic. It can also fill out forms using information gathered online or extracted from files stored on the computer. Once a form is completed, users can review it manually before submitting it.
 – ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) October 15, 2026
Users can also tag ChatGPT with "@Chrome" directly in the ChatGPT app or on the website to perform browser tasks without opening the extension's side panel. Additionally, ChatGPT can now be restricted to specific tabs, preventing it from accessing other open pages.
Another new feature is a dedicated ChatGPT tab in Chrome that contains the user's ChatGPT history. Users can ask questions in Chat mode or perform tasks in Work mode from this tab. When accessing chat history or visiting new websites, ChatGPT will ask for permission, allowing users to choose between "allow once," "allow for this site," "allow for all sites," and "decline."
The new features are available for free in several Chromium-based browsers, including Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi. However, they will not be immediately available in Firefox or Safari. The updated extension can be downloaded from the Chrome Web Store.
OpenAI originally integrated ChatGPT into Chrome last July, allowing users to access several AI features through the extension's Side Chat panel. The update enabled ChatGPT to summarize articles, explain complicated content in simple English, answer questions about YouTube videos, and translate text from a wide range of supported languages.
While OpenAI continues to improve ChatGPT's support for third-party browsers, its own Atlas browser, which debuted last year with ChatGPT integration, was retired in August after failing to capture a substantial share of the browser market from established competitors such as Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Firefox.

articles.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
articles.text:
GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes. The October 1 release focuses on reducing unnecessary Kubernetes API requests, improving controller throughput and making upgrades and shutdowns more predictable, particularly for environments managing large numbers of runner scale sets.
ARC is a Kubernetes operator that automatically scales self-hosted runners in response to workflow demand. It allows organisations to run their own execution infrastructure while creating and removing runner instances as jobs arrive and finish. This is particularly useful for enterprises that need control over build environments, network access, compute resources, or workload isolation without maintaining a permanently provisioned pool of runners.
One of the main themes in version 0.15.0 is reducing the work the controller performs to keep runner resources in sync. Controller updates now use Kubernetes patch requests instead of full update requests, reducing the size of API payloads. Runner status aggregation has also moved to metrics for EphemeralRunnerSet and AutoscalingRunnerSet, reducing the number of status updates sent to the Kubernetes API.
The controllers now filter incoming events to avoid unnecessary reconciliation, while listener API client rate limits can be configured through queries-per-second and burst settings. Teams can also configure reconciliation concurrency globally or for individual controllers using max-concurrent-reconciles flags. Together, these changes give platform teams more control over how ARC behaves under load and should help reduce avoidable processing and API traffic in larger deployments.
The release also addresses lifecycle management. Patch-version upgrades now update resources in place, maintaining a one-to-one mapping between autoscaling runner sets and ephemeral runner sets and reducing disruption during upgrades.
Controller shutdown behaviour has also been improved. The terminationGracePeriodSeconds setting is now configurable and aligned with the controller manager's graceful-shutdown timeout, allowing operators to better control how the controller exits during restarts or upgrades.
ARC can also re-register a runner scale set when its recorded counterpart no longer exists in the GitHub Actions service. This helps the controller recover from a mismatch between its local Kubernetes state and the scale-set state maintained by GitHub.
Finally, ephemeral runners can be deleted faster when their runner pods exit successfully because ARC skips an additional server-side check for runner removal. While individually small, these changes address the operational details that become increasingly important when runner environments are created and destroyed continuously.
Moving runner status aggregation into metrics is particularly relevant to teams operating ARC as shared CI infrastructure. Large runner fleets generate frequent lifecycle events as jobs are queued, runners are provisioned, workloads execute, and ephemeral environments are removed. Reducing status patches can ease pressure on the Kubernetes API, while metrics provide a more suitable basis for monitoring aggregate controller and runner behaviour.
Configurable reconciliation concurrency and listener rate limits also help operators tune the balance between throughput and API pressure. However, these settings are not simply performance switches: increasing concurrency can increase the rate at which the controller interacts with Kubernetes and GitHub services. Teams should therefore validate changes against their workload patterns and cluster capacity rather than assuming higher concurrency is always better.
ARC is part of a broader move towards dynamically managed CI execution infrastructure. CircleCI's Machine Runner Orchestrator, for example, focuses on scaling machine-based runners and supports different resource classes, including CPU, GPU, and ARM workloads. ARC instead integrates directly with Kubernetes to manage GitHub Actions runner scale sets, commonly using ephemeral runner environments. The two approaches address the same broad challenge, matching execution capacity to CI demand, but differ in their platform integration and runner execution models
For organisations already standardised on GitHub Actions and Kubernetes, ARC provides a native way to manage runner capacity alongside other cluster resources. Its trade-off is that platform teams must also operate the controller, manage Kubernetes capacity and understand how runner scaling interacts with cluster scheduling, API limits and workflow demand.
ARC 0.15.0 is an incremental release, but its emphasis reflects a significant engineering concern: once CI infrastructure serves many repositories and teams, controller efficiency and lifecycle reliability become delivery concerns in their own right.

articles.title: OpenBSD 8.0 arrives with security record still intact
articles.text:
OpenBSD 8.0 is here, marking the project’s 61st release and continuing its schedule of semiannual releases dating back to 1996. What started more than 30 years ago as a fork of NetBSD has grown into one of the most security-conscious operating systems in active development. In a post to the project’s announcements mailing list, OpenBSD founder Theo de Raadt highlights a host of improvements included with the latest version and writes that the project remains “proud of OpenBSD’s record of more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install.”
The latest OpenBSD version brings new features and improvements across the board. These changes, particularly the new Intel Arc support and expanded virtual address space, should improve compatibility with modern graphics cards and allow the system to map more than 4GB of VRAM. Some of the major updates noted in the release newsletter are as follows:
- Added support for Intel Arc A-Series (DG2/Alchemist) graphics cards.
- 512GB kernel virtual address space on AMD64, up from 4GB, allowing VRAM mapping above 4GB.
- Added hibernation support for ARM64 systems.
- A new RPKI-to-router daemon: rtrd(8).
- RISC-V improvements including kernel support for the ‘V’ vector extension and support for Advanced Interrupt Architecture.
- Wireless network driver additions and improvements, including 802.11n and 40 MHz channels for the qwx(4) wireless driver.
- Added support for up to 64 virtual CPUs per guest virtual machine.
- Security and internal improvements for LibreSSL 4.4.0 and OpenSSH 10.6.
- Improvements to the vmm/vmd virtualization stack.
The new OpenBSD also retires support for Loongson architecture after the port stopped working with the Clang 22 compiler. If you’re interested in reading over all the changes that come with the new OpenBSD 8.0, you can take a look at the release announcement.

articles.title: Elon Musk quer doar ações da SpaceX para crianças nos EUA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Elon Musk quer doar ações da SpaceX para crianças nos EUA
CEO da empresa estaria disposto a ceder US$ 10,5 bilhões em programa de contas para crianças e adolescentes.
Elon Musk afirmou que pretende doar ações da SpaceX para crianças dos Estados Unidos. Embora não tenha detalhado como a iniciativa funcionaria, a contribuição pode chegar a US$ 10,5 bilhões (R$ 52,5 bilhões). Em uma publicação no X, o bilionário disse que a proposta seria viabilizada pelo programa Trump Accounts, criado para incentivar a independência financeira de crianças nascidas no país durante o segundo mandato do atual presidente.
Além de Musk, a iniciativa já conta com doações da própria presidente da SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, e da gigante de semicondutores Micron, que já investiram US$ 6,2 bilhões (R$ 31 bilhões) e US$ 250 milhões (R$ 1,2 bilhão), respectivamente. A medida surge em meio às eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos.
No post feito no X/Twitter, o também CEO da Tesla não deu detalhes de quanto será doado ou qual faixa etária vai receber o projeto. A estimativa dos US$ 10,5 bilhões se dá a partir do valor de cada ação da SpaceX hoje (cerca de US$ 147, ou R$ 740 em conversão direta) e as 72 milhões de crianças nos Estados Unidos. Segundo o bilionário, a doação seria feita a partir do ano que vem, e seria “a primeira de muitas”.
Além da SpaceX e da Micron, que já realizaram doações, outras empresas têm planos de participar do projeto, incluindo Uber, Intel, IBM e Nvidia. Em resposta a Brad Gerstner, um dos criadores da Trump Accounts, Musk agradeceu: “Obrigado por ajudar a tornar isso possível”.
As Trump Accounts têm como objetivo garantir a independência financeira das crianças nos Estados Unidos. Todos os nascidos durante o segundo mandato do presidente Donald Trump, no cargo desde 2024, têm uma conta aberta automaticamente com US$ 1 mil (R$ 5 mil) depositados pelo governo.
Os pais também podem deduzir até US$ 2,5 mil (R$ 7,5 mil) anuais do pre-tax, imposto que sai do salário antes da cobrança do imposto de renda. Também é possível investir além disso por conta própria, com limite de US$ 5 mil (R$ 25 mil) por ano.
Um ponto importante do programa é que as contas não podem ser movimentadas até essas crianças chegarem aos 18 anos, sob risco de multas que seguem as leis de aposentadoria do país. Isso significa que uma família que contar apenas com os US$ 1 mil investido pelo governo em 2026 terá pouco menos de US$ 4 mil em 2044 garantidos para investir em seus filhos, considerando um retorno anual de 7% nas Trump Accounts.

articles.title: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia's stronghold with AI app developers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On Tuesday, Google announced that TorchTPU, its long-awaited version of PyTorch, is now available as an open source project. With this, Google joins Amazon in trying to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on the AI industry, where most AI apps are written by default to run on Nvidia’s chips, or GPUs.
PyTorch is the popular open source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. At the time, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the standard hardware for AI research, so many of PyTorch’s features were built to work specifically with them. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects.
Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud. Developers can do this with a simple configuration change and no rewriting of their apps.
Amazon made a similar announcement Monday, when it released its own version of PyTorch, called TorchNeuron. TorchNeuron allows AI apps to be ported to Amazon’s homegrown AI chip, Trainium, and to AWS with no rewriting. Amazon also said it’s going even further in its effort to loosen Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch. It is submitting code to the main PyTorch project that decouples various features from Nvidia’s chips, making it more open to any hardware by default.
Google may be one-upping Amazon in a few ways, however. It says it worked directly with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (maker of vLLM), RadixArk (maker of SGLang), and others to ensure that TorchTPU’s features and code libraries work well with these popular AI development tools, just as the original PyTorch does.
Plus the search giant has launched a dedicated tool, the TPU agent suite, to help developers move their apps to Google’s chips and cloud and fix errors along the way. It even updated its popular LiteRT tool, which runs AI on phones, laptops, and embedded devices, to work better with PyTorch AI apps.
None of this means AI app developers will automatically ditch Nvidia’s hardware en masse just because they can now easily move to alternative chips and clouds. But Amazon and Google are clearly working to end Nvidia’s advantage.

articles.title: Amazon Canada to hire 9,000 seasonal workers for the holidays
articles.text:
Amazon has announced plans to hire 9,000 seasonal employees in Canada this holiday season.
The e-commerce giant is looking to fill roles across 55 Canadian sites, including fulfillment centres, sortation centres, and delivery stations. It adds that the average hourly base wage for seasonal roles is nearly $24, with roles including select benefits on day one, including mental health and wellbeing support and a new 10 per cent discount on grocery and daily essentials purchases.
Amazon says available roles will be posted on hiring.amazon.ca, with more positions posted on a “rolling basis” throughout the holiday season. The company says this comes amid a $78 million increase in pay increases in Canada this year, including raising the average hourly base wage by $1 to more than $26 per hour. In the U.S., Amazon says it will also hire over 300,000 workers for the holiday season.
Of course, the holidays will be an especially busy period for Amazon, although it remains to be seen whether demand will be more muted than usual given the continued rise in the cost of living.

articles.title: Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
articles.text:
Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
Impressive benchmark results should make it easy for engineers to select the right open model for the outcome they are tasked with developing. However, that is not the case.
Benchmarks indicate an open model’s optimal performance, but in production, a model must work repeatedly. The challenge is that in production, other factors matter, such as the information provided to the model and its accuracy. So benchmarks can’t tell an engineer whether the AI they are developing will complete the task accurately, or even at all. This is especially important for long-horizon AI tasks.
Ryan Hanrui Wang, SVP of Applied AI at AI cloud provider Nebius, tells The New Stack it is important to measure an open model by the industry benchmarks in conjunction with internal benchmarks and harnesses to ensure you get the inference outcomes the organization requires, something he says the Amsterdam, Netherlands-based company always does in partnership with its clients.
Wang joined Nebius when it acquired Eigen AI, the inference-optimization startup he co-founded and led as CEO, in a roughly $643 million deal announced in May; Nebius sells inference through its Token Factory platform.
“Customers often have their own benchmarks, so we can use their agent workflow and its traces to see the level of success we can work with. We always work closely with them to define the benchmarks.”
Wang goes on to add: “The public benchmark may not cover the multi-domain tasks that an engineer wants inference to do in the actual production environment.” He says this can misalign agent tasks with the true cost of inference calls. “The workflow is not tested by the benchmark design. There needs to be in-context learning.”
Engineers and organizations should therefore not spend too much time selecting the open model; they should look at the entire inference stack. Model selection should depend on whether the engineer needs a lower-cost, flexible open-model stack or a frontier model for inference.
For those who need lower cost, Wang says Nebius evaluates open models such as Kimi and DeepSeek, as well as lighter “flash” models, to see whether they can meet inference accuracy needs and whether fine-tuning is required.
Those who want superior accuracy and quality usually narrow it down to two or three large open models and then fine-tune them to improve accuracy. Wang says open model selection is only the first step; after selection, they need to ensure long-context tasks and cached inputs deliver the expected outcome.
Inference and post-training
In post-training, Wang says the organization uses its data to improve accuracy and task fit, while the serving layer, quantization, batching, caching, and kernel optimization drive inference speed. In addition, engineers should develop the cache system for production traffic, ensuring the hit rate is maximized for the workload so repeated inputs hit the cache rather than being recomputed.
“The other important thing is throughput, the measure of how many tokens are generated in a certain time span, as they are a major trade-off against interactivity,” Wang adds. Engineers need to balance better utilization and cheaper tokens with acceptable interactivity– per-user speed.
Getting concurrency right ensures the organization uses the open model effectively; it is a fine balancing act for engineers. If compute isn’t fully utilized, token cost is high. But high utilization with increased concurrency can reduce end-user token-per-second speed.
Engineers also need to watch tail latency, not just averages. “P95 and P99 are important metrics for the per-user token speed and time to first token (TTFT); the time they need to wait needs to be below five seconds for some of our customers,” Wang says. A system can post a great average response time and still be unusable if one request in twenty stalls.
Modeling for accuracy
Engineers need to be careful when considering benchmark results and accuracy. Benchmarks may test reasoning on a mathematical problem, which isn’t very useful if the engineer is developing an AI agent for customer support, where high emotional intelligence (EQ) matters more. “So there is a misalignment between the different benchmarks and actual production,” Wang says.
On cost per successful task, Wang says engineers must remember that cheap tokens are useless if the model is inaccurate.
Engineers need to consider the end-to-end process the AI will perform. This lets engineers select the right-sized open model for the AI task. Wang gives the example of a specialized assistant agent where Nebius gathered 6,000 traces to refine a small model and improved accuracy by 11% while executing 22% fewer tool calls.
He raises this point because it counters the tendency to think bigger is better, but accuracy gains from increasing model size diminish. “There is typically a tipping point for this kind of task,” Wang says. For a task like customer support, he says, 10 billion parameters could be enough, while 100 billion or even a trillion parameters yields only minimal accuracy gains. “What we want to do is find the sweet spot.”
Engineers can use large models as a reference point, then tune the reasoning with their organizational data to find an open model with the right accuracy and size for the task.
“We typically do a sweep of several models, using the largest model as a reference to know where the sweet spot for model size is,” Wang says. “For a complicated task, we can dissect the complex task into smaller subtasks, working with the customer, which connects workflows and can then use smaller models.”
Wang describes this process as a division of labor, referencing the famous economist Adam Smith.
This approach shows the course of AI engineering maturity. Like every sector in technological and engineering history, the initial gold rush targets bigger-is-better. As the engineering matures, it focuses on outcomes and engineering excellence, and therefore on working with partners who understand how to achieve them.
Sometimes that is a bigger model; other times a small niche development is best.

articles.title: Zeabur shutting down after second security breach in two months
articles.text:
Development platform Zeabur has disclosed details of a cybersecurity incident in which an attacker used leaked internal credentials stored in plaintext to compromise its infrastructure and steal over 3.2 million environment variable records and information for 321,810 accounts.
The attackers used stolen administrator credentials and cloud access keys to compromise Zeabur’s shared hosting infrastructure and dedicated servers, eventually gaining access to its production database.
“On October 14–15, 2026, an attacker used leaked Zeabur internal credentials to break into the shared cluster, some Dedicated Servers, and Zeabur internal systems, and eventually read the platform database,” Zeabur’s announcement reads.
Zeabur is a developer hosting and deployment platform that lets developers connect a GitHub repository and have the platform handle deployment, databases, HTTPS, and infrastructure management.
In late August 2026, the company suffered another security breach when hackers exploited a flaw in a customer’s NextChat application and then moved through poorly isolated internal systems.
This led to the theft of AWS credentials and access to the production database, exposing account information, API keys, and other secrets stored there.
In the latest incident, Zeabur says the compromise was broader, affecting shared clusters across nine regions, 321,810 accounts, and roughly 3.2 million environment-variable records.
Also, Zeabur confirmed root sign-ins on 101 GCP servers by 92 users, with the attackers adding SSH keys to 50 servers and attaching 16 customer disk copies to their own virtual machines.
The company says that attackers likely obtained the credentials they used in the second attack during the August breach, though it hasn’t confirmed this.
Beyond failing to store credentials in encrypted form, Zeabur also failed to rotate all administrator account credentials since the August incident, while administrator portals remained accessible to the public internet.
“The admin tokens had no expiry, had not been rotated since they were created in January 2024, and were not included in the post-August rotation,” explained Zeabur.
Users are urged to rotate exposed credentials and secrets immediately, revoke all active sessions, and rebuild compromised GCP servers.
Variables previously migrated exclusively to customers’ own servers as part of the August incident response escaped this latest platform database exposure, although compromised hosts could still expose them.
Zeabur announces shutdown
After discovering the latest security incident, Zeabur announced over the weekend that it will shut down its services starting December 1, 2026, and finish by December 31, 2026.
The decision comes after 3.5 years of continuous growth, including a record year in 2026, but Zeabur said scaling the project to meet market demand has made it increasingly complex and difficult to maintain, and the recent security failures reflect that.
“After the August incident, we spent a long time discussing and struggling with what to do next,” explained Zeabur.
“Following this latest incident, we reassessed what it would take to keep operating and the responsibilities our team could carry. We ultimately decided to wind down.”
On December 1, renewals will be disabled, and all running services on shared clusters will be paused. By the end of the year, all dedicated servers will expire and shut down, and all shared clusters will stop.
Users may be given additional time for data migration, though no concrete timelines on that front have been provided yet.

articles.title: Eloelo's Saurabh Pandey bets that Dolphin AI can break the gatekeepers of Indian storytelling
articles.text:
Eloelo's Saurabh Pandey bets that Dolphin AI can break the gatekeepers of Indian storytelling
The Eloelo Group founder says AI-led production could turn India's storytellers into a global export force.
When James Cameron's epic sci-fi movie Avatar hit cinemas in late 2000s, plenty of Indians watched it and wondered why we weren't making films like that. According to Saurabh Pandey, Founder and CEO of Eloelo Group, that question is about to lose its force.
Eloelo Group is an Indian entertainment and technology company headquartered in Bengaluru, founded in 2020 by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey. It began as a live social entertainment and social gaming platform and has since evolved into a broader entertainment ecosystem spanning microdramas through Story TV and Elo TV, micro-learning through Masters, and AI-powered video production through Dolphin AI.
At the 17th edition of TechSparks, YourStory's flagship event, Pandey showed off Dolphin AI, Eloelo's AI video creation tool, in a session titled 'Can AI turn India into a global content export hub?', moderated by Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project.
Dolphin AI currently has a waitlist, with the platform releasing invite codes in batches.
For now, Dolphin AI is free as Eloelo is giving away generous early credits so creators can make their first few videos and get a feel for the solution. However, a credit-based pricing model will arrive eventually. Pandey said the team mainly wants to see how people use Dolphin AI, and early signs are promising: roughly 15,000 videos were built in about eight days, mostly through organic discovery.
The end of the budget bottleneck
Pandey's pitch centres on who gets to tell big stories. In the VFX era, he said, movie making belonged to whoever had the money. A good storyteller with a period drama in mind simply could not afford the visuals it demanded, and that made budgets the real gatekeeper of content.
AI is a total game-changer, he argued. Production usually eats up 50 to 60% of revenue in this category, squeezing distribution budgets and destroying unit economics. By slashing those production costs, creator imagination finally gets the breathing room it needs to thrive.
Distribution, meanwhile, has become largely algorithmic. A creator in India now competes for attention in the US or Europe on the same footing as anyone else.
Why this time might be different
The conversation then moved to another area of content that is seeing traction: micro-drama and short-form content. These have attracted plenty of Indian startups, yet few have become popular.
In India, he said, the top four or five micro-drama players together are running at more than Rs 5,000 crore, a level they reached in just 18 months.
He also pointed to South Korea, a country of 52 million people that has built a $15-billion content export economy. India has 1.4 billion people and no shortage of creative talent, he said. What it has lacked is intent, technology, ambition and capital. Too many Indian creators, in his view, still focus only on local audience. Nobody asks whether a new LLM is launching for India, he noted; it just launches for the world. Why shouldn't Indian stories do the same?
Platforms will consolidate, but supply is wide open
Pandey doesn't expect micro-drama to escape the pattern seen elsewhere. Food delivery, quick commerce, ecommerce and ride-hailing all ended up with two or three heavily funded players holding 70 to 75% of the market, and he expects the same for content.
The real opportunity, he said, lies on the supply side.
Eloelo launched about 200 new micro-dramas last month, roughly five or six a night, and works with around 90 production houses. His advice to would-be founders is to skip the platform race and build lean AI studios instead: a handful of writers, editors, promo producers and a line producer who could feed micro-dramas, OTT content and exportable IP to the big platforms.
He also had a message for writers and producers wary of AI. Use it as a brainstorming partner, he said, and ship more. As an example, he floated an idea close to his heart. An AI Ramayana already exists, but nobody has yet made a spectacular AI Mahabharata.
Eloelo has grown from one platform to five within the same group, Pandey said, and an IPO is not on the cards anytime soon. The focus is on growing profitably and sustainably.

articles.title: Un pájaro diminuto revoluciona Mieres: la aparición de una curruca gavilana, vista solo 14 veces en España, desata una peregrinación ornitológica
articles.text:
Si usted no es ornitólogo, la frase “curruca gavilana en Mieres” quizá no le diga absolutamente nada. Para quienes miramos pájaros, equivale a ver un cometa desde el balcón. Pero mejor hagamos un examen a vista de pájaro, para no confundir plumaje. Solo adelanto un detalle: tirarles fotos a estas aves es esencial, pero si lo hacen un puñado de aficionados con carísimos teleobjetivos, es normal que cualquiera que lo vea por la calle piense que son unos ladinos paparazzi intentando cazar a la influencer de turno.
Qué pasó. El 12 de octubre, Clemente Álvarez Usategui, responsable de la Coordinadora Ornitológica de Asturias, paseaba por el parque Aníbal Vázquez, en La Mayacina, como hace casi a diario desde finales de julio. Había notado que el parque funcionaba como corredor para aves migratorias, así que iba cada día.
Esa mañana, entre los arbustos, fotografió una curruca gavilana. Según contó él mismo, es la cuarta vez que se ve en Asturias y la número 14 en España. Los registros públicos de observación sitúan al ave en el parque el 12 y el 13 de octubre, y un observador la calificó de una de las rarezas del otoño asturiano.
Quién es. Mide 15,5 centímetros y alcanza entre 23 y 27 de envergadura. Diminuta comparado con una paloma, enorme para una curruca (porque pesa entre 26 y 30 gramos). El macho adulto luce dorso gris plomizo, pecho y flancos barrados como un gavilán y ojo amarillo. De ahí el nombre. Come insectos y, en verano y otoño, pequeños frutos. No está amenazada: la UICN la clasifica en “preocupación menor”. Es decir, lo raro es verla allí.
Cómo identificarla. En otoño abundan los jóvenes: iris oscuro y poco barrado. Se parecen a la curruca mosquitera. Delatan a la gavilana su aspecto más robusto, el pico grande de base pálida y las plumas moteadas bajo la cola. Con ese gris sin chispa, cuesta reconocerla incluso a ojos entrenados.
¿Y por qué no pintaba nada allí? Pues porque cría desde el Báltico y el este de Alemania hasta Mongolia, con poblaciones en Polonia, Rumanía y Ucrania. Pasa el invierno en la península arábiga y en África oriental, en torno a Kenia. Para llegar, rodea el Mediterráneo por el este. Y Asturias queda muy al oeste de esa ruta.
Cómo se pierde un pájaro. La migración es un programa genético: dirección y duración del viaje se heredan. Si el programa falla, el ave vuela como el conductor que entra en sentido contrario en la autopista, según la comparación de un equipo de la Universidad de Marburgo.
Un análisis con datos de eBird sobre pájaros terrestres hallados en pleno Pacífico encontró más casos en otoño. Entre las causas se barajan vientos fuertes, nubes que ocultan el paisaje y alteraciones del campo magnético. SEO/BirdLife añade un patrón: muchas currucas gavilanas, sobre todo de primer año, aparecen en otoño en el oeste y noroeste de su área de cría, como Gran Bretaña o Países Bajos.
Lista breve. La historia de la curruca gavilana (Sylvia nisoria) en España tiene, hasta ahora, cinco citas homologadas, y todas dibujan una ventana otoñal sorprendentemente precisa. Las dos primeras llegaron desde Baleares: un ejemplar en Menorca, el 27 de septiembre de 1983, y otro en Formentera, el 7 de octubre de 1989. En ambos casos, eran aves capturadas para anillarlas.
Hubo que esperar hasta 2015 para volver a tener noticias de la especie. El 28 de septiembre, un ejemplar fue observado desde un buque oceanográfico, a unas 15 millas de Cabo Prior (A Coruña). Seis años después, el 26 de octubre de 2021, una curruca gavilana de primer invierno apareció entre los pequeños tarayes de las dunas de Ponzos, en Ferrol. A estos registros se suma un adulto observado el 16 de octubre de 2020 en Luces (Colunga), según recoge el informe de rarezas.
En resumen, todas se concentran entre el 27 de septiembre y el 26 de octubre. Por eso, el ejemplar de Mieres, observado el día 12 encaja de lleno en el patrón de aparición conocido para la especie. Ahora queda el último paso: su homologación por el Comité de Rarezas de SEO/BirdLife. La observación aún está pendiente de veredicto, aunque desde 2020 el Comité dispone de un procedimiento exprés que permite resolver algunos casos en apenas unos días.
Del parque a la peregrinación. Y aquí empieza lo curioso, porque esta ave se hizo algo más que el Camino de Santiago y atrajo como Shakira. Llegó gente de Salamanca, Galicia, Madrid, Cantabria, Burgos y Aragón llegó con sus dispositivos. Un aficionado cogió el AVE en Madrid, ida y vuelta en el día, solo para verla.
Con teleobjetivos y prismáticos, los visitantes asustaron a los vecinos, que avisaron a la policía. Una pareja de agentes se presentó pensando en algo grave y se encontró con una cuadrilla de aficionados a las aves. Y que aparezca en ese parque no es casual. Durante años, los ornitólogos asturianos insistieron en plantar vegetación autóctona: cornejos, servales y matorrales. La impulsó la entonces concejal Delia Campomanes. Y dichos frutos forman parte del menú que retiene a la curruca.
¿Afición de nicho? Ni hablar. La RAE aceptó en diciembre de 2022 que pajarear también significa observar aves; antes solo recogía cazarlas y vagar sin oficio. Merlin, la aplicación gratuita que identifica aves por foto o sonido, sumaba 40 millones de instalaciones y más de 16 millones de usuarios activos en 2025, un 35% más que el año anterior. En Reino Unido, la RSPB cifra en unos 750.000 los jóvenes de 16 a 29 años que observan aves con regularidad, un 1.088% más que en 2018.
Móvil y libreta. Anotar fecha, hora y rasgos, y fotografiar el ave, convierte un "creo que vi" en un dato validable. Lo recuerda Clemente Álvarez: el ornitólogo Elías García Sánchez falleció sin poder enviar dos fotos de curruca gavilana de Cabo Peñas y Peroño. Para homologar una cita hace falta documentarla, con fotos y descripción. Solo así entra en el conocimiento científico. Para muchos, además, la libreta es un pequeño acto artístico, porque dibujar obliga a mirar despacio.
Y el resultado sirve, ya que las observaciones de miles de aficionados alimentan los programas de seguimiento de SEO/BirdLife, uno de los principales indicadores del estado de la naturaleza en España. En cualquier caso, tarde o temprano la curruca de Mieres seguirá su viaje, pero ya se puede marcar un punto nuevo en el mapa. Es su nuevo vecindario.

Le vidéoprojecteur Full HD Wielio est à 107,99 € (-58 %) avec coupon
Le vidéoprojecteur Wielio propose une définition Full HD, Android 14 et une connexion Wi-Fi 6, avec un support inclinable et une mise au point électrique.
Amazon affiche le vidéoprojecteur Full HD Wielio à 119,99 €, avec un coupon à cocher pour payer 107,99 €. Ce prix représente une réduction d’environ 58 % par rapport à l’ancien prix de 259,99 €, également indiqué comme le plus bas des 30 derniers jours. L’offre est vendue par HuaQian Tech et expédiée par Amazon.
Pour obtenir ce tarif, activez le coupon sur la fiche produit avant l’ajout au panier et vérifiez son application au moment du paiement.
Une projection Full HD et des réglages électriques
Le vidéoprojecteur Wielio affiche une définition de 1 920 × 1 080 pixels. La compatibilité 4K annoncée correspond au décodage des vidéos : l’image projetée reste en Full HD. Pour regarder un film, mieux vaut prévoir une pièce assombrie afin de préserver le contraste.
L’appareil dispose d’une correction automatique du trapèze et d’une mise au point électrique. Son support inclinable permet d’orienter la projection sans multiplier les cales sous le boîtier. La télécommande fournie sert à piloter les fonctions et à effectuer les réglages.
Android 14 et plusieurs possibilités de connexion
La fiche annonce Android 14, 1 Go de mémoire vive et 8 Go de stockage pour installer des applications. La disponibilité et le fonctionnement des services de streaming dépendent toutefois de leurs exigences de compatibilité et de certification.
Le Wi-Fi 6 et le Bluetooth 5.4 complètent les connexions HDMI et USB. Un lecteur multimédia externe peut ainsi servir de source via HDMI, tandis que le Bluetooth permet de relier un équipement audio compatible. Un haut-parleur est également intégré pour utiliser le vidéoprojecteur sans enceinte supplémentaire.

articles.title: Netflix : nouveau séisme sur la plateforme avec un changement majeur en interne
articles.text:
Netflix n’a même pas attendu de présenter ses résultats trimestriels aux analystes de Wall Street, prévus ce mardi 20 octobre. Face à une action en baisse de plus de 20 % depuis janvier et à un temps de visionnage qui n’a progressé que de 2 % au premier semestre, le co-CEO de Netflix, Ted Sarandos, a sorti le couperet. Vingt-quatre heures après l’éviction brutale de sa directrice des contenus Bela Bajaria, c’est Dan Lin (qui s’occupait du cinéma) que Ted Sarandos a appelé vendredi pour lui annoncer son renvoi, officialisé ce lundi 19 octobre.
La fin de l’ère de l’austérité pour Netflix : Dan Lin et le piège du « zéro chèque en blanc »
L’aventure aura duré deux ans et demi, soit la moitié de son contrat de cinq ans, pour celui qui avait été nommé en février 2024 pour succéder à Scott Stuber. À son arrivée, Lin incarnait la rupture : fini la distribution de billets verts à l’aveugle, fini le gavage des stars hollywoodiennes et la promesse intenable d’un film inédit par semaine.
En juin, dans le New York Times, Dan Lin affirmait que Netflix avait « accepté » de ne plus travailler avec les cinéastes qui tiennent à une sortie en salles. Mais à Hollywood, la rigueur budgétaire se paie cash dès que les chiffres de visionnage ne suivent plus. Malgré la réorganisation des équipes par genre et quelques sorties en salles à titre d’essai, Lin n’a pas trouvé l’équilibre entre films taillés pour le streaming et sorties au cinéma, principal motif de son renvoi selon les sources du média américain.
Clashs avec Greta Gerwig et Ben Affleck : quand le patron agace les superstars
En coulisses, la méthode cassante de Dan Lin chez Netflix a fini par créer un climat délétère avec l’élite hollywoodienne. Selon Variety, une réunion Zoom consacrée à Narnia (qui s’est fait détruire son premier trailer par les fans), la superproduction au budget de 250 millions de dollars (environ 215 millions d’euros), a mal tourné plus tôt dans l’année. Dan Lin se serait montré « dédaigneux » envers Greta Gerwig, la réalisatrice de Barbie, plus gros succès mondial au box-office de 2023.
L’incident a pris une telle ampleur que l’agent surpuissant de la cinéaste, Bryan Lourd, est intervenu directement auprès de Ted Sarandos. Dan Lin s’est ensuite effacé du projet au profit de son bras droit, Doug Belgrad, lui-même licencié la semaine dernière. Dan Lin se serait aussi opposé à Ben Affleck sur l’usage, pour son film Animals, d’InterPositive, la start-up d’IA cofondée par l’acteur et rachetée par Netflix en juillet, comme le détaillait nos amis de chez Frandroid. Les représentants de Ben Affleck contestent toute dégradation de ses relations avec la plateforme.
Que se passe-t-il vraiment chez le géant du streaming ?
Cette purge au sommet en dit long sur le virage chaotique que traverse Netflix. En confiant l’ensemble de ses contenus (séries, films, programmes en direct) à Peter Rice, ancien dirigeant de Disney et de Fox, la plateforme admet à demi-mot l’échec de sa ligne d’austérité.
Pour rassurer Wall Street, Netflix tente désespérément de retisser des liens avec les réseaux de salles de cinéma traditionnels (un comble pour le pionnier qui méprisait la projection en salle) tout en cherchant sa nouvelle recette magique. Peter Rice prendra ses fonctions le lundi 26 octobre et devra désigner le successeur de Dan Lin. D’après Variety, Mike De Luca et Pam Abdy, anciens patrons du cinéma chez Warner Bros., discuteraient déjà avec Netflix.

articles.title: Jeder Fünfte ist von zu vielen Chats überfordert – warum eine Antwort auch mal dauern darf
articles.text:
Jeder Fünfte ist von zu vielen Chats überfordert – warum eine schnelle Antwort gar nicht immer sein muss
Familienchat, Freundesgruppe, Sprachnachrichten: Viele Menschen in Deutschland fühlen sich einer Befragung zufolge von der Menge an Nachrichten in Messenger-Apps überfordert. 72 Prozent der Nutzerinnen und Nutzer kennen das Gefühl, 20 Prozent geht es sogar häufig so, wie aus einer repräsentativen Umfrage des Unternehmens Bitkom Research im Auftrag des Digitalverbands Bitkom hervorgeht.
69 Prozent lassen Nachrichten gelegentlich unbeantwortet
Ältere fühlen sich demnach häufiger überfordert als Jüngere. Bei den Nutzern ab 65 Jahren kennen 78 Prozent das Gefühl, 28 Prozent häufig. Bei den 16- bis 29-Jährigen sind es 68 Prozent, häufig überfordert sind 16 Prozent. Für die Erhebung wurden den Angaben zufolge 1.006 Menschen ab 16 Jahren zwischen Juli und August telefonisch befragt, darunter 875 Messenger-Nutzer.
    „Viele setzen sich selbst stärker unter Antwortdruck, als sie es von anderen erwarten.“
Insgesamt nutzen demnach 87 Prozent der Menschen ab 16 Jahren privat zumindest gelegentlich Messenger wie Whatsapp, Signal, Telegram oder Threema. 69 Prozent lassen Nachrichten zumindest gelegentlich länger unbeantwortet, weil es ihnen zu viel wird. Zwölf Prozent machen das öfter. 73 Prozent haben dann zumindest gelegentlich ein schlechtes Gewissen, 75 Prozent entschuldigen sich für späte Antworten.
„Viele setzen sich selbst stärker unter Antwortdruck, als sie es von anderen erwarten“, sagte Bitkom-Experte Sebastian Klöß. 87 Prozent haben zumindest gelegentlich Verständnis, wenn andere nicht sofort antworten. Die Geduld hat aber Grenzen: Für 69 Prozent ist es zumindest gelegentlich ein Grund, einen Kontakt auslaufen zu lassen oder abzubrechen, wenn Freunde sehr lange zum Antworten brauchen. Häufig ist das allerdings nur bei neun Prozent der Fall.
Auch eine Umfrage der IU Internationalen Hochschule hatte im Mai Hinweise auf digitalen Stress gefunden. Dort hatten 56,2 Prozent das Gefühl, ihr Umfeld erwarte zeitnahe Antworten. 44,3 Prozent fühlten sich von der Menge an digitalen Informationen überfordert.

articles.title: Le patron de Rivian en est convaincu : la conduite autonome va transformer radicalement le design des voitures
articles.text:
Et si la conduite autonome changeait la forme même de nos voitures ? RJ Scaringe, le patron de Rivian, assure que l’automobile va subir une profonde mutation.
Le constructeur américain, connu pour ses pick-up et SUV pensés pour l’aventure, a lancé en juin le R2, une voiture plus compacte et plus abordable. Et son modèle commence à porter ses fruits après des années de pertes : Rivian a livré 19 248 véhicules au troisième trimestre, un record, soit environ 46 % de plus qu’un an plus tôt.
RJ Scaringe, son fondateur et P.-D.G de Rivian, s’est justement exprimé il y a quelques jours lors du TechCrunch Disrupt, grande conférence américaine consacrée aux nouvelles technologies. Ses prédictions sont fascinantes.
Des « expériences radicalement différentes »
Il a en effet expliqué à TechCrunch que l’autonomie permettrait à son entreprise de construire des « expériences radicalement différentes ». Le dirigeant se dit « follement enthousiaste « à l’idée de ce que les dix prochaines années vont rendre possible dans le secteur, et il est même prêt à repousser la rentabilité de Rivian pour y parvenir.
L’enjeu dépasse le simple confort de conduite. Si la voiture n’a plus besoin d’être pilotée, ses concepteurs n’ont plus à respecter les codes actuels de l’automobile, « on imagine les formats que l’on veut construire pour un véhicule autonome », étaye-t-il. Selon lui, cela « ouvre toutes sortes d’opportunités de design ».
Et Scaringe s’oppose directement à Tesla : il ne croit pas à un monde où tout le monde laisserait sa voiture au garage pour appeler un robotaxi. Même si les voitures savent un jour conduire seules sur certains trajets, il estime peu probable que les habitudes changent radicalement. Reste à voir à quoi ressembleront ces voitures personnelles et autonomes.
Des concepts, mais c’est tout
Mais ce concept n’est pas nouveau. Il y a dix ans, constructeurs automobiles et spécialistes de la conduite autonome annonçaient que les voitures sans conducteur, associées aux moteurs électriques plus simples et moins encombrants que les moteurs thermiques, feraient naître des formes de véhicules inédites.
Quand Mercedes présentait une cabine en forme de bulle, Toyota imaginait des « salons sur roues » tandis que Hyundai dévoilait une voiture dotée de pattes. Aucun de ces projets n’a dépassé le stade du prototype : l’autonomie a demandé bien plus de temps que prévu, et lancer une toute nouvelle catégorie de véhicule s’est révélé bien plus compliqué. Les robotaxis, eux, sont bien là, même s’ils doivent encore faire face à des défis.
De son côté, le système de conduite autonome de Rivian permet aujourd’hui de lâcher le volant, à condition de continuer à surveiller la route. D’ici à la fin de l’année, il doit être capable de mener une voiture d’un point de départ à une destination sans intervention, toujours sous le contrôle du conducteur. La véritable autonomie devrait arriver en 2028, avec la version robotaxi de la R2.

articles.title: Serveurs PHP : préparez-vous à mettre à jour ce mercredi à 16 heures, deux failles critiques corrigées — Frandroid
articles.text:
Branle-bas de combat pour les administrateurs système et les développeurs web. PHP publiera ce mercredi 21 octobre à 16 heures (heure de Paris) des correctifs d’urgence pour colmater deux failles de sécurité critiques.
L’équipe chargée de la sécurité de PHP a publié un avis ce mardi 20 octobre. Elle y annonce des correctifs pour deux failles critiques, attendus ce mercredi 21 octobre à 14 heures UTC, soit 16 heures à Paris. Moins d’une journée sépare donc l’alerte de la mise à jour. Et le public concerné est énorme : PHP est utilisé par 69,3 % des sites dont on connaît le langage côté serveur, d’après les relevés de W3Techs. On y trouve WordPress, une bonne partie des boutiques en ligne et une foule d’applications maison.
Les deux failles portent les identifiants CVE-2026-109618 et CVE-2026-109619, la référence du registre public qui numérote les vulnérabilités. PHP les note 9,2 sur 10 selon CVSS v4.0, la grille standard qui mesure la gravité d’une faille. Pour le reste, l’équipe garde tout jusqu’à la sortie des correctifs : versions touchées, mode d’exploitation et versions corrigées. Elle demande aux utilisateurs de se préparer dès maintenant pour mettre à jour dès la publication.
Une fuite sur Hacker News a bousculé le calendrier
Si PHP prévient avec si peu de délai, c’est que l’information circulait déjà. Le 20 octobre, peu avant l’avis officiel, un utilisateur nommé « petecooper » a publié un message sur Hacker News, le forum tech de l’incubateur Y Combinator. Il y annonçait deux failles d’exécution de code à distance (RCE) dans PHP. En clair, ce type de faille permet à un attaquant de lancer ses propres commandes sur le serveur visé.
Le message a été supprimé depuis, mais BleepingComputer a pu le lire. Il donnait les mêmes identifiants CVE, une note de 10 sur 10 et une divulgation prévue le 22 octobre.
D’après Ars Technica, la fuite comprenait aussi une vidéo, non authentifiée, d’un outil baptisé PHP2Shell. On l’y voyait exécuter du code sur des sites WordPress, Drupal, Magento ou Joomla.
Plus d’un site PHP sur trois tourne encore sur une vieille version
Les sources ne s’accordent pas sur la gravité. watchTowr et le message de Hacker News parlent d’une note de 10, le maximum. De son côté, PHP s’en tient à 9,2, et personne n’a encore expliqué cet écart.
Toujours selon watchTowr, les failles toucheraient PHP 5, 6, 7 et 8. PHP 6 n’est jamais sorti en version stable (le projet l’a abandonné en 2010 et est passé directement de PHP 5 à PHP 7), mais le reste de la liste inquiète davantage. Le site officiel de PHP ne cite aujourd’hui que quatre branches maintenues, de PHP 8.2 à PHP 8.5.
Pourtant, au 20 octobre, 27 % des sites sous PHP utilisaient encore PHP 7 et 7,7 % PHP 5, une version sortie en 2004, toujours d’après W3Techs. Si watchTowr a raison, plus d’un site PHP sur trois tourne donc sur une version que le projet ne suit plus. Surtout, les détails techniques sortiront en même temps que les correctifs.
Cités par Ars Technica, les chercheurs de Sansec, spécialisés dans la sécurité des boutiques en ligne, s’attendent à des attaques de masse dans le quart d’heure qui suivra.
Alors que faire ? Vérifiez la version de PHP de vos serveurs (la commande php -v suffit) et prévoyez une fenêtre de maintenance ce mercredi après-midi. Sur un hébergement mutualisé, la mise à jour dépend de l’hébergeur : demandez-lui quand il compte l’appliquer. PHP annoncera les versions corrigées à 16 heures, heure de Paris, dans la rubrique actualités de php.net.

articles.title: iPhone 16 (512 GB) baixa preço em oferta até 12x sem juros na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
iPhone 16 (512 GB) baixa preço em oferta até 12x sem juros na Amazon
iPhone 16 (512 GB) traz câmera wide de 48 MP e tela OLED de 2.000 nits; celular da Apple com bastante espaço interno sai quase pela metade do preço em suaves prestações
O iPhone 16 de 512 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 5.499 em até 12x sem juros na Amazon. O celular da Apple, equipado com tela OLED de 2.000 nits, chip A18 e câmera wide de 48 MP, recebe desconto de 46% sobre o preço original de R$ 10.099.
Esta é uma rara chance de levar para casa um iPhone com bastante espaço interno para vídeos, apps e games, e em parcelas que cabem no bolso.
Lançado em 2024, o iPhone 16 permanece como um dos melhores celulares da Apple. Seu kit de câmeras inclui uma wide com OIS de 48 MP e uma ultrawide de 12 MP com ângulo de 120º, que capturam belas cenas em ambientes amplos, e uma frontal de 12 MP que tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K.
Seu chip Apple A18 e os 8 GB de RAM o permitem rodar apps pesados em multitarefa, games e funções da suíte Apple Intelligence localmente. Já os 512 GB de armazenamento oferecem espaço interno de sobra para guardar fotos e vídeos.
A tela LTPO Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,1″ possui brilho de até 2.000 nits e reproduz imagens com cores realistas, além de possuir visibilidade garantida em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Ceramic Shield protege o display contra arranhões e pancadas.
O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 16 recebe a certificação IP68, que adiciona proteção em cenários como ambientes empoeirados e mergulhos acidentais, conferindo assim maior resistência por mais tempo.
Sua bateria de 3.561 mAh resiste a até 22 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte ao MagSafe e carregamento rápido de 25 W via USB-C o permite ser usado pelo dia inteiro, poupando o usuário de ficar sem energia durante o corre-corre diário.
O iPhone 16 de 512 GB (apenas R$ 5.499 em até 12x sem juros) foi atualizado para o iOS 27 e deve receber pelo menos mais quatro versões do sistema operacional. O celular da Apple possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.3 e NFC.

articles.title: Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer
When companies talk about the cost of artificial intelligence, the conversation almost always starts with models: which one to use, what it costs per million tokens, and whether a smaller model is “good enough.” That made sense when AI meant a chatbot.
It makes much less sense now that agents are doing real work in production. A single agent task can fire off dozens of queries, pull context from several systems, call a model several times and write results back. What a task costs and how fast it runs are increasingly determined by everything that happens around the model.
During a pre-briefing ahead of this week’s expansion of the company’s AI Data Plane, Tim Finley, Couchbase Inc.‘s senior vice president of AI, highlighted a key trend. The company announced native Amazon Bedrock integration with semantic caching, a fully managed Agent Memory and Model Context Protocol server on Amazon Web Services, and vector search in its analytics engine, now called Operational Insights.
The more interesting part is the reasoning behind the release, which points to a problem most information technology leaders haven’t fully accounted for.
Agents are a different kind of user
Finley opened with queuing theory to explain the problem. As load rises, latency grows faster than traffic, and agents quickly drive upload. Finley cited a Cisco Systems Inc. study finding that agents generate 450% more traffic per task than humans performing the same work, along with Cloudflare data showing that machine traffic surpassed human traffic on the web in June, about 18 months earlier than forecast.
“Capacity plans built for human growth curves are likely to break,” Finley said. He described agents as “probably the nastiest, most demanding user that you can ever imagine when it comes to running a system.” I think this is the most underappreciated risk in agentic AI. Most production databases were sized for people who click, wait and click again. Agents fan out into parallel tasks, need current and historical data in the same loop, and never sleep. Treat them as “just more users,” and the data tier becomes the bottleneck, usually right after a successful pilot convinces the business to scale.
Companies are downgrading intelligence to pay the bill
The pre-briefing comment that should concern IT and business leaders was the trade-off between model choice and capabilities. “Customers are actively sacrificing intelligence by downgrading models because of the bill once they hit scale,” Finley said. That matches what I hear from IT leaders.
The pilot runs on a frontier model, the results look great, then finance sees the inference bill at production volume, and the team falls back to a cheaper model, degrading the results that justified the project. Often, that trade-off isn’t necessary because much of the spend is waste: the same questions sent repeatedly, bloated prompts,and agents that start every session from scratch.
This is where Couchbase’s announcements can help mitigate the tradeoff. Semantic caching serves similar queries without calling the model again, and the company says it cuts large language model calls by 40% to 60%. It also claims Agent Memory reduces token usage by 33% to 45% compared with alternatives on the LoCoMo, or long-term conversational memory, benchmark, and that vector-based context retrieval produces prompts about 70% smaller than those from full-context approaches.
These are Couchbase’s own numbers, and results will depend heavily on how repetitive a workload is. But the direction is right: most organizations have more room to cut token waste than to improve model quality.
Convergence versus consolidation
During the briefing, Finley explained the difference between convergence and consolidation. The latter reduces the number of tools you pay for. With the former, “a converged system is greater than the sum of its parts” because every capability shares a single copy of the data.
The vector search in Operational Insights is a good example. Finley walked through a phone manufacturer’s use case to determine which factories are linked to the most positive battery-life reviews. Typically, that involves a relational database, a key-value store, a vector database, an ETL pipeline and a warehouse.
Couchbase says it answers it in one SQL query, using “cluster by” much like “group by,” then writes the result back so agents can read it. “There has been a fallacy for a long time with analytics that a really great insight was the finish line,” Finley said. “We think it’s the action.”
Every hop between systems adds latency, introduces a sync job that can fail, adds another security model and creates another place where data can go stale. An agent working from stale data can be confidently wrong. Fewer moving parts matter as much for AI speed and accuracy as they do for cost.
The competitive picture
Snowflake Inc. and Databricks Inc. have both bet on Postgres, and Postgres with pgvector is the default for many AI teams because it’s free and familiar. Finley, who came from AWS’ database business, didn’t discount this value, but he argued that it strains at Fortune 2000 scale once vector counts reach the hundreds of millions. Couchbase also points to deployments at LinkedIn, Amadeus and telecom software provider Mavenir.
Brandon Larson, senior vice president and general manager of Cloud, AI & IMS Business Strategy, explained, “Couchbase has been a key component in achieving high availability in Mavenir’s voice solutions for years,” explained Brandon Larson, senior vice president and general manager of Cloud, AI & IMS Business Strategy. “Now we’re creating new AI voice services that require getting reliable context fast, and Mavenir is building that context layer with Couchbase because of their proven performance in production.”
Recommendations for IT leaders
Model agent load, not user load. Rebuild capacity plans around parallel fan-out, many queries per task and sustained bursts. Load-test the data tier with simulated agent traffic before scaling a pilot. If latency climbs faster than request volume, the queuing effect is at work.
Measure cost per task before downgrading models. Find out how many prompts are near-duplicates, how much context is resent each turn, and how often agents rebuild state they already have. Caching, memory, and better retrieval should be the first levers. Switching to a cheaper model should be a quality decision, not a budget one.
Count the hops in your agent loop. Map every system and sync pipeline an agent touches to complete a typical task. Each hop is a latency cost, a failure point and a governance gap. Whatever vendor you choose, that map shows where convergence pays off.
Treat caches and memory like production data. Semantic caches and agent memory store customer context and model outputs. Apply retention policies, user-level isolation, access controls and audit trails from day one. A cache that returns a “similar” answer to a genuinely different question poses a correctness risk, so tune and monitor similarity thresholds.
Insist on proof at your scale. Vendor benchmarks are a starting point. Test at your data volumes, concurrency and vector counts, and check both recall and throughput. What works at 10 million vectors may not at a billion.
Keep the memory layer portable. Agent frameworks are evolving quickly. Choose memory services that work across LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex and other frameworks, so switching frameworks doesn’t require rebuilding the most valuable part of the stack.
Final thoughts
The industry has spent two years arguing over models. The next two will focus on the cost and reliability of running agents at scale, and much of that will be decided in the data layer. Couchbase is right that agents are a fundamentally different kind of user, and its focus on token economics speaks to the conversation chief information officers are having with chief financial officers right now. Its challenge is winning the architectural argument before customers default to the Postgres-plus-point-tools stack they already know.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Air Canada now charges you $30 fee for phone bookings
articles.text:
Air Canada has started charging customers a $30 fee for booking flights over the phone.
As spotted by CP24, the change went into effect on Oct. 15, per Air Canada’s website. On the page, the airline notes that this $30 (plus applicable taxes) charge will apply to each passenger on new bookings made by phone. It adds that the booking fee will continue to apply for Aeroplan flight reward bookings.
Fliers will still be able to call Air Canada for support with existing reservations, travel disruptions and other inquiries without paying any fees.
In an FAQ on its site, Air Canada says the reason it has introduced this fee is to push its self-serve digital tools.
“Air Canada’s website and mobile app make it easy to book and manage your travel,” writes the airline. “Using these digital tools for everyday travel needs helps reduce wait times and allows our Contact Centre agents to focus their expertise on situations that require personalized support. ”
It should be noted that other Canadian airlines WestJet and Flair already charge for phone bookings, although their prices are $25 each.
While most people likely book their flights online anyway, it’s always annoying to see more fees added onto services, especially when, in this case, it’s literally for the purposes of giving money to Air Canada. If nothing else, charging people for speaking to an agent isn’t as bad as Cineplex, which for the past couple of years has charged a $1.50 booking fee for online purchases where it saves money because it’s a self-serve process where you don’t even deal with any actual humans.
