articles.title: Eva Ngigi Sarwari, Equity’s head of payments, dies at 45
articles.text:
Eva Ngigi Sarwari, managing director of Finserve Africa and Equity Group’s director of payments and international banking, has died aged 45 while on a business trip to China, according to a statement from her colleagues.
Her death cuts short a career that spanned over two decades in banking and payments, from introducing customers to electronic banking at Co-operative Bank of Kenya to leading Visa’s business across three East African markets.
“It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of our dear friend and colleague, Eva Ngigi Sarwari,” her colleagues said in the statement on Tuesday.
They described the news as a “sudden and profound shock” and said they would make further updates as details became available. The statement did not disclose the cause or date of her death.
Sarwari joined Equity in January 2025 as group director for payments and international banking, with responsibility for executing the bank’s payments strategy across Africa. In April 2026, she became managing director of Finserve Africa, the group’s payments and digital financial services subsidiary, overseeing its strategy, commercial direction and operations.
The roles brought her back into a banking group after more than four years at Visa, where she served as senior director and country manager from September 2020 to December 2024. Her role covered three neighbouring markets, including Kenya, South Sudan and Somalia.
The appointments brought together experience accumulated across local banks, an international banking group and one of the world’s largest card networks.
Before Equity, Sarwari spent more than four years at Visa as senior director and country manager for Kenya, South Sudan and Somalia. From September 2020 to December 2024, she was responsible for developing and implementing the company’s growth strategy in those markets.
She joined Visa from SC Ventures, Standard Chartered’s venture-building arm, where she served as a venture lead during 2020. That role followed more than seven years in Standard Chartered’s transaction banking business.
As head of transaction banking for commercial banking from July 2017 to January 2020, she helped shape the bank’s strategy for Kenya and East Africa, with responsibility for revenue growth, product relevance and digital transformation. Previously, as a principal in transaction banking, she worked with development organisations and public-sector clients across East Africa.
Sarwari moved to Standard Chartered in November 2012 after just over two years at Stanbic Bank Kenya, where she managed sales of transactional products and services.
She began her banking career at Co-operative Bank of Kenya in June 2005. As a relationship manager, she helped bring customers onto electronic banking systems, demonstrating products, overseeing installations and training users. It was practical work that would run through her subsequent career.
“Our thoughts and prayers are with Eva’s family, friends and colleagues during this difficult time,” the statement added.

articles.title: ElevenLabs wants to run your voice agent. Here's what developers give up.
articles.text:
ElevenLabs wants to run your voice agent. Here’s what developers give up.
ElevenLabs launched Eleven Realtime on Tuesday, introducing two managed voice-agent models, Mini and Max, that integrate speech recognition, reasoning, turn-taking, and voice generation. Both use a cascaded architecture, but developers can’t select or independently configure the underlying models.
With this launch, the company is effectively taking over the voice-agent harness, including turn detection, interruption handling, and orchestration.
With this launch, the company is effectively taking over the voice-agent harness, including turn detection, interruption handling, and orchestration. That reduces the work required to build and maintain a voice-agent stack, but limits developers’ ability to independently troubleshoot, optimize, or replace its underlying components.
Developers can configure prompts, voices, tools, knowledge bases, and turn-taking settings, including eagerness, timeouts, and interruption handling, through ElevenAgents.
The alternative is Custom mode, which lets developers select the underlying language and speech models and configure the pipeline themselves. Realtime trades that flexibility for a managed implementation. Developers retain control over agent behavior, but not the individual models responsible for it.
Benchmarks from an outside tester
Artificial Analysis generated the performance figures by evaluating both models on speech reasoning, conversational dynamics, and human preference. On Big Bench Audio, a benchmark of 1,000 spoken reasoning questions, Max scored 98.8%, compared with 75.9% for Mini.
ElevenLabs recommends Max for agents that make frequent or complex tool calls.
The gap was even more apparent in tool use. Max completed 87.1% of tasks, while Mini managed 60.3%. ElevenLabs recommends Max for agents that make frequent or complex tool calls. Developers building agents to handle bookings, customer accounts, or other multi-step workflows will want to test that difference for themselves.
The company sets Mini as the default, saying that it is capable of handling most use cases. Mini also performed slightly better on Full-Duplex-Bench, which tests pauses, interruptions, and turn-taking, scoring 95.8% against Max’s 94.1%.
The two models are much closer on latency. Max averaged 570 milliseconds to first audio, compared with 620 milliseconds for Mini. Artificial Analysis’s June Speech-to-Speech Index recorded a faster result of 440 milliseconds for Deepslate Opal, although that earlier benchmark isn’t a direct comparison with Eleven Realtime.
Migrating from OpenAI’s Realtime API
ElevenLabs is also courting teams that already run OpenAI’s Realtime API. The migration guide says Eleven Realtime speaks the same protocol over the same WebSocket transport, so an app built on OpenAI’s SDK can point at ElevenLabs without switching SDKs. The change is the endpoint and the model name.
Migration isn’t free, though. The endpoint supports WebSocket only, so a WebRTC app has to change transports first. The SDK handles audio on its own only over WebRTC. On WebSocket, developers capture and play 24kHz PCM16 audio themselves. A WebRTC app gets that capture and playback from the SDK today, so moving over means building both.
The Realtime API also runs apart from ElevenAgents. Phone and WhatsApp channels, knowledge bases, and monitoring all sit on the platform side. The company says teams that need those features should build on ElevenAgents from the start since a team that begins with the bare API to move quickly may end up rebuilding them later.
Mini versus Max tradeoffs
According to the ElevenAgents documentation, Mini and Max agents can transfer calls between each other, but neither can transfer calls to or from agents running in Custom mode. Mini also lacks support for Zero Retention Mode and HIPAA configurations. Max supports both in the US and EU, although it isn’t available in the India or Singapore data residency environments.
Max costs more per token, but its stronger tool-use performance could make it cheaper for workloads where Mini requires more attempts to finish a task.
Both models are billed at the standard ElevenAgents per-minute rate, plus token charges. Max costs more per token, but its stronger tool-use performance could make it cheaper for workloads where Mini requires more attempts to finish a task.
Testing Before Trusting
ElevenLabs handles the underlying models and orchestration, but developers still need enough diagnostic information to figure out what went wrong when a call fails. It’s unclear how much of that information Realtime makes available.
The benchmarks are promising, but they don’t show how Realtime performs under production load. Developers will need to see whether performance holds up and whether ElevenLabs provides enough information to track down failures.
ElevenLabs did not respond to The New Stack’s request for comment by publication time.

articles.title: US bans DeepSeek from federal agencies, prompting angry response from China
articles.text:
What just happened? DeepSeek might be one of the most popular non-US AI companies right now, but it's being shown the door across US federal civilian agencies. Washington has ordered the removal of the Chinese firm's AI products from government IT systems and blocked future purchases, and the restrictions include third-party tools built using its technology. Beijing, unsurprisingly, isn't happy.
The Department of Homeland Security's notice was made public on October 19, ahead of today's Federal Register publication. The underlying order dates back to late July, according to AP, making this a public disclosure of an earlier decision rather than a ban signed this week.
The directive covers DeepSeek, its affiliates, and products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations. That last part means the directive is more than just blocking access to the company's chatbot. Agencies also have to consider what powers the software they buy.
DHS invoked the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018. Its stated concerns include DeepSeek's servers being located in China and the possibility that Chinese authorities could access sensitive US information. The order added that DeepSeek's AI models "present multiple threat vectors." It also warned of potential malware and other security flaws, pointing to publicly available research that found several critical vulnerabilities in DeepSeek's iOS app.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning hit back on Tuesday, accusing Washington of stretching national security arguments and politicizing technology and trade. Ning added that China will "will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies." DeepSeek did not immediately respond to AP's request for comment.
Executive agencies have 60 days from the order's issuance to submit a written justification to DHS seeking an exception, including more time to comply.
This is familiar ground for the Chinese firm. In January 2025, the US Navy warned personnel against using DeepSeek. However, the military branch subsequently clarified that the message reflected existing restrictions on publicly accessible generative AI for official work, which also covered ChatGPT. It wasn't a newly invented policy aimed solely at one Chinese chatbot.
American AI companies have faced restrictions, too. The House of Representatives banned Copilot in April 2024 over concerns about congressional data reaching unapproved cloud services. That position changed in September 2025, when the House announced a Copilot rollout with additional legal and data protections. There's also the whole Anthropic saga.
While DeepSeek isn't facing a nationwide ban, the directive does affect companies selling AI software powered by its models to US federal civilian agencies.

articles.title: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
articles.text:
It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation.
The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded.
The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.
Four forthcoming rockets all have engines built by the rocket’s manufacturer in the United States. Each of these companies has taken various lessons from SpaceX’s successful Falcon 9 rocket, arguably the most important of which is to build as much of one’s rocket, and particularly the engines, in-house as possible to control timelines and costs.
Now, with SpaceX pulling the Falcon 9 rocket from the commercial market as soon as 2028, the “race” to bring new medium-lift capacity into service is for more than bragging rights. There are fortunes to be made, and commercial space startups to be saved.
Satellite operators legitimately don’t know who to book launches with in the 2027 to 2030 timeframe because of uncertainty over which rockets will be available. The Falcon 9 is no longer for sale. The larger Vulcan and New Glenn rockets have stacked manifests and are expensive for small- and medium-sized satellites. And no one really knows which new medium-lift vehicles will be ready and capable of scaling up their launch cadence.

Following the first closing of approximately €3.5 million in March 2026 (as covered by EU-Startups), Cellbox Solutions has attracted additional investors. Among them are members of the Baltic Business Angels Invest GmbH. Existing investors NRW.BANK and Fraunhofer Venture also participated in the financing.
“Over the past years, we have built a strong foundation for the controlled transport of living biological materials,” says Prof. Dr. Kathrin Adlkofer, founder and CEO of Cellbox Solutions. “With the successful completion of our Series A round, we are now expanding our established warm-chain technology platform into a broader offering for physiological logistics. This will allow us to support customers more comprehensively across their logistics workflows and expand our presence in key international markets.”
This financing follows several other 2026 funding announcements in Europe’s cell-therapy and life sciences technology sectors.
In the Netherlands, Scinus Group secured €3 million to commercialise its cell-expansion platform, while Italy’s Cellply raised €7.15 million for cell-therapy quality-control technologies and the UK’s Tozaro attracted €6.9 million to improve cell and gene therapy manufacturing.
In Germany, Leipzig-based Primogene secured €4.1 million for enzymatic biomanufacturing, with related investments also recorded by Dutch startup QT Sense (€4 million) and Switzerland’s ALP Bio (€1.9 million).
Together with Cellbox Solutions’ €5 million Series A, these 2026 financings amount to approximately €32 million across related but distinct life sciences technologies, including grant funding.
“Completion of the Series A gives us additional resources to scale the commercial model behind our technology. By expanding rental and recurring service offerings and combining them with transportation, monitoring, and complementary logistics services, we can build longer-term customer relationships and a more scalable service model across markets. Our focus is now on translating the strength of the Cellbox platform into sustainable commercial growth,” adds Dr. Bernd Muehlenweg, CBO and CFO of Cellbox Solutions.
Founded in 2017, Cellbox Solutions is a Cologne-based warm-chain logistics technology company providing solutions for the global healthcare and life sciences industries to transport sensitive biological materials and therapeutics that cannot be frozen and require controlled physiological conditions.
The company’s portable CO₂ incubator platform, Cellbox, creates a regulated environment for the transport of living cells, organoids, tissues, and other advanced biological materials. Temperature and CO₂ levels are individually adjustable to ensure reproducible incubation conditions throughout shipment. Cellbox systems are deployed globally and support research, clinical, and advanced therapy applications.
Today’s financing marks the next phase in the company’s commercial growth, and will help leverage the established technological, product-related, and regulatory advances Cellbox Solutions has achieved in recent years.
A key focus is building on the company’s specialized transport capabilities to link controlled transport under physiological conditions even more closely with additional logistics and service offerings.
Cellbox Go and Cellbox Shipper make up the core of the company’s technology platform. Both incubators provide controlled temperature and CO₂ conditions during ground and air transport and are already used internationally in research and cell therapy applications.
With over 400 Cellbox systems currently on the market, a growing number of customer relationships and a regulatory foundation that includes Drug Master Files for the CellboxTM product family, the company believes they are well positioned to expand its commercial offering.
This includes combining CellboxTM systems with rental and transport options, as well as recurring services such as monitoring, fleet management, and shipment coordination.
To this end, the company is continuing to expand its activities in Europe, Asia, and North America and is increasingly focusing on strategic partnerships with logistics providers.

articles.title: Homebase launches AI assistant to take on scheduling and payroll for small business owners - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Homebase launches AI assistant to take on scheduling and payroll for small business owners
Small business team management company Homebase today introduced Homebase Assistant, an artificial intelligence tool for owners who run hourly teams without a back office.
Homebase bills it as the only AI built specifically for that market. Assistant targets the desk work that comes with running a small business.
In Homebase’s telling, most owners are on the floor all day, so payroll and scheduling wait until they can get to a computer at night. The company said a job such as building a schedule or writing a job post can drop from hours to minutes, with the owner still signing off on the result.
Founder and Chief Executive John Waldmann said every owner he talks to has “the same 6 a.m. moment,” when an employee calls out sick and the day becomes a hunt for a replacement. In his view, most AI tools would stop at telling the owner that a shift is uncovered. He called the Homebase approach “AI that acts.”
In the sick-call scenario Waldmann described, the assistant works out which employees could cover. None of them is contacted before the owner gives the go-ahead, at which point the software takes over the outreach until somebody accepts the shift.
On the payroll side, timecards get a check before each pay run. Homebase said the assistant catches missing punches and similar errors early enough that an owner can sort them out in one go. Overtime trends get the same early warning, as do gaps between scheduled and actual hours, so staffing can be changed before the costs land.
Candidate screening is part of the package too. Reuben Pressman, founder and managing partner of Florida pickleball club St. Pete Athletic, said the club ran more than 3,000 job applications through Homebase’s AI-powered screening. He put the time saved at more than 1,000 hours. The process still turned up “the absolute best talent” for the team, he said.
The new product follows the hiring and scheduling assistants the company launched in June 2025, plus a payroll assistant that arrived later that year. Those tools have handled more than 4.7 million administrative tasks since launch, according to Homebase.
Shift cover is not new territory for the company. That earlier scheduling assistant was built to identify and rank replacements whenever a schedule changed.
Homebase is a venture capital-backed company with more than 150,000 small business customers. Bain Capital Ventures and Khosla Ventures were among the existing investors that came back when L Catterton Growth led its $60 million Series D round in April 2024.

articles.title: Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips — AI agentic workflows said to favor Arm chips, but firm will keep x86 chips deployed in heterogeneous server fleet
articles.text:
Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips — AI agentic workflows said to favor Arm chips, but firm will keep x86 chips deployed in heterogeneous server fleet
Modal plans to use Nvidia's Vera CPUs due to performance advantages, but will keep AMD and Intel CPUs in the fleet.
Nvidia has earned billions selling AI accelerators, but with the emergence of agentic AI, CPUs are going to play a considerably more significant role than before, which creates new opportunities for the company. Reuters reports that Nvidia has secured a major design win with its Vera CPUs with AI cloud provider Modal. According to Modal, preliminary evaluations showed that Vera could deliver twice the throughput of its existing AMD and Intel processors, although the company does not intend to cease using CPUs from its current suppliers.
Modal provides cloud infrastructure that enables AI developers to deploy AI agents that can perform complex operations autonomously over extended periods. Such workloads require substantial CPU resources for software execution, data processing, and other tasks that cannot be efficiently handled by GPUs. Modal currently relies exclusively on AMD and Intel processors for these operations, but its tests indicate that Nvidia's new Vera CPUs could significantly improve performance in its specific workloads. Of course, since Vera is based on an Arm instruction set architecture, Modal's decision to adopt Vera will require substantial modifications to its software. Nevertheless, Modal believes that the potential performance improvements justify the additional engineering effort.
The reported 2x throughput advantage is particularly interesting because agentic AI workloads can involve numerous independent tasks that compete for CPU cores, cache capacity, and memory bandwidth. However, Modal has not disclosed detailed benchmark configurations it used, specific AMD and Intel processor models, or performance-per-watt figures. Consequently, it remains unclear whether Vera's advantage is enabled by advantages of its Arm v9.2-based Olympus CPU cores that can decode and execute up to 10 instructions per cycle, its memory subsystem with 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth, or other architectural characteristics. Also note that tests compared Vera against currently available AMD and Intel processors rather than their upcoming generations that will compete against Vera in the coming years.
Since Modal cannot port all of its software to Arm ISA overnight, the company will continue using x86 CPUs from AMD and Intel, according to Modal chief executive Erik Bernhardsson. Rather than sticking to one ISA for everything, Modal intends to operate a heterogeneous server fleet and select the most suitable processors for each workload. Naturally, the company intends to evaluate upcoming AMD and Intel processors once they become available to make its choices in the future.
For Nvidia, the agreement represents a major step toward making Vera a standalone server processor that commands a major share of the server market. The company expects Vera sales to generate at least $20 billion during its current fiscal year and estimates the potential total available market for these CPUs is approximately $200 billion. The company is on track to sell at least four million Vera CPUs in fiscal 2026.
The announcement comes shortly after Modal secured $750 million in financing led by Accel, which valued the company at $15.75 billion. Modal expects its annual revenue to reach $1 billion within the next year. The company's service consumption has increased 3X in the last 12 months, while revenue has surged more than 15 times compared with the previous year, Reuters reports.

articles.title: Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about half as much of Anthropic as CEO Dario Amodei | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger. The former Google CEO is reported to own about 1% of Anthropic after investing tens of millions of dollars in the leading AI lab’s Series A round in 2021, per Bloomberg. The startup was valued at $461 million at the time, according to PitchBook data.
If Bloomberg’s estimate is accurate, Schmidt’s stake is remarkably large compared with the 2% of the company that co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei holds. Anthropic is widely expected to go public before the end of the year, with top-end market estimates valuing the company at as much as $2 trillion. At that valuation, Schmidt would add as much as $20 billion to his net worth, which Bloomberg currently puts at $57.5 billion.
Schmidt has been an active tech investor since stepping down as Google CEO in 2011. He deploys capital through multiple entities, including Tomorrow Ventures, Innovation Endeavors Management, and his family office, Hillspire. His other AI bets include Mistral, General Intuition, and Reflection AI.
Schmidt and Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to our request for comment.

articles.title: 'They wanted GTA 6's weapon system to be more like Red Dead, where you couldn't just carry an unlimited number of guns' — Rockstar 'spent months, if not years' trying out different loadout UI iterations, but in the end 'they just wound up back at a weapon wheel'
articles.text:
Rockstar 'spent months, if not years, trying a million different things that would replace the weapon wheel' to make loadouts 'more realistic' in GTA 6
Jason Schreier reports that this was a "dark period" of development
- Bloomberg's Jason Schreier says Rockstar Games spent years developing an alternative weapon system for Grand Theft Auto 6
- He says, "They wanted GTA 6's weapon system to be more like Red Dead," with a reimagined weapon wheel
- However, after years of iteration, Rockstar stuck to a classic design
Rockstar Games reportedly spent years developing a new weapon interface for Grand Theft Auto 6, but eventually stuck with the classic weapon wheel the series is known for.
As reported by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, who shared a YouTube video about his visit to Rockstar North, co-studio head and head of development Rob Nelson said that the team wanted the game's weapon loadout system to be more like Red Dead Redemption 2 than GTA 5.
"They wanted GTA 6's weapon system to be more like Red Dead, where you couldn't just carry an unlimited number of guns," Schreier said, which was "a little more realistic."
In Red Dead Redemption 2, loadouts are tied to your horse, and players can only carry a certain number of weapons on their person at a time, whether a pistol or a shotgun, while the rest is stored on your saddle.
The team wanted to recreate a similar system for GTA 6 by having storage tied to the player's car and a limited loadout of weapons that players can carry at any given time, but wanted to reimagine the weapon wheel.
"So the idea that they were thinking was like, well, if we use a weapon wheel, is that just going to remind people of all these blank spots in it? It'll remind people of what they can't actually do, what they can't carry. And so maybe we shouldn't use a weapon wheel," Schreier explained.
"And so they spent months, if not years, trying a million different things that would replace the weapon wheel."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Schreier revealed that Rockstar tried "trays and webs and all sorts of different things in the UI" and other ways to replace the weapon wheel, but in the end, the team ended up back at the weapon wheel.
"They tried not having one," he said. "They tried all these different iterations on this. After all that, they just wound up back at a weapon wheel, and in the final game it's just a weapon wheel again."
Schreier believes this was part of the "dark periods" of development that "led to some problems for the game", as developers continuously reworked prototypes for the UI, only to end back at square one.
However, he added that "really ended when the game started coalescing, I would say around [the] end of 2022, beginning of 2023, something like that is where they really started to see it all come together."
"As I mentioned in the story, the first trailer that they released in December 2023 was really a guiding light for a lot of the people on the team to see, 'Oh, this is what the game is going to look like,'" Schreier said.
Rockstar recently released the cinematic GTA 6 launch trailer, ahead of GTA 6's launch on November 19. The game is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X, and Series S, with a new report claiming the PC version could launch in early 2027.

articles.title: Bell boosts wireless in Toronto with another new wireless site
articles.text:
Bell has upgraded its wireless service in another part of Toronto as part of the company’s ongoing network densification program.
In an email to MobileSyrup, Bell said it completed construction of and put into service a new wireless site that will “help enhance network capacity and performance in the Earlscourt, Carleton Village and Stockyards communities” in Toronto.
Bell says the upgrade will support the connectivity needs of residents, businesses, and visitors in these neighbourhoods.
“As wireless usage continues to increase, Bell is making targeted investments to add capacity and improve network performance in areas where demand is growing.”
The upgrade is part of a larger wireless network expansion and densification program that aims to strengthen Bell’s wireless network across Canada.
Previously, as part of this program, Bell added a new wireless site in Roncesvalles Village in Toronto and shared images of other upgrades in Ontario and Quebec.
The program started in 2024 and, as of May of this year, has seen Bell add 167 new wireless sites in 76 communities across the country, as well as enhance 349 existing sites in 50 communities. Bell says its workers have spent a combined 600,000 labour hours planning and installing upgrades and towers.
We also recently reported on Bell’s effort to bring better service to Orilla, Ont., which included partnering with a local church to use its land for a new wireless tower. Elsewhere, Bell brought fibre internet to remote island communities in Nova Scotia.

articles.title: YouTube quiere ponértelo más difícil para dar 'No me gusta' a un vídeo
articles.text:
Ponerle No me gusta a un vídeo en YouTube estaría por volverse algo más complicado. La plataforma de Google ha comenzado a probar cambios en su interfaz que esconden el botón del pulgar abajo, obligando a los usuarios a completar un paso extra para usarlo.
En primera instancia puede no parecer algo demasiado relevante, pero la historia es bastante diferente. Después de todo, YouTube lleva algunos años experimentando con el No me gusta con cambios que no han sido del agrado de la mayoría de los usuarios.
Según ha publicado TheBobPony en X (Twitter), YouTube está probando mover el botón de No me gusta al menú de tres puntos que aparece en cada vídeo. De esta manera, el citado control ya no es visible junto con las opciones de dar like, compartir, guardar o preguntar a Gemini, sino que queda oculta en segundo plano.
Desde YouTube no se han pronunciado en público respecto de este experimento. Tampoco se sabe qué tan amplia es el test que se está realizando, aunque es bastante común que Google realice pruebas limitadas a un número reducido de usuarios. De allí a que se concreten en el producto final, es una historia diferente.
No obstante, no deja de llamar la atención el empecinamiento de YouTube con cambiar el modo de usar el No me gusta. Tengamos en cuenta que la compañía ya había modificado la forma de mostrar el uso de dicha reacción hacia el público general, y a finales del año pasado optó por quitarlo definitivamente de los Shorts.
YouTube podría ocultar el botón de No me gusta en todos los vídeos
Como ya indicamos, no es la primera vez que YouTube experimenta con el botón No me gusta. La compañía quedó envuelta en una polémica en 2021 cuando optó por dejar de mostrar públicamente el conteo de pulgares abajo en un vídeo. Según la explicación oficial, el objetivo detrás de esa decisión fue para evitar el mal uso de la característica, especialmente en campañas de review bombing.
La determinación se dio en un momento clave, cuando el mundo poco a poco regresaba a la normalidad tras el tramo más duro de la pandemia de COVID-19. Por entonces, la explosión en la creación y el consumo de contenidos disparó la popularidad de gran cantidad de creadores, pero también llevó al rápido desaliento de muchos que, con razón o no, veían que el conteo de No me gusta en sus vídeos era más alto que el de Me gusta.
YouTube habló por entonces de velar por el bienestar de los creadores más pequeños y de evitar que campañas de calificaciones injustas terminen sesgando la recepción del público general. A finales del año pasado, en tanto, quitó el No me gusta de los Shorts, como parte de la adopción de un sistema de corazones como el de TikTok e Instagram.
Ya veremos qué sucede con esta cuestión, pero es difícil pensar que ocultar el No me gusta pueda tener una utilidad real. A no ser que YouTube tenga datos muy concluyentes de que el botón se está usando mal o con fines pura y exclusivamente dañinos, es curioso que la compañía se tome la molestia de quitarlo u ocultarlo de su UI.

articles.title: Whatsapp: So lädst du Freunde ohne Konto jetzt zum Videochat ein
articles.text:
Ohne App oder Profil: So nimmst du an Whatsapp-Videocalls einfach über den Browser teil
Im Sommer 2024 hatte Meta die Zahl der möglichen Teilnehmer:innen an einem Videochat in Whatsapp auf 32 erhöht. Damit war die Messaging-App zu einem ernst zu nehmenden Konkurrenten für dedizierte Konferenzdienste wie Zoom, Microsoft Teams oder Google Meet geworden. Jetzt baut Meta die Funktion weiter aus.
Videochat-Teilnahme ohne Whatsapp-Konto
Wie der Konzern mitteilt, ermöglicht das neue Gastanrufe-Feature auch Personen ohne Whatsapp-Konto die Teilnahme an Videochats. Eine Installation der App sowie eine Registrierung sind dafür nicht notwendig. Stattdessen können die Eingeladenen über den Browser ihres Computers an der Videokonferenz teilnehmen.
Um eine Person als Gast zu einem Videochat einzuladen, gehen Whatsapp-Nutzer:innen in der App auf den Bereich Anrufe. Dort tippen sie rechts oben auf das Plus-Zeichen und anschließend auf „Neuer Anruflink“. Die jeweiligen Nutzer:innen fungieren dann als Gastgeber:in des Chats. Der Link lässt sich auf verschiedenen Wegen teilen.
Meta: Videochats Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselt
Im Rahmen der Erstellung des Links lässt sich noch einstellen, ob es sich um einen Video- oder Sprachanruf handeln soll. In beiden Fällen verspricht Meta Ende-zu-Ende-Verschlüsselung. Auch kann man festlegen, ob Teilnehmer:innen, die nicht bei Whatsapp registriert sind, eine Beitrittsgenehmigung benötigen. In diesem Fall müssen sie darauf warten, dass die Gastgeber:innen ihnen den Zutritt erlauben.
Für Gäste sind zudem die Funktionen des Videochats etwas eingeschränkt. So können sie nicht die Telefonnummern anderer Teilnehmer:innen sehen, Nachrichten senden oder andere Personen zu dem Chat hinzufügen. Weitere Funktionen wie das Teilen des Bildschirms oder Reaktionen per Emoji sowie Meldungen per Handzeichen sind aber auch Gast-Teilnehmer:innen möglich.
Kalenderintegration bis Ende 2026 geplant
Meta hat darüber hinaus angekündigt, bis Ende 2026 eine Kalenderintegration für Whatsapp-Videochats an den Start zu bringen. Dann soll die Erstellung eines Einladungslinks direkt über ein entsprechendes Plugin aus Google Kalender oder Outlook heraus möglich sein.

articles.title: « Un bonbon », « je me revois dans la mienne » : ce que le public pense à chaud de la Citroën 2 CV au Mondial
articles.text:
Sur le stand Citroën à la Porte de Versailles, la foule compacte ne trompe pas : le concept 2 CV a attiré énormément de monde. Il fallait même parfois jouer des coudes et savoir quand battre en retraite. Alors que les nouveautés électriques peinent parfois à susciter une réelle ferveur populaire auprès du grand public, la résurrection de la 2 CV en version 100 % électrique attire tous les profils.
Entre les habitués du modèle historique, les badauds attirés par sa silhouette pétillante et quelques sceptiques, j’ai voulu recueillir les réactions à chaud. Dans l’ensemble, la bouille néo-rétro et le pragmatisme affiché font un carton presque unanime.
Le style extérieur et intérieur fait mouche
À proximité du concept, les premiers mots lâchés spontanément sont souvent : « C’est rigolo » ou « C’est marrant ». Deux qualificatifs que j’ai entendus de nombreuses fois entre le mardi et le vendredi. Citroën voulait diffuser de la joie aux visiteurs avec ce modèle, c’est mission réussie. L’aspect néo-rétro semble également respecter le contact avec les fans du modèle : « Comme l’originale… Je me revois dans la mienne », commentait à voix haute une visiteuse du salon en quittant le stand.
Si un duo d’observateurs plus circonspects tempère en évoquant un « premier coup de crayon » qui pourrait être moins convaincant sur le modèle de série, l’immense majorité tombe sous le charme.
« C’est un bonbon, je suis acheteuse tout de suite ! », s’enthousiasme une visiteuse qui s’est invitée dans la discussion lancée avec deux fans du modèle original. « Elle est tellement belle que j’aurais presque peur de l’abîmer. Je la trouve féminine. Vraiment trop belle. »
Ce groupe improvisé de trois personnes a disséqué plusieurs détails :
- Un gabarit plus court que l’ancienne : la perte de dix centimètres en longueur par rapport aux citadines modernes est immédiatement remarquée : « D’habitude, à chaque nouvelle voiture, ça grossit, donc là, c’est vraiment bien. »
- Des choix stylistiques validés : « Heureusement qu’ils n’ont pas caché les roues arrière, sinon ça aurait été trop lourd en design », analyse un propriétaire de plusieurs anciennes (1957, 1976 et 1981). « Et ils doivent absolument garder les phares ronds ainsi. Quatre portes, c’est capital aussi. »
- La question de la capote : l’un des visiteurs prévient toutefois la marque avec malice : « J’espère juste que la capote sera simple d’utilisation au quotidien, pas comme la galère de la C3 Pluriel ! » J’ai également surenchéri en rappelant l’effort nécessaire sur la Citroën e-Méhari.
- Entre interrogations et enthousiasme pour l’intérieur : le groupe s’est interrogé sur les éléments qui resteront à l’intérieur : « L’intérieur est particulièrement réussi, parce qu’il y a de la joie de vivre là-dedans. » Ils insistent néanmoins sur un point important : « Ce que j’aime dans ces voitures-là, c’est la simplicité. »
Si le modèle est un vrai aimant pour le public français, même les touristes étrangers s’arrêtent, à l’image d’un couple allemand séduit mais attentif : « C’est une excellente idée, ça nous plaît ! », tout en s’interrogeant sur le volume du coffre et des passages de roues jugés « un peu trop gonflés ». Un couple d’Anglais m’a également confié « ne pas s’attendre à craquer pour ce genre de modèle sur le salon ».
« Pour les petits trajets, c’est parfait » : le bon sens technique à 15 000 €
Au-delà de la carrosserie, c’est l’équation économique et technique qui met tout le monde d’accord. Face à la dérive des fiches techniques, le choix d’une batterie modeste (que certains visiteurs évaluent eux-mêmes à environ 30 kWh) pour contenir la facture sous les 15 000 € est largement salué par le public : « C’est une voiture de ville, pas besoin d’une grosse autonomie », tranche un duo de visiteurs.
Un fidèle de la marque depuis 35 ans résume la philosophie avec un franc-parler réjouissant : « 30 kWh max pour faire des trajets pissotières (NDLR : je ne connaissais pas cette expression), c’est très bien ! Tous les soirs, on la recharge tranquillement dans le garage et le tour est joué. On garderait notre C3 essence pour les longs trajets d’autoroute, et ça pour le quotidien, c’est parfait. » Si Citroën tient sa promesse de lancer le modèle d’ici deux ans, il est prêt à l’acheter. Plusieurs détails achèvent de le convaincre : « Ce que j’aime à l’intérieur, c’est le sélecteur en hauteur. Et il faut absolument laisser la banquette d’un seul bloc, même si elle n’est pas amovible ! »
Un groupe de trois trentenaires compare immédiatement la proposition aux autres stars du moment : « Par rapport à la R5, elle est bien mieux positionnée en tarif. Et sortir des coloris plus peps, ça fait du bien, exactement comme pour la R5. Elle a de très beaux jours devant elle à notre avis. »
Le remake du phénomène Fiat 500 ?
L’enthousiasme est tel que certains ont vraiment passé du temps à la disséquer : « On est venus la voir dès notre arrivée au salon ce matin, et on revient la regarder une dernière fois avant de partir », confie un duo d’amis. Et pour beaucoup, le parallèle avec le succès populaire de l’ancienne 2 CV ne fait aucun doute : « Les gens ont bien fini par adopter la laideur géniale de celle de 1948, ils vont adopter celle-là sans aucun problème. Citroën a l’occasion de réussir son coup avec la 2 CV exactement comme Fiat a réussi le sien avec la 500. »
Seuls quelques irréductibles restent campés sur leurs positions, comme ce couple plus âgé croisé le mardi : « C’est sympa, il y a plein de clins d’œil, mais nous on a toujours été branchés Renault, on roulait en 4L à cette époque. Un ami a une 2 CV, on lui a envoyé la photo, mais nous ne sommes pas clients pour ça. »
La déclinaison Fourgonnette, gardée secrète jusqu’au salon, a aussi séduit le groupe de trentenaires rencontré plus haut. Ils y voient un utilitaire enfin joyeux et décalé. Certains ont d’ailleurs préféré le style plus conventionnel de la version fourgonnette et sa teinte grise, qui permettait de « mieux se projeter sur un modèle de série ».
Le mot de la fin revient à cette visiteuse, qui résume l’enthousiasme général devant le stand : « Si Citroën la sort vraiment à 15 000 euros d’ici 2028, elle partira comme des petits pains. » Le message est envoyé aux décideurs de Stellantis. En une vingtaine d’échanges, j’aurais presque pu faire signer quatre bons de commande : c’est assez prometteur.

articles.title: Egypt’s Tactful AI gets backing from former e& CEO Hatem Dowidar - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian agentic AI customer experience (CX) startup Tactful AI has secured investment from Hatem Dowidar, the former group CEO of e&, as part of an extension of its pre-Series A funding round.
Founded by Mohamed Elmasry, Mohammad Hassan and Sherif Khairallah, Tactful is a unified customer experience platform that provides businesses with a single dashboard through which to manage, engage, augment, and understand customers’ journeys across various touch points.
In 2022, the company was acquired by Dstny, a leading European company that offers a series of interactive communication tools that brings employees and customers closer together, but it was reacquired by its founders in July 2025.
Disrupt Africa reported in February Tactful AI had raised US$1 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Foras AI and M Empire, and it has now extended that round with the investment from Dowidar, the size of which is undisclosed.
Dowidar has spent more than 25 years in telecoms and technology. He led e& as group CEO from 2020 until March 2026, after joining the company as chief operating officer in 2015. Before e&, he spent 16 years in executive roles at Vodafone, including as CEO of Vodafone Egypt.
The extra funding is a boost for Tactful AI at a time when it is about to launch a next-generation version of its technology, which aims to let enterprises build, modify and evolve end-to-end CX workflows in-house, cutting development cycles from months to hours while keeping human sign-off at every step.
The startup has been growing fast. Since January 2025, its annual recurring revenue (ARR) has risen 11.7 times, and the number of monthly customer conversations processed through its platform has increased 32-fold. Its clients include Elaraby Group, Raneen, 2B, Lucky One, Erada Finance and Simplex.
“Enterprises across the region are actively seeking practical, reliable solutions to integrate AI into their customer operations safely and at scale. Tactful has successfully deployed this infrastructure in live production environments,” Dowidar said. “Seeing the capabilities of their next-generation technology convinced me that this team has everything it takes to set the industry benchmark, both regionally and globally.”
Elmasry said few leaders understood as well as Dowidar what large enterprises need before they trust new customer-facing technologies.
“His support and trust come at a pivotal moment as we take our boldest step yet toward defining a new era of agentic AI-driven customer experience,” he said.
Tactful AI plans to raise a Series A round in 2027.

articles.title: CJIS v6.1 Compliance: 5 Practical Priorities for Agencies
articles.text:
For agencies responsible for protecting Criminal Justice Information (CJI), meeting CJIS requirements means more than putting security controls in place. Those controls need to work across the systems staff use every day, and agencies need to be able to prove they're effective.
But, between legacy systems, stretched IT teams, and constantly changing access needs, even agencies with strong security practices can struggle to apply controls consistently and keep the evidence auditors expect.
So, where should you focus your efforts? In this article, we'll walk through five key areas agencies should be paying attention to under CJIS v6.1, with practical advice to make compliance easier to manage.
Multi-Factor Authentication
CJIS v6.1 requires MFA for both privileged and non-privileged accounts under controls IA-2(1) and IA-2(2), covering local, network, and remote access. The challenge is making sure no accounts slip through the cracks.
Start by reviewing MFA coverage across your environment, paying particular attention to legacy applications and administrative accounts. When implementing MFA, consider phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 security keys.
You'll also need reliable processes for enrolling, replacing, and revoking authenticators.
Solutions like Specops Secure Access help agencies comply by extending MFA protection to Windows logons, RDP, RADIUS, and offline access, with flexible options including authenticator apps and YubiKeys. Its event API integrations also help provide evidence for compliance audits.
Remember, MFA isn't a one-time fix. Revisit your configurations as systems and access needs change.
Secure your Active Directory passwords with Specops Password Policy
Verizon’s Data Breach Investigation Report found stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches. 
Effortlessly secure Active Directory with compliant password policies, blocking 4+ billion compromised passwords, boosting security, and slashing support hassles!
Account Management and Privileges
Access permissions can quickly become outdated as employees change roles or leave, a risk which CJIS v6.1 aims to reduce by enforcing effective account management and least privilege.
Start by keeping an accurate inventory of user, administrative, service, and temporary accounts. Limit permissions to what is needed for each role, separate administrative privileges from everyday activities, and automate account provisioning and removal where possible.
Review accounts and privileges at least annually. Temporary and emergency accounts must be removed within 72 hours, while accounts inactive for 90 days must be disabled within one week. The key is making access reviews an ongoing process, not just an annual exercise.
Passwords
IA-5 sets an eight-character password minimum and is a Priority 1 control, so has been sanctionable since October 2024. Aligning with NIST recommendations, agencies should encourage longer, unique passphrases and use approved password managers to reduce reuse.
Agencies should also:
- Screen for compromised passwords, updating password blocklists at least quarterly and whenever compromise is suspected.
- Block weak or reused passwords during creation or reset.
- Limit failed login attempts to no more than five per account.
This is where Specops Password Policy can help. It simplifies password policy management across Active Directory, continuously checking against over 6 billion compromised passwords and scanning daily for newly exposed credentials.
Customizable grace periods help reduce unnecessary lockouts when a compromised password is found, while compliance templates and reporting make it easier to track your progress.
Finally, check annual password change requirements with your CJIS Systems Agency, as IA-5 still specifies a yearly change or refresh despite guidance discouraging unnecessary resets.
Logging
Audit logs help agencies detect suspicious activity and investigate security incidents. However, collecting logs isn't enough. Agencies also need to capture the right events, review records regularly, and protect them against tampering.
Start by checking logging coverage across systems handling CJI. Make sure records capture who did what and when, as well as the outcome. Centralizing logs in a SIEM can make suspicious activity easier to spot.
Audit Readiness
Agencies are audited at least once every three years, but you’re expected to maintain compliance between audits. Rather than scrambling to pull evidence together at the last minute, it’s better to treat CJIS compliance as an ongoing responsibility.
Some best practices include:
- Maintaining an inventory of applicable security controls and identifying who is responsible for implementing, reviewing, and documenting each one.
- Keeping evidence organized, including records of MFA configurations, access reviews, audit logs, security policies, training, and assessment results. That makes it easier to demonstrate compliance.
- Documenting identified weaknesses and setting deadlines for resolving them. In line with CA-5, you should update remediation plans at least every six months or when new information becomes available.
- Conducting internal assessments to identify issues before a formal assessment.
- Building security monitoring and compliance reviews into everyday IT operations, so changes or new risks don't go unnoticed.
By making audit preparation part of routine security management, agencies can identify gaps earlier, reduce the work involved in formal assessments, and maintain a stronger compliance posture between audits.
Strengthen Your CJIS Compliance Posture
CJIS compliance isn't a one-and-done exercise. As systems and security risks change, agencies need to make sure their controls keep pace. By regularly reviewing controls and keeping evidence organized, you can make compliance easier to manage while strengthening your agency's security.
Passwords are a good place to start when assessing your CJIS compliance. But how do you know where the gaps are?

articles.title: Google DeepMind presume de haber batido a Minecraft con agentes controlados por Gemini 4 Argon en apenas 27 horas
articles.text:
'Minecraft' no es sólo uno de los juegos más exitosos de la historia y una base genial tanto para divertirse como para aprender. El título de Mojang lleva años usándose para medir de qué son capaces los modelos de inteligencia artificial y Google Deepmind acaba de anotarse un tanto: su Gemini 4 Argon ha completado 'Minecraft' de principio a fin in intervención humana.
Y parece que esta IA lo ha hecho sin trampas.
En corto. Cuatro agentes basados en Gemini 4 Argon derrotaron al Ender Dragon en 27 horas y 14 minutos. Se trata del jefe final del juego y los resultados se publicaron en un paper en arXiv en el que los autores son algunos de los responsables de Google Deepmind.
Se trata de uno de los últimos modelos de la compañía, uno que lleva semanas en un circuito cerrado para que expertos en ciberseguridad lo pusieran a prueba, pero que se liberó a suscriptores de pago el pasado 13 de octubre. Ahora bien, tiene cierto truco.
A ciegas. La prueba se realizó en un mundo generado al azar, en dificultad fácil y con los comandos de trampa desactivados. A los agentes sólo se les dio el objetivo de matar a la dragona, sin otras instrucciones, herramientas específicas para Minecraft o estrategias para acelerar el progreso. Cada uno de los agentes controlaban a un jugador mediante Mineflayer, una bibloteca de código abierto para crear bots del juego y, para actuar, vibecodeaban un programa corto en Java que era el que emitía las órdenes.
Por ejemplo, ir a un sitio, minar ciertos materiales y ese tipo de cosas. Entre los cuatro agentes escribieron 2.783 programas, intercambiaron 229 mensajes y murieron 605 veces. Y hay un par de cosas curiosas: la primera es que, de todas esas muertes, sólo 69 de ellas fue a manos del jefe. La segunda es que se repartieron el trabajo por su cuenta.
Uno fabricaba herramientas, otro reunía suministros, otro encendió el portal y otro localizó la fortaleza. Cuando lo tuvieron todo, fueron a por la dragona y se embarcaron en una batalla de 14 horas en la que también idearon diferentes estrategias para minimizar las opciones del rival, como romper los cristales de regeneración.
El truco. Ya hemos contado que la dificultad estaba en 'fácil', pero hay otros detalles interesantes que ilustran un poco mejor esta victoria. Según los investigadores, el 22% de todos los programas que escribieron terminaron en error y había una app que informaba a los agentes de qué recursos y criaturas tenían a su alrededor, incluso aquellos que estaban fuera de su vista.
Un plugin también les planificaba las mejores rutas y partían con ventaja porque en el proceso de entrenamiento del modelo ya estaba 'Minecraft', así que aunque no hubiera un mundo preparado o humanos haciendo cosas, es evidente que los agentes no se enfrentaron al juego de nuevas.
Y, sobre el precio, hasta la victoria los agentes necesitaron unos 1.350 tokens de entrada y, aparte de los cuatro agentes jugadores, había un quinto que se encargaba de supervisar la sesión para que ninguno hiciera trampas. La sesión completa salió por unos 810 dólares.
Por qué Minecraft. Algo interesante es que, de entre todos los juegos que hay, sólo unos pocos son aptos para pruebas así. 'Minecraft' es uno de los elegidos para varios experimentos y, en el de DeepMind, lo que se busca poner a prueba es la constancia a lo largo de miles de pasos dependientes durante más de un día. Antes, la Universidad de Michigan ya había hablado de las bondades del juego debido a que era un entorno 3D flexible ideal para tareas de aprendizaje por refuerzo con observación parcial y recompensas diferidas.
Otras IAs se han entrenado con 'Minecraft' y esto no es sólo algo exclusivo de la IA, ya que en entornos educativos es un juego extremadamente interesante porque se pueden poner en práctica ejercicios colaborativos, deductivos, pensamiento lateral, entrenar esa paciencia, desplegar la imaginación, la creatividad y porque enseña pensamiento computacional casi sin querer.
El sistema del juego funciona con una lógica similar a la electónica y, además, hay herramientas de programación por bloques que hacen que sea una buena puerta de entrada a la programación. Es lo mismo que lo hace interesante para entrenar la IA, en definitiva, y ese mundo abierto con reglas claras, pero objetivos abiertos en los que hay que planificar a largo plazo y coordinarse es justo lo que DeepMind quería evaluar en su modelo.
La IA tramposa. Pero si 'Minecraft' es un buen patio de juego para la IA, otro juego que se usa mucho es 'StarCraft'. De hecho, antes de que la IA fuera el monstruo que es hoy, ya se usaba StarCraft como uno de los exámenes finales de la IA junto al juego chino Go. Recientemente, en una competición de bots en 'StarCraft: Brood War donde los modelos tenían una hora para programar un bot que controlara a una de las facciones del juego, GPT-6 Astra optó por la vía rápida.
GPT-6, que acumulaba varias derrotas, en lugar de mejorar su propio programa se descargó Stardust, un bot escritop por humanos que es una auténtica bestia en el competitivo. Esto es, evidentemente, una trampa, pero también algo conocido como 'reward hacking' o lo que es lo mismo: cumplir el objetivo usando atajos, como aprobar un examen con chuletas.
No era la primera vez y ya hubo una IA de DeepmMind que se pasó 'Sonic The Hedgehog' usando fallos en el código del juego y, precisamente, para eso estaba ese quinto agente en el nuevo experimento de DeepMind controlando a los otros cuatro de 'Minecraft': para que no usaran esa vía rápida de las trampas.

articles.title: PS6 : et si la manette permettait de rendre les jeux plus fluides ?
articles.text:
L’optimisation des performances graphiques des jeux vidéo passe aujourd’hui par des algorithmes de plus en plus poussés que Sony compte bien utiliser pour sa PS6. Un nouveau document officiel déniché sur le web détaille justement une méthode de génération d’images qui va permettre d’améliorer la fluidité des images affichées sur votre TV ou votre écran de PC.
Anticiper vos mouvements grâce à la manette
Contrairement au DLSS qui récupère uniquement les données de mouvement depuis le moteur du jeu, le modèle imaginé par Sony intègre un paramètre supplémentaire qui exploite les informations de la manette pour anticiper avec plus de précision vos déplacements d’une image à l’autre. Avec cette approche, Sony cherche à limiter le décalage qui peut exister entre ce que vous faites avec la manette et ce qui s’affiche à l’écran (ce que l’on appelle l’input lag).
Le brevet mentionne également la prise en charge potentielle de la génération de plusieurs images, un procédé que l’on connait déjà sur PC avec les cartes graphiques haut de gamme comme la RTX 5090. Le brevet précise que « Dans certaines configurations, les prédictions ne se limitent pas à l’image qui suit immédiatement dans le flux », soulignant que le système de décodage peut être entraîné pour prédire un nombre variable d’images situées avant ou après l’image d’entrée. On peut se poser la question de l’utilité d’une telle option sur un téléviseur classique dont la fréquence se limite généralement à 120 Hz, même si le fait d’avoir le choix est toujours bon à prendre.
La PS6 prépare ses armes
Si la technologie en elle-même est intéressante, on espère que les studios ne l’utiliseront pas comme une béquille pour masquer une piètre optimisation de leurs jeux qui tourneraient, par exemple, à 20 images par seconde. Une telle pratique risquerait d’introduire des artéfacts visuels, même si l’intégration des commandes du joueur grâce à la manette pourrait en partie corriger ces défauts.
Découvrez : Notre test de la PS5 Pro : très fluide, trop chère
Cette trouvaille ne représenterait qu’une des briques technologiques de la PlayStation 6, Sony ayant récemment racheté une technologie d’IA pour encore plus de photo-réalisme. Il faudra bien ça pour justifier le prix de la PS6 qui s’annonce extrêmement salé.

articles.title: Por qué la IA podría poner fin al futuro de las consolas de PlayStation, Xbox y Nintendo
articles.text:
Las consolas de videojuegos podrían dejar de ser un producto de masas en la próxima década, según un informe de Bloomberg Intelligence, la división de análisis financiero de la agencia estadounidense. El documento sostiene que la inteligencia artificial, lejos de ser ajena al mundo del entretenimiento doméstico, terminará redefiniendo el modo en que millones de personas juegan.
La proyección central es que el mercado de videojuegos a través de streaming o la nube alcanzará los 38.000 millones de dólares en 2035. Ese crecimiento convertiría a las máquinas de sobremesa, como PlayStation, Xbox o Switch, en dispositivos de nicho para una porción menor de usuarios.
Qué se dice sobre el fin de las consolas de videojuegos
El informe, liderado por el analista Nathan Naidu, plantea una paradoja. Las inversiones multimillonarias que las compañías tecnológicas destinan a centros de datos para inteligencia artificial están absorbiendo capacidad de fabricación de memoria y encareciendo los componentes electrónicos en el corto plazo.
Sin embargo, esa misma expansión dejará disponible, con el tiempo, una cantidad mayor de GPU (unidades de procesamiento gráfico). Según Bloomberg Intelligence, ese excedente intensificará la competencia entre los proveedores de cómputo en la nube y reducirá el costo de esos servicios.
El mercado del juego en la nube crecerá porque la infraestructura de IA dejará disponible más capacidad de cómputo, lo que abaratará el acceso a videojuegos sin necesidad de comprar hardware costoso. Esa es la lógica de fondo que atraviesa todo el informe.
A esto se suma otro factor: los títulos AAA exigen cada vez hardware más potente, lo que compromete el rendimiento de las consolas actuales y acorta su vida comercial. Para Bloomberg Intelligence, ese desgaste técnico empuja a los jugadores hacia alternativas de transmisión por internet.
Cómo el precio de las consolas ya refleja la crisis de componentes
El declive proyectado no depende únicamente de una estimación a diez años. Ya existen señales concretas en el mercado actual.
En esta generación, los usuarios debieron afrontar subidas de precio en lugar de las habituales rebajas que suelen acompañar el paso del tiempo. Hoy, comprar una PlayStation 5, una Xbox Series X o S, o una Switch 2 cuesta más que cuando esas máquinas llegaron a las tiendas.
La escasez de memoria, impulsada por el auge de los centros de datos para IA, golpeó directamente a fabricantes como Microsoft y Sony, que debieron ajustar precios de sus consolas durante este año. Todo indica que las próximas generaciones de ambas compañías llegarán con un costo superior al de sus predecesoras.
A ese escenario se suma la desaparición progresiva del formato físico. Sony mantiene su decisión de dejar de fabricar juegos físicos para PlayStation a partir de enero de 2028, lo que deja ese segmento prácticamente en manos de Nintendo, mientras Microsoft refuerza su apuesta por la distribución a través de internet.
Cómo podría cambiar el reemplazo de las consolas
El escenario que describe Bloomberg Intelligence no implica la desaparición inmediata de las consolas, sino un cambio de rol: de puerta de entrada obligatoria al entretenimiento a dispositivo reservado para quienes busquen la mejor experiencia local posible.
El reemplazo vendría de la mano del juego en la nube, un modelo en el que el usuario transmite el videojuego desde servidores remotos sin necesidad de hardware potente en su hogar. La combinación de consolas más caras, fin del formato físico y conexiones de fibra óptica cada vez más veloces configura, según el análisis, un terreno favorable para esa transición.
El antecedente más citado para cuestionar este pronóstico es lo que sucedió con Google Stadia, el servicio de transmisión de videojuegos que la compañía cerró en enero de 2023. Sin embargo, el propio análisis advierte que la coyuntura actual es distinta a la que llevó al cierre de ese servicio.
En aquel momento, la infraestructura de nube para videojuegos resultaba mucho más costosa y la latencia seguía siendo un obstáculo sin resolver. Los recursos de computación en la nube son hoy mayores, y la propia expansión de la IA podría terminar liberando espacio en los centros de datos para servicios como el juego en streaming.
A mediano plazo, el informe no anticipa la desaparición de las consolas de videojuegos. Lo que plantea es un desplazamiento gradual: mientras el hardware físico se encarece y pierde margen de maniobra frente a las exigencias técnicas de los juegos más recientes, la infraestructura de cómputo en la nube avanza en sentido contrario, con costos a la baja y mayor disponibilidad de capacidad de procesamiento.

articles.title: World, de Sam Altman, veut protéger les réunions Zoom grâce au scan de l’iris
articles.text:
World, la société cofondée par Sam Altman, lance World ID for Zoom. L'outil affiche un badge sur la vignette d'un participant dont l'"humanité" a été vérifiée (oui, on en est là). Il est proposé aux clients professionnels de Zoom via la Zoom Marketplace.
Nous sommes arrivés à un stade où voir un visage en visioconférence ne garantit plus que la personne est celle qu'elle prétend être. Selon une enquête Gartner de septembre 2025, 62% des responsables cybersécurité interrogés avaient vu leur organisation subir une attaque par deepfake (une vidéo ou une voix truquée par IA) l'année précédente.
Trois images à faire concorder pour décrocher le badge
Nous rapportions en octobre 2024 que World, anciennement Worldcoin, dévoilait son Orb 2.0 et un service baptisé World ID Deep Faces contre les deepfakes en ligne. Deux ans plus tard, elle s'attaque aux réunions Zoom. Bain Capital, OpenExchange, Outtake, Pantera Capital et VanEck Funds font partie des premiers partenaires.
Tout part de l'Orb, l'appareil de World qui scanne l'iris. Chacun peut y obtenir une "Proof of Human", une preuve d'humanité. Il peut être installé au bureau ou apporté à domicile. Son image est signée cryptographiquement, un peu comme un sceau numérique, ce qui empêche de la modifier, affirme World. Le participant relie ensuite son World ID à son compte Zoom. Pendant une réunion, une notification arrive sur son téléphone et il prend un selfie dans l'application. Ce contrôle permet donc qu'une personne bien vivante est devant l'appareil. Trois images sont alors comparées : celle de l'Orb, le selfie et le flux vidéo que voient les autres invités. Si elles concordent, le badge s'affiche pour tous.
World insiste sur la différence avec la détection classique. Celle-ci analyse les images pour deviner si elles sont truquées. Résultat, une course entre faussaires et détecteurs, où un seul faux non repéré peut coûter cher. Ici, on compare à une référence signée. L'intégration repose sur les Realtime Media Streams de Zoom, une interface donnant accès au flux vidéo en direct. Elle tourne sur AWS et n'analyse que la vidéo, pas l'audio ni les transcriptions. la validité du badge est fixée par les organisateurs. Par la suite, la vérification s'effectuera au sein d'une salle d'attente virtuelle.
Reste la vie privée. Selon heise, World affirme chiffrer l'identité des personnes scannées, si bien que l'entreprise ne peut pas la lire. Tiago Sada, directeur produit, explique que le protocole de World ID repose sur du code open source. Les concurrents peuvent donc le reprendre à leur compte. Pour décentraliser et chiffrer les données, il s’appuie sur la blockchain, un registre numérique partagé. Plusieurs banques et prestataires financiers déploient aussi l'outil, sans passer systématiquement par l'iris. L'application propose trois niveaux. Le premier vérifie un document officiel, le deuxième demande un selfie, le troisième, la Proof of Human, passe par l'Orb. C'est donc celui qu'utilise Zoom.

articles.title: Scripted tests can't keep up with AI-written code. Datadog is betting agents can.
articles.text:
Scripted tests can’t keep up with AI-written code. Datadog is betting agents can.
Nearly a year into the agentic coding explosion, many teams now use AI to write software as their de facto approach. As a result, Anthropic’s engineers are shipping eight times as much code as before, and some engineers are shipping thousands of PRs per month.
Management teams expecting their engineering capacity to explode will find that AI-written code doesn’t necessarily compress the software development lifecycle (SDLC) on its own.
The critical bottleneck in software creation has shifted from writing code to a later SDLC stage. After coding agents spit out new code, it still needs testing, and traditionally that meant humans writing the tests. That work includes deciding which user flows need testing, scripting tests for them, and rejiggering them when those flows change.
We’ve made it easy to write code and, in the process, increased the burden on humans to test new code. If we want to slash software development timelines, something has to change.
The observability and monitoring giant Datadog bought Propolis earlier this year, adding agent-written, goal- and output-oriented test writing to its platform. The approach lets agents explore applications, follow user flows on their own, and generate tests from plain-language prompts.
Add Datadog’s observability heft, and you get a system that can test code while providing the logs and traces it needs to vet system performance without the fragility hardcoded testing brings.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The New Stack will sit down with Ruxanda Lueck and Matthew White of Datadog on Wednesday, November 4, at 9 a.m. Pacific / 12 p.m. Eastern.
Lueck is a group product manager working on goal-based testing of AI features. White co-founded and served as CTO of Propolis. These are precisely the people to help us understand the current state of the art and what comes next.
We’ll ask how much test-writing teams can offload today and whether agentic testing has reached its own Claude Code moment. We’ll also ask whether plain-language testing instructions expand the number of staffers who can help test new code, and how long it will be before agents can read agent-written code and handle testing without humans lifting a finger.
Agent-written code has created tensions across the SDLC that no single tool can settle on its own. If testing can speed up code writing, though, teams clear one more obstacle between an idea and working software in production.
You’ll learn:
- How agents can test user flows that no one thought of
- How to write plain-language testing prompts
- How goal-based testing persists even when user flows change
- How to test AI features that return probabilistic, instead of deterministic, outputs
- Where scripted tests still have their place

articles.title: Face à ElevenLabs et ses 90 langues, Mistral dégaine Voxtral 3 — Frandroid
articles.text:
Guillaume Lample, cofondateur et directeur scientifique de Mistral AI, a annoncé ce mardi 20 octobre sur X l’arrivée de Voxtral 3. Il présente cette famille de modèles vocaux comme « SOTA », l’état de l’art dans le jargon. Quelques mois après l’annonce de son grand modèle de langage Large 4, la start-up parisienne vend cette fois aux entreprises de quoi faire décrocher une IA au téléphone. Et elle peut tourner sur les serveurs du client, qui garde alors ses appels chez lui.
Sur sa page de présentation, Mistral publie ses prix et une série de graphiques comparatifs. Ses modèles de transcription couvrent plus de 50 langues, sa synthèse vocale plus de 35. En mars 2026, Voxtral TTS, son premier modèle de synthèse vocale, n’en gérait que 9.
Quatre briques pour faire parler une IA au téléphone
La transcription repose sur deux modèles, Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 et Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3, qui traitent des fichiers audio en différé. Ils savent séparer les voix (qui a dit quoi) et s’aider d’une liste de mots techniques fournie par le client. La version Mini coûte 0,0035 dollar la minute, soit environ 19 centimes d’euro HT pour une heure d’audio.
Pour le direct, Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 transcrit en moins d’une demi-seconde dans plus de 35 langues. Il repère aussi le moment où l’interlocuteur a fini sa phrase, pour que l’agent ne lui coupe pas la parole.
La synthèse vocale (ou TTS, pour text-to-speech) passe par Voxtral Mini TTS 3, en différé comme en streaming. Ses voix adaptent l’émotion, le débit et l’accentuation à la conversation.
Mistral la facture 13 dollars (environ 11,60 € HT) le million de caractères, soit quelques centaines de pages de texte.
Son option Pro Voice clone une voix de façon plus fidèle, mais demande 30 minutes d’enregistrement, quand Google clone une voix en 30 secondes avec Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS.
Le kit de développement (SDK) d’agent vocal assemble le tout, en s’appuyant sur LiveKit, une brique open source de communication audio en temps réel. Entre l’écoute et la réponse, un modèle de langage comme Mistral Small réfléchit et déclenche des actions dans d’autres logiciels (le tool calling), comme consulter une facture ou réserver un créneau.
Dans sa démo, l’agent lit une lettre de médecin en français et prend rendez-vous chez un dermatologue pour une patiente anglophone. Selon Guillaume Lample, Voxtral 3 fait aussi tourner la nouvelle API d’agents vocaux de Mistral.
Plus de 50 langues comprises
Les « plus de 50 langues » du titre de Mistral concernent la transcription, dont les 24 langues officielles de l’UE et plusieurs langues asiatiques et indiennes peu dotées en données d’entraînement. La voix couvre plus de 35 langues, et les voix prêtes à l’emploi n’existent qu’en 18. Pour un service client international, un agent pourra donc comprendre des langues dans lesquelles il ne sait pas répondre.
Chez les concurrents, ElevenLabs revendique plus de 90 langues pour Eleven v4, annoncé le 28 septembre. OpenAI, lui, a attendu Live 1.1 pour que ChatGPT parle français sans accent américain.
Sur la transcription, Mistral publie des taux d’erreur mesurés sur FLEURS, un jeu de test public, pour 45 langues. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 y rate environ 4 mots sur 100, à égalité avec Microsoft AI Transcribe 2 et loin devant Whisper large-v3 d’OpenAI (16 %). Microsoft avance d’ailleurs sur une IA qui transcrit les paroles avant même la fin des phrases.
Pour la voix, les comparaisons sont des évaluations internes, notées par Gemini 3.8 Flash, l’IA de Google utilisée comme juge. Le test multilingue ne porte que sur 11 langues. Pour Large 4, il avait fallu attendre des benchmarks indépendants pour confronter les chiffres maison.
L’installation sur ses propres serveurs reste l’argument souverain de Mistral, qu’OVHcloud veut aussi lui disputer. Son fondateur Octave Klaba promet son propre modèle open source et tacle Mistral au passage.
Voxtral 3 est disponible dès ce mardi via l’API de Mistral, sur des serveurs européens, américains ou mondiaux. Les agents vocaux, la transcription et le clonage de voix s’essaient dans les Playground du Studio de Mistral.
