articles.title: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
articles.text:
On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the past year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or meet other deadlines despite warnings that it would result in the case being dismissed.
Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit
Ann Altman’s lawsuit against her brother was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled.
When the case was filed last year, a statement shared by Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers said, “Annie has made deeply hurtful and entirely untrue claims about our family, and especially Sam… All of these claims are utterly untrue. This situation causes immense pain to our entire family.”
Bluestone granted Sam Altman’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled in that court, while denying Sam’s request for attorney fees and costs. Santos Perez, a lawyer who had represented Ann until withdrawing this month, told The Guardian in a statement that “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”

articles.title: Motorola desafía a Xiaomi: su próximo móvil tendrá una batería gigante y precio rompedor
articles.text:
Motorola prepara el lanzamiento de un nuevo móvil de gama media con gran autonomía. A unos meses de presentar el Moto G47, el fabricante tiene todo listo para desvelar el Moto G47 Power, la variante que llega con una batería de mayor capacidad. Tal y como ha ocurrido con las generaciones anteriores, Motorola tomará como base el G47, por lo que este terminal comparte muchas de sus características.
Una filtración reciente ha revelado todas las especificaciones, incluido el precio. De acuerdo con GSMArena, el Moto G47 Power llegará con una batería de 7.000 mAh que es prácticamente idéntica a la que vimos en el G37 Power. Esta garantiza hasta dos días completos de uso sin necesidad de conectarlo y admite carga rápida TurboPower de 30 W por cable.
Por fuera, el Moto G47 Power ofrece una pantalla LCD de 6,67 pulgadas con resolución de 1604 x 720 píxeles y tasa de refresco de 120 Hz y recubrimiento Gorilla Glass 7i. Bajo el capó encontraremos un procesador MediaTek Dimensity 6300 de ocho núcleos junto con una configuración de 4 GB de RAM y 128 GB de almacenamiento interno. La filtración no menciona otras variantes, aunque podríamos esperar una de 8 GB + 128 GB, si es que la escasez de memoria lo permite.
En el apartado fotográfico tampoco habrá muchos cambios, ya que el Moto G47 Power usaría la misma configuración que su hermano menor. El módulo trasero incluye una cámara principal de 108 megapíxeles con zoom de 3 aumentos sin pérdida de calidad y una lente macro dedicada para fotografía de cerca. Este modelo no incluye gran angular y la cámara frontal solo alcanza los 8 MP, que son suficientes para las selfies y las videollamadas.
Moto G47 Power vs Moto G47: ¿qué cambia?
La diferencia fundamental entre ambos modelos está en la autonomía. El Moto G47 Power eleva la capacidad de la batería hasta los 7.000 mAh, mientras que el Moto G47 se queda en los 5.200 mAh. Otro ajuste importante lo vemos en la carga rápida, que pasa de 20 W a 30 W por cable. El resto de especificaciones se mantiene idéntico, incluidas las cámaras y el procesador.
Si lo comparamos con el G37 Power que se presentó en abril de este año, la única diferencia es el tiempo adicional de soporte que obtendrás. A juzgar por las filtraciones, el Moto G47 Power sería prácticamente idéntico, por lo que podrías comprar esta variante y ahorrarte unos cuantos euros.
De acuerdo con el último rumor, el Moto G47 Power tendría un precio de salida cercano a los 270 euros para la versión de 4 GB + 128 GB. El móvil se venderá en dos acabados: uno negro y otro verde turquesa con el acabado fino de Pantone que caracteriza a la marca. Por el momento no hay detalles sobre su disponibilidad, aunque está confirmado que lo veremos en España, puesto que Motorola publicó su documentación sobre la Etiqueta Energética Europea hace unos días.

articles.title: Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis — ICs from SK hynix DDR5-5600 16GB modules used to create DDR5-7800 desktop sticks
articles.text:
Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis — ICs from SK hynix DDR5-5600 16GB modules used to create DDR5-7800 desktop sticks
You have to be lucky to find such cheap DDR5 SODIMMs, and specialist equipment and skills are required for success.
What if you could buy a cheap used DDR5 SODIMM (laptop memory) kit and transform it into a super-fast DDR5 desktop kit? That’s what electronics hobbyist Blighted Agent recently did when they succeeded in converting a SK hynix 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM kit they got from Facebook Marketplace for $120 into a 2x 16GB DDR5-7800 desktop kit, claimed to be worth around $1,000. They also had to buy some blank DDR5 desktop memory PCBs from AliExpress for around $16 each, and a set of heatsinks for around $18.
In the above video, our hero says they bought the donor laptop 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 sticks for just $120, which is a bargain. With extra bits and pieces from AliExpress (desktop DDR5 PCBs, etc.), the total bill of materials came to $175. Blighted Agent comments that the SODIMMs used what he believed to be SK hynix A-die modules, which are the same as the ICs used in expensive desktop DDR5 modules like the G.Skill Trident Royal line.
The process began with taking the memory ICs from the donor modules using a hot air station. Then they were cleaned and had 0.45mm leaded solder balls added, using a DDR5 stencil, reballing jig, and hot air. Next, the blank desktop DDR5 PCBs were prepared. A little solder was added to the plethora of BGA connectors to be ready for the memory chips to connect to.
The old DDR5 ICs and the new desktop modules could now be mated, using flux, the preheater, hot air, and watching and prodding carefully with a dental pick. Blighted Agent’s experience lets him know when the BGA chips have successfully mated with the PCB. You can eyeball when they pop precisely into place due to surface tension, and offer up a modicum of resistance to pick prodding.
Finally, the enthusiast added the SPD chip and BIOS chip from the SODIMMs to the new desktop DIMMs. These new desktop DIMMs were quickly tested in a PC before they were finished off with carefully applied thermal pads and the fancy-looking heatsinks.
Blighted Agent felt lucky that there were no issues with the newly created desktop modules. There’s a lot of intricate things that can go wrong during such a process. The initial boot verification showed them recognized in his Asus ROG Maximus Z790 Apex Encore motherboard as two “SK hynix 16,384MB 5600MHz” modules, which was correct. Some tuning resulted in rock-steady performance at DDR5-7800 CL38 and 1.40V. This was verified by stress testing for 90 minutes, which the enthusiast reckons was ample for a gaming PC. It is very likely a better result than using those mechanical SODIMM-to-DIMM converters you can buy, which can be problematic.
Blighted Agent seems to specialize in BGA soldering work, and has also successfully upgraded several graphics cards with double the VRAM. Though videos like this are edited to be brief, and they make the process look easy, the TechTuber admits there is a lot that can go wrong during this kind of rework. Moreover, with RAM modules, they lack the testing equipment to locate an issue with any particular IC on the PCB. So, if this module didn’t work, they might have ended up in a world of pain, not knowing which memory chip had an issue due to either an internal fault or a BGA soldering glitch.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Looking around at used DDR5 SODIMMs, it looks like Blighted Agent was very lucky to get a used working 32GB kit for $120. I just checked eBay U.S., and the best deal there was $320. Meanwhile, the best price for a new 32GB DDR5-6000 kit seems to be $449 at the time of writing.
We reported on Russian enthusiast VIK-on succeeding in a similar project earlier this year, but all their costing was in Rubles, and they went the extra mile in flashing custom firmware so the remade modules would be auto-detected with 6400 MT/s XMP support on most motherboards. In late 2026, DDR5 RAM continues to be too expensive.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Oubliez PowerPoint : voici ChatGPT Slides
articles.text:
Le mois dernier, OpenAI officialisait l’arrivée de ChatGPT Space avec son lot d’outils bureautiques intégrant des pages et des feuilles de calcul, tout en précisant que les présentations arriveraient plus tard. C’est désormais chose faite avec le lancement de ChatGPT Slides. L’entreprise détaille les nouvelles possibilités offertes à ses abonnés pour générer rapidement des supports visuels directement à partir de documents existants ou de modèles prédéfinis. PowerPoint et Google Slides n’ont qu’à bien se tenir.
Collaboration en direct et options d’exportation
Une fois le diaporama généré par l’intelligence artificielle, il est possible de le partager avec des collaborateurs pour travailler simultanément sur le projet. Les membres invités peuvent donc apporter des modifications et laisser des commentaires en direct. De son côté, ChatGPT peut même appliquer automatiquement des changements en fonction des retours des membres de l’équipe.
Lorsque le résultat final vous convient, l’outil permet d’ouvrir directement le fichier dans des logiciels tiers comme PowerPoint ou Google Slides. Vous pourrez évidemment télécharger le document au format PDF ou l’exporter directement sous forme de fichier PowerPoint pour l’utiliser hors ligne.
Qui peut profiter de ChatGPT Slides ?
ChatGPT Slides est disponible dès maintenant pour les personnes abonnées aux formules Pro, Business et Enterprise d’OpenAI. Pour en profiter, il suffit de demander directement à l’IA de créer des diapositives à partir d’un fichier texte ou d’une conversation en cours.
À lire : Avec Atlas enterré, ChatGPT s’installe dans vos onglets Google Chrome
En revanche, les utilisateurs payants de la formule Plus ne peuvent malheureusement pas en profiter. On peut l’expliquer par le fait que ChatGPT Slides est intégré à l’écosystème ChatGPT Space, lequel est déjà réservé aux abonnements supérieurs. Une distinction qui n’est pas sans rappeler le retrait par Google de ses meilleurs modèles sur son abonnement payant Google AI Plus.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : ChatGPT

articles.title: Disrupt Africa, Touch Inspiration launch accelerator to help non-technical founders build and launch apps - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Disrupt Africa has partnered with Kenya-based digital product and technology company Touch Inspiration to launch Disrupt Launchpad, an app development accelerator that helps non-technical founders turn their ideas into working applications and bring them to market.
Founded in 2014, Disrupt Africa is the leading news platform dedicated to the African tech startup ecosystem, and a producer of research publications and podcasts.
Touch Inspiration was founded in 2017 and helps entrepreneurs and businesses turn their ideas into working digital products. The company specialises in developing web and mobile applications, AI-powered solutions and business platforms, taking products from defined requirements through development and launch.
The two organisations have joined forces to launch Disrupt Launchpad, a programme designed for entrepreneurs who have a clear app idea but lack the technical skills, team or resources to bring it to life. Through Touch Inspiration, founders can get their apps professionally built and launched at startup-friendly rates, while Disrupt Africa helps put those products in front of a wider audience of potential users, customers and investors.
“We meet so many people who are inspired to create something, but don’t know how to bring it to life. What makes this partnership with Disrupt Africa so exciting is that we get to help those people build their apps and, just as importantly, get them in front of the people who will actually use them. It’s one thing to have a great idea, but seeing it come to life and reach the market is where the real value is realised,” said Robert M., founder of Touch Inspiration.
“The whole point of Disrupt Africa has always been to make entrepreneurship accessible to everyone, and with this partnership with Robert M. and the amazing team at Touch Inspiration we’re going right in at the start. Funding is important, networking is key, but being able to build your great idea in the first place is absolutely essential,” said Tom Jackson, co-founder of Disrupt Africa. “This programme will help you build, and launch, and put you in a strong position to turn it into a success.”
Aspiring entrepreneurs and existing startups with clear app ideas are invited to apply through Disrupt Launchpad. The programme offers startup-friendly development rates, while selected ventures may even qualify for an equity-based partnership, reducing the upfront cost of getting their applications built.

articles.title: From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Giving supply chain teams direct access to the systems behind their decisions.
Every supply chain generates constant signals: orders in approval, shifting lead times, slowing ports, drifting prices, disruptions. The problem isn’t scarce data. It’s the distance between the data and the decision-maker.
Answering “which top-revenue SKUs are exposed to the current port closure, and what will it cost?” used to mean knowing which system held each piece and stitching them together by hand while the domain expert waited.
Could that manager instead ask in plain language and get an actionable, cross-system answer in seconds? Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the intelligence layer, exposing enterprise Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers as a composable tool layer. Amazon Quick turns that into action for personas with no setup. Answers come from live systems of record and grounded documents, not model recall, and every change waits for a named human. In this post, we walk through this pattern end to end, from a conversational walkthrough in Amazon Quick to the AgentCore tool layer behind it, and we show you how to deploy it yourself.
The problem: Data-rich, insight-poor
Each question needs its own tool: inventory from the enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, disruptions from email or news, a request for quotation (RFQ) from procurement, and compliance from a checklist. Correlating is manual.
A day in the life
A manager’s morning traditionally spans the ERP (inventory exceptions), monitoring tool (alerts), procurement (alternatives), email (RFQ), and a tracker: 45–60 minutes across five systems with a dozen-plus context switches.
Conversationally it’s three prompts in one tool, “Any critical disruptions affecting my top-revenue SKUs?” → “Assess the TechComp halt and issue an emergency RFQ to approved alternatives” → “Looks good. Send it.”, in minutes.
Deep dive: Supply chain scenario walkthrough
The following five steps follow one disruption from detection to an approved emergency RFQ, all in a single Amazon Quick conversation.
Step 1: Discovery – “What tools do I have?”
The user asks “What supply chain tools do I have?” and Amazon Quick lists the supply chain MCP servers published in AWS Agent Registry. Because an administrator has turned on the registry integration, the four business MCP servers already appear as connector cards, with connection details pre-populated and no URLs to enter by hand. The orchestration agent is added as its own MCP connector.
Step 2: Querying – “Show me active disruptions”
“Check active supply disruptions” calls the Disruption Alerts MCP (assess_disruption_impact): three disruptions with severity, region, and SKU counts. How we solve it: Quick routes the request through AgentCore to the MCP server, which queries backend monitoring and returns a structured result, no dashboard or export.
Step 3: Drill-down – “Assess the critical one”
The user opens the TechComp Production Halt. assess_disruption_impact(disruption_id="DISR-002") correlates order, customer, and inventory data: $750K at risk, 23 orders, three days of supply. How we solve it: one MCP tool call fans out across systems of record, so the manager gets a consolidated impact read without touching the ERP.
Step 4: Action – “Get mitigation recommendations”
The user asks for mitigation. recommend_mitigation(disruption_id="DISR-002") chains the Governance MCP (verify approved alternatives) and Quoting MCP (contract-aligned quote), one flow from one request. How we solve it: the agent plans and sequences the calls, so a single ask spans disruption, governance, and quoting with no manual hand-offs.
Step 5: Automated follow-up
The user then sets up proactive monitoring (“Alert me every morning if there’s a new critical disruption”). The same flow can run unattended from an inbound supplier email. How we solve it: the same agent and tools run on a schedule or email trigger, posting review-ready cards to the Activity Feed for a person to approve.
Put end to end, those five steps are a single runtime sequence:
Solution architecture
That’s the experience. Here’s how it is built: the pattern separates the intelligence layer from the interface layer, so each evolves independently, with Amazon Quick as the interface and AgentCore as the intelligence.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: The intelligence layer
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a modular agentic platform for building, deploying, and operating agents securely at scale. It offers more than we use here. Four of its services are relevant to this pattern:
- Runtime – Serverless hosting for MCP servers and agents, with session isolation and built-in identity.
- Gateway – Turns APIs, AWS Lambda functions, and services into MCP-compatible tools behind a secure managed endpoint, standardizing tool access. Reasoning is the calling agent’s.
- Identity – Authentication and credential management, compatible with existing identity providers.
- Policy – Deterministic authorization rules, authored in natural language or Cedar, that intercept every tool call before execution, keeping an agent in its lane on procurement and financial data.
The MCP protocol: How tools communicate
MCP is an open standard for how AI models interact with external tools. Each server exposes tools with typed parameters:
This means:
- AI clients (Quick, custom agents, other MCP apps) can consume the same servers.
- Backends (SAP, Oracle, custom microservices) can be wrapped as an MCP server.
- Tool discovery is automatic. Clients query the registry for schemas at runtime.
AWS Agent Registry: The discovery layer
The registry is the governed discovery layer: a publisher submits a record, a curator approves it, and only then is it discoverable through hybrid search, browsing, or the registry’s MCP endpoint. One scale reality worth noting: because schemas are discovered at runtime, treat each as a contract, versioning new alongside old for breaking changes.
Multi-step orchestration
The reasoning layer is an agent on AgentCore Runtime, an agent record at its direct invocation URL through a Custom MCP connector, with no Lambda or gateway. Here, it’s the Order Fulfillment Agent. Given one request it plans which tools to call and in what order:
Security and governance architecture
Every tool call passes through the same AgentCore control set before it reaches a backend.
The MCP servers in this pattern
| MCP server | Capabilities | Example queries | 
| Quoting Engine ( sc-quoting-gateway) | Quote generation, pricing rules, validation | “Contract-aligned quote for 500 units of SKU-A” | 
| Governance Engine ( sc-governance-gateway) | Supplier approval, budget authority, regulatory compliance, policy rules | “Is SupplierCo on our approved vendor list?” | 
| Invoice Processing ( sc-invoice-gateway) | Invoice approval routing, AP aging, payment schedules | “What invoices are pending approval this week?” | 
| Disruption Alerts ( sc-disruption-alert-gateway) | Active disruptions, severity, impact assessments, mitigation | “Critical disruptions affecting our APAC suppliers?” | 
| Order Fulfillment Agent ( sc-order-fulfillment-agent) | Multi-step orchestration across all four business MCPs (AgentCore Runtime, direct invocation URL) | “A supplier went down, find alternatives, check compliance, issue an RFQ” | 
Amazon Quick: The enterprise AI assistant
Amazon Quick puts AgentCore tools before business users through chat, agents, the Activity Feed, and automated workflows, with no technical setup.
Key components used
| Component | Role in this pattern | How it works | 
| Agent Registry connection | Surfaces MCP servers as connectors | Admin links the registry once. Records become connector cards | 
| Quick Agent | One SC agent that adapts to role | Tailors to persona (manager, procurement, analyst) | 
| MCP connectors | Expose MCP tools in chat | A card connector exposes tools across Chat, agents, schedules | 
| Activity Feed | Proactive alerts and actions | Agents post cards. The user acts | 
| Schedules | Recurring natural-language automation | For example, “every morning” | 
| Outlook Integration | Email into the feed | Supplier replies parsed and validated | 
| Structured data connectors | Query operational records | Quick queries Space datasets (orders, inventory, suppliers, contracts) for the MCP rule check | 
| Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) knowledge base | Retrieval over documents | Invoices, contracts, policies in an S3 knowledge base, grounding answers through Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) | 
| CRM connector (optional) | Reads customer records (optional) | CRM (for example, Salesforce) accounts, opportunities, contacts. Can also load into datasets | 
Automated Activity Feed and proactive monitoring
The Activity Feed is the proactive surface of Amazon Quick, a unified inbox where agents post results, alerts, and recommendations. Feed items are:
- Actionable, each carries context and next-step actions.
- AI-triaged, with priority indicators (Reply needed, Follow up, Deadline).
- Cross-source, spanning email, schedules, agent runs, and external systems.
- Human-in-the-loop, where agents propose and humans decide.
How automated monitoring works
AgentCore tools plus the proactive capabilities of Amazon Quick give two paths, time-based and email-driven, through a common trigger → agent → output pipeline.
Use case: Validate supplier responses from email
Suppliers reply to an emergency RFQ by email with pricing. The agent validates each (approved supplier? within guidelines?) and stages the result. It does not author a quote, pick a winner, or issue a purchase order (PO).
Phase 1: Setup (one-time, approximately 5 minutes)
- Connect Outlook: in Amazon Quick, choose Settings → Connections → Add Outlook.
- Configure Activity Feed: turn on email monitoring in feed preferences.
- Create SC Agent: build an agent with these instructions:
- Create Schedule: “Every 2 hours during business hours, check for new supplier replies and validate them.”
Phase 2: Runtime (fully automated)
The feed card carries the validation results and decision-relevant facts:
| Supplier Response: Ready for Review | Details | 
| Supplier | TechSupply Co, ✅ approved vendor | 
| SKU / Qty / Price | MCU-7200 · 10,000 units · $2.45/unit | 
| Price check | ✅ within purchasing guidelines | 
| Actions | Select for PO · Compare responses · Reject | 
Phase 3: Human-in-the-loop
The reviewer compares validated responses and either selects a supplier and issues the PO, or rejects with a logged reason. Selection and the PO stay with a person.
Use case: Proactive disruption monitoring
Schedule-triggered, the same pattern applies: a daily 8:30 AM agent checks for new critical or high-severity disruptions, assesses impact, flags anything under seven days of supply as URGENT, and posts an alert card with an Issue Emergency RFQ action.
Where this fits alongside traditional BI
| Dimension | Traditional business intelligence (BI) / dashboards | AgentCore + Amazon Quick | 
| Access model | Navigate, log in, find the dashboard/report | Ask in natural language. The system finds the source | 
| Time to insight | Minutes to hours (find → filter → export → correlate) | Seconds (ask → answer with cross-system context) | 
| Multi-system correlation | Manual: 3-4 tabs, copy-paste | Automatic: the agent orchestrates across MCP servers from one query | 
| Action gap | Insight in one tool → switch → act in another | Insight → action in the same conversation | 
| Setup cost | Weeks/months (dashboard design, ETL, permissions, training) | Minutes to connect, once your MCP servers exist | 
| Run cost | Fixed: pipelines cost the same whether or not anyone asks | Usage-based: serverless scales to zero, cost tracks questions (Lambda + agent tokens) | 
| Trust & accuracy | As fresh as the last ETL load | Computed live from systems of record and grounded docs, every write human-gated | 
This isn’t a “replace everything” argument. Dashboards remain superior for trend visualization, collaborative analysis, regulatory reporting, and exploratory analysis. Use conversational AI for real-time operational decisions and BI for strategic analysis. They complement, not compete.
Personas and use cases
One Quick Agent serves all three personas: the manager maintains continuity, procurement sources with compliance-awareness, the analyst correlates signals. Persona also bounds reach, through row/column-level security and per-persona MCP-tool scoping, so procurement does not see finance data.
| Persona | Use case | Tools invoked | Outcome | 
| SC Manager | Morning disruption check | Disruption Alerts MCP | Disruptions, revenue at risk, days of supply | 
| SC Manager | Emergency procurement | Governance → Quoting MCP | Verified alternatives + RFQ, one flow | 
| Procurement | Supplier verification, budget authority | Governance MCP | Approval, compliance, limits | 
| Procurement | RFQ generation and response validation | Quoting MCP | RFQ issued + responses validated | 
| Ops Analyst | Cross-system correlation | SC Operations Agent | Multi-MCP reasoning, one query | 
| Ops Analyst | Payment queue, audit, disruption trends | Invoice / Governance MCP | AP aging, audit log, patterns | 
Getting started
Deploying the pattern takes three phases: provision the infrastructure, connect Amazon Quick to your data and the registry, and turn on monitoring.
Prerequisites
Before you begin:
- An AWS account with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AWS Agent Registry.
- AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) v2, AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) CLI, and Docker (the agent runs as an arm64 container).
- Python 3.12 or later, with Boto3 1.43.94 or later for the registry step.
- Active credentials with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to deploy and register (aws sts get-caller-identity returns the target account).
- Data layer: a database (Snowflake, PostgreSQL/RDS, or a SQLAlchemy engine), an Amazon S3 bucket, optionally a Salesforce org.
- Amazon Quick set up for your organization.
- (Optional) An Outlook account for email automation.
Setup uses two surfaces, so each of the following steps names where it happens: the Amazon Quick web console in a browser (Amazon Quick Sight permissions, Agent Registry linking, connectors, and agent settings) and the Quick Desktop App (connecting Outlook for email automation). The conversational experience in the Desktop App comes last, once setup is done.
Deploy the infrastructure
Everything is open source and scripted: clone the quick-for-supply-chain example in the aws-samples/sample-amazon-quick-suite-knowledge-hub repository and follow its README.md, or point a coding agent like Kiro at it.
The README.md covers three phases. Phase 1 deploys the AgentCore stack: the identity layer (an Amazon Cognito user pool and app client, authorization-code OAuth flow, plus a test user), four business-rule MCP servers (each an AWS Lambda function fronted by its own AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using CUSTOM_JWT authorization), the gateway targets mapping the tools of each Lambda function, and sc-order-fulfillment-agent on AgentCore Runtime as a container, with least-privilege IAM roles. Phase 2 uploads the synthetic dataset to Amazon S3. Phase 3 verifies gateways and runtime are Ready. Six Agent Registry records are approved.
Grant Amazon Quick access to your data
In the Amazon Quick web console (browser): grant Amazon Quick access from the Amazon Quick Sight admin page (Manage Quick Sight → Security and permissions) to both the S3 bucket and Amazon Athena, since each table is served through an Athena source over an AWS Glue database. Without the Athena grant, dataset creation fails.
Link the registry and create connectors
Linking the registry is one-time and administrator-level. Creating a connector is per-user. Both happen in the Amazon Quick console. See the AWS Agent Registry integration guide.
Link the registry (administrator, one-time)
An administrator links one Agent Registry to the Quick account. In the Amazon Quick web console (admin): go to Manage account → Permissions → AWS Agent Registry and turn on the registry (sc-supply-chain-registry, one per account). Only registries in your account and Region, agent-registry namespace, AWS_IAM (SigV4) authorization, and READY status appear. The Quick-managed service role links it.
Create a connector
After the registry is linked, approved MCP server records become connector cards: the four business MCPs as cards, the order-fulfillment agent added manually. At scale, federate connector authentication through your identity provider and provision connectors to groups, with the Cognito user pool as the seam.
In the Amazon Quick web console (per user): the four cards appear on the Connectors page (sc-quoting-mcp, sc-governance-mcp, sc-invoice-processing-mcp, sc-disruption-alert-mcp). Authenticate through the OAuth authorization-code flow (OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE) with client ID, secret, and token, authorization, and redirect URLs from the deploy script. Sign in as the test user, turn on tools, create and share.
Registry-sourced connectors are Custom MCP connectors (relevant for custom permissions). Removing the link later doesn’t delete connectors already created.
Add the order-fulfillment agent connector
In the Amazon Quick web console: because it is an agent record, create its connector manually (Connectors → Create for your team → Model Context Protocol → Create new): name it sc-order-fulfillment-agent, point it at the AgentCore Runtime direct invocation URL from the deploy script, complete the same OAuth sign-in, create and share.
Attach the connectors to your agent
The deployment creates the Supply Chain agent: a Quick Space, imported datasets and S3 knowledge base, and the agent with instructions, starter prompts, and welcome message. What remains is attaching the connectors.
In the Amazon Quick web console (agent settings): open the deployment-created Supply Chain agent (default id sc-supply-chain-agent) and attach all five connectors (four business MCPs plus sc-order-fulfillment-agent), or pass the five connector IDs to the setup script.
Set up proactive monitoring
To make it proactive, Quick runs the same agent on a schedule or on incoming email and posts results to the Activity Feed. Both paths reuse the agent and tools you configured.
In the Quick Desktop App (Settings → Connections): connect Outlook and turn on email monitoring. Then, in Quick Chat, create two natural-language schedules, time-based (“Every morning, check for new critical disruptions”) and email-driven (“Every two hours in business hours, check supplier replies and validate”). The agent extracts pricing, runs the checks, and posts a card.
Try it in Amazon Quick
With the agent and connectors ready, ask in natural language in Amazon Quick Chat. Each prompt shows the data-then-rules pattern.
| Ask Amazon Quick | What you get | 
| “What supply chain tools do I have?” | The five MCP connectors (quoting, governance, invoice, disruption alerts, order-fulfillment agent), with status. | 
| “Show me active supply disruptions.” | Active disruptions with severity, region, SKU counts (Disruption Alerts MCP). | 
| “Assess the impact of the TechComp production halt.” | Revenue at risk, affected orders, days of supply, from your datasets. | 
| “Is this supplier an approved vendor, and do we have budget authority for a $72,000 PO?” | An approval from the Governance MCP (vendor status, budget authority, compliance). | 
| “Generate a contract-aligned quote for 1,000 units for this customer.” | A contract-aligned quote from the Quoting MCP, as a branded document. | 
| “A supplier just went down. Find alternatives, verify compliance, and issue an emergency RFQ.” | The Order Fulfillment Agent chains disruption, governance, and quoting MCPs into one recommendation. | 
Conclusion
AgentCore and Amazon Quick are a repeatable enterprise-AI pattern: separate intelligence from interface. AgentCore turns fragmented backends into a composable, governed, AI-accessible layer through standard MCP interfaces. Amazon Quick democratizes access in natural language.
The gain is the collapsed decision chain: detect, research, decide, act, and log once spanned five tools, now one conversation. The AI researches, correlates, validates. The person decides. Every call is authenticated, authorized, policy-checked, and audited, and a 45-60 minute routine across five systems can collapse to minutes.
That is the shift from data-rich, insight-poor to data-rich, decision-ready. Start with one MCP server and one persona. The registry grows and the experience stays the same.

articles.title: Une mission révolutionnaire : mais que va faire le rover français IDEFIX sur la lune de Mars, au juste ?
articles.text:
Le Japon vient de lancer MMX, une mission inédite pour ramener sur Terre des morceaux de Phobos, l’une des deux lunes de Mars. À son bord, le petit rover franco-allemand, IDEFIX, jouera un rôle crucial.
Mars n’est pas seule : notre voisine est accompagnée de deux petites lunes, Phobos et Deimos. Découvertes en 1877 par l’astronome américain Asaph Hall, elles ressemblent à deux gros cailloux difformes, souvent comparés à des pommes de terre.
Phobos, la plus grande, mesure environ 22 kilomètres de large. Et elle se rapproche inexorablement de Mars et finira, dans 50 millions d’années, par s’écraser sur la planète ou se disloquer en anneau. Deimos, elle, atteint 15 kilomètres seulement. Leur origine reste, à ce jour, un mystère : sont-elles les débris d’un impact géant sur Mars, ou des astéroïdes capturés par sa gravité ?
IDEFIX, un éclaireur sur Phobos
C’est justement la question à laquelle va tenter de répondre la mission MMX de la JAXA, l’agence spatiale japonaise. Elle a décollé ce 19 octobre à bord d’une fusée H3, depuis le centre spatial de Tanegashima, dans le sud-ouest de l’archipel.
La sonde va voyager environ dix mois dans l’espace pour rejoindre la planète rouge, où elle doit arriver en août 2027. Elle se placera ensuite autour de Phobos et y restera près de trois ans. C’est à ce moment-là qu’IDEFIX entrera en scène. Ce petit rover a été conçu par l’agence spatiale allemande (DLR) et le CNES. De la taille d’une caisse de boissons, il pèse 25 kilos sur Terre. Mais sur Phobos, où la gravité est infime, il ne fera plus que 15 grammes.
Largué fin 2028 ou début 2029, il tombera de 40 à 100 mètres, rebondira tout doucement, puis se redressera tout seul. Pendant 100 jours, il parcourra le sol pour repérer les deux sites où la sonde pourra se poser. Un éclaireur, en somme.
Comprendre l’origine de Phobos
Une fois que les sites seront choisis par IDEFIX, MMX viendra se poser à deux reprises sur Phobos, sur la face tournée vers Mars, puis sur celle qui y est opposée. Deux outils lui permettront de prélever de la matière : un carottier pour creuser sous la surface, puis un échantillonneur pneumatique, qui va soulever la poussière grâce à un jet de gaz. L’objectif est de récupérer plus de 10 grammes de roche.
La sonde embarque également l’instrument MEGANE de la NASA, un spectromètre à rayons gamma et neutrons qui doit repérer la présence d’éléments légers comme l’hydrogène. Ce point est crucial, et doit nous éclairer sur les origines de Phobos. En effet, ces éléments s’évaporent facilement quand la température monte.
Si la lune est née d’un impact géant, les débris projetés dans l’espace auraient été portés à très haute température, ils auraient donc presque tous disparu. À l’inverse, un astéroïde venu des confins du Système solaire en contiendrait beaucoup plus. Cette mesure devrait donc nous éclairer sur les origines de la lune
Une première mondiale
Le retour de MMX vers la Terre est prévu en novembre 2030, et la capsule doit atterrir en Australie en 2031. Ce sera une première : jamais un échantillon d’une lune martienne n’aura été ramené. Il pourrait même contenir des fragments de Mars, projetés dans l’espace puis tombés sur Phobos. De quoi mieux comprendre l’histoire de la planète rouge et, peut-être, l’origine de son eau.
Une course effrénée : la mission Tianwen-3 de la Chine, prévue pour 2028, doit rapporter des roches directement depuis la surface de Mars en 2031.

articles.title: Après l'Allemagne, Waymo annonce des taxis autonomes à Madrid : bientôt à Paris ?
articles.text:
Après l’Allemagne, c’est au tour de l’Espagne. Ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, sur son blog et sur X, Waymo a annoncé son arrivée dans la région de Madrid. Cette filiale d’Alphabet, la maison mère de Google, fait déjà rouler des taxis sans chauffeur dans plusieurs villes américaines.
Ses Jaguar I-Pace électriques rouleront à Madrid « dans les prochains jours », et l’entreprise y vise ses premiers clients en 2027. Waymo a ouvert trois filiales européennes en juin, et la française est désormais la seule à ne pas avoir de ville annoncée.
Waymo dans Madrid et sa périphérie
À Madrid, Waymo applique sa méthode habituelle. Les voitures roulent d’abord en conduite manuelle pour cartographier les rues. Elles passent ensuite en mode autonome, avec des « spécialistes » formés au volant, avant de retirer le conducteur à la dernière étape. Selon le journal El Español, les essais suivent l’instruction VEH 2025/07 de la DGT, la Direction générale de la circulation espagnole, qui encadre les tests de véhicules automatisés sur route ouverte.
Les premiers trajets se feront à Madrid ainsi que dans les communes adjacentes d’Alcobendas et de Getafe. Pour l’instant, Waymo n’a indiqué ni les prix des courses ni la taille de la flotte qu’elle comptait déployer dans le pays.
La firme ne sera pas la première sur place. Le chinois WeRide, associé à Uber, prévoit aussi de lancer son propre service de taxi autonome dans la capitale espagnole avant la fin de l’année.
Paris, prochaine étape logique ?
Madrid arrive deux mois après Munich. Le 25 août, Waymo avait annoncé un service commercial dans la capitale bavaroise « vers la fin 2027 », le premier prévu dans l’Union européenne. Dans les deux pays, Waymo dit travailler avec les autorités nationales et locales pour obtenir les autorisations qui lui manquent encore pour transporter des clients sans conducteur.
Pour mémoire, Waymo a enregistré entre le 11 et le 23 juin trois filiales européennes : en Allemagne, en Espagne et en France. En suivant la logique, Paris pourrait donc être la prochaine ville dans laquelle l’entreprise américaine déploiera son service.
Sur le papier, la France a déjà un cadre légal. Depuis 2022, une ordonnance de 2021 autorise des véhicules de niveau 4 sur des parcours validés. Ces véhicules roulent sans conducteur, mais uniquement dans une zone et des conditions définies à l’avance. Justement, WeRide s’en sert déjà pour un minibus sans chauffeur près de Valence.
Waymo n’est pas le seul à viser l’Europe. En septembre, Bolt et Lucid ont annoncé vouloir déployer 25 000 taxis autonomes sur le continent, sans donner de calendrier précis. Pour Madrid, Waymo a ouvert une page d’inscription qui permet de suivre l’avancée du projet.

articles.title: Eine manipulierte Nachricht, zwei Angriffsmethoden: Phishing-Mails zielen jetzt auch auf KI-Assistenten ab
articles.text:
Phishing: Wie Betrüger mit manipulierten E-Mails KI-Agenten austricksen
Den meisten Menschen ist das Risiko betrügerischer Phishing-Mails inzwischen bewusst. Aber gilt das auch für KI-Agenten, die zunehmend für die Verwaltung von Postfächern zuständig sind? Eine Analyse des Cybersecurity-Anbieters Barracuda deutet darauf hin, dass Betrüger:innen mit ihren Phishing-Versuchen direkt agentische KI-Systeme ansprechen wollen.
Phishing bekommt eine neue Dimension
Phishing zählt zu den größten Cybergefahren. Klassische Phishing-Mails verleiten Menschen dazu, auf einen Link zu klicken, einen Anhang zu öffnen oder sensible Daten preiszugeben, aber auch betrügerische SMS oder Whatsapp-Nachrichten spielen eine Rolle. Der Data Breach Investigations Report 2026 zeigt die Dimension des Problems: Der Telekommunikations- und Technologiekonzern Verizon analysierte dafür mehr als 31.000 Sicherheitsvorfälle und über 22.000 bestätigte Datenpannen aus 145 Ländern. Das Ergebnis: In 16 Prozent der Fälle war Phishing der erste Zugangsweg.
KI-Agenten könnten dieses Risiko jetzt weiter erhöhen. Nutzer:innen verwenden sie immer öfter, um E-Mails zusammenzufassen oder Posteingänge zu priorisieren. Laut den Forscher:innen von Barracuda manipulieren Angreifer:innen deshalb zunehmend sowohl die Nutzer:innen als auch deren KI-Assistenten – und das mit ein und derselben E-Mail. Während sie Menschen etwa mit Social Engineering manipulieren, bedienen sie sich mit Blick auf KI-Agenten der Prompt-Injection, um zum Beispiel vorige Anweisungen gezielt außer Kraft zu setzen.
KI-Agenten bergen zusätzliche Risiken
Eine von Barracuda analysierte Betrugskampagne zeigt, wie klassisches Social Engineering mit Prompt-Injection kombiniert wird. Die E-Mail wirkt auf den ersten Blick wie eine normale Korrespondenz: Die Adressen stimmen überein, die Nachricht trägt einen hohen Spam-Vertrauenswert und stammt von einer Domäne des öffentlichen Sektors. Die E-Mail wirkt somit legitim und besteht die reputationsbasierte Filterung. Laut den Forscher:innen hat sie allerdings mehrere Ebenen: Eine zeigt dem Empfänger Text und Bilder, eine andere enthält versteckte Prompt-Injections für den KI-Agenten.
Die erste Technik ist Sicherheitsexpert:innen bekannt. Die E-Mail wirkt vertrauenswürdig – öffnen Nutzer:innen aber den Anhang, kommt es zum Diebstahl von Anmeldeinformationen oder zur Installation von Malware. Aber selbst dann, wenn sie die betrügerische E-Mail übersehen oder bewusst ignorieren, birgt sie noch Gefahren. Da die Angreifer:innen in der zweiten Ebene zusätzlich auf Prompt-Injection setzen, wird der KI-Assistent so manipuliert, dass er die E-Mail als legitim oder dringend einstuft und die Anhänge eigenständig öffnet.
Zwei Angriffsmethoden in einem
Laut Barracuda bedienen sich Angriffe auf KI-Agenten häufig vier verschiedener Methoden. Erstens verstecken Angreifer:innen Anweisungen in Kommentar-Tags, die kein E-Mail-Client darstellt, die eine KI aber im Rohquellcode ausliest. Zweitens blenden sie Text per Null-Pixel-Schriftgröße oder weißer Farbe aus, den das Modell trotzdem mitliest. Drittens verstecken sie Anweisungen in codierten Blöcken, wie etwa einer Bilddatenzeichenfolge, die eine Pipeline dekodieren kann. Eine weitere Methode ist, unsichtbare Unicode-Zeichen über normalen Text zu schichten, um betrügerische Inhalte einzuschleusen.
In einem Beispiel enthält ein versteckter Textblock in einer Rechnungs-E-Mail eine Anweisung an das KI-Modell, eine gefälschte Prioritätsaktion hinzuzufügen. Dadurch ändern sich die Zahlungsdetails – und das Geld wird an ein betrügerisches Konto überwiesen. „Der gefährlichste Aspekt dieser aufkommenden Bedrohung ist, wie gewöhnlich sie aussieht“, heißt es im Bericht. „Eine einzelne E-Mail kann jetzt zwei separate Angriffe durchführen: einen, der darauf abzielt, eine:n Empfänger:in dazu zu bringen, einen bösartigen Anhang zu öffnen, und einen anderen, der darauf abzielt, die KI-Systeme zu manipulieren, denen das Verarbeiten von E-Mails anvertraut wird.“ Am wichtigsten sei es deshalb, externe Inhalte als Daten zu behandeln und von Anweisungen zu trennen.

articles.title: OPINION: Europe needs more than just successful exits | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The acquisition of Berlin-based Talon.One by Dutch payments provider Adyen in July 2026 offers a useful perspective on European technology investing. A company founded in Germany developed technology valuable to a global payments business, and its next chapter is being written within Europe. This is a significant outcome for the founders and investors. However, it also raises a larger question: how can Europe turn individual successes into an ecosystem capable of producing them repeatedly?
The answer is not simply to encourage more European acquisitions. Successful startups need access to the best opportunities available, whether their future lies with a European buyer, an international technology group or the public markets. What matters is that these decisions reflect commercial potential rather than a lack of viable alternatives. For Europe, the challenge is to create the conditions in which successful companies can scale, attract investment and generate lasting economic value.
Exits are a measure of maturity, not the final destination
From a venture capital perspective, exits matter because they return capital to investors and founders, establish reference points for valuations, and help to finance the next generation of start-ups. Therefore, an acquisition is more than just the end of an investment cycle. The wider impact of an acquisition depends on whether experienced founders start again, whether employees launch new businesses, whether investors reinvest, and whether specialist knowledge remains accessible to the local ecosystem.
The Talon.One transaction is particularly interesting in this respect. Adyen paid €750 million for the loyalty and incentives platform, combining complementary European technologies together in a business with international reach. The company’s founders also reinvested some of their proceeds in Adyen shares. This is one possible model for maintaining continuity, although the long-term consequences for jobs, innovation and further investment will only become apparent over time.
Yet a European buyer does not automatically guarantee a better outcome. An acquisition by a US technology group can also give European innovation access to new markets, capital and expertise. The relevant questions concern what happens after the transaction: where future investment takes place, whether technological capabilities continue to develop and how much value flows back into the startup ecosystem. While the identity of the buyer is important, the industrial logic and long-term consequences also deserve equal attention.
Germany’s progress reveals the next challenge
Germany is a useful test case for Europe’s progress. According to the German Startup Monitor 2026, the country added ten unicorns in 2026, indicating that more companies are achieving significant valuations. Yet 62% of respondents considering a stock market listing favour the US. These figures measure different things, but together they capture a tension: Germany is producing ambitious technology companies while many founders still see stronger exit opportunities outside its domestic market.
This preference is not irrational. Founders and their investors have a responsibility to consider factors such as access to capital, market depth, suitable buyers, and prospects for future growth. US markets can offer genuine advantages. Rather than persuading companies to reject opportunities abroad, Europe needs to build more competitive options.
This is important long before a potential exit. Investors assess the availability of future funding and realistic exit routes when deciding whether to back a company. If these options appear limited, promising businesses may struggle to attract the necessary capital to reach their full potential. Therefore, a stronger exit environment can support investment across the entire startup lifecycle.
What a stronger European exit market would require
Three priorities stand out:
- Deeper growth capital: European startups need access to substantial later-stage funding and patient institutional investors, without having to reshape their strategy around capital availability elsewhere. This would also give founders greater flexibility over when and how they pursue an exit.
- More strategic buyers: Acquisitions can provide distribution, customers and resources for expansion. Talon.One and Adyen illustrate the potential of cross-border European combinations. A broader base of established technology companies willing to acquire and develop innovative businesses would create additional exit opportunities.
- Earlier exit planning: Founders should consider which investors could fund the next round, which buyers could offer strategic value, and the potential impact of a transaction on teams, research and future ventures. Investor nationality alone is no substitute for that assessment.
The objective is choice
Europe’s ambition should not be to keep every company, every shareholder or every exit within its borders. International capital and global customers are essential for building competitive businesses. In my experience, a European startup acquired by a US company can still create substantial value for its founders, employees and investors, and a European acquisition can likewise bolster a regional technology group.
The more meaningful test is whether European founders have real alternatives, such as sufficient capital to scale up, credible paths to public markets and a strong base of strategic acquirers and investors who can recycle returns into new ventures.
Successful exits show what European technology can achieve. A mature ecosystem makes those successes less exceptional. This requires a joint effort by founders, investors, established companies and policymakers alike.
Editor’s note: IRIS was an investor in Talon.One.

articles.title: DeepSeek open-sources the inference engine behind its API. And Huawei gets equal billing with Nvidia.
articles.text:
DeepSeek open-sources the inference engine behind its API. And Huawei gets equal billing with Nvidia.
DeepSeek has open-sourced the inference engine it uses to serve its models in production, a step it said last year wasn’t yet practical.
Dubbed DeepInfer, the framework is designed to let developers run DeepSeek’s V4.1 Flash model on their own infrastructure, with many of the same optimizations the company uses behind its API. Support for future DeepSeek models is also planned.
“Running a model efficiently is a different matter altogether.”
DeepSeek has, of course, long made its model weights available for developers to download and run using third-party software such as vLLM. But running a model efficiently is a different matter altogether. The software that manages requests, distributes work across chips, and generates responses can have a significant impact on speed, throughput and computing costs. And so DeepInfer essentially gives developers access to DeepSeek’s own approach to those challenges.
“We’re sharing our production stack to help the community lower compute costs, reduce energy use, and make AI more affordable.”
‘Making AI more affordable’
Taking to X on Tuesday, DeepSeek said it was making its internal inference technology available to outside developers in an effort to bring down the expense of running large AI models.
“We’re sharing our production stack to help the community lower compute costs, reduce energy use, and make AI more affordable,” the company writes.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license, DeepInfer includes optimized computing kernels and communication libraries, including DeepSeek’s previously open-sourced FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, and DeepEP, alongside mechanisms for distributing inference across multiple chips. It also supports speculative decoding, a technique that speeds up response generation by predicting and verifying multiple tokens at once, and asynchronous scheduling to reduce the time processors spend waiting for new work. The framework also supports structured outputs, allowing developers to specify how model responses should be formatted.
Alongside DeepInfer, the company is also open-sourcing deepseek-recipe, a companion library that handles how API requests are converted into model inputs, and how the resulting output is processed into responses. Available for Rust and Python, it’s designed to help developers reproduce the behavior of DeepSeek’s official API when running their own deployments. The library was quietly released in September, with an updated version published on Tuesday.
The announcement comes just days after DeepSeek released an updated version of V4.1 Flash, called DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, touting improvements in coding performance and efficiency. That release coincided with the company making its in-house web search technology available to developers through new Search and Fetch APIs, as per The New Stack‘s report on Monday.
Why DeepSeek held back in 2025
DeepInfer goes further than DeepSeek’s previous plans to share its inference technology. Back in April 2025, the company published a document outlining its plans for its inference engine, explaining that it had considered releasing the entire system before deciding to contribute individual components and improvements to existing projects instead.
At the time, DeepSeek identified several obstacles. Its inference software had evolved from an early version of vLLM into a highly customized system, and the company questioned whether its relatively small research team could maintain another major open-source project. There were also practical difficulties in making the software usable outside DeepSeek’s own infrastructure.
“The engine is tightly coupled with our internal infrastructure, including cluster management tools, making it impractical for public deployment without significant modifications,” the company wrote at the time.
So what’s changed now, exactly? Well, DeepSeek hasn’t explained how it overcame those earlier difficulties, although the scope of the new release offers some clues. The DeepInfer documentation makes clear that the publicly available software currently supports offline inference, with “the core features needed for serving at scale,” as the company puts it. However, several components needed to operate a complete production service are still missing. These include a KV cache management system, infrastructure for separating different stages of inference across machines, and load balancing across replicas.
In other words, DeepSeek has opened up much of the engine responsible for running its models, while leaving developers to supply some of the surrounding infrastructure required to operate a full-fledged service. That narrower release may help explain how the company has made its technology available despite the challenges it identified last year.
Nvidia and Huawei, side by side
While the release of DeepSeek’s inference engine is significant enough in its own right, arguably the more interesting tidbit is the hardware supported from day one.
“Arguably the more interesting tidbit is the hardware supported from day one.”
Nvidia is included, as expected, though support is restricted to its SM100 architecture, used in Blackwell data center GPUs. Notably, the other supported platform is Huawei’s Ascend 950 NPU series, putting the Chinese chipmaker alongside Nvidia in DeepSeek’s list of compatible hardware. Older Nvidia architectures, including Hopper, are conspicuously absent.
This also ties back to DeepSeek’s published open-source plans from 2025. While the company was reluctant to release its entire inference engine at the time, it committed to working with hardware manufacturers ahead of future model launches, with the aim of making its models available across different chip architectures from day one.
US export restrictions have complicated Chinese companies’ access to Nvidia’s most advanced chips, adding another dimension to DeepSeek’s growing ties with Huawei. In September, Bloomberg reported that DeepSeek was planning to deploy at least 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT chips at a new data center in Inner Mongolia, specifically to run its models. The company has largely relied on Nvidia for training, although The Information reported in September that DeepSeek also plans to increase its use of Huawei chips for training, with deliveries expected as early as the fourth quarter.
Later that month, Reuters reported that DeepSeek and Huawei were collaborating on software tools intended to make Ascend processors easier to program, further underlining the company’s investment in Chinese AI hardware.
The Huawei inclusion has already attracted attention among the wider developer community. In a discussion on Reddit, one commenter singled out the two supported hardware platforms as a highlight of the news, while another pointed to DeepSeek’s origins in quantitative finance as a possible explanation for its technical expertise.
“Once again Deepseek shows how good high-frequency traders are at optimizing performance… On Ascend NPUs nonetheless!!,” the commenter wrote.
Another user seemingly poked fun at Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, following reports that requests involving kernel programming for Huawei’s AI chips could trigger safeguards that redirect certain advanced AI development tasks to an older model.
“Don’t let Opus 5.5 see this! It will delete the Ascend support,” the user joked.
It is worth noting that feature support differs between the Nvidia and Huawei implementations. DeepInfer’s batch-invariant inference and deterministic sampling features, which help ensure reproducible outputs under specified conditions, are available only on Nvidia hardware. DeepSeek’s published performance measurements also use Nvidia GPUs, with four SM100 GPUs used for prefill and 64 for decoding, leaving open the question of how the framework performs on Huawei’s chips by comparison.
For developers without access to either chip family, the immediate value may lie in studying the newly available code and adapting its optimizations to other inference engines. For now, DeepSeek has given the wider open-source community considerably more of its inference technology to experiment with.

articles.title: Ver gratis Barcelona vs PSG en Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa aumenta el robo de contraseñas y malware
articles.text:
Buscar partidos gratis de la UEFA Champions League como Barcelona vs PSG en Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa puede exponer contraseñas, datos personales y dispositivos a malware.
Según las advertencias del Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (Incibe), el riesgo no se limita a la calidad de la transmisión ni a la publicidad invasiva. Algunas páginas inducen a instalar archivos fuera de las tiendas oficiales o a conceder permisos que no guardan relación con la reproducción de un partido.
De qué manera una app pirata puede robar las contraseñas
Una aplicación maliciosa puede incorporar un keylogger, una herramienta que registra las pulsaciones realizadas en la pantalla o el teclado. Con ese mecanismo, extraños podrían capturar usuarios, contraseñas, números de tarjetas y otros datos que se introduzcan desde el teléfono.
El robo de credenciales no siempre requiere un correo falso o una web que imite a un banco. Si el programa tiene permisos excesivos o capacidad para supervisar la actividad del dispositivo, puede recolectar información mientras el usuario inicia sesión en redes sociales, servicios de correo o plataformas financieras.
Pese a que los códigos de verificación por mensaje de texto añaden una capa de seguridad en operaciones bancarias y accesos a cuentas, una aplicación con permiso para leer SMS puede visualizar esos códigos y permitir que un extraño confirme transacciones o modifique credenciales.
Por esta razón, antes de instalar una aplicación, conviene revisar cada permiso solicitado. Una herramienta para ver una transmisión no debería requerir acceso a contactos, cámara, ubicación, mensajes o llamadas.
Cómo puede un malware bloquear fotos y archivos personales y financieros
Una de las amenazas es el ransomware, un programa que cifra o bloquea archivos del dispositivo. La víctima puede descubrir que no tiene acceso a fotos, documentos o videos y recibir un mensaje que exige un pago a cambio de una supuesta recuperación.
El pago no garantiza que los archivos vuelvan a estar disponibles. Por ese motivo, Incibe sugiere realizar copias de seguridad periódicas en un servicio de almacenamiento en la nube o en una unidad externa. Esa medida permite conservar una alternativa ante una infección, un robo o una falla del dispositivo.
Qué pasa cuando una página pide instalar una app para ver el partido sin costo
Las plataformas streaming no autorizadas pueden mostrar mensajes que prometen habilitar el video mediante una aplicación, una extensión o un archivo de instalación. Ese contenido puede ocultar un programa malicioso capaz de alterar el funcionamiento del teléfono, la tableta o la computadora.
Incibe advierte que muchas aplicaciones de este tipo circulan a través de repositorios no oficiales, enlaces directos y sitios con descargas de contenido gratuito. A diferencia de Google Play y App Store, esas vías no cuentan con los mismos controles previos para detectar comportamientos fraudulentos o software dañino.
Por qué aparecen muchos anuncios y el celular se vuelve más lento
La aparición de publicidad constante, redirecciones a páginas desconocidas y un funcionamiento más lento pueden ser indicios de una aplicación intrusiva. Algunos programas aprovechan el dispositivo para mostrar anuncios, aumentar visitas a sitios externos o recopilar datos sobre la actividad del usuario.
El problema puede comenzar con una ventana que simula un reproductor, un botón de “ver ahora” o una alerta que pide actualizar una aplicación. Los enlaces sospechosos y las descargas directas deben evitarse, en especial cuando proceden de una web que ofrece gratuitamente una transmisión que requiere derechos de emisión.
Qué pautas ayudan a reducir riesgos
La medida principal es descargar aplicaciones únicamente desde las tiendas oficiales y comprobar quién es el desarrollador. Al mismo tiempo, se debe leer valoraciones, revisar comentarios de usuarios y desconfiar de nombres, logos o descripciones que intenten imitar a servicios conocidos.
Asimismo, mantener actualizado el sistema operativo, las aplicaciones y la solución de seguridad reduce la exposición a vulnerabilidades ya identificadas. Un antivirus actualizado puede detectar archivos dañinos, aunque no sustituye la precaución frente a enlaces y descargas.

articles.title: Windows Server 2025 gets support for quick machine recovery
articles.text:
Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update.
Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems.
When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows 11 fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates.
"With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update.
"Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations."
On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation.
For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor. In domain configurations, they can use Group Policy Management on a Windows Server or an administration computer, but they also need permissions to edit the GPO and link it to the intended organizational unit (OU).
To disable QMR through Group Policy, admins have to explicitly turn off 'Enable Cloud Remediation' to prevent cloud-sourced remediation and disable 'Enable Auto Remediation' to block automatic application of local remediation packages.
This can be done by going through the following steps:
- Open the local policy or domain GPO that manages the target Windows Server 2025 computers.
- Go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery.
- Open Enable Cloud Remediation, select Disabled, and select Apply, then OK.
- Open Enable Auto Remediation, select Disabled, and select Apply, then OK.
- (Optional) Verify the effective configuration.
Microsoft introduced quick machine recovery in November 2024 as part of its Windows Resiliency Initiative at Ignite 2024, in response to a July 2024 outage caused by a buggy CrowdStrike Falcon update that rendered millions of Windows devices unbootable.
It began testing in late March 2025, rolling it out to Windows Insiders in the Beta Channel. In November, it also began testing a faster version that now runs a single scan to fix systems with boot problems, rather than looping through solutions.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Bloqué par un sabot, ce SUV BYD lève sa roue de 30 centimètres et s'en va — Frandroid
articles.text:
Sur une vidéo publiée sur Douyin, le TikTok chinois, un gros SUV de BYD remonte une rue commerçante à deux voies avec la roue avant gauche en l’air. Sur cette roue est toujours fixé un sabot jaune et rouge, ce bloc de métal censé empêcher une voiture de bouger. La scène a été filmée ilmée à Jinshan, dans la ville de Lianyungang. Le conducteur aurait simplement soulevé la roue bloquée pour repartir sur les trois autres.
La vidéo a ensuite tourné sur les réseaux sociaux chinois pendant tout le week-end des 17 et 18 octobre. Le SUV en question est un Bao 8, de Fang Cheng Bao (FCB), la marque tout-terrain de BYD, un constructeur qu’on croise désormais aussi en France avec ses modèles électriques. Hors de Chine, ce même engin de 5,2 mètres de long se vend sous le nom de Denza B8.
La version Flash Charge, celle qui reçoit cette suspension, est vendue en Chine depuis le 13 mai 2026 à partir de 419 800 yuans, soit environ 56 000 euros. C’est un hybride rechargeable, avec un moteur essence 2.0 turbo de 272 ch épaulé par deux moteurs électriques, pour 550 kW au total (environ 750 ch). Sa batterie de 46,7 kWh et son réservoir lui donnent une autonomie combinée annoncée d’environ 1 380 km, presque un Paris-Marseille aller-retour.
Une suspension conçue pour sortir du sable
Tout repose sur le DiSus-P Ultra, la suspension hydraulique pilotée que BYD a lancée en mai sur ce modèle. Elle gère chaque roue séparément en jouant sur la pression d’huile. Ce qui veut dire, concrètement, qu’elle peut lever un coin de la voiture sans bouger les trois autres.
BYD annonce jusqu’à 30 centimètres de levée pour une seule roue (presque deux marches d’escalier) et 20 centimètres de réglage de hauteur pour la suspension. Le système peut soulever jusqu’à 9 tonnes, l’équivalent de six citadines d’une tonne et demie.
Lors de sa démonstration de mai sur un terrain d’essai tout-terrain, BYD a montré à quoi tout ça sert. Le SUV s’est sorti d’un piège de sable profond en jouant sur la hauteur de ses roues. Il a aussi changé une roue sans cric : le levage prend moins d’une minute selon la marque, et un changement de pneu complet a été bouclé en 1 minute et 56 secondes.
Le troisième usage est justement celui de la vidéo. Rouler sur trois roues doit servir à franchir un obstacle sans racler le châssis, ou à se dépanner en urgence. BYD limite d’ailleurs ce mode à 15 km/h.
Aito, la marque soutenue par Huawei, et Li Auto ont eux aussi montré au printemps des SUV capables de lever une roue, et les constructeurs chinois font de la suspension active un argument de vente. BYD, lui, aime les démonstrations spectaculaires, de la recharge en cinq minutes promise sur l’Atto 8 à sa conduite autonome lâchée place de l’Étoile.
