articles.title: NCC device verification questions Nigeria's phone imports
articles.text:
Nigeria’s telecom regulator launched a device verification tool that lets buyers check whether a phone is approved for use on local mobile networks. But enforcing compliance across an import-dependent market could test the agency’s technical reach.
With 99% of smartphones imported into Nigeria and an estimated 63 million mobile devices sold annually, the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) faces a market structured around multi-layered supply chains, informal distribution networks, and varied entry routes.
Launched on October 7, 2026, the NCC’s Device Checker requires consumers to dial *315# to verify whether a phone meets Type Approval requirements—the NCC’s mandatory regulation that all communication equipment must meet before connecting to local networks.
The regulator says the tool is part of a broader effort to enforce its Device Management System (DMS) under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003.
The checker uses a phone’s International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique 15-digit identifier, to verify its status against the NCC’s approved equipment records. By linking device records to import declarations, the regulator says it can investigate whether a phone was properly declared to the Nigeria Customs Service and trace the business responsible for importing it.
However, the stakes are substantial in a market that imports an estimated ₦50 billion ($30 million) worth of mobile devices every month. Its near-total reliance on imports creates a complex supply chain that could hamper enforcement.
As a result, a consumer whose phone gets flagged risks navigating an informal multi-tier supply chain with no clear recourse, no standard refund procedure, and no guarantee of compensation.
How device verification works across categories
Consumers can check a mobile device’s status by dialling *315#. Selecting “Check this device” on the menu displays whether the handset is NCC Type Approved and verified for use. Alternatively, buyers can retrieve the 15-digit IMEI code by dialling *#06# and entering it on the NCC’s online portal.
These verification methods enable buyers to detect non-compliant devices before completing a transaction rather than discovering issues after payment.
For personally imported devices, the workflow differs. Individuals bringing phones into the country for use with local SIM cards must contact the NCC via its 315 helpline for guidance on individual verification.
Foreign visitors roaming on international SIM cards do not need to register their devices. Devices connected to a local network before October 7 are automatically allowed. However, new, unverified handsets imported by visitors are subject to a cumulative 30-day grace period per year before registration becomes mandatory.
Commercial entities importing SIM-enabled hardware—including smartphones, tablets, connected laptops, smart meters, and point-of-sale (POS) terminals—must verify compliance with type approval before distribution.
Regulatory responsibility lies upstream: original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), commercial importers, and primary distributors are legally required to obtain Type Approval before offering hardware for sale.
The distinction between consumer verification and enterprise registration is critical: consumers verify network eligibility, whereas supply-chain entities bear the burden of regulatory compliance.
Through the DMS portal, the regulator states it can track SIM-enabled devices back to primary importers, log total import volume, and initiate sanctions against non-compliant entities.
However, backend traceability does not guarantee immediate redress for consumers when an unapproved device is flagged post-purchase.
Enforcement challenges in a fragmented market
Sellers in Abuja’s GSM Village support the regulator’s initiative, yet there are concerns that structural complexities within Nigeria’s device distribution networks could impede implementation. Elsewhere at Banex Plaza in Abuja, TechCabal‘s findings from sellers were not different.
Nigeria records an estimated 63 million mobile device sales annually. Trade data from Volza shows mobile phone imports totalled 4,886 shipments between July 2024 and June 2025, involving 11 international exporters and 12 registered major buyers in Nigeria.
While import metrics do not quantify grey-market volume, the NCC’s enforcement partnership with the Nigeria Customs Service highlights lingering vulnerabilities around grey-market imports and border smuggling.
In 2024, the Nigeria Customs Service reported 3,555 contraband seizures. Although specific device counts were omitted, persistent illicit inflows indicate that unapproved hardware continues to enter retail channels, creating post-purchase compliance risks for consumers.
Regularising upstream accountability
The NCC states that approximately 231 million active devices registered before October 7, 2026, have been automatically onboarded into the DMS database without requiring subscriber intervention. However, the commission did not disclose the number of devices flagged or pending clearance.
Merchants holding inventory imported before that date can regularise their stock by registering their business documentation and uploading batch IMEI records to the NCC enterprise portal. Support is available via the 315 desk.
This transition window aims to protect compliant trade vendors from regulatory penalties on legacy stock.
Traders contend that regulatory enforcement must target primary importers rather than downstream micro-retailers who lack the technical means to evaluate upstream Type Approval status.
Secondary retailers rarely receive customs documentation or Type Approval certificates from distributors. While this does not absolve vendors knowingly trading in illicit goods, it creates operational friction when stock is acquired in good faith.
The NCC’s digital ledger could help trace undeclared devices to sellers and suppliers. But as Ogoh suggests, having “empirical data” is only the first step; turning that evidence into accountability and consumer refunds remains the bigger test.
The commission indicates that these audit trails help regulators distinguish between deliberate contraband trading and inadvertent distribution by secondary vendors.
However, audit trails alone do not determine financial liability or resolve refund disputes once non-compliant hardware has passed through multiple intermediaries to reach end users.
Enforcement and consumer protection
Consumer protection underpins the rationale for the Device Checker. Yet the tool’s impact will depend on whether enforcement mechanisms can penetrate multi-tiered supply chains to guarantee consumer indemnification.
Although the regulator maintains that automated verification prevents erroneous network blocking, dispute resolution remains complex. Nigeria’s Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018 grants rights to repair, replacement, or refund for non-compliant goods, but practical enforcement across informal markets remains difficult.
The Device Checker’s ultimate success hinges on converting technical detection into actionable consumer safeguards. Identifying unverified IMEIs offers little relief to buyers left holding deactivated hardware without a clear, enforced refund path in informal trade hubs.
To scale sustainably, the NCC must strengthen inter-agency coordination with the Nigeria Customs Service to stop unapproved hardware at entry ports rather than at retail points of sale. Without stringent primary-importer enforcement and structured consumer indemnities, digital verification risks transferring systemic supply-chain failures onto consumers.

articles.title: Google suspende una inversión de miles de millones en centros de datos en España a la espera del decreto del Gobierno
articles.text:
En el mapa europeo de centros de datos de Google, el norte, con Finlandia al frente como "la Texas de Europa", está lleno de chinchetas. Sin embargo, el sur de Europa sigue casi en blanco. España parecía la candidata ideal para rellenar ese hueco pero algunos proyectos se están poniendo en pausa ante la incertidumbre regulatoria de un Gobierno que ha anunciado medidas más estrictas en un próximo Real Decreto.
Hasta que se conozcan los detalles de la nueva normativa española, Google ha suspendido su apuesta por un gran campus tecnológico en España, según adelantaba El Mundo.
El nodo Sol en pausa. La incertidumbre regulatoria ha hecho que Google y otras empresas tecnológicas hayan puesto en pausa sus proyectos en España a la espera del contenido del próximo Real Decreto que prepara el Gobierno para regular las condiciones ambientales y de sostenibilidad energéticas de los centros de datos.
De acuerdo a lo publicado por El Mundo, Google habría pausado sus proyectos de ampliación de su capacidad de cómputo en España y su correspondiente inversión de miles de millones de dólares. Google ya contaba con un centro de datos en Madrid con servidores alojados en centros de terceros, pero el proyecto más afectado es el que contemplaba la construcción de la estación para el cable submarino Sol que unirá Santander con Florida en una parcela de casi 6.000 m2 en Cantabria. Amazon, por su parte, tiene comprometidos 33.700 millones en Aragón hasta 2035.
Hambre de capacidad de cómputo. Alphabet ha elevado su previsión de gasto para este año hasta una horquilla de 195.000 a 205.000 millones de dólares. Además, admite que la demanda de IA supera su actual capacidad de cómputo.
Mientras tanto, otros países se postulan como competencia para llevarse esos proyectos que ya estaban sobre la mesa. En septiembre, la compañía anunció la inversión de 13.000 millones de euros en Finlandia, la mayor inversión de su historia en Europa. Allí también se aseguró el suministro de energía incluyendo una central nuclear.
Unas reglas más estrictas con la sostenibilidad. El borrador del Gobierno obliga a los centros de datos a cubrir el 80% de su consumo con nuevas fuentes de energía renovable. Y ese porcentaje debe cumplirse hora a hora, no como media anual. La patronal SpainDC, de la que Google es asociada, avisa de que algunos proyectos serían mucho más caros o inviables.
UN VISTAZO A...
El Ejecutivo quiere evitar que la factura de la luz se dispare. Los números le dan argumentos. La CNMC cifra en unos 12 GW los permisos de acceso ya concedidos. La Estrategia de IA preveía como máximo 4 GW para 2030.
Lobby en Madrid. Google no se ha quedado quieta y, junto a otras tecnológicas ha enviado a sus mejores negociadores a Europa. Tal y como publicaba El Confidencial, Kent Walker, jefe global de asuntos públicos de Google, se reunió el 8 de octubre con el presidente de la CNMC. El regulador asegura que hablaron de competencia y no del decreto.
Poco después se conoció el informe de la CNMC, que pide flexibilizar varias exigencias del borrador del Real Decreto. Con el texto actual, peligra entre el 80% y el 90% de la nueva inversión. Begoña Villacís, directora ejecutiva de Spain DC se muestra contundente con estas nuevas medidas: "Se construirá en otro lugar y será allí desde donde presten los servicios digitales a empresas y ciudadanos españoles".
Gobierno a contrarreloj. El Gobierno quiere aprobar el decreto antes de las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, pero no lo tiene fácil. Hay más de 600 alegaciones sobre la mesa y el texto aún debe superar el examen del Consejo de Estado. Eso deja margen para aplicar cambios.
Según adelantó El País, responsables del Ejecutivo se abrieron a suavizar algunas exigencias incluidas en el borrador del Real Decreto si los centros de datos no contribuyen a encarecen el precio de la luz. Google, de momento, espera con la cartera guardada.

Le kit EZVIZ CB3 associe une caméra extérieure 2K sur batterie à un panneau solaire, avec détection des personnes et des véhicules et mode d’enregistrement AOV.
Amazon propose le kit caméra EZVIZ CB3 2K avec panneau solaire à 64,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 79,99 €. L’économie atteint 15 €, soit environ 19 %. Une caméra sur batterie accompagnée d’un panneau solaire
La caméra de surveillance EZVIZ CB3 filme en 2K et communique en Wi-Fi avec le réseau domestique. Sa batterie évite de tirer une alimentation électrique jusqu’à son emplacement. Le panneau solaire fourni se raccorde à la caméra pour contribuer à sa recharge : son efficacité dépend de l’exposition et des conditions d’ensoleillement.

Un mode AOV pour suivre aussi les périodes sans événement

articles.title: This 3D-printed 1980s brick phone brings back the days when mobile phones were just for making calls
articles.text:
In a nutshell: A lot of people cite the 1990s Nokia 3210 as the old-school brick-like mobile phone. But for something that fits the description a lot closer, go back another decade to the 1980's and the first handheld mobile phones: brick phones. Now, a designer has 3D-printed one of these devices, retaining the originals' primary function of making and receiving calls – so there are no modern smartphone distractions.
Cologne-based designer and maker Kevin Noki created the ADHD ONE, the first part of the name being an acronym for Anti Distraction Handset Device.
The device resembles a snazzy update of 1980s brick phones sported by the likes of Wall Street's Gordon Gekko, such as the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X. There's the physical 19-key keypad, small display, and a concerning large antenna.
The phone has a much more modern set of internals. It's powered by a Raspberry Pi Pico and features an FSC-BT1026C Bluetooth module based on Qualcomm's QCC3024 chip. There's also a rechargeable lithium battery, charging controller, and custom-printed circuit board.
Unlike the 1980s originals, the ADHD ONE doesn't have its own cellular connectivity. Instead, it relies on a Bluetooth connection to an iPhone to make and receive calls, so it's not like you can completely replace your distraction-filled smartphone with one of these, but you can at least keep it hidden in a drawer.
Noki designed the phone's enclosure using Autodesk Fusion before 3D-printing the components. He's made the files available on his website for €29.99 ($33.68). The package includes 3D-printable STL files for the main housing, back panels, internal mounting frame, display cover, battery holder, and all 19 keypad buttons.
There are also three speaker grille designs (Classic, Holes, and Stripes), three antenna options (Retro, Slim, and Screw), and an alternative housing without an antenna hole. Other included files cover ready-to-flash firmware in UF2 format, Gerber and drill files for manufacturing the custom PCB, a bill of materials with component sourcing notes, and a quick-start guide to assembling the device.
The package doesn't include the firmware's source code, editable 3D/CAD files, or editable PCB design files. It's also a digital download, so no physical components are supplied. Buyers receive a ZIP file of approximately 20MB immediately after payment. The files are licensed for personal use only, meaning they cannot be redistributed or resold.
Several devices have been released in recent years promising a break from the distractions – such as depression-inducing social media apps – found on smartphones. There were the $299 Light Flip and Light Phone III, the Minimal Phone, and Commodore's Callback 8020, to name a few.

articles.title: Polestar tries to quantify what it’s like to drive a performance car
articles.text:
The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.”
A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the chariot—and humanity was ready to roll. Now, about five millennia since that first horseback ride, equestrianism is mostly a leisure activity, and we drive cars, propelled by motors with more power than an entire herd of beasts could muster.
Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. But measuring a car’s performance is easy—all you need is a stopwatch and a track. How about measuring the effect of car performance on the driver? That’s a question Polestar is trying to answer with researchers at the University of Oxford.
“As electric cars redefine what performance can be, we wanted to understand something that can’t be captured by a specification sheet alone: the human experience behind the wheel,” said Christian Samson, Polestar’s head of product attributes. “Working with University of Oxford allows us to look at performance through a different lens—connecting the engineering of the car with the experience of the person driving it.”
The pilot study involved 12 drivers who track-tested both rear- and all-wheel-drive versions of the Polestar 4 at a track in Sweden. The Polestar 4 is the OEM’s midsize crossover, a compelling Porsche Macan alternative that you can sadly no longer buy here in the US. The drivers were instrumented with heart rate monitors and skullcaps studded with electrodes, plus the cars’ gaze-tracking driver monitoring system to gather physiological data, which was combined with telemetry from the cars and subjective interview assessments after the fact. While being measured, drivers lapped the Gotland Ring circuit gently, then dynamically.

articles.title: The Key to AI Software Security Isn’t Speed, It’s Maturity
articles.text:
Agentic artificial intelligence software development has all the traits of a summer blockbuster, with the prospects of Godzilla-sized productivity gains thrilling business leaders and security implications sending chills down the spines of developers and SOC teams. One difference, though, is that those thrills and chills are going to last longer than a summer, and the fallout could be a lot more serious than some spilled popcorn.
The proliferation of large language models, whether for software development or general use, alongside both sanctioned tools and shadow AI brought in by employees, is expanding the attack surface too quickly for traditional controls to keep up, particularly with the growing use of agentic AI. And the increased risks are coming home to roost, with Gartner predicting that the costs of incidents driven by agentic AI will increase fourfold through 2027.
The impact of agentic AI is a particularly sharp double-edged sword, with SonarSource noting that the frontier LLMs such as Claude and Gemini that write the best, most functional code also produce the most severe security vulnerabilities.
Organizations are aware of the need to gain control over agentic AI’s risk factors, but the protections implemented so far may well be insufficient. Governance is the go-to concept for reigning in AI-driven software development, and with good reason. It’s critical for maintaining control over what AI agents can and can’t do. Along with the improved observability of AI tool use and commits, this can help organizations limit the risk levels of AI while reaping the rewards of improved productivity.
But governance and Governance only go so far when organizations are in other critical ways still working in the dark regarding security controls. Specifically, they may not know where they are on the ascending scale of AI adoption and as a result may not understand what they need at their current stage. Without a clear understanding of the capabilities of their current AI projects, the risks involved and the level of developer skills required to manage AI, they can fall far short in implementing security best practices. They need a governance plan that fully addresses the new reality of software development.
Know the Different Stages of AI Adoption and Maturity
Organizations can navigate the AI implementation puzzle without losing control of risk management, with the context provided by a three-phase, eight-stage AI Adoption Model that mirrors the steps you’ll take along the AI path, from relatively bare-bones AI assistants performing routine tasks to AI agents capable of initiating and finishing tasks completely on their own.
The model is highly detailed in describing each stage, but to summarize it briefly, it consists of eight observable stages defining activity, risk levels and developer skill requirements across the three phases of AI implementation: AI Assisted, AI Native and Agentic.
Phase 1. AI Assisted
The first phase includes stages 1 (Minimal AI Use) and 2 (Supervised Assistance) and covers organizations in the foothills of AI implementation, using AI models that work directly for developers and present low to moderate risk levels. These early stages are an ideal time to establish governance policies. Developers, meanwhile, should receive upskilling on topics ranging from secure coding to code review, and these skills should be verifiable using a tool to establish baselines and track developer performance.
Phase 2: AI Native
Applying to stages 3 (Unsupervised Assistance) and 4 (AI-Primary Development), this is the phase where developers are allowing AI models to work more on their own without close supervision. Productivity can skyrocket with agents taking advantage of information-sharing standards such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), but risk levels run high. A major risk arises when developers trust AI too much, but tools are available to detect over-trust and track MCP activity. Stage 4 begins the transition from AI Native to Agentic. Developers have become code reviewers rather than authors, a significant shift that requires effective education and upskilling.
Phase 3: Agentic
This phase is what every organization is shooting for, but it comes with risk levels ranging from very high and critical to extreme and maximum. The stages steadily climb the ladder of both capability and risk. At Stage 5 (Single Agent), Command Line Interface (CLI) agents, such as Claude Code or Gemini CLI, perform operations from start to finish on their own. At Stage 6 (Multi-agent Parallel), AI can scale quickly as multiple agents work together. Stage 7 (Scaled Agent Management) takes it to the next level, with multiple agents operating at scale, and Stage 8 (Autonomous Orchestration) requires developers to coordinate agents as a unified team. Developer education should cover policy enforcement, the use of application risk scorecards, and the ability to track commits for audit purposes.
As the progression of these stages makes clear, establishing governance and a comprehensive learning program early on is essential because risk levels can quickly get out of hand as AI agents perform more complex, autonomous and unsupervised operations. Failing to establish a governance foundation early can come back to bite you in a big way.
Fortunately, most developers are somewhere between stages 2 through 4 right now, so it’s not too late for organizations to implement the guardrails, oversight and education programs necessary to manage the entirely new world of the Agentic Development Lifecycle (ADLC).
Where to Start, How to Proceed
As with many a new technology, adoption of AI is running well ahead of organizations’ abilities to secure it. The headlong rush into AI, compounded by unskilled employees bringing their own LLMs into the network without understanding how to manage security assessments or perform contextual reviews, has left organizations lacking visibility into who is using AI, how they are using it and the impact it has on production code. They may be flying fast with AI adoption but in many ways are also flying blind without the oversight, guardrails and developer-level observability they need to ensure that AI is being used safely.
Establishing effective AI governance can feel daunting. Organizations can reasonably ask, “Where do we start?” The answer is to understand where they are in the first place. It helps organizations identify the security controls and developer skill levels needed at their current stage of adoption, as well as what will be required at the next one.
No matter where an organization is in AI adoption, the next level of both capability and risk will arrive faster than expected.

articles.title: Families of Wes Hall, Patsy Anderson make $3-million donation to SickKids’ AI initiative | BetaKit
articles.text:
The self-proclaimed “King of Bay Street,” Wes Hall, and philanthropist Patsy Anderson are supporting the Hospital for Sick Children’s (SickKids) AI program.
The news: SickKids announced on Friday that Hall and Anderson joined forces to make a $3-million donation to the SickKids Artificial Intelligence (SKAI) program, which focuses on deploying “responsible AI” across clinical care, research, education, and operations, according to the hospital’s foundation.
The donation also establishes the SickKids Artificial Intelligence Innovator in Child Health award, with its inaugural recognition going to Dr. Devin Singh, the co-lead of SickKids’ SKAI Service.
From the source: In a statement, Hall said the donation “backs a visionary team helping to ensure Canadian innovation shapes the future of health care.”
“SickKids has world-class AI researchers and clinicians positioned to transform health care,” the Dragons’ Den star added. “We should be doing everything in our power to foster and keep their breakthrough undertakings here in Canada.”
The context: SickKids launched SKAI in March 2025 as a flagship initiative of the SickKids 2030 strategy. SKAI’s three major components include an in-house service to develop and support AI systems, a research arm with scientists using AI for medical discovery, and an AI literacy and knowledge-sharing component. Before Hall and Anderson’s donation, SKAI had received investments of $1 million or more from approximately a dozen backers.
In his own statement, Singh said the donation provides the SKAI team with a runway to develop and scale machine learning algorithms safely, from research validation to everyday clinical operations.
Final thought: This isn’t the only recent tech news tied to SickKids. On Tuesday, the pediatric hospital announced a five-year partnership with Microsoft Canada. The agreement will expand the use of Microsoft Azure as SickKids’ primary cloud platform, and include Azure credits so the hospital can, among other things, “build the AI capabilities needed to support the future of care.”
Feature image courtesy Wes Hall via Facebook.

articles.title: AuxoAI raises over $20M to bring AI expertise to the enterprise and redesign how work gets done - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AuxoAI raises over $20M to bring AI expertise to the enterprise and redesign how work gets done
AuxoAI Inc., an enterprise engineering and consulting company that helps large businesses build and deploy artificial intelligence systems, today announced it has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding to accelerate growth and scale its enterprise AI consulting model.
The company said it has spent over three years working with Global 2000 enterprises and strategic partners, bringing AI into the core of their operations. It focuses on combining business-process expertise, data engineering and AI agents – autonomous systems that use artificial intelligence to work with little or no human oversight, with deep insight into company data to complete long-term tasks.
AuxoAI builds AI solutions by sending on-site engineers and strategy teams to understand enterprise culture, data, workflow automation and customer engagement to tailor experiences to business and employee needs.
At the core of the company’s platform is Damia, which the company describes as an FDE Workbench, or “forward-deployed engineer” toolkit that also transforms data into applications and licenses for customers. It combines reusable agent capacities with tools for capturing a company’s business knowledge and processes.
The company said that over the years, it has learned how to work with customers to encode relevant knowledge and relationships and use that to create AI agents around the company’s processes. This preserves what the team learns in software and structured knowledge, rather than only interviews or paper documents, but in living software that can work alongside employees.
The company calls this effect “intelligence embedded in the work itself,” where consulting treats AI as a lever or tool for the customer rather than an end product.
AuxoAI partners with companies that businesses already know and trust, including Google LLC, Amazon Web Services Inc., Snowflake Inc., Databricks Inc. and Microsoft Corp., allowing the company to provide enterprise-ready AI, cloud, data and productivity via these platforms.
NTT Venture Capital, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm backed by Japanese technology conglomerate NTT Inc., led the funding round. The round also included participation from prominent industry executives and strategic investors, such as George Still Jr., partner emeritus at Norwest Venture Partners; Amit Zavery, president, chief product officer and chief operating officer at ServiceNow Inc.; and Giacomo Sonnino, managing director at Charlesbank Capital Partners and former chief operating officer of Quantum Black North America.
NTTVC’s portfolio includes Anthropic PBC, which will bring on another major artificial intelligence leader to extend AuxoAI’s capabilities.
The company said the new funding will serve to accelerate the next phase of its journey to expand its global reach. It aims to provide onsite consulting talent for enterprise AI transformation, invest in proprietary technology and AI-native delivery capabilities, and scale up its presence and strategic ecosystem.

articles.title: TSE cobra Meta por tratamento igual a Lula e Flávio; empresa nega favorecimento
articles.text:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ouviu representantes da Meta e das campanhas de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nesta terça-feira (20), para discutir o cumprimento de uma decisão que exige tratamento igualitário aos dois candidatos nas plataformas digitais. A empresa, responsável por Facebook, Instagram, Threads e WhatsApp, nega favorecer qualquer candidatura e afirma ter adotado medidas para cumprir as determinações da Justiça Eleitoral.
A reunião foi conduzida pelo ministro substituto Marco Aurélio Bellizze, após a Meta apresentar informações sobre as medidas adotadas e solicitar o encontro. A empresa havia sido intimada a prestar esclarecimentos em 24 horas sobre os mecanismos usados para distribuir conteúdos políticos e veicular anúncios eleitorais.
A decisão foi motivada por questionamentos sobre possíveis diferenças no alcance de publicações e no funcionamento de ferramentas de inteligência artificial (IA), incluindo os sistemas de recomendação de conteúdo.
A campanha de Lula alegou que publicações ligadas ao candidato enfrentavam restrições de alcance, enquanto conteúdos favoráveis a Flávio Bolsonaro teriam recebido tratamento mais vantajoso. A equipe petista também questionou a atuação da Meta AI na produção e distribuição de conteúdo eleitoral.
A Meta rejeitou as acusações e atribuiu os problemas relatados a questões técnicas. Durante a reunião, Bellizze afirmou que o objetivo da representação é garantir transparência e igualdade entre os candidatos.
O que o TSE determinou à Meta?
- Na sexta-feira (16), o plenário do TSE manteve, por unanimidade, a decisão que proíbe a Meta de interferir na distribuição de conteúdo político-eleitoral das duas candidaturas. A determinação vale até o fim do segundo turno, marcado para 25 de outubro;
- A ordem impede a empresa de reduzir a distribuição de publicações, excluí-las dos sistemas de recomendação, restringir buscas ou alterar métricas de conteúdos políticos e eleitorais de Lula e Flávio;
- Há exceções para políticas da própria plataforma que tenham sido divulgadas previamente e sejam aplicadas de forma idêntica aos dois candidatos, para a regra eleitoral que retira os perfis oficiais dos candidatos dos sistemas de recomendação e para o cumprimento de ordens judiciais;
- O ministro também estabeleceu que a Meta deve adotar critérios iguais para as duas candidaturas em sua ferramenta de IA, além de revisar determinadas restrições a contas de anúncios;
- Pela decisão, bloqueios automáticos de contas publicitárias das campanhas devem passar por revisão humana em até duas horas. A empresa também precisa impedir anúncios eleitorais pagos por pessoas ou entidades que não estejam autorizadas a contratá-los;
- Outra determinação envolve a apuração de 255 perfis apontados como possível rede inautêntica e a verificação da identificação de conteúdo produzido ou alterado por IA em 1.204 publicações;
- A Meta também foi obrigada a repor, até 21 de outubro, o impulsionamento de anúncios contratado pela campanha de Lula que não havia sido entregue.
Leia mais:
- Deepfakes podem dificultar análise de provas, alertam OpenAI e Meta
- Lula vai pedir cassação da chapa de Flávio Bolsonaro por atuação da Meta
- Comitê da Meta aponta falhas na moderação durante eleições no Brasil
Meta diz ter analisado mais de mil publicações com IA
Em manifestação apresentada ao TSE, a Meta afirmou que aplica as mesmas regras de distribuição de conteúdo a todos os candidatos e que adotou medidas para impedir abusos durante a disputa eleitoral.
Entre as providências informadas pela empresa está a análise de 1.204 publicações. Desse total, 720 foram suspensas por não identificarem o uso de IA ou de conteúdo sintético, conforme exigido pelas regras eleitorais.
A companhia também afirmou que criou lista de permissões para anúncios, restringindo a propaganda eleitoral paga a candidatos, partidos, coligações e federações devidamente cadastrados na Justiça Eleitoral.
A decisão do TSE prevê multa diária de R$ 500 mil pelo descumprimento das determinações. O valor pode subir para R$ 1 milhão por dia caso a empresa não comprove o cumprimento integral das medidas no prazo estabelecido.
O ministro, porém, não apontou comprovação de manipulação deliberada da distribuição de conteúdos pela Meta para favorecer ou prejudicar Lula ou Flávio. A medida tem caráter preventivo e busca impedir eventuais desigualdades na reta final da campanha.
Meta também se recusa a criar canal de apoio a jornalistas
Além da discussão eleitoral, a Meta foi alvo de questionamentos do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública por se recusar a criar um canal direto para atender casos urgentes envolvendo jornalistas, comunicadores e veículos de imprensa.
Segundo nota divulgada pelo ministério nesta terça-feira, o mecanismo permitiria encaminhar com mais rapidez situações de ameaças, assédio, ataques digitais, bloqueios e suspensões de contas.
A proposta foi formalizada pelo Observatório da Violência contra Jornalistas e Comunicadores Sociais, vinculado à pasta, após uma reunião com representantes da empresa no início de outubro.
Em resposta enviada em 16 de outubro, a Meta rejeitou a criação do canal. A empresa argumentou que o mecanismo poderia representar a assunção de novas obrigações regulatórias e alegou complexidade técnica, jurídica e operacional.
Segundo o ministério, a companhia também afirmou que suas políticas são aplicadas de forma igualitária aos usuários e que os canais gerais de atendimento existentes seriam suficientes. A pasta acrescentou que a Meta declarou não saber por que contas de jornalistas são removidas.
O governo defendeu a criação de mecanismos específicos e permanentes de proteção a profissionais e veículos de comunicação no ambiente digital, independentemente do período eleitoral.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself | TechCrunch
articles.text:
JustWatch, a company offering a search engine and guide for streaming movies and TV shows, is now moving directly into the streaming business itself. On Tuesday, the company behind the popular guide that’s used by 50 million people is launching JustWatch TV. The new streaming service will feature content from 30 partners and will offer both free and paid tiers, as well as a movie rental store.
The media and entertainment company behind the streaming guide, the JustWatch Group, initially announced its plans to venture into streaming last month. At the time, it said partners like Paramount, New Regency, Fremantle, Bleecker Street, and Vortex Media were on board. The company has since announced other content partners, including Cineverse in the U.S., LEONINE Studios in Germany, SND in France, and Altitude in the U.K.
The 12-year-old company has long been known for its online guide to movies and TV. Essentially, it’s a “TV Guide” for the streaming era, helping users navigate a landscape where movies and shows move from one service to another, making it harder to keep up with what’s streaming where.
Available in 140 markets globally, the guide provides streaming options for more than 500,000 movies and shows across more than 1,500 service providers worldwide. This “where to watch” information and streaming chart data are also used to power some 1,400 partner websites and apps and are valuable to studios, distributors, streamers, and agencies that use the data to target their campaigns across social media platforms like Meta, YouTube, TikTok, and others.
Now the company believes there’s an even bigger opportunity to grow its audience data and insights by running its own service.
“At a time where there is so much choice, yet with so many people constantly searching for a place to find their favourite film, the series they just heard about, or something exciting that fits them, it is a great moment to be a hub for all things entertainment,” said Quentin Carbonell, JustWatch SVP of Global Content Acquisitions and Strategy, in an email shared with TechCrunch. “By having our own service with titles to watch directly on JustWatch TV, we can grow our already massive audience, while continuing to direct them to all our streaming partners. This is a natural continuation of our mission to contribute to the entire ecosystem, from the big screen to the small one.”
The new streaming service will be available within JustWatch’s existing apps and website across 12 markets, including the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Ireland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Australia, and New Zealand.
Its free tier will offer a selection of ad-supported titles, while the ad-free version, JustWatch TV Plus, will offer more than 300 ad-free titles in the U.S., as well as other exclusive features, like advanced filters and the option to hide previously seen or disliked titles in the guide.
A movie rental store will also initially be available in the U.S., U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand, with more markets to follow in time.
While the ad-supported tier competes with free streamers like Tubi and Plex, the Plus tier will compete with low-cost streamers like Roku’s $2.99 per month ad-free service, Howdy. It will be similarly priced at $3.99 per month or $49.99 for a lifetime subscription. (The latter is an interesting way to price streaming, given the evolving content costs, but JustWatch believes there will be additional value in the data collected.) Paid subscribers will also be able to take 10% off on hundreds of rentals in the JustWatch TV Store, the company noted.
Like most low-cost services, JustWatch’s content lineup focuses on older movies and shows, as well as more indie content.
Another unique feature is that users will be able to influence the service’s content to some extent. JustWatch says users will be able to request titles they want to see to help shape what comes to the service.

articles.title: A reason to eat carbs
articles.text:
A reason to eat carbs
MIT researchers have found that a ketogenic diet may fuel the growth of some intestinal tumors.
A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet can help some people lose weight, and some research has shown that it may protect against colon cancer. But a new study suggests that such a ketogenic diet may also increase the risk of cancer in the small intestine.
This type of diet forces the body to burn fatty acids instead of carbohydrates for fuel, producing by-products called ketone bodies. One of these, BHB, was thought to be responsible for the protective effect observed against colon cancer.
Omer Yilmaz, director of the MIT Stem Cell Initiative, worked with colleagues including MIT postdocs Jessica Shay and Fangtao Chi to investigate whether the effects were similar in the small intestine. But instead, they found that mice on a ketogenic diet were more likely to develop tumors in that part of the gastrointestinal system than those on a control diet were.
Additional studies revealed that this tumor growth was driven by the way intestinal cells burn dietary fat for energy—a metabolic pathway called fatty acid oxidation. This pathway activates proteins that signal stem cells to multiply more rapidly.
“Having more stem cells means that when you injure the small intestine, it can repair itself better, but the downside is that having more active stem cells can lead to tumor formation,” Yilmaz says.
Though the researchers confirmed that a ketogenic diet suppressed the development of colon tumors, their findings suggest that ketone bodies are not involved. “These molecules are essentially metabolic bystanders,” Yilmaz says.
One implication is that commercial ketone supplements probably do little to either help or harm people who take them. But the deeper issue is “why the same diet has opposite consequences in two adjacent parts of the gut,” Chi says. “That is what we are working to understand next.”
Whatever they discover, as Yilmaz says, “the message here is that we need to be very careful in generalizing the effects that these diets can have.”

articles.title: Apple restringe las reservas del iPhone Duo para combatir la reventa
articles.text:
Apple parece haber tomado medida para combatir la reventa del iPhone Duo. En las últimas horas, la firma de Cupertino ha implementado un límite a la cantidad de unidades de su móvil plegable que un mismo cliente puede reservar. Esto, luego de que las fechas de entrega se demoraran hasta enero de 2027 apenas minutos después del inicio de la preventa.
Según se observa en las versiones online de la Apple Store, las reservas del iPhone Duo se han limitado a un máximo de 2 unidades por cliente. Si intentas cargar una cantidad mayor, la tienda muestra un mensaje informando de la restricción y obligando a respetar el tope para poder continuar con el procedimiento de compra.
El nuevo límite de dos iPhone Duo por comprador impacta sobre todas las variantes del smartphone. Esto da a entender que el objetivo de Apple es limitar el impacto que los scalpers tienen sobre la disponibilidad de su primer smartphone plegable, si bien ya estuvieron haciendo estragos durante la primera jornada de reservas.
La preventa del iPhone Duo se puso en marcha el pasado viernes 16, con un alto nivel de demanda. Esto, combinado con la poca cantidad de unidades del móvil que se han producido hasta la fecha, resultó en una combinación fatal para la mayoría de los compradores que apostaban a recibirlo el primer día.
Las unidades disponibles para entregar el viernes 23 de octubre se agotaron en apenas minutos, de modo que un gran número de compradores debió conformarse con fechas esparcidas entre noviembre y diciembre próximo, y también en enero de 2027. La situación no fue puntual de un mercado, sino que afectó a todas las versiones de la Apple Store.
Apple restringe las reservas del iPhone Duo: solo 2 por comprador
Más allá de la demanda genuina del público, el lanzamiento del iPhone Duo ha padecido el accionar de los scalpers. Esto no solo ha derivado en la aparición de unidades del plegable en eBay, revendiéndose a precios infladísimos (y ridículos), sino que también expuso operaciones para obtener el móvil usando sistemas total o parcialmente automatizados.
Es cierto que el uso de bots para comprar productos de escasa disponibilidad ni bien se habilita su venta, no es algo nuevo. Sin embargo, con el iPhone Duo generó todavía más ruido por la expectación generada entre el público y porque el responsable de una de las maniobras de scalping no tuvo mejor idea que salir a presumirlo en X (Twitter).
Que Apple ahora limite las reservas del iPhone Duo es una señal de que se están tomando medidas para evitar que la situación se repita. Claro que el daño inicial de los revendedores ya está hecho y nunca se va a dar respuesta definitiva a este tipo de problemas. Por lo pronto, el plegable de la manzana mantiene su fecha de entrega más temprana para el 22 de enero del próximo año.
Lo que todavía es un misterio es si el iPhone Duo se podrá comprar sin reserva previa y de forma presencial en las Apple Store físicas. Los de Cupertino no han brindado detalles sobre cómo piensan lidiar con este asunto cuando se formen largas colas en sus tiendas alrededor del mundo.

articles.title: Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program
articles.text:
Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday that the Trump administration was giving right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million bounty program for members of the public to report fraud.
Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program
In December 2025, Shirley published a viral video alleging fraud at daycares in Minnesota that were operated by members of the local Somali community. Shirley lingered in parking lots and asked to enter childcare centers, taking refusals as evidence that the centers weren’t actually caring for children. The video quickly went viral, triggering a massive governmental response: Federal immigration agents descended on the Minneapolis area, and the Trump administration froze Minnesota’s federal funding for childcare. Shirley has since visited other states in the US under similar pretenses, showing up unannounced to grocery stores and hospice centers in search of evidence of fraud. Vance and others in the administration publicly praised Shirley, who has since become a mainstay in the MAGA-aligned content creator ecosystem. He’s helped popularize a genre of so-called independent journalism popular on the right in which content creators and influencers confront businesses or people they suspect of fraud or crime as the basis for their online content. Harassment — or even immigration crackdowns — often follow.
The administration told Fox News that it was also launching the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program (WHIP), a pool of $25 million open to anyone who believes they’ve witnessed fraud. A “particular emphasis” is placed on fraud in hospice, home healthcare, daycares, and special services, a government website says. A chatbot collecting responses instructs the reporting party: “Briefly describe what you saw, heard, or read. A few sentences are enough. Include names, dates, amounts, or records if you have them, and how you know. Note any details you’re unsure about.”
According to Fox News and the reporting portal, members of the public who flag fraud are eligible to get up to $30,000 if a tip submitted leads to a conviction or significant federal action. But speaking on Tuesday, Trump contradicted the $30,000 ceiling.
”If you turn somebody in and … you find $1 billion, we are giving a commission to that person of 1 percent,” Trump said today. (One percent of $1 billion would exceed the $30,000 cap.) “And if it’s $10 billion, $200 billion, $400 billion, we’re giving a 1 percent commission to that person,” Trump continued.
The White House didn’t immediately clarify how the $10,000 payment to Shirley was calculated or how the program is being funded in the first place.
Shirley’s methods have been criticized particularly in Minnesota, where sweeping fraud investigations were already taking place before he arrived to make content. He accused businesses of faking childcare services based on little more than being denied entry to facilities, and — to the frustration of many — acted as if his video was the first fraud investigation in the state. Subsequent state official visits to the centers Shirley featured found them operating “as expected.”

articles.title: Chinese crime ring steals more than $5 million in gift cards from Staples customer service — more than 15,000 gift cards acquired through internal Nexus system, nearly $500,000 spent before being deactivated
articles.text:
Chinese crime ring steals more than $5 million in gift cards from Staples customer service — more than 15,000 gift cards acquired through internal Nexus system, nearly $500,000 spent before being deactivated
Over $5 million worth of gift cards for retailers like Target and Sephora were stolen when thieves gained access to a system called Nexus.
Millions of dollars worth of gift cards were stolen and then used to buy high-value tech gear at retailers like Target, Sephora, and Lowe's after a Chinese crime ring gained access to an internal Staples system and then used it to issue more than 15,000 cards to itself. While the hack hasn't been made public to date, a 404 Media report notes that it actually took place back in 2023.
The outlet reviewed court records that show that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) was told about the hack in October of that year. The hack came to light after it led to a search warrant that was unsealed last week. And while the document doesn't specifically name Staples as the victim of the hack, 404 Media has confirmed that it was the company affected based on other information. Such information includes the fact that the victim company is headquartered in Massachusetts, that it uses Blackhawk Networks to fulfill gift card orders, and that the company uses an internal customer support system called Nexus. The report notes that a reference to Nexus can be found on a former Staples executive's LinkedIn profile.
While Staples was under the impression that Nexus could not be accessed from beyond its own network, hackers found that not to be the case. They then "performed multiple heap dump requests," a process that captures all of the data held in an app's memory. That information gave the hackers the tools they needed to hijack logged-in sessions of Staples customer service employees. From there, they were able to issue gift cards at will.
Once the gift cards had been issued, the crime group sent runners to physical retail stores to spend them before they were identified and canceled. Target found that 35 gift cards were used at a New Hampshire store, with high-value products from Apple, Bose, and Beats all bought. All 35 cards were used within a period of just a single hour, although not all of them were obtained via this hack.
In total, Target told investigators that 3,850 gift cards worth over $140,000 were used across 85 different stores in just two days. Sephora was hit for $58,600 worth of sales, while Lowe's saw $226,000 spent across online and in-store purchases. In total, 4,630 stolen gift cards were used with a value of around $425,000.
This hack was just the tip of the iceberg, too. Last April, a Department of Justice announcement confirmed that three Chinese nationals had been sentenced for their part in a gift card fraud conspiracy. Including the Staples hack, the crime group stole more than $100 million worth of gift cards.
Chinese organized crime groups often pop up on the radar of U.S.-based law enforcement. Earlier this year, a Chinese phishing service that was used to generate scam websites using AI was dismantled. The service was linked to almost $2 billion in losses.

Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

articles.title: Des hackers détournent des serveurs Plex non mis à jour pour miner des cryptos, le vôtre est-il en danger ?
articles.text:
Plus de deux mois après la publication des correctifs, des pirates exploitent plusieurs failles de Plex Media Server. Les machines compromises servent à miner des cryptomonnaies, mais aussi à relayer du trafic Internet à l'insu de leurs propriétaires.
Début septembre, Plex appelait une nouvelle fois ses utilisateurs et utilisatrices à installer une mise à jour de sécurité sur leurs serveurs multimédias. Si l'éditeur se montrait discret sur la nature des vulnérabilités corrigées, il ne faisait alors état d'aucune exploitation active. C'est désormais chose faite depuis la publication, le 16 octobre dernier, d'un code permettant d'exploiter quatre de ces failles pour exécuter du code à distance sur un serveur, sans authentification. Dès le lendemain, un chercheur observait des tentatives d'intrusion sur un serveur leurre, tandis que des propriétaires d'installations non patchées signalaient à leur tour des activités suspectes.
Plex2Shell, quatre vulnérabilités exploitées en chaîne
Baptisée Plex2Shell, cette méthode d'attaque repose sur l'enchaînement de quatre vulnérabilités, référencées CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 et CVE-2026-96656. Leur exploitation combinée permet de contourner les contrôles d'accès de Plex, de récupérer le jeton d'administration du serveur, puis d'y déposer un fichier malveillant que le logiciel exécutera avec les privilèges du processus Media Server.
Le chercheur Zach Main avait signalé ces failles à Plex dès le 27 juillet, permettant à l'éditeur de les corriger le 4 août dans Media Server 1.43.3.10861. De son côté, l'auteur de BoredHackerBlog avait déployé, en septembre, un serveur Plex volontairement vulnérable et accessible depuis Internet, afin de surveiller d'éventuelles attaques. Pendant plusieurs semaines, il n'y avait relevé que des scans et des tentatives d'exploitation génériques, jusqu'à l'apparition de requêtes correspondant à la méthode Plex2Shell.
Ces tentatives provenaient d'au moins trois adresses IP distinctes. En modifiant la configuration de son serveur leurre pour autoriser les connexions sortantes, le chercheur a également pu observer le téléchargement de fichiers malveillants et récupérer plusieurs échantillons pour les examiner. Le 19 octobre, Plex a confirmé que les vulnérabilités faisaient désormais l'objet d'attaques généralisées contre les installations non corrigées, sans préciser combien de serveurs avaient été compromis.
Des serveurs détournés pour miner des cryptomonnaies et relayer du trafic Internet
Parmi les fichiers récupérés par BoredHackerBlog figure une version de XMRig, un logiciel de minage de cryptomonnaies que les pirates installent sous le nom de mylovelyminer. Une fois lancé, il exploite les ressources du processeur pour générer des revenus à leur profit, au prix d'une dégradation des performances de la machine et d'une hausse de sa consommation électrique. Sur Reddit, plusieurs témoignages abondent dans ce sens, des propriétaires de serveurs Plex rapportant avoir découvert des processus de minage sur leurs installations, parfois après avoir constaté une utilisation anormalement élevée du processeur.
Les investigations ont également révélé la présence d'un second programme, baptisé myawesomeproxy, dont la fonction est bien différente. Associé à des communications vers le domaine proxystream.st, ce logiciel permet de faire transiter le trafic Internet de tiers par le serveur compromis. Les pirates peuvent ainsi utiliser l'adresse IP de leur victime comme relais, et masquer l'origine réelle de leurs connexions. Un détournement particulièrement intéressant lorsque le serveur utilise une adresse IP résidentielle, susceptible d'inspirer davantage confiance à certains services en ligne.
Face à ces compromissions, Plex recommande de vérifier sans attendre la version de Media Server, mais aussi de rechercher d'éventuels processus suspects, des fichiers inconnus dans le répertoire Codecs ou une consommation anormale du processeur. Pour les installations déjà infectées, une simple mise à jour ne suffit pas : l'éditeur préconise de réinstaller le serveur sur un environnement propre, de déconnecter tous les appareils associés au compte Plex et de modifier son mot de passe. Il invite également les personnes qui n'en ont pas l'utilité à désactiver l'accès distant, afin de limiter l'exposition de leur serveur sur Internet.

articles.title: Les Joy-Con 2 bleu et jaune de la Switch 2 passent en promo sur Amazon
articles.text:
Nintendo les avait présentés lors de son Nintendo Direct du 9 juin 2026. Ces Joy-Con 2 bleu et jaune clair sont arrivés en magasin le 23 juillet, le jour de la sortie de Splatoon Raiders. Leurs couleurs reprennent celles des Tridenfer, le groupe fictif apparu dans Splatoon 3. Le Joy-Con gauche est bleu, le droit jaune clair.
La Switch 2 est livrée avec une seule paire de manettes. Pour que deux joueurs aient chacun leur paire, il faut en racheter une. Amazon propose justement la paire à 69,99 € au lieu de 89,99 €, soit 20 € d’économie.
Que valent les Joy-Con 2 bleu et jaune de la Switch 2 ?
Ces Joy-Con 2 sont les manettes officielles de la Switch 2, identiques à celles fournies avec la console, à la couleur près. Elles s’aimantent sur les flancs de l’écran pour le jeu en mode portable. Une fois détachées, elles servent à jouer en solo avec une manette dans chaque main, ou à deux avec un Joy-Con par joueur dans les jeux compatibles.
Côté fonctions, ces Joy-Con 2 gèrent les commandes par mouvements et les vibrations HD 2, le retour haptique fin de Nintendo, qui simule des sensations précises au lieu d’un simple tremblement. Elles ajoutent un mode souris, qui permet de faire glisser un Joy-Con sur une table pour déplacer un curseur dans les jeux compatibles. Un bouton C donne enfin un accès direct à GameChat, le chat vocal et vidéo de la console, qui demande un abonnement payant Nintendo Switch Online.
La boîte contient le Joy-Con gauche, le Joy-Con droit et deux dragonnes. Attention si vous avez encore une Switch de première génération : ces Joy-Con 2 ne fonctionnent qu’avec la Switch 2.
À ce prix, les Joy-Con 2 bleu et jaune sont-ils une bonne affaire ?
Nintendo commercialise toutes ses paires de Joy-Con 2 au même prix de 89,99 €, qu’il s’agisse du modèle standard, de la version violet clair et vert clair ou de cette édition bleu et jaune. Proposée à 69,99 €, cette dernière profite donc d’une réduction de 20 € et se rapproche des meilleurs prix observés pour des Joy-Con 2 officiels. Un bon plan pour s’équiper à moindre coût ou disposer d’une paire supplémentaire.
Les fêtes de fin d’année approchent, et avec elles les parties à plusieurs sur le canapé. Si vous comptiez offrir une seconde paire ou équiper un deuxième joueur, autant le faire avec 20 € de remise. Gardez en tête que les prix varient vite sur Amazon et que rien ne garantit que cette remise durera longtemps.

articles.title: Jusqu'à deux fois plus de tâches qu'Intel et AMD : le processeur ARM Nvidia Vera convainc un gros acteur — Frandroid
articles.text:
Nvidia ne veut plus seulement vendre ses GPU, il veut aussi placer ses CPU dans les centres de données. Cela tombe bien puisque Nvidia a un client de plus pour son processeur Vera.
Dans un billet de blog publié ce lundi 19 octobre, Modal annonce qu’elle va faire tourner une partie de ses services sur ce CPU. Cette start-up américaine loue de la puissance de calcul aux développeurs d’IA.
Ses serveurs n’utilisaient jusqu’ici que des puces x86 d’Intel et AMD. Nvidia domine déjà le marché des GPU pour l’IA, et la voilà qui prend pied sur le terrain historique de ses deux concurrents.
Modal pèse déjà lourd dans le secteur. La société a levé 750 millions de dollars (environ 670 millions d’euros) le 14 octobre, pour une valorisation de 15,75 milliards de dollars (environ 14 milliards d’euros), et vise le milliard de dollars de chiffre d’affaires sur un an. Vera servira à son produit Sandboxes. Ce sont des environnements isolés où les agents IA (ces programmes qui enchaînent seuls des tâches longues, comme écrire et tester du code) exécutent leurs commandes.
Deux fois plus de tâches, mais sous forte charge
Pour comparer les puces, Modal a construit son propre test, baptisé Agentless Agent Bench. Il fait tourner 50 tâches typiques d’un agent (compiler du code, fouiller des fichiers, manipuler un dépôt Git) dans des conteneurs Docker lancés en parallèle, sans appel réseau. Face à Vera, on trouve des serveurs Intel Granite Rapids, AMD Zen 5 et AWS Graviton 4 et 5.
Sur une machine au repos, avec une tâche à la fois, Vera est souvent devant, « mais pas toujours, et pas avec une marge particulièrement large », reconnaît Erik Dunteman, l’ingénieur de Modal qui signe le billet. Par contre, quand les conteneurs s’entassent, Vera traite jusqu’à deux fois plus de tâches par minute que la machine Intel avec le même nombre de cœurs logiques alloués, et chaque tâche ne prend pas plus de temps. Sur toute la machine, avec 150 conteneurs, l’écart tombe à environ 40 %. Vera valide alors 6 500 tâches par minute, contre 4 600 pour le serveur Intel, qui a pourtant 256 threads contre 176.
Modal ne précise pas les références exactes des puces et ne donne aucun chiffre de consommation. Surtout, Vera était opposé aux générations actuelles d’Intel et AMD. Leurs successeurs, qui seront ses vrais concurrents dans les années à venir, n’ont pas encore été testés.
Il est fort à parier que les charges des agents IA favorisent les puces ARM. Mais, attention, le graphique de Modal nuance cette lecture : les Graviton d’AWS, eux aussi basés sur ARM, plafonnent bien plus bas que Vera. Pour Modal, l’écart provient plutôt de la bande passante mémoire de Vera, qui permet de faire tourner plus de conteneurs par cœur sans que le processeur ralentisse.
Nvidia a justement soigné ce point. Vera est son premier processeur serveur avec des cœurs maison, baptisés Olympus, construits sur le jeu d’instructions Arm v9.2. La puce compte 88 cœurs et 176 threads. Elle offre jusqu’à 1,2 To/s de bande passante mémoire, le double de Grace, le processeur précédent de Nvidia, d’après le livre blanc publié par Nvidia en juillet.
Nvidia veut aussi le processeur central
Nvidia a gagné des milliards avec ses accélérateurs GPU. Pourtant, avec les agents, le CPU redevient un point de blocage. D’après Modal, un agent passe beaucoup de temps à attendre la réponse du modèle, puis il peut demander d’un coup dix fois plus de calcul pour une simple installation de paquets. Et quand le CPU traîne, les GPU attendent. Erik Dunteman le résume ainsi : « tout temps gagné sur le CPU est du temps gagné sur le GPU ».
Nvidia prévoit au moins 20 milliards de dollars (environ 18 milliards d’euros) de ventes de Vera sur son exercice en cours. Le groupe estime le marché total à 200 milliards de dollars (environ 180 milliards d’euros).
Il s’invite aussi dans les PC avec sa puce RTX Spark. Les clouds de l’IA pourraient donc acheter les GPU, les CPU et l’interconnexion au même fournisseur, et dépendre de lui pour tout. Intel, de son côté, mise sur d’autres terrains, comme une carte graphique de 480 Go pour l’IA ou des puces pour robots humanoïdes prévues pour 2028.
Modal garde quand même Intel et AMD. Passer à ARM l’oblige à adapter toute son infrastructure, et son patron, Erik Bernhardsson, a assuré à Reuters que la flotte resterait mixte.

articles.title: Elon Musk y Anthropic discrepan sobre cómo repartir la riqueza generada por la IA
articles.text:
Anthropic se ha comprometido a hacer todo lo que esté en su mano para atenuar el impacto que el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial (IA) ya está teniendo en el mercado laboral. Este laboratorio estadounidense es uno de los más importantes de la industria de la IA, y, como os explicamos ayer, ha concretado su propuesta asegurando que va a destinar el 5% de sus acciones al Fondo de Beneficio Público, si lo aprueban sus accionistas.
Dario Amodei, el máximo responsable de Anthropic, ha declarado en varias ocasiones que la cada vez mayor penetración de la IA provocará que en menos de cinco años la mitad de los empleos de oficina de nivel inicial desaparezcan. Su tesis defiende que los modelos de IA podrán llevar a cabo esos trabajos con las máximas garantías, de modo que para las empresas será más rentable ceder esa responsabilidad a un modelo de lenguaje y prescindir de algunos de sus empleados.
Si observamos el ritmo al que ha evolucionado la IA durante los últimos seis meses, la previsión de cinco años de Amodei resulta incluso demasiado conservadora. Sea como sea, es evidente que es necesario abordar esta discusión y concretar cuál es la responsabilidad de los laboratorios de IA en el impacto que sus modelos ya están teniendo en el mercado laboral. Curiosamente, la perspectiva de Elon Musk es muy diferente al enfoque que ha puesto sobre la mesa Dario Amodei.
UN VISTAZO A...
Dos respuestas para una misma pregunta: quién debe beneficiarse de la IA
El punto de partida de Elon Musk, que, además de liderar Tesla y SpaceX, dirige el laboratorio de IA xAI, es distinto. Su propuesta pasa por repartir directamente entre los ciudadanos una parte de la riqueza generada por sus empresas en lugar de canalizarla a través de un fondo filantrópico. De hecho, Musk ha planteado entregar acciones de SpaceX a los niños estadounidenses, de manera que puedan beneficiarse de la revalorización de la compañía a largo plazo.
SpaceX repartiría aproximadamente 11.000 millones de dólares ciñéndonos a su valoración actual
Si Musk finalmente lleva a cabo su propuesta, SpaceX repartiría aproximadamente 11.000 millones de dólares ciñéndonos a su valoración actual, aunque el valor real de las acciones que recibiría cada niño dependería de la evolución futura de la compañía. De esta forma, los menores no recibirían dinero en efectivo, sino una participación en el capital de SpaceX cuyo valor podría aumentar o disminuir con el tiempo.
Si analizamos con cuidado las propuestas de Anthropic y Elon Musk nos daremos cuenta de que tienen implicaciones muy diferentes. Las acciones de SpaceX que recibirían los menores estadounidenses son activos financieros cuyo valor depende de la evolución de esta compañía, mientras que las acciones que Anthropic planea entregar a un fondo de beneficio público pueden destinarse a necesidades colectivas concretas. No obstante, ambas estrategias tienen algo en común muy importante.
Y es que las dos abordan la responsabilidad de los laboratorios de IA a la hora de distribuir la enorme concentración de riqueza que presumiblemente va a desencadenar esta tecnología. No obstante, este reparto de la riqueza no debería reemplazar las políticas públicas que son necesarias para afrontar el desplazamiento de los trabajadores, la desigualdad de la población o los riesgos derivados del uso de sistemas de IA cada vez más avanzados. La filantropía está muy bien, pero es razonable concluir que estas decisiones tan importantes no deberían estar solo en las manos de los laboratorios de IA.

articles.title: Halloween : de Netflix à Prime Video, 10 séries flippantes à voir en streaming
articles.text:
Halloween : de Netflix à Prime Video, 10 séries flippantes à voir en streaming
À la recherche d'une ou plusieurs séries effrayantes à regarder en attendant Halloween ? Les Numériques vous a trouvé 10 séries horrifiques à ne pas manquer en streaming.
Halloween approche à grands pas et vous avez peut-être envie de regarder des séries horrifiques en plus de vous faire peur devant des films du même genre. Cela tombe bien car Les Numériques a fait le tour des plateformes de streaming pour vous proposer une sélection de séries d'épouvante parfaites pour la saison qui donne la chair de poule.
De fictions franchement flippantes comme Ça : bienvenue à Derry et From à des séries plus gentillement effrayantes comme Mercredi et Les nouvelles aventures de Sabrina, voici 10 fictions sérielles pour vous préparer à la fête du 31 octobre à retrouver sur Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, HBO Max et Paramount+ (dont l'offre est accessible via Canal+).
Ça : bienvenue à Derry (HBO Max)
Ça : Bienvenue à Derry
HBO Max
- Date de sortie
- 27/10/2025
- Genre
- Epouvante-horreur
- Durée
- 60 min
- Episodes
- 9
Des événements étranges se déroulent dans la ville de Derry dans les années 1960, liés au clown Grippe-Sou, un personnage mystérieux qui hante les lieux.
Ça : Bienvenue à Derry se base sur le roman Ça de Stephen King pour étendre son univers et la vision mise en place par Andy Muschietti dans ses deux films Ça. Résultat ? Une série absolument terrifiante et magistrale, un petit bijou horrifique du petit écran racontant une histoire captivante, soutenue par des protagonistes attachants, une mythologie fascinante et une mise en scène aussi glaçante que poignante. Tant pis si ça fait peur, on ne veut plus quitter Derry.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
The Haunting of Bly Manor (Netflix)
Dans l'Angleterre des années 1980, après la mort tragique d'une jeune fille au pair, Henry Wingrave engage une gouvernante américaine inexpérimentée pour s'occuper de sa nièce et de son neveu. Ces deux orphelins résident à Bly Manor avec le responsable du domaine Owen, la gardienne Jamie, et l'intendante Mrs Grose. Mais le manoir regorge de faux-semblants, et des siècles de sombres secrets n'attendent que d'être exhumés au fil de cette terrifiante romance gothique sur l'amour et le deuil. Car à Bly Manor, les morts ne sont pas tous des disparus...
Ce drame gothique inspiré de plusieurs histoires surnaturelles emblématiques d'Henry James est le deuxième volet de l'anthologie The Haunting de Mike Flanagan. Portée par une distribution épatante, des décors inquiétants et un récit captivant, cette série sait émouvoir autant que donner la chair de poule.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Widow's Bay (Apple TV)
Le maire d'une ville de Nouvelle-Angleterre souhaite en faire une destination touristique, malgré les avertissements sur le fait qu'elle est maudite.
Vous aimez l'horreur, les intrigues pleines de mystère et l'humour noir ? Alors vous serez comblés par cette série portée par un Matthew Rhys (The Americans) en grande forme. Sur fond de petite île à l'atmosphère inquiétante, Widow's Bay déroule une histoire prenante, soutenue par une mise en scène experte et des performances irréprochables de la part de l'ensemble de la distribution.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Entretien avec un vampire (Paramount+)
En 2022, le vampire Louis de Pointe du Lac raconte son histoire au célèbre journaliste Daniel Molloy. En 1910 à La Nouvelle-Orléans, Louis et Lestat forment une famille vampirique à laquelle vient s'ajouter Claudia, la novice adolescente.
Entretien avec un vampire est l’une des meilleures séries de ces dernières années et a su s’approprier Les Chroniques des vampires d'Anne Rice pour en faire une version plus sensuelle et contemporaine que l'adaptation cinématographique de 1994 avec Tom Cruise et Brad Pitt. De la distribution à l’écriture, en passant par la mise en scène, la cinématographie et les costumes, tout est soigneusement calibré pour proposer au spectateur une histoire gothique délicieusement addictive, portée par les performances impeccables de Sam Reid et Jacob Anderson.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Chair de poule (Disney+)
Cinq lycéens se lancent dans une terrible enquête pleine de rebondissements afin de cerner les circonstances du décès tragique, trente ans plus tôt, d’un adolescent, et découvrent au passage les lourds secrets de leurs parents.
Avec cette série, Disney+ modernise les histoires cultes de R.L. Stine et propose une fiction horrifique à la Stranger Things, avec une bande d'ados confrontée à des forces surnaturelles. Chair de poule mélange humour, drame et épouvante pour donner lieu à une histoire rythmée qui ouvre la porte au genre de l'horreur pour ceux qui ne s'y aventurent pas souvent.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Les nouvelles aventures de Sabrina (Netflix)
La magie se mêle au trouble alors que Sabrina, demi-humaine demi-sorcière, navigue entre deux mondes, sa vie d'ado mortelle et son héritage familial, l'Église de la Nuit.
Cette production Netflix réinvente la sitcom culte des années 1990 pour en faire une série bien plus sombre et tournée vers l'occulte, le macabre et l'épouvante. Sur fond d'histoire sur le passage à l'âge adulte, la série brille par son atmosphère inquiétante, son casting épatant (Kiernan Shipka, Miranda Otto, Lucy Davis...) pour offrir aux spectateurs un mélange de série pour ados, surnaturel et frissons.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Penny Dreadful (Prime Video)
Londres, 1891, une menace quasi invisible massacre la population. Vanessa Ives, une jeune femme aux pouvoirs puissants et hypnotiques, rencontre et propose à Ethan Chandler, un homme rebelle et violent, de s'allier à elle ainsi qu'à Sir Malcolm Murray, un homme riche d'un certain âge aux ressources intarissables, pour combattre cette nouvelle menace.
Laissez-vous séduire par cette série gothique à souhait qui a eu droit à trois saisons entre 2014 et 2016. Portée par Eva Green, Timothy Dalton et Josh Hartnett, cette série entre fantastique, épouvante et drame met en scène des personnages phares de la littérature du 19e siècle pour raconter une histoire aussi macabre que poétique. Des décors aux costumes en passant par la distribution, tout sort son plus grand jeu pour donner vie à une fiction sans pareille.
- Regardez une bande-annonce de la série :
From (Paramount+)
L'histoire d'une ville effrayante au milieu des États-Unis où toute personne qui y entre se retrouve piégée. Les habitants de la bourgade essaient de maintenir les choses aussi normales que possible tout en cherchant un moyen de s'échapper, car la nuit venue ils sont terrorisés par des monstres meurtriers.
Créée par John Griffin (Le Cratère, La Quatrième Dimension) et produite par des anciens de Lost, cette série d'horreur et de science-fiction plaira aux spectateurs qui aiment les personnalités fortes coincées dans une situation impossible. La série captive grâce à une histoire et des personnages fascinants tout en donnant des sueurs froides avec des créatures cauchemardesques.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Mercredi (Netflix)
La série suit les aventures de Mercredi Addams, désormais étudiante à la Nevermore Academy. Alors qu’elle apprend à dompter ses nouveaux pouvoirs psychiques, la jeune fille doit aussi déjouer une série de meurtres monstrueux qui terrorisent la ville et résoudre le mystère auquel ont été mêlés ses parents il y a 25 ans, le tout en tentant péniblement de nouer de nouvelles relations au sein de Nevermore.
Mercredi propose une histoire palpitante et bardée de rebondissements. Une série généreuse et délicieusement macabre qui saura plaire à tout le monde, de l’ado rebelle à ses parents déboussolés, en passant par l’adepte d’énigmes rondement ficelées. Un tour de force pour une famille Addams dont on a définitivement envie de faire partie.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
American Horror Story (Disney+)
Maisons hantées, asiles, sorcières, hôtels maudits ou sectes : la série change d’époque, de décor et de personnages à chaque nouvelle intrigue, tout en conservant certains visages familiers au casting. Les histoires mêlent surnaturel, violence, croyances, crimes et traumatismes profondément ancrés dans la société américaine. Certaines saisons finissent aussi par se répondre ou partager des personnages, dessinant peu à peu un univers commun derrière cette anthologie. Chaque chapitre explore ainsi une nouvelle forme de peur, souvent inspirée autant par les monstres que par les êtres humains.
Créé par Ryan Murphy, le showrunner et scénariste derrière les séries Dahmer, Glee et Ratched, American Horror Story est LE programme parfait pour les fans de frissons et d'horreur. Chacune de ses saisons possède sa thématique propre, de la maison hantée au cirque, en passant par l'apocalypse et l'asile, et joue avec brio de son ambiance glauque et de sa tension pour vous river à votre siège.
