articles.title: Cómo se verían Las Guerreras K-pop en el universo de Dragon Ball Super: Beerus
articles.text:
El estreno de Dragon Ball Super: Beerus abre una posibilidad para que los seguidores del anime imaginen a Las Guerreras K-pop dentro del universo de Goku y Vegeta.
Con referencias visuales y un pedido preciso, una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) puede crear una escena de combate que enfrente al grupo con Beerus en un escenario espacial.
El procedimiento puede realizarse desde un navegador actualizado, sin instalar archivos de origen desconocido ni programas externos que soliciten permisos innecesarios.
Cuál es el primer paso para recrear imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop
El primer paso es reunir una imagen grupal de Las Guerreras K-pop donde se distingan los rostros, los peinados, las prendas y los accesorios de cada integrante.
Una toma de cuerpo entero o desde la cintura permite que el generador identifique mejor las diferencias entre las protagonistas y reduzca la posibilidad de repetir caras o mezclar los vestuarios.
Además, se debe tener una referencia de Beerus, Goku y Vegeta. La imagen debe mostrar elementos reconocibles de cada personaje, como las orejas y el atuendo del Dios de la Destrucción, el uniforme naranja de Goku y la armadura de Vegeta.
Si la escena incluirá transformaciones, conviene que las referencias ya exhiban el cabello azul y las auras de energía correspondientes.
Qué plataforma permite generar imágenes con IA
Las imágenes pueden adjuntarse en el chat de Gemini, la herramienta de inteligencia artificial de Google. El acceso se realiza desde el sitio oficial mediante un navegador actualizado, una alternativa que evita instalar aplicaciones desde páginas no verificadas o archivos cuyo origen no se puede comprobar.
Dentro de la conversación, los archivos se incorporan con el botón de adjuntar o al arrastrarlos hacia la ventana del chat. Es preferible enviar las referencias de Las Guerreras K-pop y de Dragon Ball en un solo mensaje. De ese modo, la herramienta recibe el conjunto visual antes de interpretar la instrucción.
Antes de avanzar, se debe revisar que las miniaturas se vean completas. Una imagen borrosa, un recorte que elimine parte del vestuario o la presencia de figuras ajenas pueden modificar el resultado y dificultar que cada personaje conserve sus rasgos.
Cómo debe redactarse el prompt para la IA
El texto debe indicar el estilo de animación, los personajes, sus ubicaciones y el tipo de enfrentamiento. Las imágenes de referencia permiten conservar la apariencia general, mientras que el prompt define la acción.
Un ejemplo de pedido es: “Crear una ilustración de acción estilo anime. Tres guerreras K-pop inspiradas en las referencias visuales enfrentan a Beerus, Goku y Vegeta en un planeta destruido. Ubicar a las guerreras a la izquierda y a Beerus a la derecha, con Goku y Vegeta detrás. Mostrar plano panorámico, escombros flotando, expresiones de combate y destellos de energía”.
La instrucción puede sumar datos para distribuir los ataques. Por ejemplo: “Beerus concentra una esfera violeta en la mano derecha; Goku usa una energía azul; Vegeta avanza con el puño cerrado; una guerrera sostiene una espada, otra forma un escudo de energía y la tercera prepara dagas luminosas”.
Asimismo, la ambientación requiere elementos propios de la saga para que el cruce tenga coherencia visual. Un cielo oscuro con galaxias, cráteres, ruinas, rocas suspendidas y explosiones de ki pueden situar a las protagonistas en una batalla similar a las de Goku y Vegeta contra adversarios de gran poder.
Qué hacer antes de descargar y compartir la imagen
La primera generación debe revisarse por partes. Es común que la IA produzca manos con dedos adicionales, armas deformadas, ojos desalineados, accesorios repetidos o personajes que aparecen en un lugar distinto al indicado. Puede confundir el cabello de una integrante con el aura de otro peleador.
Las correcciones funcionan mejor con órdenes breves y puntuales. Se puede pedir: “Mantener tres guerreras”, “corregir la mano izquierda de Beerus”, “eliminar el brazo duplicado de Goku”, “ubicar a Vegeta detrás de Goku” o “hacer que la guerrera de cabello trenzado conserve su chaqueta amarilla”.
Una vez elegida la versión final, el archivo puede descargarse desde la misma conversación. Antes de compartirlo en redes sociales, mensajes o una publicación, hay que aclarar que se trata de una imagen creada con inteligencia artificial y de una recreación realizada por usuarios, sin vínculo oficial con las producciones originales.

articles.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
articles.text:
Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.
The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.
The rocket’s upper stage accelerated the MMX spacecraft to a top speed of more than 24,000 mph, fast enough to break free of Earth’s gravitational pull for the 10-month voyage to Mars. The nearly 9,900-pound (4.5-metric ton) spacecraft—two-thirds of its mass comprised of propellant—separated from the H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff.
Hiroshi Yamakawa, president of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), declared the launch a success. “A long journey of five years has just started,” Yamakawa said.
MMX established contact with ground controllers, unfurled its solar panels, and was in a “very stable condition” soon after separating from the H3 rocket, according to Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, the mission’s project manager at JAXA. “So far, so good.”
“The MMX [mission] we launched today is a challenging mission aiming for the world’s first sample return from the Martian moons,” said Yoshihiro Seki, Japan’s science minister. “We hope that the results obtained through this mission will contribute to the development of our nation’s space science and exploration technology.”
Building on a legacy
The mission to the Martian moons builds on Japan’s success in leading the Hayabusa and Hayabusa 2 missions, the world’s first two spacecraft to bring back pristine specimens from asteroids. Scientists believe Phobos could itself be an asteroid that was captured into orbit around Mars billions of years ago. One of MMX’s science goals is finding out if that theory is correct.

articles.title: Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference
Canadian organizations building generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock often need the latest foundation models (FMs), such as OpenAI GPT-6.1, OpenAI GPT-6, and GPT-5.6, accessible from the Canadian AWS Regions. With Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference (CRIS), you can now access these models from Canada. OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (Sol, Terra, and Luna), GPT-6 (Astra, Sol, and Luna), and GPT-6.1 Sol are available from the Canada (Central) and Canada West (Calgary) Regions. Inference is processed in North America, with data-residency controls described later in this post.
Cross-Region inference is a capacity mechanism. Your application calls the Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint in your source Region. Amazon Bedrock then routes the request to a supported destination Region for processing. With this approach, you get access to a broader capacity pool that can help your application sustain throughput during demand spikes. You don’t need to manage destination Region routing in your application.
In this post, we walk through the GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 models available from Canada and the cross-Region inference profiles that serve them. We then show how to set up permissions and invoke the models with the OpenAI Responses API, Chat Completions API, and the Amazon Bedrock Converse API. For the Responses API, we include streaming and tool-use examples. Finally, we cover how to request quota increases, review the observability signals available in your source Region, and clean up when you are done.
Models available from Canada
With Amazon Bedrock, you can access three families of OpenAI models in Canada through cross-Region inference. The following table summarizes each model and its positioning.
| Model | Positioning | 
| GPT-6.1 Sol | Strong reasoning and coding for tasks where both performance and cost matter | 
| GPT-6 Astra | Complex end-to-end reasoning and agentic tasks | 
| GPT-6 Sol | Strong reasoning and coding for recurring tasks with economics suited to regular use | 
| GPT-6 Luna | Fast, low-cost inference for high-volume repeated tasks with adjustable reasoning effort per request | 
| GPT-5.6 Sol | High reasoning, coding, and agentic workloads | 
| GPT-5.6 Terra | Balanced performance and cost for everyday production | 
| GPT-5.6 Luna | Fast and affordable for high-volume, latency-sensitive applications | 
These models accept text and image inputs, return text, and support a 1-million-token context window, reasoning mode, and tool calling. GPT-6.1 Sol supports the same context window and tool calling, with additional input and output modalities documented in its model card. GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 also support prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock (see the Prompt caching section). These models are available through the OpenAI Responses API, the OpenAI Chat Completions API, and the Amazon Bedrock Converse API on the bedrock-runtime endpoint.
For pricing, see Amazon Bedrock pricing. For per-model Region availability, see the model cards in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
Cross-Region inference profiles from Canada
Amazon Bedrock inference profiles are logical identifiers you pass in place of a raw model ID. Each profile defines a model and the set of Regions to which Amazon Bedrock can route a request. Two profile types are available from Canada:
- US geographic (prefixed us.) routes requests to your Canadian source Region and US Regions. Choose this profile when your workload requires inference processing to remain within North America (Canada and the US).
- Global (prefixed global.) routes requests to supported commercial AWS Regions where the model is deployed. This draws on a broader capacity pool at the time of the request.
Endpoint availability differs by model and source Region, as shown in the following table.
| Model | US geographic profile | Global profile | 
| GPT-6.1 Sol | ca-central-1, ca-west-1 | ca-central-1, ca-west-1 | 
| GPT-6 Astra / Sol / Luna | ca-central-1, ca-west-1 | ca-central-1, ca-west-1 | 
| GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna | ca-central-1, ca-west-1 | ca-central-1 | 
Profile membership and model availability can change. The global profile for the GPT-5.6 models is available only from ca-central-1. From ca-west-1, use the US geographic profile for GPT-5.6. Verify the active profiles for your source Region before deployment, either with the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) or on the console (see the following section), or see the Cross-Region inference support documentation.
Getting started
The following sections walk through the setup and code needed to invoke these models from your Canadian source Region.
Prerequisites
Before you begin, confirm that you have the following:
- An AWS account with the Canada (Central) ca-central-1 or Canada West (Calgary) ca-west-1 Region enabled as your source Region.
- An AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role or user with permissions to invoke the inference profiles (see Set up permissions).
- A service control policy (SCP) that allows the inference profiles in your source Region, if your organization enforces SCPs (see SCP considerations).
- Python 3.9 or later with the openai, boto3, and aws-bedrock-token-generator packages installed.
Set up permissions
For quick exploration, attach the AWS managed policy AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess. For deployed workloads with stricter access controls, use a least-privilege custom policy. The following example grants access to the GPT-6 Astra global profile from ca-central-1:
If you authenticate through the API-key path (bearer token for the OpenAI SDK), also grant bedrock:CallWithBearerToken. For the Responses API, add bedrock:InvokeModel on arn:aws:bedrock:ca-central-1:*:project/default.
SCP considerations
If your organization restricts Regions through SCPs, use the bedrock:InferenceProfileArn condition key to allow CRIS traffic while blocking direct calls to unapproved Regions. The following SCP denies Amazon Bedrock inference outside your approved source Regions unless the request uses a CRIS inference profile:
With this condition, Amazon Bedrock can route to the profile’s destination Regions even when those Regions are otherwise denied by your SCP. Every destination Region in your chosen profile must be allowed for the request to succeed. For more detail, see Set up cross-Region inference in multi-account environments.
Verify active inference profiles
Before invoking a model, you can verify which profiles are active in your source Region with the AWS CLI. The following command lists the active OpenAI profiles from ca-central-1. To run the same check from Calgary, replace ca-central-1 with ca-west-1.
The Amazon Bedrock console offers the same view. Open the console, choose Canada (Central) or Canada West (Calgary) as your Region, choose Cross-Region inference under Inference, and review the available profiles.
The following screenshot shows the active OpenAI inference profiles listed on the Amazon Bedrock console for the Canada (Central) Region.
Invoke the models through Amazon Bedrock Runtime
GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 support three access paths on the bedrock-runtime endpoint: the OpenAI Responses API, the OpenAI Chat Completions API, and the Amazon Bedrock Converse API. The OpenAI-compatible APIs are called on the /openai/v1 paths of the endpoint. The endpoint accepts either AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) or an Amazon Bedrock API key.
The following examples use the Amazon Bedrock token generator for Python to create a short-term Amazon Bedrock API key from your current AWS credentials, so your application does not need to store a static key.
OpenAI Responses API
For applications that already use the OpenAI SDK with the Responses API, point the client at the Regional Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint and pass the inference profile ID as the model.
For streaming output, set stream=True and iterate over the response events, printing text as it arrives:
OpenAI Chat Completions API
The OpenAI Chat Completions format works through the same endpoint.
For the full list of supported parameters, including reasoning effort levels, see the model cards in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
Amazon Bedrock Converse API
Use the Converse API when your application calls Amazon Bedrock through an AWS SDK. Boto3 resolves credentials through the standard AWS credential chain.
The same call works for GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and GPT-6.1 Sol by changing the inference profile ID. The following example uses the US geographic profile for GPT-6 Sol and the global profile for GPT-6 Luna. Both were validated from ca-central-1.
Tool use
These models support client-side tool use (function calling). Define tools in the tools parameter, and the model returns a structured tool-call request for your application to execute.
Prompt caching
GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 support prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock to reduce the cost and latency of repeated prompt prefixes. Implicit caching requires no changes to your code: Amazon Bedrock automatically caches eligible prefixes of 1,024 tokens or more. Cached tokens read on subsequent requests are billed at a discounted rate and do not count against your tokens-per-minute quota. Cached tokens appear in the response usage object and in Amazon CloudWatch metrics so you can track usage. For cache-write pricing, minimum prefix sizes, and support for explicit cache breakpoints, see the prompt caching documentation and the individual model cards.
Quota management
Cross-Region inference quotas on the bedrock-runtime endpoint are measured in tokens per minute (TPM) per model. Each quota combines input and output tokens against a single limit. US geographic and global inference profiles have separate quota allocations, so switching between them changes the pool you draw from.
Token consumption combines input tokens, cache-write input tokens, and output tokens. Output tokens are multiplied by the model’s burndown rate, so output-heavy workloads consume quota faster than raw token counts suggest. Before a production rollout, request quota increases early and monitor quota utilization. Test with representative prompts, output lengths, streaming behavior, concurrency, and peak traffic.
To request a quota increase, follow these steps:
- Open the Service Quotas console in ca-central-1 or ca-west-1.
- Choose Amazon Bedrock, then select the quota named “Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute” for the model that you need.
- Choose Request increase at account level, enter your target value, and submit the request.
For details on how token usage and costs are tracked, see Track usage and costs in Amazon Bedrock.
Observability
Because these models run through the Amazon Bedrock Runtime API, requests made through an inference profile appear in your observability tooling the same way on-demand requests do. Invocation logs and Amazon CloudWatch metrics are recorded in your source Region. This holds regardless of where the request was processed. Your observability stays in one place.
- AWS CloudTrail logs every request, recording which destination Region served it in the additionalEventData.inferenceRegion field. For example:
- Amazon CloudWatch metrics are published per inference profile, covering invocation count, token count, latency, throttles, and errors.
- Model invocation logging delivers full request and response payloads to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) or Amazon CloudWatch Logs. To activate it on the Amazon Bedrock console, choose Settings, then choose Model invocation logging. You can also call the PutModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration API. It is off by default.
- AWS Data Exports itemizes spend by model and profile.
Amazon CloudWatch Coding Agent Insights
If you use these models to power AI coding assistants such as OpenAI Codex, Amazon CloudWatch Coding Agent Insights provides a dedicated dashboard. It surfaces token usage, API request counts, active users, and cost attribution across dimensions such as department, team, and environment. To activate it, configure your coding agent to export telemetry to Amazon CloudWatch. For the setup steps, see Set up OpenTelemetry for OpenAI Codex.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges after testing, remove the resources you created:
- Turn off model invocation logging. On the Amazon Bedrock console, choose Settings, then choose Model invocation logging, or call DeleteModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration. This stops delivery of logs to Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
- Delete or detach the IAM policies and any Amazon Bedrock API keys that you created for testing.
The inference profiles themselves are system-defined and incur no cost when they aren’t in use.
Security and compliance
Cross-Region inference is designed to protect your data in transit and at rest. Requests travel over the AWS private backbone encrypted with TLS 1.2+ rather than the public internet. For Canadian customers, your data at rest stays in your source Region by default. This includes invocation logs, knowledge bases, and configurations. Only the transient inference computation happens in the destination Region, and by default model providers don’t have access to your prompts or completions.
There’s one consideration specific to OpenAI models. Content flagged by automated abuse classifiers might be retained for up to 30 days in the destination Region for review. If you want to constrain processing to North America (Canada and the US), you can choose the US geographic profile. We recommend reviewing Amazon Bedrock abuse detection with your compliance team.
For a more detailed look at Canadian data residency patterns, see Cross-Region Inference and Canadian Data Residency: A Technical Architecture Guide.
Conclusion
In this post, we showed how to access OpenAI GPT-5.6 (Sol, Terra, and Luna), GPT-6 (Astra, Sol, and Luna), and GPT-6.1 Sol from Canada. These models are available from the Canada (Central) and Canada West (Calgary) Regions using cross-Region inference on Amazon Bedrock. We covered the available inference profiles, how to set up permissions and an example SCP, and how to invoke the models with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Converse APIs. For the Responses API, we included streaming and tool-use examples. We also showed how to request quota increases, review usage, and clean up your test resources.
To get started, review the OpenAI model cards in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide, then open the Amazon Bedrock console and send a test prompt through an inference profile. For pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock pricing page.
If you have questions or feedback, leave a comment on this post.

articles.title: Ex-OpenAI Worker Accused of Bugging Conference Room Planned to Fly to Saudi Arabia, Prosecutors Say
articles.text:
A former OpenAI engineer charged with secretly installing a recording device in a conference room to glean company details had been “mere days” away from absconding to Saudi Arabia before his arrest last week, federal prosecutors revealed in new court filings.
Abdulrahman Alfozan’s wife and young son also left the country the day after the 35-year-old Saudi national’s arrest, traveling on a one-way ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official, prosecutors said in a memo Sunday seeking his continued detention.
“Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through,” federal prosecutors wrote. “He has ample resources —including his significant compensation from a decade of high-tech employment in the Bay Area and at least two bank accounts in Saudi Arabia — and what appears to be considerable support from a foreign government.”
A federal judge in San Francisco sided with prosecutors Monday, denying a request by Alfozan’s lawyers to release him to home confinement. His next court date is Nov.
Alfozan’s lawyer William Pernik argued in court that his client had strong ties to the U.S. and was “weeks away from achieving every immigrant’s dream” — U.S. citizenship.
Alfozan had a naturalization interview with federal officials scheduled next month and has been a lawful permanent resident since 2020, his lawyers said in their legal filings. He has also lived in the U.S. for 15 years and attended MIT and the University of California, Berkeley, they said.
Pernik said Alfozan is willing to put up “almost the entirety” of his assets — about $1 million currently in a U.S. investment account — to cover his bond.
“Everything this man has he’s willing to surrender,” he said, adding that Alfozan’s wife is also willing to return to the U.S. as she still holds a visitor visa that expires in 2033.
Judge Alex Tse appeared doubtful, questioning whether Saudi Arabia’s government would simply reimburse Alfozan if he fled and forfeited his bond.
After the hearing, Pernik said he was disappointed with the ruling but declined further comment.
Pernik had argued in court filings that Alfozan purchased one-way tickets for his family to Saudi Arabia more than two weeks before prosecutors allege the recording devices were installed. They said the couple planned to spend Alfozan’s roughly two-month paternity leave in Saudi Arabia following the birth of their U.S.-citizen son.
But prosecutors said Saudi officials purchased new plane tickets for Alfozan’s wife and son after his arrest, allowing them to leave the U.S. sooner than the Oct. 12 flight Alfozan had originally booked.
Prosecutors have not said what Alfozan might have wanted to do with the recordings, but say he was in “frequent communication” with a member of the Saudi royal family. They said the royal family member repeatedly tried to recruit Alfozan to an artificial intelligence venture being launched in Saudi Arabia.
Alfozan had told the unnamed person he wouldn’t leave OpenAI until his stock was vested, even as he explored other career opportunities in the Middle Eastern kingdom, prosecutors wrote. He had worked at the ChatGPT maker since July 2025 but was fired after his arrest.
Prosecutors say Alfozan concealed an audio recording device in toilet paper and plugged it into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room he wasn’t authorized to access. They say security cameras captured him entering the room and checking behind the television after installing the device. It remained there for several days before being found Sept. 30.
Prosecutors say the conference room was typically used for meetings involving company leaders, government officials and other executives and “discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, as well as nonpublic information.”
OpenAI has said the recording device Alfozan used was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and featured advanced encryption and audio-monitoring capabilities. They also said they had evidence Alfozan planned to place other listening devices elsewhere in the office.
Alfozan has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. If convicted, he faces a five-year prison sentence.

articles.title: London’s Emerald secures €1.66 million to scale its preventive healthcare platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Emerald, a London-based preventive healthcare platform, has secured an additional €1.66 million (£1.4 million/$1.85 million) in funding. This brings the company’s total funding to date to €3.44 million (£2.9 million).
The latest funding includes an €832.2k (£700k) grant from Innovate UK, Emerald’s second award from the organisation, together with a further €832.2k (£700k) in venture capital investment secured after the award. All existing investors, along with new backers including Sequel and Highgoal, supported the round, and Emerald’s valuation increased from its previous funding round.
Alexander Badalyan, co-founder and CEO of Emerald, explained, “There’s huge demand for access to simple healthcare tools that move beyond just testing. People want to understand what those results mean and the steps they can take to boost their long-term health – informed by guidance from trusted medical experts.
“A preventative approach to healthcare significantly improves long-term health outcomes by providing a more holistic view of a patient’s health, highlighting potential issues before they become critical, and empowering people to enter the right pathway earlier.
“Achieving this ambition is a cornerstone of the current Government’s current health agenda – but the NHS cannot deliver this shift alone. Government efforts must be matched with innovative solutions that are able to have widespread reach. Emerald has unlocked access to millions of potential users through its partnerships – with ambitions to become the UK’s go-to platform for long-term health management. This additional funding allows us to build on the demand we’re already seeing, deepen these partnerships, and expand care.”
Founded in 2024, Emerald says its platform combines in-clinic laboratory screening with a digital platform that brings results, wearable data and health history together in one place. This approach helps members identify potential health risks earlier and empowers them to take control of their long-term health.
Explaining its differentiating factor, Emerald notes that traditional health checks capture one moment in time, whereas the UK startup connects comprehensive testing with users’ past results, lifestyle, and wearable data to reveal patterns, priorities, and changes.
It further notes that every member is paired with a GP who can diagnose, prescribe, and make formal referrals into both private and NHS care where appropriate.
The company highlighted that it is clinician-founded and Care Quality Commission registered, offering regulated activities including diagnostic and screening procedures and treatment of disease, disorder or injury. The platform is also authorised as a UKCA Class I medical device with the MHRA.
Since the beginning of 2026, the company reported that it has grown its member base tenfold and has now processed more than 100k laboratory tests, with repeat-screening data. According to the startup, this data highlights improvements in cholesterol levels for two out of three users, blood sugar levels dropping by a third, and reduced inflammation amongst members dropping by almost half. In January this year, the company announced the closure of its €1.78 million ($2 million) pre-Seed round.
Emerald also mentioned that it has significantly expanded its clinical capabilities and, over the last 12 months, it has announced partnerships with Pluxee, Epassi, Yonder and other businesses across the employee benefits, FinTech and fitness sectors to scale its offering.
With this approach, the company intends to enable employers to include its services as part of their existing benefits offering.
Chris Sawyer, Innovation Lead, Digital Health at Innovate UK, said, “Connecting earlier health insights with appropriate care is an important opportunity for healthcare innovation in the UK. Through this award, we are supporting Emerald’s development of AI-enabled technology designed to help clinicians deliver more personalised, proactive care. We look forward to seeing the project progress and the impact it could have on health outcomes.”
The company plans to use this additional funding to support commercial expansion and further development of its products and clinical services as the platform aims to reach one million members over the next three years.
The Innovate UK grant will specifically support the expansion of Emerald’s AI applications and underlying technology, with the aim of improving healthcare outcomes across the UK.

articles.title: Geoffrey Hinton, el padrino de la IA: “No soy catastrofista. Creo que hay un 1% de posibilidades de que nos destruya”
articles.text: El científico computacional y Premio Nobel de Física Geoffrey Hinton durante el Festival Starmus 2026 que se celebra este martes en el municipio de Arona en Tenerife. Hace años, cuando la gente preguntaba a Geoffrey Hinton por qué trabajaba con la inteligencia artificial, él repetía una frase de Oppenheimer, uno de los creadores de la bomba atómica: “Cuando ves algo grandioso, sigues adelante y lo llevas a cabo”. Ya no lo dice. Ahora se dedica a alertar sobre los peligros de continuar la carrera que él mismo empezó. Confiesa que, en parte, se arrepiente del trabajo al que ha dedicado una vida. Su reconversión de padrino de la IA a profeta de la catástrofe marcó un punto de inflexión en la industria. Sucedió en 2023, cuando abandonó su puesto como vicepresidente de Google entre advertencias funestas. Entonces, algunos vieron su reacción exagerada. Tres años después, muchos han seguido sus pasos. Seguir leyendo

articles.title: IBM-backed llm-d framework adds controls for running AI models in-house - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM-backed llm-d framework adds controls for running AI models in-house
IBM Corp. and several other contributors to the open-source llm-d project are releasing version 1.0 of their distributed artificial intelligence inference framework, adding operational controls intended to help enterprises run large models reliably on their own infrastructure.
The release, announced ahead of the PyTorch Conference North America in San Jose today and tomorrow, focuses on managing competing workloads, maintaining service during upgrades and improving hardware efficiency as AI agents generate growing volumes of model requests.
Built for Kubernetes, llm-d coordinates model serving across computing infrastructure. IBM, its Red Hat subsidiary and Google LLC are its lead maintainers. They co-founded the project last year with CoreWeave Inc. and Nvidia Corp. Other contributors include Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Cisco Systems Inc., Hugging Face Inc., Intel Corp. and Mistral AI SAS.
The project offers organizations seeking more control over inference costs and infrastructure choices a way to reduce dependence on a single model provider, cloud or hardware platform.
“At IBM Research, we are seeing that open large language models and llm-d can greatly lower the costs of inference in computationally demanding problems such as designing hardware for quantum error correction, helping achieve a 11.8X efficiency advantage,” Ruchir Puri, IBM Research’s chief scientist, vice president of IBM’s Technology & Technical Community and IBM Fellow, wrote in e-mailed comments. “Llm-d 1.0 extends these savings by delivering the operational readiness needed for enterprises to extract more out of their computational capacity.”
The project is focused on what happens after deployment. A production inference service must handle changing traffic, hardware failures, software updates and users competing for resources while maintaining acceptable response times.
Version 1.0 adds support for quality of service across multiple tenants, zero-downtime operations and serving patterns tailored to AI agents. Flow controls and prioritization are designed to keep bursts of agent activity from overwhelming services that require fast responses, such as coding assistants used by people.
The release “adds the maturity to run it like any other critical service: a stable [application programming interface], multiple tenants with competing priorities sharing the same infrastructure and upgrades that don’t interrupt operations,” said Carlos Costa, distinguished engineer at IBM Research and a project co-founder and lead maintainer.
Workloads can behave differently even when they reach models through the same endpoint. An agent may issue many requests, pause to use an external tool and return for additional model calls.
The framework can keep requests directed to appropriate infrastructure across multiple turns, increasing opportunities to reuse previously processed context. That matters because agents repeatedly consult the same code, documents, instructions and conversation history while completing assignments.
A routing system directs requests toward replicas that already hold relevant cached context. Another capability moves cached information among graphics processing unit memory, CPU memory and storage, preserving reusable information when GPU capacity becomes constrained.
These techniques were previously available, but version 1.0 integrates them with operational controls, along with methods that separate prompt processing from response generation, optimize work batches and distribute large mixture-of-experts models across accelerators. IBM cited a recent agentic coding test in which the framework’s router captured 97% of available cache reuse.
In a separate demonstration, IBM and Red Hat said they ran 3,000 software-engineering agents concurrently on self-hosted infrastructure at a cost five to 10 times lower than serving the same open model through a hosted service.
The economics become more significant as agents perform multiple rounds of reasoning, tool use and revision for a single assignment, IBM said. Reprocessing identical material at each step consumes additional computing resources.
Llm-d works with inference engines including vLLM and SGLang, supplying distributed routing and operational capabilities around model servers. It is currently hosted as a sandbox project by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.
“It delivers high-performance, distributed inference with the reliability and scale enterprises need within an operational model they already know,” said Stephen Watt, vice president in Red Hat’s chief technology officer’s office.

articles.title: This program is pushing startups to plan for security sooner | BetaKit
articles.text:
Startup founders spend plenty of time thinking about their product, customers, and capital. Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst wants security added to the top of that list.
The Catalyst’s upcoming Cyber for Startups program aims to show that cybersecurity can play an outsized role in the most critical stages of company-building. The no-cost program will offer online and in-person cohorts this fall. Participating early- and mid-stage Canadian technology startups will have access to assessments, workshops, tools, templates, and coaching, all aimed at building security into products, operations, and growth plans, from the beginning.
“Cybersecurity doesn’t have to be overwhelming or prohibitively expensive.”
Charles Finlay,
Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst
“For startups, cybersecurity isn’t just about protecting against threats but about creating opportunities,” said Charles Finlay, founding executive director at Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst. “Strong security practices can help founders win customers’ confidence, attract investment, and compete for larger contracts. When security is treated as an afterthought, startups risk closing doors to opportunities they’ve worked hard to create.”
According to Finlay, strong security practices should be considered part of best practices, as those practices help startups with customer trust, enterprise procurement, investment readiness, and access to regulated markets. It also helps companies avoid technical debt, which becomes more costly to address as they grow. Cyber for Startups is geared toward companies that are building or scaling technology products, preparing to sell into enterprise or regulated markets, or looking to strengthen their cybersecurity posture as they grow. These companies face security expectations across several important parts of the business.
Enterprise buyers and regulators, for example, usually want to understand how a startup protects sensitive information, and often ask about controls, policies, or even SOC 2 attestation. Investors may also scrutinize security practices as part of due diligence. Security can also reach back into product development itself, influencing decisions around architecture and how data is handled within a product.
Cyber for Startups is designed to help companies work through each of those challenges in a structured way. During the program, participants will assess their current security posture, identify gaps, and turn those findings into a tailored, long-term roadmap that details which issues need attention now and which should become a milestone later. Crucially, the program focuses on how to communicate security posture to potential clients, helping founders gain trust even when the work is in progress.
“One of the biggest challenges comes when a startup moves from building a product to selling it,” Finlay added. “Suddenly, prospective customers are asking detailed questions about how their data will be protected, what security controls are in place, and how risks are managed. Founders can find themselves scrambling to meet expectations they hadn’t anticipated. We want to help companies prepare for those conversations well before they’re sitting across the table from a potential customer.”
Cyber for Startups is designed to help founders build security into their product development and go-to-market strategies from the outset because cybersecurity requirements need to inform how a product is built, who it will be sold to, and which markets the company plans to enter. Startups that put off these critical decisions risk accumulating technical debt, leaving them with costly and complex security problems to untangle as the business grows.
“Decisions about how data is collected and stored, who has access to systems, and how security is built into a product can seem relatively minor when a company is small,” Finlay said. “But those decisions become much harder and more expensive to reverse as the business grows. Getting the fundamentals right early on can save founders from having to rebuild critical parts of their technology down the road.”
The program is targeted toward the people making these decisions, including technical founders, product leaders, and executives responsible for compliance, risk, or growth. No prior formal cybersecurity training is required.
Cyber for Startups will be delivered across several cohorts across Canada this fall, both virtually and in person. The first in-person cohort will take place in Brampton, Ont., on Nov. 12, in partnership with the City of Brampton, Brampton Innovation District, and the Canadian Cyber Threat Exchange, with funding provided in part by the Government of Ontario. Applications for the Brampton cohort are open until Oct. 30.
“When security is treated as an afterthought, startups risk closing doors to opportunities they’ve worked hard to create.”
Charles Finlay,
Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst
RBC will support two other offerings: an online cohort running through November and December, and an in-person Vancouver cohort scheduled for February. Rolling registration will be available for both.
Offering both formats is intended to make the program more accessible to startups in different regions and stages of growth in Canada. In-person cohorts will run over a single day and prioritize networking and coaching, while the online version spreads the program across four weeks, focusing on roadmapping work.
As startups grow, the financial stakes of cybersecurity can grow with them. Data from the Canadian Internet Registration Authority found that 39 percent of Canadian organizations surveyed this year had experienced a cyber attack in the last 12 months.
The costs of these incidents can also be significant. Statistics Canada’s most recent survey on the topic found that Canadian businesses spent roughly $1.2 billion recovering from cybersecurity incidents in 2023, nearly double the amount reported in 2021.
Cyber for Startups is designed to make security an early decision for founders, before growth turns it into a more expensive one.
“I want founders to leave understanding that they don’t need to have everything figured out on day one, but they do need a plan,” Finlay said. “Cybersecurity doesn’t have to be overwhelming or prohibitively expensive. It’s about understanding your risks, making informed decisions, and taking practical steps as your business grows. That’s exactly what we’re trying to help startups do through this program.”
PRESENTED BY
Build security into your startup from the start. Apply for the next cohort of Cyber for Startups.
Feature image courtesy Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst.

articles.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
articles.text:
8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
On October 19, 2026, at approximately 17:00 UTC, Cloudflare became aware that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised. These certificates were widely trusted by browsers, operating systems, and also within Cloudflare. Because the keys themselves are weak, an attacker can create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic. This is a serious security incident with implications across the Internet. For reference, here is a link to more information about how SSL certificates work and why they are so critical to the operation of the Internet.
We immediately prioritized patching critical services across Cloudflare to protect our customers ahead of the public disclosure of the vulnerability. Our security review has not identified active exploitation of this issue on Cloudflare services.
We have released updates for the Cloudflare One Clients, also known as WARP or the 1.1.1.1 app, and Cloudflare Tunnel, also known as cloudflared. We have also deployed mitigations across our CDN, Developer, and Zero Trust products. If you are using Cloudflare Zero Trust with Gateway and an up-to-date client (see below), you are automatically protected.
Our response
We prioritized updating services that use public certificates to authenticate remote endpoints, including proxies connecting to origins and applications calling external APIs. In parallel, we updated shared trust stores, base images, and other shared foundations, providing a common mitigation path for services that inherit their certificate trust from those sources. We paired these updates with reloads, restarts, and image deployments needed to activate them. Applications with bundled or custom trust stores received separate assessment and updates. This work addresses certificate-based authentication, not a weakness in TLS’s encryption algorithms.
Teams across Cloudflare are presently working on further remediation. We are making progress, but there's much work still to be done. Some customers will need to take action on software or trust configurations that they operate, especially on their origin servers. The recommended actions are summarized below.
What customers should do
| Users of these software or services | Action the customer should take | 
| Cloudflare One/WARP | Cloudflare One Client: Upgrade to: v2.5.6 (Android), v1.12.16 (iOS), Windows Desktop (2026.8.2115.0), macOS (2026.8.2115.0), Linux (2026.8.2115.0) 1.1.1.1 app: Upgrade to: v6.38.10 (Android), v6.31.7 (iOS), Windows Desktop (2026.8.2115.0), macOS (2026.8.2115.0), Linux (2026.8.2115.0) | 
| Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) | Upgrade to 2026.10.2. For container deployments, update and redeploy the fixed image | 
| Customer-configured TLS client authentication | Review and update your mutual TLS trust store/uploaded CAs used to verify client certificates | 
| Customer Origin TLS Servers configuration | Review your custom origin certificates and server configurations if using Full (strict) encryption mode or Strict mode. We are updating Automatic SSL/TLS to automatically notify you if you still use these distrusted certificates, which would cause breakages. | 
| Cloudflare Containers | Customers using Cloudflare Containers, including Sandboxes, should review their container images and application dependencies for affected certificate trust stores and apply updates based on your deployed image. Customers can also enable HTTPS egress interception to route outbound HTTPS requests through Cloudflare, moving remote-server certificate validation from the application to Cloudflare-managed infrastructure. This allows Cloudflare’s trust-store mitigations to protect intercepted connections. Containers that have this enabled are already protected. | 
Developer guidance
For developers, look beneath the SDK.
An API client may delegate certificate verification to an HTTP library, a language runtime, the operating system, or a custom trust configuration. Updating the SDK alone may not change the underlying policy.
Once you patch, you may notice certificate errors in your dashboards. It's important to not resolve these errors by disabling verification. That would remove the authentication protection these updates are intended to restore.
This incident affects many software stacks that rely on the WebPKI for authentication. Mozilla’s Dennis Jackson has crowdsourced a list of commonly used packages that have been patched. We advise readers to upgrade as soon as possible. (Note that some of these may be indirect dependencies of your software stack, so look at the dependency tree.) Apply the relevant dependency updates, rebuild affected images, and confirm whether applications require a reload, restart, or redeployment.
Dennis Jackson’s test site provides browser checks, non-browser testing instructions, and package update information. Results apply to the verification path being tested, not every application on the device. Validate through the application’s actual TLS path. A successful browser test does not prove that a background service is protected. Neither does a curl test if the application uses a different verifier.
Timeline
The timeline of events so far is below.
| Date and Time | Event | 
| October 19, approximately 17:00 UTC | Cloudflare becomes aware of the compromise and begins assessment. | 
| October 20, 02:00 UTC | Cloudflare One Client and WARP app security updates published across platforms (except Cloudflare One Agent on iOS, for which app review is still pending). | 
| October 20 09:15 UTC | Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) security update published. | 
| October 20 19:20 UTC | CDN and server-side Zero Trust mitigations fully deployed. | 
Looking forward
The impact of this incident is not felt equally. Browser maintainers were able to remediate the issue with a flip of a switch. They of course have just one application to update, instead of hundreds, but they do have a neat trick up their sleeves: most browsers use quick-revocation mechanisms (like Chrome CRLSets). At Cloudflare we also use such a mechanism for some of our products. To bring it to more systems at Cloudflare and industry, we’re excited about projects like upki that understand a trust store can’t be a static list of root certificate authorities, but needs the ability to be quickly updated with information like revocation and certificate transparency keys.

articles.title: An 'enormous influx' of new Garmin Connect IQ apps and watch faces spark fears of poor-quality AI slop flooding the store
articles.text:
'Poorly made, AI-generated watch faces will consume everything': Garmin's Connect IQ store has been hit by an 'enormous influx' of submissions, and Garmin users could soon be grappling with a wave of AI slop
Garmin has a Connect IQ problem
- Garmin's Connect IQ store has seen an 'enormous influx' of new submissions
- These include apps and watch faces, and are causing a big backlog as developers struggle to get their submissions reviewed
- It's likely AI is to blame, as the sudden wave of submissions 'was never a problem in the past'
If you wear one of the best Garmin watches, you might have used the Garmin Connect IQ store to download an app like Spotify or Komoot, a new free or paid watch face (even a Pokémon-branded one), or a fun community-made complication like the Walk with Frodo app. However, downloading stuff from the Connect IQ store in future may involve sifting through thousands of low-quality, AI-generated submissions.
Watch face and app developers are complaining on Garmin's forums about delays in submission review: while the process typically takes 1-2 days, according to some devs, the process is now taking up to 13 days.
Garmin Connect IQ moderator/representative Brandon posted directly to one thread, stating: "This is not due to a bug — we have gotten an enormous influx of app submissions in the last month, with no signs of slowing down, and are working through approvals as quickly as we can.
"This was never a problem in the past, except perhaps delays because of a long holiday weekend (e.g. Christmas)."
The fact this glut of submissions is a sudden problem or new phenomenon points to one thing only — AI. Garmin Connect IQ has likely been flooded with vibe-coded or AI-generated products designed to make a quick buck by flooding the digital marketplace.
One Garmin user said in response to Brandon: "You need to limit the upload frequency for each developer; those poorly made AI-generated watch faces will consume everything."
Another said: "I have observed this trend worsening significantly as well. The Connect IQ Store is increasingly flooded with low-effort, repetitive submissions that hurt discoverability, degrade user trust, and crowd out well-crafted apps."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While this is bad for developers (who get charged $100 annually to sell apps on the Connect IQ store) it's also bad for Garmin users. We'll now have to wade through a sea of AI slop watch faces in order to get to faces and apps created the old-fashioned way — with human-led, thought-out complications developed and designed by real Garmin users.
It's just one more example of digital merchants being reduced to dealing with an avalanche of AI slop submissions, just like other app stores, and almost every other breed of online storefronts for digital products. We reported as far back as 2023 that AI-generated e-books were flooding Kindle Unlimited, making it difficult for users to find new books, and the problem has only gotten worse with time. The same will likely happen to the Connect IQ store.
I've reached out to Garmin for comment on the situation, and will update this article if I get any response. In the meantime, if you're a Connect IQ user and you've noticed the change, let us know in the comments below.

Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: TikTok staff raised child safety concerns, but executives reportedly failed to act | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok was repeatedly warned by employees about the risks the social media platform posed to children, according to court records obtained by NPR. The documents say employees were frustrated with how executives responded to their concerns about risks to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide-related content.
Depositions of employees filed in March 2026 are shedding new light on TikTok’s child safety practices.
According to NPR, TikTok employees warned that minors were appearing in sexual content that was available for purchase on TikTok, raising concerns that the company could profit from potentially illegal activity. They also flagged that minors were exploiting loopholes to access age-restricted content and hide their activity from parents.
Additionally, the court documents show that TikTok didn’t conduct surveys to determine the age of its users out of concern that it would have to share the results with the Federal Trade Commission.
“These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works,” a TikTok spokesperson said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch. “It’s unfortunate that NPR has chosen to ignore the numerous documents and resources we have provided that demonstrate how these claims mischaracterize our record and platform features.”
The statement continues, “We have invested billions of dollars in Trust & Safety and rolled out more than 50 preset safety, privacy, and security settings for teens, including Family Pairing, which helps parents and guardians customize the experience for their teens. We remain steadfast in our commitment to the well-being of our community.”
TikTok, in addition to Meta, Google, and Snap, faces hundreds of lawsuits consolidated in federal court. The lawsuits allege that these companies’ platforms harm minors and that they failed to disclose known risks to young users.
TikTok has reached settlements in several of these cases before they went to trial, including one in Los Angeles where a jury found that Meta and YouTube had designed their platforms to be addictive to young users.
Update 10/20/2026 10:00 a.m. PT: The article was updated to include a statement from TikTok.

articles.title: A good TA: priceless
articles.text:
A good TA: priceless
Tom Davis ’84, SM ’85
These are images of quizzes I took in 3.091, Introduction to Solid-State Chemistry, in the fall of 1980.
One is my very first exam at MIT, and getting 49 out of 100 was a soul-crushing experience. I can still picture the TA, Leszek Pawlowicz, PhD ’87, returning my paper. He had a big smile on his face, and he said something to the effect of “I expect to see you double your score on the next quiz!”
Well, I got the message. Studying at MIT was not like studying in high school, but I got 100 on the next quiz and graduated with good enough grades to get me into grad school. All it took, it seems, was that initial kick in the seat of my pants, then a kind hand helping me up off the ground.
Recently, I connected with Leszek, and he replied with a charming note. It felt good to let him know how much his encouragement meant to me. A good TA can really have lasting impact!

articles.title: SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
articles.text:
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company would attempt to catch Starship and its booster next month, with the goal of recovering the entire orbital launch system for the first time. If successful, Musk said, the attempt would mark the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered.
SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
If successful, it would be the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered.
“This is a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization consciousness,” he said during the company’s third quarter earnings report Tuesday.
But he also allowed for the possibility of a failure. “Success is not guaranteed on these first flights, but I’d say it’s more likely than not that this succeeds next flight,” Musk said. “And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year and then accelerating next year.”
“Success is not guaranteed on these first flights, but I’d say it’s more likely than not that this succeeds next flight.”
— Elon Musk
Starship is a two-stage system, composed of the Super Heavy booster (first stage) and the Starship spacecraft (second stage). It stands approximately 120 meters (around 400 feet) tall with a 9-meter diameter, and is powered by SpaceX’s Raptor engines burning liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Starship, which was first introduced in 2018, was designed to return to the launch site, where launch towers with mechanical “chopstick” arms catch the vehicle mid-air.
Last month’s Starship launch represented two firsts for its next gen rocket: send the spacecraft into Earth orbit, and insert a few dozen of SpaceX’s larger and more capable V3 satellites into the Starlink constellation for the first time. Still, the launch wasn’t without its snafus: one Raptor engine shut down prematurely during ascent, prompting mission control to adapt and complete the climb on remaining. Because of the issue, SpaceX cut the planned 10-hour, 6-orbit mission short after about 3 hours and 2 Earth orbits.
The Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico, while the Starship upper stage executed a de-orbit burn and ended with a fiery vertical splashdown in the Pacific Ocean north of Hawaii. Neither piece was recovered.

articles.title: Google DeepMind says four AI agents beat Minecraft in 27 hours by writing 2,783 programs of their own — AI team died 605 times on Easy difficulty and ran up an estimated $520 in tokens
articles.text:
Google DeepMind says four AI agents beat Minecraft in 27 hours by writing 2,783 programs of their own — AI team died 605 times on Easy difficulty and ran up an estimated $520 in tokens
About half the run was spent fighting the dragon, solved by stacking dirt to reach its crystals.
The game of Minecraft is no match for a team of four Gemini 4 Argon agents, as they were able to defeat it in 27 hours with 2,783 self-written programs, a paper from Google DeepMind reveals. The agents did die 605 times, even on Easy, and about half the run was spent fighting the Ender Dragon, the final boss of the game. The run finally came to completion when the End was solved by stacking dirt to reach the boss’s crystals, at an estimated cost of around $520 in tokens.
The experimental run was designed from the get-go with one goal: kill the Ender Dragon. The playthrough involved a random, shared survival world on Easy with four agents — a fifth agent existed only for reporting — from Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s latest frontier model. Each agent had its own player through the open-source Mineflayer JavaScript library for Minecraft bots, but they were able to coordinate through in-game chat and shared notes. Every program used in the run was written by the agents themselves, and the emphasis is on coding and teamwork rather than game-playing.
The authors say this is the “first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents,” at least “to our knowledge,” qualified by the use of Mineflayer “without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans.” Mineflayer tells the agents where blocks and creatures are, with a pathfinding plugin to plan routes. There was “no human input during the run” and “no one assigned roles or wrote game logic.” The run, starting with the first program and ending with the dragon's death, took 27 hours and 14 minutes.
Although the agents were not given roles, within about 10 minutes a division of labor was proposed in chat by bot janesick. Bot Auratian offered an alternative plan while Bot Gyldenia acknowledged it. The roles ended up being: Gyldenia for food, beds, and flint; Bulicame for diamonds; Janesick for iron and tools; Auratian for the Nether portal. Moments of losses, such as a Ghast fireball destroying dropped items, led the team to diagnose the cause and write rules to prevent it in the future.
Finding the stronghold involved janesick, who threw two Eyes of Ender from different spots and sampled each eye’s flight once every 50 ms, triangulating the location. Carrying the eyes involved its own dire moment when Auratian drowned during the task, but the spot was noted, and the eyes were rescued.
The eventual fight with the dragon led to 69 deaths, and the ten crystals kept regenerating the boss until Auratian discovered they could use dirt pillars to reach the crystals. Four hours and 40 minutes later, all ten crystals were downed, and the dragon was dead 39 minutes after that.
The agents operated by writing short JavaScript programs, almost 2,800 in total, with 42 helper functions kept alive between programs, while a Mineflayer bot ran them in the shared world. Text was returned with status data, not pictures. This is a shared approach to the non-screenshot GPT-6 Astra clear of the Orc starting zone in World of Warcraft earlier this month. AI agents playing games is an ongoing trend, with Pokémon Red probably being the most popular, a game defeated in multiple ways, including with a Jev decision model layer.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Minecraft has also been a popular target, and the authors admit this, highlighting two earlier community dragon kills: a planner with an action-selection model on a fixed speedrun seed in Peaceful mode, and a single Claude Opus 5 agent that used 37 ready-made, high-level tools on Normal, versus Mineflayer alone for the Gemini team. AI Bengineering’s Claude run, relying mostly on Opus 5 at high effort, took 3 hours and 56 minutes from start — “no human input after the prompt” — to kill with 388 tool calls and only one death. The cost in that case, at API-equivalent rates, was about $93.
Google’s Minecraft run, using Gemini 4 Argon’s 50% introductory pricing, which runs from initial API access that followed the model announcement through Nov. 30, cost more than half a grand; at normal pricing, that’s more than a grand. A GPT-6 Astra Portal run last month, which took about 24 hours, came in at $571 in tokens.
Google’s run took about 1.35 billion input tokens with 91% served from cache. About 24,000 model calls involved around 16 million output tokens, a quarter of them thinking. In total, if we’re also including the observer agent, the session would be estimated at $810, or $1,620 after the promotion, at list prices.
Each player is driven by a “general-purpose Gemini 4 Argon coding agent,” which is a fancy way of saying that it’s not specialized for Minecraft. Gemini 4 Argon itself is a frontier model for “real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense,” according to a company blog. With Minecraft, 22% of the agents’ programs ended in an error, with more than 600 deaths.
Although the model was used for a game here, the run was designed to show that Argon is capable of “complex, long-horizon workflows” for complex real-world tasks and agent coordination. Such long projects can involve decompiling a game back into source code, as we covered recently with a Modern Warfare 2 rebuild that now has 83% of its functions matching the original byte for byte.

Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Revolut outage disrupts online banking operations worldwide
articles.text:
Fintech company Revolut is working to resolve a massive outage that disrupted most of its services worldwide earlier today.
Since the incident began, thousands of users on the Downdetector outage tracking platform have reported issues with the Revolut app, mobile banking services, and transferring funds between accounts.
In a statement today, the company said the outage has affected its services since Tuesday morning and added that customers' data and funds are safe.
"We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers' money and data are safe," Revolut said.
"We've been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused."
On its official status page, the company says the outage affects 28 services, including sign-ins, card payments, transfers, currency exchange, stock trading, and live support chat, which are now flagged as partially unavailable.
According to Reuters, the Revolut outage is reportedly linked to ongoing service disruptions affecting Google Cloud's London-based europe-west2 data center after a "power event."
A Revolut spokesperson was not immediately available when BleepingComputer reached out earlier about the root cause of today's outage.
Last month, Revolut also disclosed a data breach after it shared personally identifiable information (PII) from an undisclosed number of customers with a threat actor who was impersonating a government agency.
Four years ago, Revolut disclosed another data breach after threat actors stole the personal, contact, and financial information of more than 50,000 customers in September 2022.
Revolut provides banking, money management, and investment services to more than 80 million customers across 160+ countries and regions, including 800,000 business customers.
Update October 20, 13:52 EDT: Revolut has linked today's outage to the Google Cloud incident and said that all services have now been restored.
"Due to a recent Google Cloud outage, customers may have experienced temporary service disruption on the Revolut app today," the company said.
"The issue has now been fixed, and services are now restored. All our customers’ money and data is safe, and has remained safe throughout this incident. We apologise for any inconvenience caused."

articles.title: Jeep pourrait faire renaître la Willys, mais pas forcément comme un vrai 4x4
articles.text:
Alors que les marques du groupe Stellantis semblent toutes se tourner vers leur passé pour trouver des inspirations pour les modèles futurs, Jeep n’avait pas encore relancé un design historique. La marque américaine, intégrée au groupe franco-italien et spécialisée dans les tout-terrains, pourrait faire renaître sa mythique Willys. Voici à quoi on peut s’attendre.
Un modèle urbain et électrique
Même si Jeep reste avare en informations concernant cet éventuel retour de la Willys, on peut raisonnablement attendre l’arrivée d’un véhicule électrique et urbain dans la gamme Jeep pour compléter le succès de l’Avenger. Au Mondial de l’Auto, Jeep a donné sa feuille de route pour 2030 et a ajouté qu’une piste intéressante serait d’imaginer des modèles compacts et électriques s’inspirant des produits mythiques de la marque. On pense évidemment à la Willys.
La Jeep Willys n’a pas de véritable descendante dans la gamme Jeep. Il y a bien le tout-terrain Wrangler, qui en reprend certains traits de design, mais le véhicule a tellement grossi qu’il est difficile de le voir comme une réinterprétation. Pour l’instant, Jeep ne confirme pas la production en série du modèle, mais la marque ne semble pas fermée à l’idée.
Un modèle urbain, mais pas tout-terrain ?
Jeep pourrait se servir de la nouvelle plateforme e-Car de Stellantis, qui servira déjà à la future 2CV, puis à la Panda, pour développer sa Jeep Willys électrique. L’idée serait alors de faire davantage un modèle urbain électrique et abordable qu’un véritable tout-terrain, comme l’était la Jeep Willys arrivée lors du débarquement de Normandie en juin 1944.
Conserver les qualités de tout-terrain chères à la marque Jeep paraît difficile avec cette plateforme, pensée uniquement pour les deux roues motrices pour l’instant. Toutefois, ce ne serait pas la première fois qu’un modèle Jeep serait proposé uniquement en deux roues motrices. L’Avenger a souffert quelque temps de l’absence d’une déclinaison à quatre roues motrices, importante pour l’image de marque de Jeep.
Jeep pourrait participer aux travaux sur la plateforme e-Car de Stellantis pour en proposer une version à quatre roues motrices. Cela permettrait aussi à Fiat de relancer la Panda 4×4, très importante dans l’histoire du modèle italien. Citroën pourrait également rêver du retour d’une Méhari, même si les versions les plus diffusées de cette dernière étaient à deux roues motrices, comme la 2CV. Tous ces modèles citadins à quatre roues motrices pourraient contrer la future Renault 4 E-Tech 4×4, qui semble en préparation du côté de la marque au losange.
